a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six') · also 'to, towards' with spirant mutation (parth a Hardlech 'towards Harlech'; y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall') · also (10) linking a fronted adjective to its noun, with soft mutation of the noun (ys drwc a gedymdeith 'a bad companion'); here a is not the conjunction
ac: a — 'and' before a vowel (ac ef); also the preposition a 'with' before a vowel (ymgael ac ef 'meet with him', ymordiwes ac ef) · the manuscript also writes ac before some consonants (Ac wal, Ac val, ac racdaw) · also 'as' after an equative or kymeint (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'; mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'as unseemly as what she had done')
achaws: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m. ('Pa achaws' 'what reason, why') · also in o achaws 'because of' (o achaws y carchar hwnnw 'because of that prison')
achos: achos — variant spelling of achaws 'cause, reason'; 'o achos' = 'because of'
adeiladeu: adeilad (adeilad) — buildings; noun pl. ('o adeiladeu' 'of buildings')
adnabydy: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognize; 2 sg. future/present 'you will know' (yd adnabydy uoes y llys 'you will learn the court's custom')
adnappo: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognize; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may know', in the negative relative ni'th adnappo 'who does not know you'
aeth: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. preterite 'went' (a'y vreic a aeth attaw 'and his wife went to him')
aethant: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. preterite 'they went' (yd aethant 'they went')
af: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 sg. present/future 'I go, I will go' (a af 'will go')
allan: allan — out, forth; adverb ('o hynny allan' 'from then on')
am: am — preposition 'about, around; concerning' (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck'; am dir a dayar 'about land') · also 'for, in return for' (am y gam 'for his wrong'; am pob un 'for each one')
amdanaw: am — conjugated preposition 'about him' (3 sg. m.); clothing/objects are 'about' a person (gwisc ... amdanaw)
amdanei: am — conjugated preposition 'about her' (3 sg. f.); eurwisc amdanei 'a gold garment about her'
amgen: amgen — other, different; adjective/adverb ('beth amgen' 'what else?'; 'amgen noc' 'other than')
amser: amser — time; noun m. (Amser a doeth udunt 'the time came to them')
amserach: amser — comparative 'more timely, more fitting' (phan uu amserach kymryt hun 'when it was more time to sleep')
angheu: angheu (angau) — death; noun m. (uy angheu i 'my death'; teruynedic angheu 'death is determined')
angheuawl: angheuawl (angheuol) — deadly, mortal; adjective from angheu 'death' (angheuawl dyrnawt 'a deadly blow')
anglot: anglot (anglod) — dishonour, disgrace; an- 'un-' + clot 'fame' (o anglot itt 'dishonour to you')
annwuyn: Annwuyn (Annwfn, Annwn) — the realm Arawn rules, a world alongside this one; proper name
anryded: anryded (anrhydedd) — rank, standing; noun m./f. ('o anryded' 'of rank')
ansawd: ansawd — (1) form, appearance (pryt ac ansawd 'form and appearance'); (2) means, condition (Nit oes ansawd y mi 'I have no means')
anuon: anuon (anfon) — to send; verbal noun ('anuon o pop un y gilid' 'each one sending to the other')
anwybot: anwybot (anwybod) — ignorance; an- 'un-' + gwybot 'know', noun (dy anwybot dy hun 'your own ignorance')
ar: ar — (1) preposition 'on, upon; at' (ar Hafgan; ar y carw; ar y gilyd 'against the other'); (2) the article yr after a vowel, 'that which' (noc ar a uu 'than what was'; Ar ny del 'and whoever does not come') · also (3) 'with, accompanied by' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen'); 'in' (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses'; ar perued y digrifwch 'in the middle of the merriment'); ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'; ar uyrr 'quickly'; ar hynny 'thereupon' (see yny) · also 'over' (ar yr ynys hon 'over this island'); 'after the manner of' (ar ureint kyweirdeb 'in the manner of the arrangement'); 'on' a decision (disgynnu ar gymryt hynny 'settled on taking that'); 'ar ol' 'after' (ar ol Matholwch 'after Matholwch'); ar dec 'on ten' (see dec) · also 'concerning, about', where am would be expected (ac ar Yspydaut Benn 'and concerning the Hospitality of the Head'; the Red Book also ar) · ar + verbal noun, 'to, in order to' (doethwyf i ar diuetha y pryf 'I have come to destroy the creature')
arall: arall — other, another; adjective (yr erchwys arall 'the other pack') · also pronoun 'another (woman)' (heb arall 'said another') · also 'again, more' after kymeint (y gymeint arall 'as much again')
arawn: Arawn — proper name, king of Annwfn; meaning unknown
arberth: Arberth (Arberth) — proper name, Pwyll's chief court, modern Narberth in Dyfed
archo: erchi — to ask, request; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may ask' (A chyt archo ef 'and though he ask')
ardurn: ardurn (adurn) — adornment, array; noun m. (yr ardurn teccaf 'the fairest adornment')
arglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m., term of address
arglwydes: arglwydes (arglwyddes) — lady; feminine of arglwyd, term of address
arglwydiaeth: arglwydiaeth (arglwyddiaeth) — lordship, rule; noun f. (y arglwydiaeth ef 'his lordship')
arnaf: ar — conjugated preposition 'on me' (arnaf i 'on me')
arnat: ar — conjugated preposition 'on you' (sg.) (y mae arnat o anryded 'there is rank on you'; a'm ansawd arnat ti)
arnaw: ar — conjugated preposition 'on him, on it' (llithiau dy erchwys dy hun arnaw 'feeding your own pack on it')
arnei: ar — conjugated preposition 'on her' (a charyat arnei 'and love on her') · also 'on it', of a feminine noun (a eistedo arnei 'who may sit on it', of the mound)
arnunt: ar — conjugated preposition 'on them' (Sef lliw oed arnunt 'this was the colour that was on them')
arueu: arueu (arfau) — arms, armour; noun pl. (yny dyrr yr arueu oll 'so that all the armour breaks')
at: at — preposition 'to, towards' (at y cwn 'to the dogs')
attaw: at — conjugated preposition 'to him' (y marchawc a doeth attaw 'the horseman came to him')
attei: at — conjugated preposition 'to her' (3 sg. f.) (a'y geuyn attei hitheu 'and his back to her')
attep: attep (ateb) — answer, reply; noun m. (attep ny chauas ef 'he got no answer')
attygaf: attygu — to take back, withdraw; 1 sg. present 'I will withdraw' (Nac attygaf 'I will not')
attygy: attygu — to take back, withdraw; 2 sg. present 'you will withdraw' (nys attygy 'you will not withdraw it')
atuyd: atuyd (efallai) — perhaps; adverb, literally 'it will be' (ac atuyd y mae arnat...)
auory: auory (yfory) — tomorrow; adverb (o'r dyd auory 'from the day tomorrow')
bali: bali — brocade, rich silk; noun m., a loanword from Old French paile (eurwisc o bali 'a gold garment of brocade')
baraf: peri (peri) — to cause, bring about; 1 sg. present 'I will cause', soft-mutated after a (Mi a baraf)
bellach: bellach — any longer, henceforth; adverb (y'ch kynnal chwi bellach 'to maintain you any longer')
beth: beth — what; interrogative pronoun (beth amgen 'what else?', beth a wnaf 'what shall I do?')
beunoeth: beunoeth (beunoeth) — every night, nightly; adverb (y gyscu gyt a thi beunoeth)
blwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f. (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end')
bo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be' (Vrth ual y bo dy anryded 'according as your rank may be')
bob: pob — each, every; adjective, soft-mutated after a vowel/particle (bob un 'each one')
bogel: bogel — boss (of a shield); noun m. (bogel y daryan 'the boss of his shield')
bonedigeidaf: bonedigeidaf (boneddigeiddaf) — superlative of bonedigeid 'noble, well-born'; 'the most noble'
bordeu: bord (bwrdd) — tables; noun pl. (cherchu y bordeu 'making for the tables')
bot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun (hyt na bo... uot 'so that there be...') · also introducing a reported fact, 'that (it) was' (adnabot bot eu hennill yn pallu 'knowing that their gain was failing'; clybot bot y gwyr 'hearing that the men were')
brenhin: brenhin (brenin) — king; noun m. (Brenhin corunawc wyf i 'I am a crowned king')
brynaf: prynu (prynu) — to buy; 1 sg. present, soft-mutated after a (mi a brynaf dy gerennyd 'I will buy your friendship')
bu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (a uu 'was'; Llawen uu 'glad was')
buost: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. preterite 'you were' (ny buost gyn hygaret guas 'you were never so lovable a lad')
bwyf: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. present subjunctive 'I may be' (kyt bwyf i yno 'though I be there')
bwyt: bwyt (bwyd) — food; noun m. (bwyt a llynn 'food and drink')
byd: bot (bod) — to be; used two ways: 3 sg. future 'will be' (uyd elsewhere) and, with y-, the vivid present ual y byd 'as he is' · also 2 sg. imperative 'be!' (byd ditheu a'r got honn genhyt 'you be there with this bag') · also byt 'world', spelt with d (eliwlu y byd o lygot 'the world's host of mice'; the Red Book y byt)
bynnac: bynnac (bynnag) — -ever, indefinite particle after peth/pwy etc.; 'Peth bynnac' 'whatever'
byt: byt (byd) — world; noun m. (o helgwn y byt 'of the hunting dogs of the world')
byw: byw — alive; adjective (ny byd byw ef 'he will not be alive') · also a noun 'living, life' (hyt nat oed well genti y byw no'y marw 'so that her living was no better to her than her dying')
cadarn: cadarn (cadarn) — strong, firm; adjective (kedymdeithas gadarn 'a firm fellowship', soft-mutated after the fem. noun)
cadarnhau: cadarnhau — to strengthen; verbal noun, from cadarn 'strong' (dechreu cadarnhau kedymdeithas 'the fellowship began to strengthen')
caf: caffael (cael) — to get, obtain; 1 sg. present 'I get, shall get' (pa furyf y caf i dy gerennyd 'how shall I get your friendship')
caffael: caffael (cael) — to get, obtain, win; verbal noun (caffael o honot 'your getting/winning')
can: can — hundred; numeral, also 'white' (Hafgan = haf + can 'summer-white'); here in guerth can carw 'the worth of a hundred stags' · also can 'since, because' (can doethwyf i 'since I have come') · also can mwyaf 'for the most part, mostly', can = gan 'with, by' (ac eu harueu can mwyaf 'and their arms for the most part')
canis: canys — since, because; variant spelling of canys (canis rywelsei ef 'since he had seen them')
canlynwys: canlyn (canlyn) — to follow; 3 sg. preterite 'followed' (o'r a'm canlynwys i 'of those that have followed me')
cantref: cantref (cantref) — a 'hundred townships', the main administrative division of medieval Wales; noun m. (seith cantref Dyuet 'the seven cantrefs of Dyfed')
canu: canu (canu) — to sing, sound (a horn); verbal noun (canu y gorn 'sounding his horn')
canys: canys — since, for, because; conjunction (canys dechreueist uy llad 'since you have begun to kill me') · also for kan 'since' + nys 'not … it' (Canys collyghy yr hynny 'since you will not release it for that'; the Red Book Kan nys gellyngy) · also plain affirmative 'since' (A chanys bu 'and since she was')
canyt: canyt (canys + nid) — 'since ... not' (canyt oes urenhin 'since there is no king')
ch: ych (eich) — 'your' (pl.), infixed after y: y'ch (y'ch kynnal chwi 'to maintain you') · also the object 'you' (pl.) after a (mi a'ch differaf 'I will protect you')
chadw: cadw (cadw) — to keep; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a chadw kywirdeb 'and keeping faithfulness') · also spirant-mutated after 'y 'her' (a'y chadw gantaw 'and keeping her with him', the mouse)
chanu: canu (canu) — to sing, sound; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a chanu y gorn 'and sounding his horn')
chapla: cablu (cablu) — to blame, revile; 2 sg. imperative, spirant-mutated after the negative na (na chapla di uiui 'do not blame me')
charueidrwyd: carueidrwyd (caruaidd-rwydd) — affection, tenderness; noun, spirant-mutated after a (a charueidrwyd 'and affection')
charyat: karyat (cariad) — love; noun m., spirant-mutated after a (a charyat arnei 'and love for her') · also spirant-mutated (c>ch) after y 'her' (o'y charyat 'from her love / from love of her')
chauas: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. preterite, spirant-mutated after ny (ny chauas ef 'he did not get')
chedymdeithon: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companions; noun pl., spirant-mutated after a (ac ymdidan a chedymdeithon 'and talk with companions')
cherdet: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a cherdet yn ol y cwn 'and going after the hounds') · also the noun 'pace, gait', spirant-mutated after y 'her' (y cherdet hitheu 'her pace')
cherdeu: kerd (cerdd) — songs, music; noun pl., spirant-mutated after a (a cherdeu a chyuedach 'songs and carousing')
chorn: corn (corn) — horn; noun m., spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chorn canu 'and a hunting horn')
chwaethach: chwaethach — much less, let alone; adverb ('yn chwaethach a uei uwy no hynny' 'let alone anything more than that')
chwi: chwi (chi) — 'you' (pl.); pronoun (y'ch kynnal chwi 'to maintain you')
chyn: kyn (cyn) — although, though; spirant-mutated after a (a chyn nyt ymdialwyf 'and though I do not avenge myself') · also the equative particle cyn 'as', spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'and as stout as a boy of six') · also 'before' (a chyn penn y pedwyryd mis 'and before the end of the fourth month')
chynt: kynt (cynt) — before, formerly; adverb, spirant-mutated after no (no chynt 'than before')
chyrch: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; imperative, spirant-mutated after a (A chyrch y llys 'and make for the court')
chyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a chyrchu y bordeu 'and making for the tables')
chyskeis: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; 1 sg. preterite, spirant-mutated after ny (ni chyskeis inheu 'I did not sleep')
chyt: kyt (cyd) — although; spirant-mutated after a (a chyt archo ef 'and though he ask')
chyuarchaf: kyuarch gwell (cyfarch) — to greet ('ask well'); 1 sg. present, spirant-mutated after ny (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you')
chyuedach: kyuedach (cyfeddach) — carousing, a drinking-feast; noun m., spirant-mutated after a (a chyuedach 'and carousing')
chyweiraf: kyweir (cyweir) — well-arrayed; superlative chyweiraf, spirant-mutated after a (hardaf a chyweiraf 'handsomest and best-arrayed')
claerwyn: claerwyn (claerwyn) — bright white, shining white; adjective, claer 'bright' + gwyn 'white'
cledyueu: cledyf (cleddyf) — swords; noun pl. (nerth cledyueu 'the force of swords')
clusteu: clust (clust) — ears; noun pl. (eu clusteu yn gochyon 'their ears red')
cochet: cochet (cochder) — redness; abstract noun in -et from coch 'red' (cochet y clusteu 'the redness of the ears')
coet: coet (coed) — wood, forest; noun m. (dan y coet 'under the wood')
corunawc: corunawc (coronog) — crowned; adjective from corun 'crown' (Brenhin corunawc 'a crowned king')
cuch: Cuch — proper name, the river/valley Glyn Cuch, on the border of Dyfed
cwn: ci (ci) — dogs; noun pl. of ci, the pack as individual animals (as against erchwys, the pack as a body)
da: da — good; adjective, also 'goods, wealth' as a noun (treulaw dy da 'spending your wealth')
dalo: talu (talu) — to pay, repay; 3 sg. present subjunctive, soft-mutated after a (Duw a dalo itt 'may God repay you')
dan: dan (dan) — under; preposition (dan y coet 'under the wood')
daryan: daryan (tarian) — shield; noun f., soft-mutated after y 'his' (bogel y daryan 'the boss of his shield')
datkanu: datkanu (datgan) — to relate, tell; verbal noun (a'e datkanu oll 'and its telling in full')
dayar: dayar (daear) — earth, land; noun f. (am dir a dayar 'about land and earth')
debygei: tybyaw (tybied) — to suppose, think; 3 sg. imperfect 'he supposed' (debygei ef 'he supposed')
deccaf: teccaf (tecaf) — superlative of tec 'fair', soft-mutated after the feminine noun (y wreic deccaf 'the fairest woman')
dechreu: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor 'beginning to muster') · also the noun 'beginning' (ar dechreu kyuedach 'at the start of the carousing')
dechreueist: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 2 sg. preterite 'you began' (canys dechreueist uy llad 'since you have begun to kill me')
del: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may come' (a del yn waredauc 'whoever comes submissively')
delw: delw (delw) — image, form, manner; noun f. (Pa delw 'in what manner')
delych: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may come' (yny delych 'until you come')
delynt: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. imperfect subjunctive 'they came, as they came' (ual y delynt 'as they came')
deu: deu (dau) — two (m.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following noun (y deu wrenhin 'the two kings')
deulu: teulu (teulu) — household-troop, warband; noun m., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y deulu 'and his warband') · also deu lu 'two hosts' written as one word (y deulu 'the two hosts'; the Red Book writes y deulu where the White Book has y deu lu)
deweis: tewi (tewi) — to be silent; 1 sg. preterite 'I was silent', soft-mutated after tra (tra deweis 'while I was silent')
dewred: dewred (dewrder) — valour, courage; noun m. (drwy y dewred ef 'through his valour')
di: di — 'you' (sg.), echoing pronoun after a verb or possessive (y pryny di; dy gerennyd di); also the object 'you' (ni ladaf i di)
diarchenu: diarchenu — to take off boots/riding-gear; verbal noun, di- 'un-' + archen 'shoe' (y diarchenu 'to take off his boots')
diarwya: Diarwya — proper name (Penn Llwyn Diarwya, 'the head of Diarwya grove'); place otherwise unknown, meaning unknown
diffleeis: diffleeis — 'unfailing, staunch'; meaning uncertain, perhaps dif- 'un-' + a word for 'fail'; exact form disputed
diffygywys: diffygyaw (diffygio) — to fail, cease; 3 sg. preterite 'fell away, failed' (y diffygywys y enw ef 'his name fell away')
digaun: digawn (digon) — can, is able; 3 sg. present of a defective verb (y digaun pawb ... uot 'each of you can be')
digrif: digrif (digri) — pleasant, amusing; adjective (y bu digrif ganthaw 'it was pleasant to him')
digrifhau: digrifhau (difyrru) — to please, delight; verbal noun, from digrif 'pleasant' (digrifhau medwl y gilid 'to please the other's mind')
digrifwch: digrifwch (difyrrwch) — amusement, pleasure; noun m., from digrif
digriwwch: digrifwch (difyrrwch) — amusement, pleasure; scribal spelling with w for f of digrifwch
dilesteir: dilesteir — unhindered; di- 'un-' + llesteir 'hindrance', predicate adjective (Dilesteir uyd dy hynt 'your way will be unhindered')
dim: dim — anything, nothing; indefinite pronoun (ny russya dim ragot 'nothing will obstruct before you')
dioer: dioer — assuredly, indeed; an oath, a worn-down Duw a wyr 'God knows'
diolwch: diolwch (diolch) — to thank; verbal noun/imperative-like (diolwch y'r gwr 'thank the man') · also noun 'thanks, gratitude' (diolwch ac elwissen 'thanks and alms-merit')
dir: tir (tir) — land, territory; noun m., soft-mutated after am (am dir a dayar 'about land and earth')
diryued: diryued (di- + rhyfedd) — no wonder; predicate (Diryued oed hynny 'that was no wonder')
dissymlaf: dissyml (disyml) — superlative dissymlaf; 'most unaffected, most natural', though the sense is debated ('gracious, refined' is also proposed)
ditheu: ditheu (dithau) — conjunctive form of ti 'you' (sg.), 'you for your part'
diwallaf: diwallaf (diwallaf) — superlative of diwall 'lacking nothing, abundantly supplied'
dlws: tlws (tlws) — treasure, jewel; noun m., soft-mutated after a fob gyfryw (a fob gyfryw dlws 'and every kind of treasure')
doeth: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. preterite 'came' (a doeth 'and came')
doi: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. imperfect 'used to come, came' (kystal y doi y gof 'as well came to mind')
dosparth: dosparth (dosbarth) — governance, order, arrangement; noun m. (dy dosparth 'your governance')
drannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; adverb, the soft-mutated form used adverbially (hanner dyd drannoeth; a mi drannoeth)
dreulwys: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after a (a dreulwys trwy digrifwch 'he spent in amusement')
drigiant: trigiant (trigiant) — dwelling, sojourn; noun m., soft-mutated after i (i drigiant ef 'his dwelling')
dros: dros (dros) — over, across; preposition (dros pedrein y uarch 'over the crupper of his horse') · also 'for, instead of' before a verbal noun, which it softens (dros wneuthur 'instead of doing'; the sense there is not certain)
drwy: trwy (trwy) — through; preposition, soft-mutated form (drwy y dewred ef 'through his valour')
drych: drych (drych) — appearance, look, aspect; noun m., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y drych 'and his appearance')
duhunaw: duhunaw (deffro) — to wake; verbal noun (duhunaw a wnaeth 'he woke')
dwy: dwy (dwy) — two (f.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following feminine noun (y dwy dyrnas 'the two kingdoms')
dwyn: dwyn (dwyn) — to carry, bring; verbal noun (dwyn y dwy dyrnas yn un 'bringing the two kingdoms into one') · also 'to pass, spend, experience' a time (dwyn yspeit digriuach 'to pass a merrier time'); sense from context
dy: dy — 'your' (sg.); possessive pronoun, causes soft mutation (dy gerennyd 'your friendship') · also written for the affixed pronoun di 'you' after the presentative wely (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son')
dyd: dyd (dydd) — day; noun m. (y dyd 'the day'; dyd da 'good day')
dygaf: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 1 sg. present 'I bring' (y dygaf uy nghyffes 'I bring my confession')
dygwch: dwyn (dwyn) — to carry; 2 pl. imperative 'carry!' (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here')
dygyuor: dygyuor (dygyfor) — to muster, rally (a hunt); verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor yr hela 'beginning to muster the hunt') · also noun 'muster, gathering' (Dygyuor y wlat a doeth attunt 'the muster of the land came to them')
dyly: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, be bound to; 3 sg. present 'owes it' (pawb a'y dyly 'everyone owes it')
dylyei: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, deserve; 3 sg. imperfect, negated 'would not deserve' (ual nas dylyei 'such that it would not deserve it') · also positive 'ought' (y rann a dylyei uot am y hwyneb 'the part that ought to be about her face')
dylyet: dylyet (dyled) — a right, a due, a claim; noun m. (pa dylyet a oed iti 'what right had you')

dyn: dyn (dyn) — man, person; noun m. (y dyn eithaf 'the farthest man')

dyrnawt: dyrnawt (dyrnod) — a blow; variant spelling of dyrnaut (angheuawl dyrnawt 'a deadly blow')

dywedut: dywedut (dweud) — to say, speak; verbal noun/infinitive
dywedy: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. present 'you say' (a dywedy di 'that you speak of'; na dywedy 'that you do not say')

ediuar: ediuar (edifar) — regret, sorry; predicate adjective (yn ediuar gennyf 'a matter of regret to me')
edrych: edrych (edrych) — to look; verbal noun (edrych ar y carw 'to look at the stag') · also imperative 'look!' (Edrych i'th gylch 'look around you') and 3 sg. present (A phan edrych 'and when he looked', the bare stem as vivid present; the Red Book a phan edrychawd ef)

eiroet: eiroet (erioed) — ever, always (of the past); adverb (a welsei eiroet 'that he had ever seen')
eiryoet: eiryoet (erioed) — ever; variant spelling of eiroet (o'r a welsei eiryoet 'of all he had ever seen')
eisseu: eisseu (eisiau) — lack, absence, want; noun m. (i eisseu ef 'his absence')
eisted: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; verbal noun (eisted a wnaethant 'they sat')

eithyr: eithyr (eithr) — except; conjunction/preposition (eithyr gadu 'except to leave')

erbyn: erbyn (erbyn) — (1) against, by (a time) (erbyn hanner dyd 'by midday'); (2) 'to meet' (yn y erbyn 'to meet him')
erchlas: erchlas — a compound colour word, 'dapple-grey' or 'dun-grey' (of a horse); exact shade uncertain
erchwyn: erchwyn (erchwyn) — the edge or side of a bed; noun m./f. (at yr erchwyn 'to the bed's edge')

etteil: attal (atal) — to hold back, restrain; 3 sg. present 'holds back' (a'm etteil 'that holds me back')
eurwisc: eurwisc (eurwisg) — a gold garment; eur 'gold' + gwisc 'garment'

furyf: ffuryf (ffurf) — form, manner; noun f., variant spelling of furuf; ff does not mutate, the single f is the scribe's spelling (pa furyf 'in what manner')

gedyndeith: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; noun m., soft-mutated after ar; the scribe wrote gedyndeith for gedymdeith (ar gedyndeith 'on a companion')

geueist: caffael (cael) — to get; 2 sg. preterite 'you got' (gauael gadarn a geueist 'a firm hold you got')
geuyn: keuyn (cefn) — back; noun m., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y geuyn attei 'and his back to her')
gherennyd: kerennyd (cerennydd) — friendship; noun f., nasal-mutated after uy 'my' (uy gherennyd 'my friendship')
gilid: kilid (cilydd) — 'the other, fellow'; used in y gilid 'to the other', wrth y gilid 'towards the other'
gilyd: kilid (cilydd) — 'the other, fellow'; variant spelling of gilid (ar y gilyd 'against the other') · also pwy gilyd 'each (to) the other, one another' (o'r pryt pwy gilyd), soft-mutated after pwy; sense of pwy here uncertain
glut: glut (glud) — persistent, constant, close-sticking; adjective (Ys glut a beth 'it is a very persistent thing')
glynn: Glynn (Glyn) — valley; proper noun in Glynn Cuch 'Glyn Cuch', loses its g after y 'to' (y Lynn Cuch)
glywei: clybot (clywed) — to hear; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after a (ef a glywei llef erchwys arall 'he heard the cry of another pack')
gochyon: coch (coch) — red; plural adjective cochyon, soft-mutated after predicative yn (eu clusteu yn gochyon 'their ears red')
gof: cof (cof) — memory, mind; noun m., soft-mutated after y (y gof 'to mind') · also soft as the subject after a negated verb (ny doy gof udunt 'no memory came to them')
gorff: corff (corff) — body; noun m., soft-mutated after y (y gorff 'of the body')

gormes: gormes (gormes) — oppression; noun m./f. (guaret gormes hwnnw 'to remove that oppression')

guas: guas (gwas) — lad, young man, servant; noun m. (guas ditheu 'a lad, you')
guassanaeth: guassanaeth (gwasanaeth) — service; noun m. (y guassanaeth yndi 'the service in it')
guastat: guastat (gwastad) — level, flat; adjective (o uaes guastat 'of a level field') · also 'even, steady', of a pace (Kerdet araf guastat 'a slow, even pace')
guedy: guedy (gwedi) — after; preposition (A guedy y medwl hwnnw 'and after that thought')
gueisson: gwas (gwas) — lads, servants; noun pl. (gueisson ieueinc 'young lads')
guelei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after y (Llyma y guelei ef 'there he saw') · also left unsoftened after the relative a, as written (a neb o'r a guelei 'anyone of those who saw')

guereskynn: guereskynn (goresgyn) — to conquer, subdue; verbal noun (dechreu guereskynn y wlat)
guerth: guerth (gwerth) — worth, value; noun m. (guerth can carw 'the worth of a hundred stags')
guyrda: gwyrda (gwŷr da) — noblemen; gwyr 'men' + da 'good', plural noun (A wyrda 'O noblemen')
gwisc: gwisc (gwisg) — garment, dress; noun f. (gwisc hela 'hunting dress')
gwledychu: gwledychu (gwladychu) — to rule, reign; verbal noun (gwledychu o honaw 'his ruling')
gwn: ci (ci) — dog; plural cwn, soft-mutated c > g after e 'his' (e gwn 'his dogs') · also gwybot (gwybod) 'to know'; 1 sg. present 'I know' (Gwn, Arglwyd 'I know, Lord'), radical form, repeating the verb of the question
gwnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', unmutated after the particle y (Kyntaf y gwnaeth ef ymdidan)
gwnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do' (mi a wnaf hynny 'I will do that')
gwneuthum: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. preterite 'I did' (a wneuthum i yrot ti 'what I did for you')
gwneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun/infinitive, also used as the periphrastic auxiliary 'do' (a wneuthum itt 'that I did to you')
gwnn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. present 'I know', g often dropped after ny (ny wnn i 'I do not know') · also radical after the infixed 's (a chanys gwnn 'and since I do not know it', kan + nys)
gwr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m. (y gwr a oed yn lle Arawn 'the man who was in Arawn's place')
gwreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., meaning as context decides (a'y wreic 'and his wife')
gwrogaeth: gwrogaeth (gwrogaeth) — homage; noun f., from gwr 'man', the formal submission a man makes to his lord
gwybydwch: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 2 pl. imperative 'know! find out!' (a gwybydwch pwy a dylyo... 'and find out who ought to...')

gwyrda: gwyrda (gwŷr da) — noblemen; gwyr 'men' + da 'good' (Vy ngwyrda 'my noblemen', nasal-mutated after uy)

gydymdeithas: kydymdeithas (cydymdeithas) — fellowship; noun f., soft-mutated after dy (dy gydymdeithas 'your fellowship')
gydymdeithon: kedymdeithon (cydymeithion) — companions; noun pl., soft-mutated after 'y (a'y gydymdeithon 'from his companions')

gyfryw: kyfryw (cyfryw) — such; adjective, soft-mutated after y/a (y kyfryw le 'such a place'; a fob gyfryw dlws 'every such kind of treasure')
gymmeint: kymmeint (cymaint) — as much, so much; adjective, soft-mutated after y (y gymmeint 'as much')
gymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, receive; verbal noun, soft-mutated after i/y (iawn yw gymryt 'it is right to receive') · also soft-mutated after ar 'on' (disgynnu a wnaeth ar gymryt hynny 'he settled on taking that')
gyn: kyn (cyn) — as, equative particle before an adjective (kyn hygaret 'as lovable', spelt gyn after ny) · also soft-mutated in a run of epithets after the feminine noun morwyn (morwyn gystal, kyuurd, gyn anwylet 'a maiden so good, of equal rank, so dear') · also soft-mutated after predicative yn (yn gyn hyspysset ganthunt 'as plain to them')

gyrru: gyrru (gyrru) — to drive; verbal noun (gyrru yr erchwys … e ymdeith 'driving the pack away')
gyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y (y gyscu 'to sleep')
gystal: kystal (cystal) — as good; adjective, soft-mutated after ny (ny bu gystal dy wybot 'your judgement was never so good') · also soft after a feminine noun (morwyn gystal 'a maiden so good') and as predicate (nit wyt gystal ymdidanwr 'you are not so good a talker')

gyweirwyt: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to set in order, make ready; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'there was a making-ready' (A'r neuad a gyweirwyt 'and the hall was made ready')
hafgan: Hafgan — proper name, king of Annwfn opposing Arawn; meaning 'summer-white' (haf 'summer' + can 'white')
hagen: hagen (hagen) — however; adverb (Yr a rodwn i idau ef hagen 'however many I gave him')
hanbwyllaw: hanbwyllaw — meaning uncertain; perhaps 'to take thought, to trouble oneself'; a rare word whose sense here is inferred from context
hanner: hanner (hanner) — half; noun m. (yn deu hanner 'into two halves')
hannwyt: annwyt (anwyd) — nature, disposition; noun m., h-prefixed after i 'her' (i hannwyt 'her nature')
hanwyf: hanuot (hanfod) — to be descended from, come from; 1 sg. present 'I come from' (yd hanwyf oheni 'that I come from it')

hardaf: hardaf (hardaf) — superlative of hard 'handsome, fine' (y niuer hardaf 'the handsomest company')
hawlwr: hawlwr (hawliwr) — a claimant; noun m., from hawl 'claim'
hawsset: hawsset (hawsed) — as easy; equative of hawd 'easy' (ny bu gyn hawsset gennyt 'it was never so easy for you')

hebryngyat: hebryngyat (hebryngwr) — an escort, a guide; noun m., from hebrwng 'escort'
hela: hela (hela) — to hunt; verbal noun (uynet y hela 'to go to hunt')
helgwn: helgi (helgi) — hunting dog; plural helgwn, hel 'hunt' + cwn 'dogs' (o helgwn y byt)

hwnn: hwnn (hwn) — 'this' (m.); demonstrative (yr oet hwnn 'this appointment') · also pronoun 'the one that' (namyn yr hwnn a dyly 'but that which it deserves')
hwnnw: hwnnw (hwnnw) — 'that' (m.); demonstrative (y dyd hwnnw 'that day') · also pronoun 'that one' (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man'; yw hwnnw 'that is it')
hwy: hwy (hwy) — 'they, them'; independent 3 pl. pronoun (arnunt hwy 'over them') · also 'longer', comparative of hir (Ny bu hwy ganthunt no thrannoeth 'it was no longer with them than the next day')
hygar: hygar (hygar) — lovable, affectionate; adjective (hygaret guas 'a lovable lad')
hygaret: hygar (hygar) — equative form 'as lovable' (gyn hygaret 'as lovable')
hyllt: hyllt (hollti) — to split; 3 sg. present, vivid narrative tense (yny hyllt yn deu hanner 'so that it splits in two halves')
hymdidan: ymdidan — conversation, to converse; verbal noun/noun; h-prefix after y 'her' before a vowel-initial word (a'y hymdidan 'her conversation')
hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs') · also yr hynn 'that which, what' (yr hynn a deryw ymi 'what befalls me')
hynny: hynny — 'that (thing)'; demonstrative pronoun, very frequent (a hynny 'and that')
hynt: hynt — way, course, journey; noun f. (dy hynt 'your way')
hyt: hyt (hyd) — as far as, until; preposition/conjunction (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end'; hyt na bo 'so that there be not') · also ar hyt 'along' (ar hyt y prifford 'along the highway') · also 'as far as, so far as, as much as, to the extent that' with the subjunctive (hyt y mynnych 'as much as you wish'; hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it'); hyt oet y wled 'until the time of the feast' · also 'so that' with the indicative (hyt nat oed rym 'so that there was no use'); hyt yn Aberfraw 'as far as Aberffraw' · also the noun 'length, duration' after pa 'what' (Pa hyt bynnac y bydynt ar y ford 'however long they were on the road')
i: i — (1) emphatic independent pronoun 'I/me', echoing a verb or conjugated preposition (rof i, arnaf i); (2) spelling of y 'to' before a vowel or l/w (i waret); (3) spelling of y 'his' before some words (i wisc hela 'his hunting-dress') · (4) after ohonawch, probably the 2 pl. echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending (ohonawch i 'of you') · also echoing a possessive (wy gwreic i yw hi 'she is my wife')
iarll: iarll (iarll) — earl; noun m., a borrowing of Norse/English jarl (a'r iarll)
iawn: iawn — right, proper, correct; adjective/predicate (iawn yw gymryt 'it is right to receive') · also noun 'compensation, redress, amends' (dy iawn 'your compensation'; chael iawn 'getting redress') · also 'right (thing)' as object of gwneuthur (phei gwnelut iawn 'and if you were to do right')
idau: idaw (iddo) — to him; conjugated preposition, spelling variant (a rodwn i idau ef)
idaw: idaw (iddo) — to him; 3 sg. m. conjugated form of y 'to'
idi: idi (iddi) — to her; 3 sg. f. conjugated form of y 'to' (menegi... a wnaeth idi)
ie: ie — yes; particle of assent, taking up what was just said
ieueinc: ieuanc (ifanc) — young; plural form (gueisson ieueinc 'young lads')
ieuengtit: ieuengtit (ieuenctid) — youth, early part; noun f. (yn ieuengtit y dyd 'in the youth of the day' = early morning)
im: im (i mi) — to me; conjugated preposition, contracted spelling (Meuyl im 'shame to me')
inheu: inheu (innau) — I/mine, for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun marking contrast (a'm kyuoeth inheu 'my realm, mine')
innheu: inheu (innau) — for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun, spelling variant with double n (uy ngwyrda innheu)
it: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelling variant with single t (achos it heuyt)
iti: iti (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelling variant (a oed iti)
itt: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition (Duw a dalo itt)
iwch: iwch (i chwi) — to you; 2 pl. conjugated preposition (ys iawn a beth iwch chwi)
kedymdeithas: kedymdeithas (cydymdeithas) — fellowship, companionship; noun f. (cadarnhau kedymdeithas y ryngthunt)
keffy: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 2 sg. present/future 'you will get' (y keffy uy gherennyd)
keis: keisiaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; 2 sg. imperative 'seek' (Keis a'th lado 'seek someone to kill you')
kerdaud: kerdet (cerdded) — to go, walk, proceed; 3 sg. preterite 'he went', ending -awd (y kerdaud Arawn racdaw)
kyffy: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 2 sg. present/future 'you will get it', spelling variant of keffy (y kyffy)
kyfryw: kyfryw (cyfryw) — such, similar; adjective (yn y kyfryw le a hwnn 'in such a place as this')
kygleu: klybot (clywed) — to hear; old perfect 1 sg. with infixed 'y 'it', 'I have heard it' (mi a'y kygleu)
kymerth: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; old 3 sg. preterite without -wys ending (y kymerth ynteu y furuf e hun)
kymerwch: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 2 pl. imperative 'take' (kymerwch ych kyuarwyd)
kymmeller: kymhell (cymell) — to compel; impersonal present subjunctive 'let there be compelling' (kymmeller o nerth cledyueu)
kymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, receive; verbal noun (iawn yw gymryt; kymryt gwrogaeth)
kynn: kynn (cyn) — before; preposition/conjunction (kynn no hynny 'before that')
kynnadyl: kynnadyl (cynnadl) — appointed meeting, tryst; noun f. (An kynnadyl 'our meeting')
kynnal: kynnal (cynnal) — to maintain, support; verbal noun (y'ch kynnal chwi 'to maintain you')
kyntaf: kyntaf (cyntaf) — first; superlative of kynt, used adverbially and adjectivally
kyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun (Kyrchu y llys a oruc ynteu)
kystal: kystal (cystal) — as good, as much; equative of da 'good' (kystal y doi y gof)
kyt: kyt (cyd) — although; conjunction, takes the subjunctive (kyt bwyf i yno)
kyuanned: kyuanned (cyfannedd) — dwelling, habitation; noun m./f. (y llys a'r kyuanned)
kyuarch: kyuarch (cyfarch) — to greet; verbal noun, literally 'ask better' (kyuarch guell 'greet')
kyuarwyd: kyuarwyd (cyfarwydd) — guidance, direction, information; noun m. (pa gyuarwyd a uyd ymi) · also 'storyteller, one skilled in tales' (Gwydyon goreu kyuarwyd yn y byt 'Gwydion the best storyteller in the world')
kyueir: kyueir (cyfair) — region, direction, part; noun m. (Sef kyueir o'y gyuoeth 'the part of his realm')
kyuodi: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; verbal noun (kyuodi a oruc 'he rose')
kyuoeth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm, dominion; noun m. (a oed yn arglwyd... o'y gyuoeth)
kywir: kywir (cywir) — faithful, true; adjective (Vy ngwyrda kywir 'my faithful noblemen')
kywirdeb: kywirdeb (cywirdeb) — faithfulness, loyalty; noun m. (chadw kywirdeb wrthyt)
ladaf: llad (lladd) — to kill; 1 sg. present/future 'I will kill' (ni ladaf i di)
lado: llad (lladd) — to kill; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may kill', soft mutation after relative a'th (a'th lado)
ladyssei: llad (lladd) — to kill; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had killed'; soft mutation after relative a (a ladyssei y carw)
lannerch: llannerch (llannerch) — clearing; noun f., soft-mutated as object (gwelei lannerch yn y coet)
le: lle (lle) — place; noun m., soft-mutated after kyfryw 'such' (yn y kyfryw le a hwnn 'in such a place as this') · also soft after heb 'without' (heb le idaw 'without a place of his own')
lestri: llestri (llestri) — vessels; noun pl., soft-mutated after eur (eur lestri 'gold vessels')
liw: lliw (lliw) — colour; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ar liw yr erchwys) · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after y 'his' (y liw 'his colour')
llad: llad (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun, base form (y'm llad i 'to kill me') · also llad glwm 'to tie a knot' (idiomatic, literally 'strike a knot'): llad glwm ar garryeu y got 'to tie a knot on the straps of the bag'
llannerch: llannerch (llannerch) — clearing (in a wood); noun f., base unmutated form
llathrei: llathru (llathru) — to shine; 3 sg. imperfect 'shone' (y llathrei wynnet y cwn)
llathreit: llathreit (llathraidd) — shining, glossy; adjective (claerwyn llathreit; bali llathreit)
llawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, base form (yn llawen)
llawenn: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, spelling with double n (yn llawenn)
llawr: llawr (llawr) — ground, floor; noun m., base form (y'r llawr 'to the ground')
lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form
llef: llef (llef) — cry, voice; noun f. (llef yr erchwys 'the cry of the pack')
llithiau: llithyaw (llithio) — to feed hounds on a kill; verbal noun, spelling variant (yn llithiau y cwn)
llithyaw: llithyaw (llithio) — to feed hounds on a kill, the huntsman's reward after a hunt; verbal noun
lliw: lliw (lliw) — colour; noun m., base unmutated form (Sef lliw oed arnunt)
llwyn: llwyn (llwyn) — grove; noun m. (Penn Llwyn Diarwya 'the head of Diarwya grove')
llwyt: llwyt (llwyd) — grey; adjective (brethyn llwyt 'grey cloth') · also proper name Llwyt (Llwyd) (Miui yw Llwyt uab Kil Coet 'I am Llwyd son of Cil Coed')
llyma: llyma (dyma) — behold, here is; presentative particle throwing a scene before the reader (llyma yr erchwys)
llyna: llyna (dyna) — there is, behold that; presentative particle, distal counterpart of llyma
llynn: llynn (llyn) — drink; noun m. (bwyt a llynn 'food and drink') · also llyn 'lake, pool' (llynn o pop parth y'r eskeir 'a lake on each side of the ridge')
llys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., base form
llywenyd: llywenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (digrifwch a llywenyd)
lwydannus: lwydannus (llwyddiannus) — prosperous; adjective, soft-mutated after mor (mor lwydannus)
lynn: Glynn (Glyn) — 'glen, valley'; the g of Glynn drops after y 'to' (y Lynn Cuch 'to Glyn Cuch') · also llyn 'lake, pool', soft-mutated after dwy (y dwy lynn 'the two lakes')
lys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (parth a'y lys) · also soft after prif 'chief', which softens the noun it precedes (prif lys 'chief court')
lyssoed: llysoed (llysoedd) — courts; noun pl., soft-mutated after holl 'all' (holl lyssoed y dayar)
m: 'm — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'm, y'm, o'm etc.: 'my' (possessive, triggers soft mutation) or 'me' (object) · with h- before a following vowel (o'm hanwod 'against my will'); as 'my' before a verbal noun it may stand for that noun's object (a'm rodi 'and my giving' = and giving me); as 'me' after a relative (a'm gwrthyt 'who rejects me')
mae: bot (bod) — to be; irregular present 3 sg. 'is, there is' (y mae arnat o anryded) · also interrogative 'where is?' (Mae yr yniuer …? 'where is the company …?')
makwyueit: makwy (macwy) — squire, young attendant; noun pl., a borrowing from Old French (makwyueit a gueisson ieueinc)
manac: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, show; 2 sg. imperative (A manac ditheu y mi)
managaf: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, show; 1 sg. present/future 'I will tell' (Managaf)
marchawc: marchawc (marchog) — horseman, rider; noun m., base form
mawr: mawr (mawr) — big, great; adjective (uarch erchlas mawr 'a big dapple-grey horse')
medwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m. (yn y uryt ac yn y uedwl)
medylyaw: medylyaw (meddwl/myfyrio) — to think, ponder; verbal noun (medylyaw a wnaeth yn hir)
medylywys: medylyaw (meddwl) — to think, ponder; 3 sg. preterite 'thought' (a hynny a uedylywys hi)
meirch: march (march) — horse; noun pl. (meirch a milgwn 'horses and greyhounds')
menegi: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, relate; verbal noun (menegi y holl gyfranc a wnaeth idi)
meuyl: meuyl (mefl) — shame, disgrace; noun m., used in the oath meuyl im 'shame on me' · also meuyl ar 'shame on' (Meuyl ar uy maryf i 'shame on my beard')
mi: mi — 1 sg. independent/emphatic pronoun 'I' (mi a wnn 'I know')
milgwn: milgi (milgi) — greyhound; noun pl. (meirch a milgwn)
minnheu: mi (mi) — I, for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun (Minnheu a wnaf hynny)
miui: mi (mi) — I/me; emphatic 1 sg. pronoun, fuller spelling of mi (A miui a af)
mor: mor (mor) — so, how; adverbial intensifier, triggers soft mutation (mor lwydannus) · also môr 'sea' (hyt y mor 'as far as the sea'); noun m., no mutation
mywn: y mywn (i mewn) — in, inside; adverbial phrase (yn dyuot y mywn 'coming in') · also prepositional 'in' (y mywn gogof 'in a cave')
na: na — (1) negative particle in a subordinate clause, 'not' (na dywedy di); (2) 'neither/nor' in a series (na guas ystauell, na swydawc) · also negative imperative 'do not', with soft mutation (na ouyn di 'do not ask'; na yrrwch geu arnaf 'do not lay a lie on me'; na hawl ef 'do not claim him') · also 'not' in a main-clause denial or refusal, with soft mutation (na ellynghaf 'I will not release'; na uynhaf 'I will not have it'; na weleis 'I have not seen')
nac: nac — (1) negative used in a direct answer, repeating the verb, 'no' (Nac attygaf 'I will not'); (2) 'nor' before a vowel (nac ymdidan) · also negative imperative 'do not' (nac arch dim 'do not ask anything') · also Nac ef 'no', literally 'not it', refusing a proposal (Nac ef, heb y Manawydan 'No, said Manawydan')
namyn: namyn (namyn) — except, but; conjunction (namyn ti 'but you')
nas: ny + 's — negative particle ny with infixed 3 sg. object pronoun 's 'it/him': 'that not it/him' (ual nas dylyei)
neb: neb (neb) — anyone; pronoun, used with a positive sense in relative/superlative clauses (o'r a welsei neb 'that anyone had seen') · also 'anyone' under a negative = 'no one' (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue') · also in y neb a 'the one who/to whom' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'the one from whom one ought to take it')
neill: neill (naill) — one (of two); (o'r neill parth 'on the one side')
neithwyr: neithwyr (neithiwr) — last night; adverb (yr blwydyn y neithwyr 'a year ago tonight')
nep: nep (neb) — anyone, no one; pronoun, spelling variant of neb (Nit oes yndi nep)
nerth: nerth (nerth) — strength, force; noun m. (o nerth cledyueu 'by force of swords')
nessayssant: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; 3 pl. preterite 'they drew near' (y deu urenhin a nessayssant)
neuad: neuad (neuadd) — hall; noun f. (y'r neuad y gyrchwys)
neut: neut — affirmative particle, 'it is the case that' (neut teruynedic angheu y mi 'my death is determined') · neut is the affirmative particle neu in the form it takes before a vowel (as yd beside y), not neu + an infixed pronoun (neut athoed hi heibaw 'lo, she had gone past')
newydach: newyd (newydd) — new; comparative 'newer, more of a novelty' (ni bu newydach ganthunt)
nghyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — confession; noun f., nasal-mutated after uy 'my' (uy nghyffes)
ngwyrda: gwyrda (gwyrda) — noblemen; noun pl., nasal-mutated after uy 'my' (Vy ngwyrda)
ni: ni — (1) 1 pl. pronoun 'we/us' (yd ymdidanyssam ni); (2) negative particle, spelling variant of ny before some verbs (ni ladaf, ni bu)
ninheu: ni (ni) — we, for our part; conjunctive 1 pl. pronoun (a gaussam ninheu)
nit: nyt (nid) — negative particle 'not, there is not', spelling before a vowel (Nit oes; Nit yttoydwn)
niuer: niuer (nifer) — host, company, number; noun m. (a'r niuer hardaf a chyweiraf)
no: no (na) — than, comparative particle (no gyrru 'than driving'; no chyuedach) · also in kyn no hynny 'before that, earlier than that'
noc: no (na) — than; spelling before a vowel (noc a uu 'than what was')
nos: nos (nos) — night; noun f. (y nos honno 'that night')
ny: ny (ni/nid) — negative particle 'not', base form before a consonant with soft mutation · also spirant mutation of c, p, t (ny chewch 'you will not get'; ny thygyawd 'it did not avail'); soft mutation of g (ny wybydei 'knew not')
nyblyc: plyc (plyg) — fold; noun m., nasal-mutated after yn 'in' (yn nyblyc yn dillat guely 'in the fold of the bedclothes')
nys: ny + 's — negative particle ny with infixed 3 sg. object pronoun 's 'it': 'not it' (nys attygy 'you will not withdraw it') · also 'him, her' (nys mynnaf 'I do not want him')
nyt: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not, it is not', spelling before a vowel or in emphasis (nyt teilygdawt)
o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
odyma: odyma (oddi yma) — from here; adverb (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here')

oedwn: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. imperfect 'I was' (yd oedwn inheu)
oedynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. imperfect 'they were' (nit oedynt unllef)
oes: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. existential 'there is' (Nit oes yndi nep) · also oes 'age, lifetime, generation', noun f. (yn yr oes honno 'in that age')
oet: oet (oed) — appointed time, tryst; noun m. (y mae oet y rof i ac ef 'there is an appointment between me and him') · also a spelling of oed 'was', 3 sg. imperfect of bot (yn yd oet Pwyll 'where Pwyll was')

ohonaw: o + ef — conjugated preposition 'of/by him' (edrych ohonaw ef 'his looking')
ol: ol (ôl) — track, trace; noun m. (yn ol y cwn 'after the hounds'; yn y ol 'in its track')
oll: oll (oll) — all, wholly; adverb/adjective intensifying a preceding noun (yr arueu oll 'all the armour')
ordifnassei: gordifnu (gordyfnu) — to be accustomed to; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had been accustomed', soft-mutated after ny (ny ordifnassei hi)
oruc: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite auxiliary 'he did', soft-mutated after a, with g dropped (kyuodi a oruc)
orugant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did' (a orugant), older form beside wnaethant
orwedeis: gorwed (gorwedd) — to lie down; 1 sg. preterite 'I lay down', soft-mutated after ni (ni orwedeis)
ossodes: gossot (gosod) — to set, strike; 3 sg. preterite 'struck', soft-mutated after a (a ossodes ar Hafgan)
ot: ot (o + -t) — 'if' in the idiom ot gwnn 'if I know' = as far as I know, I trust · also 'if' before a vowel (ot oed uawr ef 'if he was big')
pa: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative adjective, triggers soft mutation of the following noun
paham: paham (pam) — why?; interrogative adverb, pa + am 'for what'
paladyr: paladyr (paladr) — spear-shaft; noun m. (a'e paladyr 'and his spear')
pan: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction with a past-time clause (pan doeth) · also interrogative 'from where, whence' (pan doy di? 'where do you come from?') · also 'from where' as a relative (Pan doaf o Loygyr 'from where I come, from England')
parth: parth (parth) — towards, side, direction; noun m./preposition (parth a'y lys 'towards his court')
pawb: pawb (pawb) — everyone; pronoun (pawb a'y dyly 'everyone owes it')
pedrein: pedrein (pedrain) — crupper, hindquarters (of a horse); noun f. (dros pedrein y uarch)
pen: penn (pen) — head, end; noun m., spelling variant with single n (hyt ym pen y ulwydyn)
pendeuic: pendeuic (pendefig) — prince, chief lord; noun m., a title (Pwyll Pendeuic Dyuet)
penn: penn (pen) — head, end; noun m., base form (Penn Annwuyn 'Head of Annwfn')
perued: perued (perfedd) — middle; noun m. (parth a pherued y llannerch 'towards the middle of the clearing')
peth: peth (peth) — thing; noun m., used with bynnac 'whatever' (Peth bynnac o garueidrwyd)

pharth: parth (parth) — towards; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A pharth a pherued)

prif: prif (prif) — chief, main; adjective (prif lys idaw 'his chief court')
pryny: prynu (prynu) — to buy; 2 sg. present/future 'you will buy' (y pryny di)
pryt: pryt (pryd) — form, appearance; noun m. (pryt ac ansawd 'form and appearance') · also 'time, hour, mealtime' (o'r pryt pwy gilyd 'from one hour to the next', sense approximate)
pwy: pwy (pwy) — who; interrogative pronoun (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')

rodes: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. preterite 'gave' (y rodes Arawn y furuf)
rodi: rodi (rhoi) — to give, put; verbal noun, base form

rof: rwng (rhwng) + i — conjugated preposition 'between me' (y rof i a Duw 'between me and God')
rom: rwng (rhwng) + ni — conjugated preposition 'between us' (o'r bu y rom ni)
rungthunt: rwng (rhwng) + wynt — conjugated preposition 'between them', spelling variant of ryngthunt (y rungthunt y dyd)
russya: russyaw (rhusio) — to hinder, obstruct; 3 sg. present 'obstructs' (ny russya dim ragot 'nothing will obstruct you')
rwng: rwng (rhwng) — between; preposition, base uninflected form
ryngthunt: rwng (rhwng) + wynt — conjugated preposition 'between them' (kedymdeithas y ryngthunt)
ryt: ryt (rhyd) — ford; noun f. (ar y ryt 'at the ford')
ryuelu: ryuelu (rhyfela) — to wage war; verbal noun (yn ryuelu arnaf yn wastat)
ryuuassei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. pluperfect with perfective particle ry-, 'had been' (y wrth ryuuassei kynn no hynny)
rywelsei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. pluperfect with perfective particle ry-, 'he had (already) seen' (canis rywelsei ef)
sef: sef (sef) — it is (this), that is; presentative particle introducing an explanation or answer
serchawl: serchawl (serchol) — amorous, loving; adjective (digriwwch serchawl 'amorous amusement')
ssegur: ssegur (segur) — idle, free (to do as one likes); adjective (a ssegur y digaun pawb o honawch uot)
swydawc: swydawc (swyddog) — officer, official; noun m. (na swydawc 'nor any officer')
talo: talu (talu) — to pay, repay; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he repay', soft-mutated after a (Duw a dalo itt)
teccaf: tec (teg) — fair, pretty; superlative 'fairest' (yr ardurn teccaf a welsei neb)
tei: tei — obscure word after brethyn llwyt 'grey cloth'; meaning uncertain, perhaps 'of the house, homespun'; editors have not settled it · also tei 'houses', plural of ty (tŷ) (tei y llys 'the houses of the court')
teilygdawt: teilygdawt (teilyngdod) — worthiness, merit; noun m. (nyt teilygdawt uy anryded)
teruynedic: teruynedic (terfynedig) — determined, fixed, final; adjective (neut teruynedic angheu y mi)
teulu: teulu (teulu) — household-troop, warband, a lord's retinue; noun m. (later came to mean 'family')
th: 'th — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'th, i'th, dy'th etc.: 'your' (possessive) or 'you' (object)
theyrndlysseu: teyrndlysseu (teyrndlysau) — royal jewels, regalia; noun pl. (teyrn 'king' + tlysseu 'jewels'), spirant-mutated after a
thi: ti (ti) — you; 2 sg. pronoun, spirant-mutated after a 'and, with' (gyt a thi 'together with you')
thrannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; noun/adverb, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A thrannoeth) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no thrannoeth 'than the next day')
threigylgweith: treigylgweith (treiglwaith) — one time, once; noun m., spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A threigylgweith)
threulaw: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A threulaw a wnaethant)
tidi: ti (ti) — you; emphatic 2 sg. pronoun, fuller spelling (na bo tidi wwyf i 'that it is not you that I am')
tirionwch: tirionwch (tiriondeb) — tenderness, gentleness; noun m. (tirionwch ac ymdidan hygar)
titheu: ti (ti) — you, for your part; conjunctive 2 sg. pronoun
tra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (tra deweis wrthyt ti 'while I kept silent') · also (2) 'very', before an adjective with spirant mutation (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty'); (3) 'while' with the verb sometimes soft-mutated (tra barhaud) · also 'beyond', preposition (tra y gefyn 'beyond his back', i.e. back again)
trannoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — the next day; noun/adverb, base form
treulaw: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); verbal noun, base form
trwy: trwy (trwy) — through; preposition (trwy digrifwch a llywenyd)
trydyt: trydyt (trydydd) — third; ordinal numeral (a'r trydyt 'and the third')
uaes: maes (maes) — field; noun m., soft-mutated after o (o uaes guastat 'a level field')
ual: ual (fel) — as, like; conjunction/preposition (ual hynn 'like this') · also 'so that' (ual yd ymglywynt 'so that they could hear one another'; ual y bydynt gadarnach 'so that they would be stronger') and 'how' (sef ual yd eistedyssant 'that is how they sat')
uarch: march (march) — horse; noun m., soft-mutated after ar (y ar uarch erchlas mawr 'on a big dapple-grey horse') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uarch 'his horse') · also soft after o 'of' (a wely o uarch 'whatever you see of horses')
uarchauc: marchawc (marchog) — horseman; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ef a welei uarchauc)
udunt: y (i) + wynt — conjugated preposition 'to them' (Amser a doeth udunt e uynet e gyscu)
uedwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uedwl) · also soft-mutated (m>u) after pa 'what' (pa uedwl yw yr eidunt 'what intention is theirs') · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after ar 'on' (ar uedwl medi 'on the thought of reaping')
uedyant: medyant (meddiant) — possession, power; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his/your' (yn y uedyant, i'th uedyant)
uedylywys: medylyaw (meddwl) — to think, ponder; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after a (a uedylywys hi)
uei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might be', soft-mutated after a (a uei uwy no hynny) · also soft-mutated after ban 'when' (ban uei uwyaf 'when it was most') · also soft after yny 'until' (yny uei agos y guyr idaw 'until the men would be near it') · also softened after tra 'while' (tra uei 'while (they) were')
ui: ui (fi) — me; object pronoun after an imperative (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here') · also the softened pronoun 'I' after a verb (Ny allaf ui arnaf a dywedy di uyth 'I cannot bring myself to do what you say') and as the second, emphatic pronoun in mi ui 'I myself' (A mi ui a rodaf 'and I myself will give'); soft-mutated from mi · also after gwae 'woe' (guae ui 'woe is me')
uilwraeth: milwraeth (milwriaeth) — prowess, soldiership; noun f., soft-mutated after 'y 'his' (a'y uilwraeth) · also soft as the object of an inflected verb (na welsam eiroet uilwraeth yn un wreic 'we have never seen such prowess in one woman')
uiui: miui (myfi) — me; emphatic pronoun, soft-mutated as the object of the imperative (na chapla di uiui 'do not blame me')
ulaen: blaen (blaen) — front, tip; noun m., soft-mutated after o (o ulaen yr erchwys arall 'ahead of the other pack')
ulwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f., soft-mutated after y/the feminine article (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn) · also adverbial, 'a year' in time phrases, soft-mutated without the article (ulwydyn y heno 'a year from tonight'; ual yd eistedyssant ulwydyn o'r nos honno 'as they sat a year from that night'), the soft mutation being that of an adverbial accusative of time · also soft after a preceding ordinal (y seithuet ulwydyn 'the seventh year')
un: un (un) — one; numeral/adjective (un dyrnaut 'one blow') · also 'same' (yn un ansawd 'in the same appearance'; yr un ford 'the same way') and the pronoun 'one (of them)' (Un a gyuodes 'one rose')
unben: unben (unben) — chieftain, lord; noun m., un 'one' + penn 'head'; vocative form of address · also 'the chieftain' as an ordinary noun (gan yr unben 'in the mind of the chieftain')
unbenn: unben (unben) — chieftain, lord; noun m., spelling with double n
ungwr: un gwr (un gŵr) — 'one man'; used exclamatorily, 'what a man!' (cadarn a ungwr y gydymdeithas)
unllef: unllef (unllef) — of one cry, sounding alike; compound adjective, un 'one' + llef 'cry' (nit oedynt unllef)
unnos: unnos (unnos) — one night; compound, un 'one' + nos 'night' (ni bu unnos)
uoes: moes (moes) — custom, manner; noun f., soft-mutated as object (uoes y llys 'the custom of the court'); the manuscript has the e inserted above the line by the scribe
uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uot yn colli 'that he was losing', lit. 'his being losing') · also soft after dy 'your' (dy uot yn kyuanhedu 'your being settled')
ureich: breich (braich) — arm; noun f., soft-mutated after y 'his' (hyt y ureich 'the length of his arm')
urenhin: brenhin (brenin) — king; noun m., soft-mutated (in apposition or as object): Hafgan urenhin, y deu urenhin · also soft as the predicate complement (a oed urenhin coronawc 'was a crowned king')
urenhines: brenhines (brenhines) — queen; noun f., soft-mutated after the article (y urenhines)
urethyn: brethyn (brethyn) — (woollen) cloth; noun m., soft-mutated after o (o urethyn llwyt tei)
uryt: bryt (bryd) — mind, intent; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uryt 'into his mind') · also ar uryt 'in the mind of', to the eye of, soft after ar (ar uryt y neb a'y guelei 'to the eye of anyone who saw it') · also soft after 'th 'your' (y'th uryt ti 'in your mind')
uu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (bu), soft-mutated after a (tirionwch... a uu y ryngthunt) · also soft-mutated after tra 'while' (tra uu da ganthunt 'while it was good with them') · also soft-mutated after yny 'until' (yny uu damunet gantunt 'until there was desire in them') and as after the relative a left unwritten (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man') · also 'she was' after a fronted predicate, the relative a understood (a lleidyr uu hi arnaf i 'and a thief she was against me') · also an apparent slip for uy (fy) 'my' in mi uu hun 'I myself' (the Red Book has miui uy hun)
uuassei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had been' (buassei), soft-mutated after a (beth a uuassei y arglwydiaeth ef) · also soft after pan 'when' (no phan uuassei Uendigeiduran yn uyw 'than when Bendigeidfran had been alive')
uuyd: buyd (ufudd) — obedient; adjective, soft-mutated after predicative yn (ny del yn uuyd 'does not come obediently')
uwrw: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast; verbal noun, soft-mutated as possessed object, 'its throwing' = throwing it (yn y uwrw y'r llawr) · also soft after a verb as its object (hi a gynsynwys uwrw neit yn y tan 'she resolved to throw a leap into the fire', i.e. to leap)
uwy: mwy (mwy) — more, greater; comparative, soft-mutated after a noun or a (ansyberwyt uwy; a uei uwy no hynny)
uwyt: bwyt (bwyd) — food; noun m., soft-mutated after o (diwallaf o uwyt a llynn 'best supplied with food and drink')
uy: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, triggers nasal mutation (uy anryded; uy nghyffes; uy gherennyd)
uych: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you be' (bych), soft-mutated (na bo miui uych ti 'that it is not I that you are')
uyd: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present/future 'is, will be' (byd), soft-mutated after a or a predicate (Dilesteir uyd dy hynt; yny uyd Hafgan)
uydaf: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. present/future 'I will be' (byddaf), soft-mutated after a (mi a uydaf hebryngyat arnat)
uynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun, soft-mutated after e/y (e uynet e gyscu 'to go to sleep') · also softened as the object of a finite verb with other words between (Ni chymellaf inheu ar neb uynet 'I will not compel anyone to go')
uynnei: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after relative a (a uynnei y hela)
uynwgyl: mynwgyl (mynwgl) — neck; noun m., soft-mutated after am (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck') · also soft directly after am (maglu y llinin am uynwgyl y llygoden 'to noose the cord about the mouse's neck')
uynyd: mynyd (mynydd) — mountain, upward; noun m. used adverbially 'upward', soft-mutated after y (a gyuodes y uynyd 'rose up')
vely: gwely (gwely) — bed; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his', spelt with v (Y vely a gyrchwys 'he went to his bed')
vreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., soft-mutated after possessive 'y, spelt with v (a'y vreic a aeth attaw)
vrth: wrth (wrth) — according to, by; preposition, spelt with v (Vrth ual y bo dy anryded)
vy: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, triggers nasal mutation, spelt with v (Vy ngwyrda kywir)
wal: ual (fel) — as, like; conjunction, the manuscript's scribal spelling with w for u (a dywot wal hynn 'and spoke like this')
waredauc: gwaredawc (gwaredog) — submissive, yielding; adjective, soft-mutated after yn (a del yn waredauc)
waret: gwaret (gwared) — to remove, take off; verbal noun, soft-mutated after i 'to' (i waret i wisc hela)
wastat: gwastat (gwastad) — constant, level; adjective, soft-mutated after yn (yn ryuelu arnaf yn wastat 'warring on me constantly')
wei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might be', soft-mutated after a (Peth bynnac o garueidrwyd a wei y rungthunt)
welas: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. preterite 'saw', soft-mutated after relative y (yny welas y llys a'r kyuanned) · also soft after the particle a (Porth y gaer a welas 'the gate of the fort she saw') and after pan 'when' (Pann welas Kicua 'when Cigfa saw')
welei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect 'he saw' (welei), soft-mutated after a (ef a welei lannerch) · also 'would see' (neu ynteu a welei rywedawt 'or else he would see a wonder')
weleis: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. preterite 'I saw/have seen', soft-mutated after ny (Ny weleis ansyberwyt uwy)
weleist: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 sg. preterite 'you saw', soft-mutated after relative a (a weleist ti)
well: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good', soft-mutated as the object of kyuarch (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you') · also soft as a comparative standing after its noun (seith cantref well 'seven better cantrefs'; heldir well 'a better hunting-land') · also soft as the predicate straight after the verb (nat oed well genti 'it was no better to her') · also na well 'no, not better', reply 'Na well' (soft-mutated gw>w after na)
welsei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had seen', soft-mutated after o'r a (o'r a welsei ef) · also soft after the negatives na and ny (hyt na welsei dyn 'so that no man had seen'; ny welsei dyn) · also soft after yr pan 'since' (yr pan welsei ef 'since he had seen')
wely: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 sg. present 'you will see', soft-mutated after a (ti a wely a wneuthum i yrot ti) · also in the presentative (a) wely di 'do you see?' = 'behold' (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son'; the Red Book has weldy), softened after the question particle a, which is absorbed
weneb: gwyneb (wyneb) — face; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive e 'his' (e weneb at yr erchwyn)
wisc: gwisc (gwisg) — garment, dress; noun f., soft-mutated after yn/predicative (yn wisc hela 'as a hunting dress') · also soft-mutated as a feminine noun after un 'same' (a'r vn wisc 'and the same garment')
wiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to dress, clothe; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wiscaw eurwisc) · also soft after an object of erchi (erchwch y wyr y llys wiscaw amdanunt 'bid the men of the court put on gear about them') · also soft as the subject of daroed (Caswallawn a daroed idaw wiscaw llen hut 'Caswallon had put on a mantle of magic', literally 'putting on … had befallen him')
wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat) · also soft as the object of a verb, with an adverb between (ny welsynt eiryoet wlat gyuanhedach 'they had never seen a more settled land')
wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a; auxiliary in 'verbal noun + a wnaeth' (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth)
wnaethant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (eisted a wnaethant)
wnaethost: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. preterite 'you did', soft-mutated after a (A wnaethost, heb ef, yrof i)
wnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do', soft-mutated after a (mi a wnaf hynny) · also 'I will see to it, bring it about that' (mi a wnaf na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'I will see that he never gets me'); auxiliary (Y gymryt a wnaf 'I will take it')
wneuthum: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. preterite 'I did', soft-mutated after a/o (gwneuthur a wneuthum itt)
wneynt: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. imperfect 'they would do', soft-mutated after a (kyuarch guell a wneynt idaw)
wnn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. present 'I know', soft-mutated after a/ny, g dropped (mi a wnn; ny wnn i)
wr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ansyberwyt uwy ar wr) · also soft after y 'to' (y wr 'to a man, to a husband') · also soft in address (A wr 'O man') and after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw wr 'what kind of man') · also subject directly after a negated verb, soft-mutated (Ny doey wr mawr 'no great man would come') · also soft after at 'to' (at wr mawr 'to a great man')
wreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., soft-mutated after a'y/possessive (ymdidan a'y wreic) · also soft after the article, as a feminine noun (y wreic 'the woman') · also soft after predicative yn (yn wreic 'as wife') and as the subject straight after a verb (ny bu wreic delediwach 'there was no comelier woman')
wrenhin: brenhin (brenin) — king; noun m., soft-mutated after deu, spelt with w for v (y deu wrenhin 'the two kings')
wrth: wrth (wrth) — to, towards, according to; preposition, base form (dywedut... wrthaw) · also 'at' (wrth y danned 'at the teeth'; wrth yr ascwrn 'at the bone') and 'because of' (wrth hynny 'for that reason') · also 'with, over' (yn ymhalogi wrth y pryf hwnnw 'defiling yourself with that creature'); in ac wrth y llinyn 'and by the cord' the sense is uncertain
wrthaw: wrth (wrth) + ef — conjugated preposition 'to/at him' (a dywedut ual hynn wrthaw) · also in y wrthaw, e wrthaw 'from him, away from him'
wrthi: wrth (wrth) + hi — conjugated preposition 'to/at her' (ny dywot ef wrthi hi)
wrthyf: wrth (wrth) + i — conjugated preposition 'to/at me' (na dywedy di wrthyf i)
wrthyt: wrth (wrth) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to/at you' (Dywedaf wrthyt; chadw kywirdeb wrthyt titheu)
wwyf: wyf (wyf) — I am; 1 sg. present of bot, the manuscript's spelling with double w (na bo tidi wwyf i)
wy: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelling variant (heb wy 'said they') · also emphatic 'them' after a conjugated preposition (ganthunt wy 'from them', ohonunt wy 'of them') · also 'them' as object, resuming the infixed -s (bei as caffwnn i wy oll 'if I were to get them all') · also a spelling of uy 'my' (wy gwreic i 'my wife'; the nasal mutation is not written)
wybot: gwybot (gwybod) — knowledge, discernment; noun m. used substantively (ny bu gystal dy wybot 'your judgement was never so good') · also the verbal noun 'to know, find out', soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wybot pwy yw 'to find out who she is') · also after heb 'without' (heb wybot dim y wrthunt 'without knowing anything of them')
wybuyssynt: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had known', soft-mutated after ni (ni wybuyssynt i eisseu ef)
wyd: gwyd (cf. gwedd) — manner, way; noun, soft-mutated after llyma (Llyma wyd y kyffy 'here is the way you will get it') · also 'presence, keeping' (gwydd), soft after dy 'your' (y'th wyd di 'to your presence, into your keeping') · also soft after y 'his' (yn y wyd 'in his keeping, in his presence'; a little uncertain)
wydwn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. imperfect 'I did not know', soft-mutated after ni (Ni wydwn achos it)
wyf: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. present 'I am' (Brenhin corunawc wyf i)
wylldeu: wylldeu (ill dau) — both of them (y deu gorff wylldeu 'their two bodies, both of them')
wyneb: gwyneb (wyneb) — face; noun m., base unmutated form
wynnet: gwynnet (gwynder) — whiteness; abstract noun formed with -et from gwyn 'white', soft-mutated as subject (ual y llathrei wynnet y cwn)
wynt: wynt (hwynt) — they, them; 3 pl. pronoun (un lliw ac wynt 'the same colour as them') · also Wynt, Gwent, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed', a region of south-east Wales
wynteu: wynt (hwynt) — they, for their part; conjunctive 3 pl. pronoun (Wynteu hagen ni wybuyssynt)
wyppo: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may know' (a wyppo na bo miui uych ti)
wyr: gwyr (gwŷr) — men; noun pl., soft-mutated after yn (yn wyr ymi 'as men to me') · also soft after o 'of' (o wyr 'of men') and in address (A wyr 'O men') · also soft after y 'to' (y wyr Dyuet 'to the men of Dyfed') and y 'his' (y wyr 'his men')
wyrda: gwyrda (gwyrda) — noblemen; noun pl., base form, gwyr 'men' + da 'good' (A wyrda, heb ef) · also soft after o 'of' (a chan hynn o wyrda 'and with these noblemen', literally 'of noblemen')
wyt: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. present 'you are' (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that') · also (13) for predicative yn 'as', with soft mutation (Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you'; the Red Book yn vach) · (14) y ar 'from off' (y ar seith cantref Dyuet 'from off the seven cantrefs of Dyfed') · also y 'its, his' before a verbal noun, standing for the noun's object and softening it (na'y werthu 'nor selling it'; na'y ollwng 'nor releasing it')
ych: ych (eich) — your (pl.); possessive pronoun (kymerwch ych kyuarwyd) · also before a verbal noun as its object, 'you' (ef a ry eill ych necau 'he may refuse you')
yd: yd — preverbal particle used when the clause opens with an adverb rather than the subject, introducing an indicative main verb (A threigylgweith yd oed yn Arberth) · also yd 'corn, grain' noun m. (y diua dy yd 'to destroy your corn')
ym: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelling variant before p/m/b (hyt ym Penn Llwyn Diarwya; ym perued) · also bot 1 pl. present 'we are' (yd ym y gyt 'we are together'; llibin yd ym pob blwydyn 'wretched that we are every year') · also 'my', a by-form of uy, in the oath ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God' (the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); the nasal mutation it brings is not written
ymbilio: ymbilio (ymbilio) — to beg, entreat; verbal noun (yr a ymbilio a thi 'however much he begs you')
ymchwelut: ymchwelut (ymchwelyd) — to turn (oneself); verbal noun (ymchwelut e weneb at yr erchwyn)
ymdialwyf: ymdial (ymddial) — to avenge oneself; 1 sg. present subjunctive 'I avenge myself', soft-mutated after nyt (a chyn nyt ymdialwyf a thi)
ymdidan: ymdidan (ymddiddan) — conversation, to converse; noun/verbal noun, base form (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth ef)
ymdidanyssam: ymdidan (ymddiddan) — to converse; 1 pl. preterite 'we conversed' (yd ymdidanyssam ni)
ymgael: ymgael (ymgael) — to meet, encounter (with a); verbal noun, takes a/ac (ymordiwes ac ef... ymgael a'r gwr)
ymgolli: ymgolli (ymgolli) — to lose oneself, get lost; verbal noun, reflexive prefix ym- (ymgolli a'y gydymdeithon)
ymgyuaruot: ymgyuaruot (ymgyfarfod) — to meet each other; verbal noun (e ymgyuaruot)
ymi: y (i) + mi — conjugated preposition 'to me' (pa gyuarwyd a uyd ymi)
ymlad: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; verbal noun (yn herwyd ymlad a frouedigaeth y gorff)
ymladei: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; 3 sg. imperfect 'he would fight' (yd ymladei a mi drannoeth)
ymolchi: ymolchi (ymolchi) — to wash (oneself); verbal noun (e ymolchi yd aethant)
ymordiwes: ymordiwes (goddiwes) — to overtake, catch up with (takes a/ac); verbal noun (yn ymordiwes ac ef)
ymouyn: ymouyn (ymofyn) — to ask, inquire (of); verbal noun (dechreu ymouyn a gwyrda y wlat)
ympenn: y (yn) + penn (pen) — 'at/to the end (of)', written as one word (hyt ympenn y ulwydyn)
ymwarandaw: ymwarandaw (ymwrando) — to listen (to, with a); verbal noun (yn ymwarandaw a llef yr erchwys)
ymwerendewch: ymwarandaw (ymwrando) — to listen; 2 pl. imperative 'listen!' (ymwerendewch yn da)
ymwlet: ymwelet (ymweld) — to see, visit; verbal noun; a scribal spelling with a letter dropped (ymwlet a'y eniuer)
ymyrru: ymyrru (ymyrryd) — to apply oneself, busy oneself (with ar); verbal noun (ymyrru ar digriwwch serchawl)
yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was') · also yn yd 'as, while, when' (Ac yn yd aeth pawb ym pen yr arueu 'and while all went to arms'; the sense uncertain) · also 'our', a spelling of an (ein), with no mutation (yn anniuer ninheu 'our own company'; yn ymborth 'our sustenance'; yn diuetha 'our destroying') · also 'into' with rithyaw (eu rithyaw yn llygot 'to change them into mice')
yna: yna (yna) — then; adverb (Yna y rodes Arawn y furuf)
yndaw: yn (yn) + ef — conjugated preposition 'in him' (angheuawl dyrnawt yndaw ynteu; yssyd yndaw ef)
yndi: yn (yn) + hi — conjugated preposition 'in her/it', feminine (Nit oes yndi nep; y guassanaeth yndi)
yneuadeu: neuad (neuadd) — hall; plural neuadeu with a prosthetic y- (hundyeu ac yneuadeu)
yniueroed: niuer (nifer) — host, company; plural niueroed with a prosthetic y- (teulu ac yniueroed)
yno: yno (yno) — there; adverb (ac yno y bu y nos honno)
ynteu: ynteu (yntau) — 'he, for his part'; conjunctive pronoun marking a change of speaker or actor (heb ynteu)
yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon', kept as written (the Red Book has ar hynny) (Ac ar yny, llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the warband')
yr: yr — (1) the article 'the' before a vowel (yr erchwys); (2) 'for, for the sake of' preposition (yr Duw 'for God's sake', yr guaret gormes 'for removing the oppression') · (3) 'for all, however' before an equative-type noun and a clause (yr araued y kerdei y uarch 'for all the slowness with which his horse went'); (4) in yr meityn 'for a while (since)'; (5) the verbal particle y, yd, written yr before a vowel (yr ymordiwedei a hi 'that he would overtake her') · also (6) the perfective particle ry written yr, softening the verb (yr gyscwys 'has slept'); the article before an independent possessive (yr eidunt 'theirs'); 'for' with an abstract noun (yr bychanet 'for the smallness') · also the article before hwnn, honn, 'the one' (yr hwnn y tu a Chernyw 'the one on the side towards Cornwall'; yr honn a uu tryded anuat paluawt 'the one that was the third unfortunate blow') · also yr (er) 'for all' before the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'for all the grief they had seen') · also the article before a consonant in kyrchu yr gaer 'making for the fort' (read as the article, as the second witness takes it) · yr pan 'since' (yr pan welsei ef 'since he had seen'); the verb after it is soft-mutated
yroet: eiroet (erioed) — ever; adverb, spelling variant (o'r a'm canlynwys i yroet 'of those that have ever followed me')
yrof: yr (er) + i — conjugated preposition 'for me' (A wnaethost, heb ef, yrof i)
yrot: yr (er) + ti — conjugated preposition 'for you' (a wneuthum i yrot ti)
ys: ys (ys) — 'it is'; copula particle introducing a predicate, esp. in time expressions (ys blwydyn 'it is a year' = for a year) · also the infixed 3 sg. object 's 'it' after pei (pei ys guelwn 'if I saw it') · also 'below, under', is, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed' · also before the verb in ac aduyd ys kymeraf 'and perhaps I will take' (the Red Book atuyd ys kymeraf): perhaps the particle, perhaps the infixed 's 'it' after aduyd; uncertain · also yd ys 'one is, people are', the impersonal present of bot (yd ys yn cadw 'one keeps'; Yd ys yn lluydaw 'a host is being raised')
yssyd: bot (bod) — to be; relative present 'is, who/that is' (sydd) (Gwr yssyd gyuerbyn; pa amgen uedwl yssyd yndaw)
ystauell: ystauell (ystafell) — room, chamber; noun f. (na guas ystauell 'no chamber-servant')
ysteuyll: ystauell (ystafell) — room, chamber; noun pl. 'rooms' (hundyeu ac yneuadeu, ac ysteuyll)
