ystlys: ystlys (ystlys) — side, edge; noun f. (ystlys y llannerch 'the edge of the clearing')
yti: y (i) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to you', variant spelling (pa furyf y caf i dy gerennyd di... yti)
yttoydwn: bot (bod) — to be; old 1 sg. imperfect 'I was' (Nit yttoydwn i yn holi dim i ti)
yw: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. copula 'is', used in equative sentences (Sef yw hwnnw, Hafgan)
threigylgueith: treigylgweith (treiglwaith) — one time, once; noun m., here spelt with gu for gw, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A threigylgueith 'and once'), the opening formula
gwled: gwled (gwledd) — feast, banquet; noun f. (gwled darparedic 'a prepared feast')
darparedic: darparedic (darparedig) — prepared, made ready; past participle in -edic of darparu 'prepare' (gwled darparedic 'a feast made ready')
bwyta: bwyta (bwyta) — to eat; verbal noun, also 'eating, a meal' (gwedy y bwyta kyntaf 'after the first eating', the first sitting of a feast)
orymdeith: gorymdeith (gorymdaith) — walking about, a progress; noun f., used after y 'to' like a verbal noun ('to walk about'); g lost by soft mutation after y 'to' (kyuodi y orymdeith 'rising to walk about')
gorssed: gorssed (gorsedd) — mound (one a lord might sit on), seat; noun f. (penn gorssed 'the top of a mound'; Gorssed Arberth 'the Mound of Arberth')
uch: uch (uwch) — above, over; preposition (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also 'high' as adjective/adverb, comparative in yn uch no bwrd y llong 'higher than the ship's board'
llaw: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., in the idiom uch llaw 'above, overlooking' (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also gyr llaw 'beside, next to' (eisted gyr llaw hwnnw 'to sit beside it') · also 'hand' without mutation after the article y (yn y llaw arall 'in the other hand')
elwit: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal imperfect in -it 'was called', g lost by soft mutation after relative a (a elwit 'that was called')
kynnedyf: kynnedyf (cynneddf) — property, peculiar nature, quality; noun f. (kynnedyf yr orssed yw 'it is the property of the mound')
orssed: gorssed (gorsedd) — mound; noun f., g lost by soft mutation after the article, as a feminine noun (yr orssed 'the mound', y'r orssed 'to the mound') · also soft (g lost) as the object after the verb and its subject pronoun (y kyrchwys ef Orssed Arberth 'he made for Gorsedd Arberth'), as the first element of a place-name
dylyedauc: dylyedawc (dyledog) — man of birth, nobleman; noun m./adjective, from dylyet 'right, due'; d- is its own first letter, so a softening word before it (pa dylyedauc bynnac 'whatever nobleman') shows nothing
eistedo: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; 3 sg. present subjunctive in -o 'may sit' (a eistedo arnei 'who may sit on it')
nat: na, nat (nad) — 'that … not'; negative conjunction of a subordinate clause, nat before a vowel (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there')
odyno: odyno (oddi yno) — from there, thence; adverb, o 'from' + yno 'there' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there')
deupeth: deupeth (deubeth) — two things; deu 'two' + peth 'thing' (un o'r deupeth 'one of the two things')
kymriw: kymriw (cymriw) — injury, bruising, hurt; noun m., near-synonym of archoll 'wound' (kymriw neu archolleu 'injury or wounds')
neu: neu (neu) — (1) 'or' (kymriw neu archolleu 'injury or wounds'; neu ynteu 'or else'); (2) the affirmative particle neu 'lo, indeed' before a verb, neut before a vowel, neur with infixed 'r (see neut, neir)
archolleu: archoll (archoll) — wound; noun, plural archolleu (kymriw neu archolleu 'injury or wounds')
rywedawt: ryuedawt (rhyfeddod) — wonder, marvel; noun m., spelt rywedawt with w for u (= v); no mutation (a welei rywedawt 'would see a wonder')
ouyn: ofyn (ofn) — fear; noun m., u for the v-sound (nyt oes arnaf i ouyn 'I have no fear', literally 'there is no fear on me') · also 3 sg. present of gouyn (gofyn) 'asks', with g lost by soft mutation after a (ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'); a different word from ofyn 'fear' · also 2 sg. imperative of gouyn (gofyn) 'ask', g lost by soft mutation after na (na ouyn di yni y mab 'do not ask us for the boy') · also verbal noun gouyn 'asking', g- lost by soft mutation after heb 'without' (heb ouyn 'without asking') and after y 'to' (y ouyn idaw 'to ask of him')
cael: caffael (cael) — to get, suffer, receive; verbal noun, cael beside caffael (ouyn cael kymriw 'fear of getting injury')
plith: plith (plith) — midst; noun m., in ym plith 'among' (ym plith hynn o niuer 'among this (much) of company')
ryuedawt: ryuedawt (rhyfeddod) — wonder, marvel; noun m., unmutated (r is how the manuscript writes rh); (Ryuedawt hagen da oed gennyf 'a wonder, however, I should like')
pei: pei (pe) — if; conjunction of an unreal or hypothetical condition, with the imperfect subjunctive (pei ys guelwn 'if I saw it'); in pei … pellaf it works like modern po 'the more … the farther'; after a 'and' written phei, ffei, fei
guelwn: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I should see, if I saw' (pei ys guelwn 'if I saw it'); gu for gw
wnath: scribal slip for wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a (Eisted a wnath 'he sat', literally 'sitting he did')
bydynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. habitual imperfect 'they were (being), they used to be', beside oedynt (ual y bydynt yn eisted 'as they were sitting')
welynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. imperfect 'they saw', soft-mutated after a (wynt a welynt 'they saw'; yny welynt 'until they saw')
canwelw: canwelw — pale white; adjective of a horse's colour, can 'white' + gwelw 'pale' (march canwelw 'a pale-white horse')
aruchel: aruchel (aruchel) — very high, lofty; adjective, ar- + uchel 'high' (mawr aruchel 'big and very tall')
eureit: eureit (euraid) — golden; adjective, from aur 'gold' (gwisc eureit 'a golden garment')
prifford: prifford (priffordd) — highway, main road; noun f., prif 'chief' + ford 'road' (ar hyt y prifford 'along the highway')
gerdei: kerdet (cerdded) — to go, walk, travel; 3 sg. imperfect 'went', soft-mutated after relative a (a gerdei 'that went')
law: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., soft-mutated after heb in heb law 'past, beside' (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound') · also 'side' in ar neill law 'on one side' (ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'), soft after neill; 'hand' after possessive 'th (y'th law 'in your hand') · also soft after y 'his' (dodi y law 'putting his hand')
kerdet: kerdet (cerdded) — going, walking; verbal noun, also a noun 'pace, gait' (kerdet araf guastat 'a slow, even pace'; o'r kerdet mwyaf 'to the greatest pace')
araf: araf (araf) — slow, gentle; adjective (kerdet araf 'a slow pace'); its equative-type form araued is used as a noun 'slowness' (see araued)
gan: gan (gan) — with, by; preposition, softening the next word; possession is 'with' a person or thing (oed gan y march 'the horse had', literally 'was with the horse'); y gan 'from' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'); base of gennyf, ganthaw, genthi etc. · also 'from', without y (ny chaffei namyn yr un atteb gan y gwraged 'she would get only the same answer from the women'; yny gigleu gan lawer 'until he heard from many')
march: march (march) — horse; noun m., base form (y march 'the horse')
ogyuuch: gogyuuch (gogyfuwch) — as high as, level with (with a 'with'); go- + kyuuch, the equative of uchel 'high'; g lost by soft mutation after y 'to' (y ogyuuch a'r orssed 'level with the mound'; the Red Book has yn ogyfuuch) · also after yn (yn ogyuuch a hi 'level with her')
ohonawch: o (o) — of, from; 2 pl. conjugated form 'of you' (a oes ohonawch i 'is there (any) of you'); the following i is probably the echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending
uarchoges: marchoges (marchoges) — horsewoman; noun f., march + feminine -oges, soft-mutated after the article (y uarchoges 'the horsewoman')
aet: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. imperative 'let him go' (Aet un 'let one go')
herbyn: erbyn (erbyn) — meeting; in yn y herbyn 'to meet her', with h- before the vowel after y 'her' · also yn eu herbyn 'to meet them', with h- after eu 'their'
ford: ford (ffordd) — road, way; noun f., f written for ff (y'r ford 'to the road'; yr un ford 'the same way')
athoed: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had gone' (athoed beside aethoed) (neut athoed hi heibaw 'lo, she had gone past')
heibaw: heibaw (heibio) — past, by; adverb (athoed hi heibaw 'she had gone past')
hymlit: ymlit (ymlid) — to pursue, chase; verbal noun, with h- after y 'her', the possessive standing for the object (y hymlit 'to pursue her', literally 'her pursuing')
gallei: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. imperfect 'he could' (ual y gallei gyntaf 'as fast as he could')
pedestric: pedestric — meaning disputed: 'going on foot' (o pedestric 'on foot') or 'speed, running' (it is also said of a horse); noun, a borrowing from Latin pedester 'on foot'
fei: pei (pe) — if; here written fei for phei, the spirant mutation after a 'and'; in A fei … pellaf … 'the more … the farther' it works like modern po
mwyf: scribal slip for mwyaf: mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'most' (A fei mwyf uei y urys ef 'the greater his haste'); the Red Book has vwyhaf
urys: brys (brys) — haste; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (y urys ef 'his haste') and after amgen (amgen urys 'other haste')
pellaf: pell (pell) — far; superlative pellaf 'farthest', in pei … pellaf 'the more … the farther' (pellaf uydei hitheu 'the farther she would be')
uydei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. habitual imperfect 'would be, used to be' (bydei), soft-mutated after a fronted word, the relative a being understood (pellaf uydei hitheu 'the farther she would be')
thygyei: tygyaw (tycio) — to avail, be of use; 3 sg. imperfect 'availed', spirant-mutated after na/ni (na thygyei idaw 'that it did not avail him'; ni thygyei ymi 'it did not avail me')
thykya: tygyaw (tycio) — to avail, be of use; 3 sg. present 'avails', spirant-mutated after ni/ny (ni thykya 'does not avail')
dos: mynet (mynd) — to go; 2 sg. imperative 'go!' (dos y'r llys 'go to the court'; dos ragot 'go on')
chymer: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 2 sg. imperative 'take!', spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chymer y march 'and take the horse')
wypych: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may know', soft-mutated after relative a (y march kyntaf a wypych 'the first horse you know of')
hol: ol (ôl) — track, trace; noun m., with h- after y 'her' (yn y hol 'after her', literally 'in her track') · also with h- after eu 'their' (yn eu hol 'in their track, behind them')
gymerth: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 sg. preterite 'took', soft-mutated after a (Y march a gymerth 'he took the horse'; a gymerth rygyng 'took an amble')
maestir: maestir (maestir) — open land, plain; noun m., maes 'field' + tir 'land' (y maestir guastat 'the level open land')
gauas: caffael (cael) — to get, find, reach; 3 sg. preterite 'got', soft-mutated after a (a gauas 'got, reached')
dangosses: dangos (dangos) — to show; 3 sg. preterite in -es 'showed'; after a the d is softened to dd, which the manuscript also writes d (a dangosses yr ysparduneu y'r march 'showed the spurs to the horse')
ysparduneu: yspardun (ysbardun) — spur; noun m., plural ysparduneu (yr ysparduneu 'the spurs')
ffei: pei (pe) — if; written ffei for phei, the spirant mutation after a 'and'; in A ffei uwyaf … pellaf … 'the more … the farther' it works like modern po
uwyaf: mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'most', soft-mutated (after pei, as after modern po) (A ffei uwyaf y lladei 'the more he would strike') · also soft after a feminine noun, adjective 'greatest, most' (y wreic uwyaf a garaf 'the woman I love most', mwyaf) · also soft as the predicate of uei (ban uei uwyaf yd ymgerynt 'when they loved one another most')
lladei: llad (lladd) — to strike, kill; 3 sg. imperfect 'would strike, used to strike' (y lladei ef y march 'he would strike the horse')
vn: un (un) — one; with the article 'the same'; written vn; softens a following feminine noun (yr vn march 'the same horse'; yr vn wisc 'the same garment'; vn gerdet 'the same pace')
gerdet: kerdet (cerdded) — going, pace; verbal noun/noun, soft-mutated after y 'to' (y gerdet 'to go'), after vn 'same' (vn gerdet; why is not clear, kerdet being usually masculine), and in amgen urys gerdet 'other haste of pace' (cause unclear) · also soft-mutated after pa 'what' (pa gerdet yssyd arnawch chwi 'what journey is on you?') and after llyna (Llyna gerdet 'there is the journey') · also soft after ar 'on' (ar gerdet 'on the move, walking') · also soft after in 'for us' (reit yw in gerdet 'it is necessary for us to go')
dechreuyssei: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 sg. pluperfect in -yssei 'had begun' (a dechreuyssei hitheu 'that she had begun')
ballwys: pallu (pallu) — to fail, give out; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'failed', soft-mutated after a (Y uarch ef a ballwys 'his horse failed')
wybu: gwybot (gwybod) — to know, perceive; 3 sg. preterite 'knew', soft-mutated after pan 'when' (a phan wybu ef 'and when he knew')
pallu: pallu (pallu) — to fail, give out; verbal noun (pallu y bedestric 'its speed failing')
bedestric: pedestric — soft-mutated after y 'his, its' (pallu y bedestric 'its speed failing', of a horse); meaning disputed: 'going on foot' or 'speed, running' (see pedestric)
ymlit: ymlit (ymlid) — to pursue, chase; verbal noun, base form (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue')
unbennes: unbennes — lady-chieftain, lady; noun f., the feminine of unben 'chieftain' (yr unbennes racco 'the lady yonder')
racco: racco (acw) — yonder; adverb after a noun (yr unbennes racco 'the lady yonder')
warch: march (march) — horse; noun m., soft-mutated (= uarch) as the object after the subject (ny wydwn i warch gynt 'I knew no swifter horse'), the w-letter written for the v-sound
gynt: kynt (cynt) — (1) 'swifter', comparative of buan 'swift', softened after a noun (warch gynt 'a swifter horse'); (2) 'before, formerly', the softened adverb, modern gynt (no'r dyd gynt 'than the day before')
kyuoyth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm; noun m., spelt kyuoyth (yn y kyuoyth 'in the realm')
ryw: ryw (rhyw) — some, some kind of; before its noun (ryw ystyr hut 'some meaning of magic') · also y ryw wr 'what kind of man'; ryw 'sort, kind' as a noun
ystyr: ystyr (ystyr) — meaning, purpose; noun (ryw ystyr hut 'some meaning of magic')
hut: hut (hud) — magic, illusion, enchantment; noun m. (ystyr hut 'a meaning of magic')
awn: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 pl. 'let us go' (Awn parth a'r llys 'let us go towards the court') or 'we will go' (ni a awn)
doethant: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Y'r llys y doethant 'to the court they came')
threulau: treulaw (treulio) — to spend (time); verbal noun spelt treulau, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a threulau y dyd hwnnw 'and spending that day')
mynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun (amser mynet y uwyta 'time to go to eat')
uwyta: bwyta (bwyta) — to eat; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y 'to' (mynet y uwyta 'go to eat')
gwedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, the spelling beside guedy (A gwedy y bwyta kyntaf 'and after the first eating')
yniuer: niuer (nifer) — company, host; noun m. with prosthetic y- (yr yniuer y buam doe 'the company that we were yesterday')
buam: bot (bod) — to be; 1 pl. preterite 'we were' (y buam doe 'that we were yesterday')
doe: doe (ddoe) — yesterday; adverb (y uarchoges doe 'yesterday's horsewoman')
thidy: tidy (tydi) — you (sg.), emphatic pronoun, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A thidy 'and you')
uakwyueit: makwyf (macwy) — page, squire, youth; noun m., plural makwyueit, soft-mutated after y 'his' (o'y uakwyueit 'of his pages')
dwg: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 2 sg. imperative 'bring!' (dwg gennyt 'bring with you')
mays: maes (maes) — field, open ground; noun m., spelt mays (yn y mays 'in the field')
makwyf: makwyf (macwy) — page, squire, youth; noun m. (y makwyf 'the page')
gyrchyssant: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they made for', soft-mutated after a (Yr orssed a gyrchyssant 'they made for the mound')
val: ual (fel) — as; conjunction, spelt val (Ac val y bydynt 'and as they were')
eiste: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; verbal noun spelt without its final -d (yn eiste 'sitting'; y eiste 'to sit')
bid: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperative 'let it be', also said to a person, 'be!' (Bid parawt 'be ready'), where the Red Book has the 2 sg. byd
was: gwas (gwas) — lad, servant; noun m., soft-mutated in address (Ha was 'ho, lad'; Bid parawt … was 'be ready, lad') and after wrth (wrth was y uarch 'to his groom', literally 'the lad of his horse') · also soft after predicative yn (yn was ieuanc 'as a young lad')
gywerbyn: kyuerbyn (cyferbyn) — opposite, facing (with a/ac); softened as an adverb, with w for the v-sound (a doeth gywerbyn ac wynt 'came opposite them')
yskynnu: yskynnu (esgyn) — to mount, climb; verbal noun (yskynnu ar y march 'mounting the horse')
chynn: kynn (cyn) — before; with a verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chynn daruot idaw 'and before he had finished')
daruot: daruot (darfod) — to finish, be finished, happen; verbal noun, with y/i of the person (kynn daruot idaw ymgueiraw 'before he had finished making ready')
ymgueiraw: ymgyweiraw — to make oneself ready, settle oneself; reflexive verbal noun, ym- + kyweiraw 'prepare, set in order', written ymgueiraw (ymgueiraw yn y gyfrwy 'settling himself in his saddle') · also ymgueiraw ar 'to equip oneself with, get together' (ymgueiraw ar y ganuet marchauc 'to get ready with his hundred horsemen'); the sense with ar is uncertain
gyfrwy: kyfrwy (cyfrwy) — saddle; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y gyfrwy 'in his saddle')
neir: neir — as Evans prints it, clear on the page; probably a slip for neur, the affirmative particle neu with the perfective 'r (neir ry adoed hi heibaw 'lo, she had gone past'); the Red Book has neur; the White Book's own reading remains uncertain
ry: ry — perfective verbal particle 'has, had' before a verb; causes soft mutation (ry adoed 'had gone')
adoed: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had gone', a by-form or spelling of athoed (ry adoed hi heibaw 'she had gone past')
chynnwll: kynnwll — a rare word, meaning uncertain; 'gap, space' is a guess from the context (a chynnwll y rygthunt 'and a gap between them'); noun, spirant-mutated after a 'and'; the Red Book has it too
rygthunt: rwng (rhwng) — between; 3 pl. conjugated form 'between them' (y rygthunt 'between them')
rygyng: rygyng (rhygyng) — amble, an easy gait of a horse; which gait exactly is not certain; noun m. (a gymerth rygyng y gan y uarch 'took an amble from his horse')
dybygei: tybyaw (tybied) — to suppose, think; 3 sg. imperfect 'supposed', soft-mutated after a (ef a dybygei 'he supposed')
araued: araf (araf) — slow; araued, with the -ed of the equative ('as slow'), here a noun 'slowness, such slowness' (yr araued y kerdei y uarch 'for all the slowness with which his horse went'); the construction is hard
kerdei: kerdet (cerdded) — to go, walk; 3 sg. imperfect 'went' (y kerdei y uarch 'that his horse went')
ymordiwedei: ymordiwes (cf. modern goddiwes) — to overtake (with a 'with'); 3 sg. imperfect 'would overtake' (yr ymordiwedei a hi 'that he would overtake her', yr being the verbal particle before a vowel)
thygywys: tygyaw (tycio) — to avail, be of use; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'availed', spirant-mutated after ny (ny thygywys idaw 'it did not avail him')
ellwg: ellwng (gollwng) — to let go, loose; verbal noun, spelt ellwg (Ellwg y uarch a oruc 'he let his horse go')
auwyneu: auwyn (afwyn) — rein; noun, plural auwyneu (wrth auwyneu 'by the reins')
nes: nes (nes) — nearer; comparative of agos 'near' (nyt oed nes idi 'it was no nearer to her')
bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk) · also the conjunction 'if' (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them')
phei: pei (pe) — if; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a phei); in a phei … pellaf … 'and the more … the farther' it works like modern po
wyaf: scribal slip for uwyaf (one letter short): mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'most', softened (a phei wyaf y lladei 'and the more he would strike'); the Red Book has vwyhaf
cany: cany — 'since … not'; conjunction can 'since' + the negative ny, softening the verb (Cany welas ef 'since he did not see') · also with the verb left unsoftened (Cany mynny hynny 'since you do not want that'; the Red Book likewise)
tygyaw: tygyaw (tycio) — to avail, be of use; verbal noun (tygyaw idaw e hymlit 'that pursuing her availed him')
wnaet: scribal slip for wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a (ymchwelut a wnaet 'he turned back')
allu: gallu (gallu) — power, ability; noun m., softened as the subject after oes (nyt oes allu 'there is no power')
weleisti: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 sg. preterite weleist with the pronoun ti written on, 'you saw', soft-mutated after a (noc a weleisti 'than what you saw') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) after na (na weleisti gedymdeith 'that you did not see a companion')
herlit: erlit (erlid) — to pursue; verbal noun, with h- after y 'her' (y herlit hi 'to pursue her')
neges: neges (neges) — errand, business; noun f. (yd oed neges idi 'she had an errand'; Pennaf neges 'the chief errand')
rei: rei (rhai) — some, some people; pronoun (rei o'r maes hwnn 'some of this field')
maes: maes (maes) — field, open ground; noun m. (o'r maes hwnn 'of this field', of those here)
gattei: gadu (gadael) — to let, allow, leave; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'would allow' (pei gattei 'if (it) would allow')
wrthpwythi: wrthpwythi — a hard word, perhaps found nowhere else; meaning uncertain; apparently a noun in gwrth- 'against', softened; the Red Book has wrthpwyll (gwrth- + pwyll 'sense, mind'), which points to something like 'contrariness, perversity'; 'stubbornness' is a guess on that basis
gerdeu: kerd (cerdd) — song, music; noun f., plural kerdeu, soft-mutated after drwy (drwy gerdeu 'through songs')
llonyd: llonyd (llonydd) — content, at ease, quiet; adjective, also noun 'peace' (ual y bu llonyd ganthunt 'as they pleased', literally 'as it was content with them')
diuyrru: diuyrru (difyrru) — to pass (time), divert, amuse; verbal noun (diuyrru y dyd 'passing the day')
wwyta: bwyta (bwyta) — to eat; written wwyta for uwyta, soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wwyta 'to eat'); listed as a slip, though the first w may simply be the w-letter for the v-sound; the Red Book has vwyta
daruu: daruot (darfod) — to finish, be finished; 3 sg. preterite 'was finished', with y/i of the person (pan daruu udunt y bwyd 'when they had finished the meal') · also 'happened, befell' (Pa daruu y Gradawc 'what befell Caradog?')
bwyd: bwyd (bwyd) — food, meal; noun m. (y bwyd 'the meal')
buom: bot (bod) — to be; 1 pl. preterite 'we were' (= buam) (y buom ni 'that we were')
echtoe: echtoe (echdoe) — the day before yesterday; adverb (doe ac echtoe 'yesterday and the day before')
llymma: llyma (dyma) — here is, behold; spelt with the m doubled (Llymma, Arglwyd 'here (it is), Lord')
thitheu: titheu (tithau) — you for your part; 2 sg. conjunctive pronoun, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A thitheu 'and you')
kyfrwya: kyfrwyaw (cyfrwyo) — to saddle; 2 sg. imperative 'saddle!' (kyfrwya uy march 'saddle my horse')
dabre: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 sg. imperative dabre 'come!', an old form (dabre ac ef 'come with it')
dwc: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 2 sg. imperative 'bring!', spelt dwc beside dwg (dwc uy ysparduneu 'bring my spurs')
gwas: gwas (gwas) — lad, servant; noun m., base form (Y gwas 'the lad')
buant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (Ny buant 'they were not')
hayach: hayach (haeach) — almost, nearly; with a negative 'hardly, scarcely' (Ny buant hayach o enkyt 'they had hardly been any while')
enkyt: enkyt (encyd) — a while, a space; noun (o enkyt 'of a while')
ha: ha — ho!, ah!; interjection before an address, the noun addressed softened (Ha was 'ho, lad')
welaf: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. present 'I see', soft-mutated after a (mi a welaf 'I see')
moes: moes — give (me)!; an old imperative found only in this form (Moes uy march 'give me my horse')
kynt: kynt (cynt) — sooner, faster; comparative of buan 'swift' (nyt kynt … noc … 'no sooner … than'); also 'before, formerly'
yskynn: yskynnu (esgyn) — to mount, climb; 3 sg. present 'mounts' (yd yskynn ef ar y uarch 'he mounts his horse')
hebdaw: heb (heb) — without, past; 3 sg. m. conjugated form 'past him, without him' (yd a hitheu hebdaw ef 'she goes past him')
troi: troi (troi) — to turn; verbal noun (Troi yn y hol a oruc ef 'he turned after her') · also 'to wrap, wind about' (guedy troi llenn o bali yn y gylch 'having wrapped a cloth of brocade about him')
gadel: gadel (gadael) — to leave, let; verbal noun (gadel y uarch … y gerdet 'letting his horse go')
drythyll: trythyll (trythyll) — spirited, lively, wanton; adjective, written softened, cause uncertain (y uarch drythyll 'his spirited horse')
llamsachus: llamsachus — prancing, bounding; adjective, from llam 'leap' (y uarch drythyll llamsachus 'his spirited, prancing horse')
neit: neit (naid) — leap, bound; noun f. (ar yr eil neit 'at the second leap')
trydyd: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal (ar y trydyd 'at the third')
gordiwedei: gordiwes (goddiwes) — to overtake; 3 sg. imperfect 'would overtake' (y gordiwedei 'that he would overtake (her)')
gymhellaud: kymhell (cymell) — to urge, drive, compel; 3 sg. preterite in -awd, spelt -aud, soft-mutated after a (Y uarch a gymhellaud 'he urged his horse')
mwyaf: mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'greatest, most' (o'r kerdet mwyaf 'to the greatest pace')
guelet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, gu for gw (A guelet a wnaeth 'and he saw')
uorwyn: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden; noun f., soft-mutated in address (A uorwyn 'O maiden'), after the article (y uorwyn 'the maiden') and after o (o uorwyn 'of maiden') · also soft after am 'about' (am uorwyn kystal 'about a maiden so good') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uorwyn gyt ac ef 'as a maiden with him')
mwyn: mwyn (mwyn) — sake; noun m., in yr mwyn 'for the sake of' (modern er mwyn); also adjective 'gentle'
mwyhaf: mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'most', spelt mwyhaf (y gwr mwyhaf a gery 'the man you love most')
gery: karu (caru) — to love; 2 sg. present 'you love', soft-mutated after a (a gery 'that you love')
arho: arhos (aros) — to wait; 2 sg. imperative 'wait!' (arho ui 'wait for me')
arhoaf: arhos (aros) — to wait; 1 sg. present 'I (will) wait' (Arhoaf yn llawen 'I will wait gladly')
llessach: lles (lles) — benefit, good; llessach 'better, more beneficial', comparative formed on the noun (oed llessach y'r march 'it would have been better for the horse')
ass: 's — the infixed 3 sg. object pronoun 'it', here written ass after pei, the s doubled (pei ass archut 'if you had asked it'; Evans affarchut)
archut: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you were to ask, had asked' (pei ass archut 'if you had asked it')
meityn: meityn (meitin) — a while; noun used adverbially (yr meityn 'for a while (since)', some time ago; modern ers meitin)
sewyll: sefyll (sefyll) — to stand, stop; verbal noun, w for the v-sound (Sewyll ac arhos a oruc 'she stopped and waited')
arhos: arhos (aros) — to wait; verbal noun (Sewyll ac arhos 'stopping and waiting')
gwaret: gwaret (gwared) — to remove, put aside; verbal noun (gwaret y rann 'removing the part')
rann: rann (rhan) — part; noun f. (y rann a dylyei uot 'the part that ought to be')
hwyneb: wyneb (wyneb) — face; noun m., with h- after y 'her' (am y hwyneb 'about her face')
phenn: penn (pen) — head; noun m., spirant-mutated after y 'her' (gwisc y phenn 'the covering of her head')
attal: attal (atal) — to hold, stop, fix; verbal noun (attal y golwc arnaw 'fixing her gaze on him')
golwc: golwc (golwg) — look, gaze, sight; noun (y golwc 'her gaze')
doy: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 sg. present 'you come' (pan doy di 'where do you come from?') · also 3 sg. imperfect 'would come', a variant of doey (ny doy gof udunt wy dim 'no memory of anything came to them') · the same 3 sg. imperfect 'would come' (ef a doy am dy benn 'it would come upon your head'; the Red Book has ef a doei)
negesseu: neges (neges) — errand, business; noun f., plural negesseu (wrth uy negesseu 'about my business')
welet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, soft-mutated after dy 'your' (dy welet ti 'seeing you', literally 'your seeing') · also soft after o 'from, because of' (o welet gwr kymeint a gerynt 'from seeing a man so loved by them') · also soft after am 'for, because of' (am welet y cledyf 'for seeing the sword') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as a verbal noun directly after the verb (ryuedu a wnaethant welet y gaer 'they marvelled to see the fort')
crassaw: crassaw (croeso) — welcome; noun (Crassaw wrthyt 'welcome to you')
diuwyn: diuwyn — worthless, unpleasing (which shade is meant is debated); adjective, di- 'without' + mwyn 'pleasing, worth', softened (bot yn diuwyn ganthaw 'that it was worthless in his eyes')
ffryt: pryt (pryd) — form, looks; noun m., spirant-mutated after y 'her', written ffr (y ffryt hi 'her form')
pennaf: penn (pen) — head, chief; superlative pennaf 'chief, principal' (Pennaf neges 'the chief errand')
keissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; verbal noun (keissaw dy welet ti 'seeking to see you')
pwll: scribal slip for Pwyll: Pwyll — proper name, the tale's hero; as a word, 'sense, discretion' (heb y Pwll 'said Pwyll')
oreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good', softened after a feminine noun (y neges oreu 'the best errand') · also soft as predicate after bu (yn gystal ac y bu oreu 'as good as he was best') · also soft-mutated (g lost) after yn (yn oreu yn y byt 'best in the world')
riannon: Riannon (Rhiannon) — proper name, daughter of Heueyd Hen
uerch: merch (merch) — daughter, girl; noun f., softened after a woman's name (Riannon uerch Heueyd 'Rhiannon daughter of Hefeydd') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uerch y urenhin 'as daughter to the king')
heueyd: Heueyd (Hefeydd) — proper name, Rhiannon's father, Heueyd Hen 'Hefeydd the Old'
hen: hen (hen) — old; adjective, as an epithet after a name (Heueyd Hen 'Hefeydd the Old')
hanwod: anuod (anfodd) — unwillingness; noun m., spelt with w for the v-sound, with h- after 'm 'my' (o'm hanwod 'against my will')
ydys: bot (bod) — to be; impersonal present 'it is being (done)' (a'm rodi y wr … yd ydys 'they are giving me to a husband')
mynneis: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 1 sg. preterite 'I wanted' (ny mynneis 'I did not want')
garyat: karyat (cariad) — love; noun m., soft-mutated after 'th 'your' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you') · also soft after gan 'with' (gan garyat a llywenyd 'with love and joy')
mynnaf: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 1 sg. present 'I want' (nys mynnaf 'I do not want him')
etwa: etwa (eto) — yet, still; adverb (nys mynnaf etwa 'I do not want him yet')
onyt: onyt (onid) — unless; conjunction (onyt ti a'm gwrthyt 'unless (it be) you (who) reject me') · also 'except, but' (un dyn yma onyt pedwar dyn 'one man here except four men')
gwrthyt: gwrthot (gwrthod) — to refuse, reject; 3 sg. present in -yt, the form a relative verb takes whatever its subject (ti a'm gwrthyt 'you (who) reject me')
deuthum: dyuot (dod) — to come; 1 sg. preterite 'I came' (e deuthum i 'I came')
caffwn: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I were to get' (pei caffwn dewis 'if I could have my choice')
dewis: dewis (dewis) — choice; to choose; noun/verbal noun (caffwn dewis 'I could have choice')
wraged: gwreic (gwraig) — woman, wife; noun f., plural gwraged, soft-mutated after holl 'all' (holl wraged 'all the women') · also soft after o 'of' (riuedi o wraged 'a number of women') and in address (A wraged 'O women') · also soft after am 'about' (am wraged 'about women') and after the numeral with the article (a'r pump wraged hynny 'and those five women', cause uncertain)
morynnyon: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden; noun f., plural morynnyon ('maidens')
dewisswn: dewis (dewis) — to choose; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive with the -ss- of the old s-forms, 'I would choose' (ti a dewisswn 'you (are the one) I would choose')
os: os (os) — if; conjunction of a real condition (os hynny a uynny 'if that is what you want')
uynny: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present 'you want', soft-mutated after a (a uynny 'that you want')
kyn: kyn (cyn) — before; with a verbal noun (kyn uy rodi 'before my being given') · also the equative particle 'as', softening the adjective (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy') · also 'although', with the subjunctive (Kyn ny bwyf arglwydes 'though I am not a lady') · also in kyn no hynny 'before that' (seith mlyned kyn no hynny 'seven years before that')
gwna: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. imperative 'make!, do!' (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me') · also 3 sg. present 'does, makes' after the particle y (ae guell y gwna neb 'is it better that anyone does'); no mutation shown
goreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good' (Goreu yw gennyf 'it is best with me' = I prefer)
mynnych: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may wish' (y mynnych ti 'that you may wish')
barawt: parawt (parod) — ready; adjective, soft-mutated after predicative yn (yn barawt 'ready') · also soft after the feminine noun cad (cad barawt 'ready for battle')
tric: trigyaw (trigo) — to stay, remain; 2 sg. imperative 'stay!' (tric yn iach 'stay in health', the farewell)
iach: iach (iach) — healthy, well; adjective (yn iach 'in health')
choffa: koffau (coffáu) — to remember, keep in mind; 2 sg. imperative koffa, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a choffa 'and remember')
gywiraw: kywiraw (cywiro) — to make true, fulfil; verbal noun, softened as the object of an imperative (coffa gywiraw dy edewit 'remember to fulfil your promise')
edewit: edewit (addewid) — promise; noun (dy edewit 'your promise') · also impersonal preterite of adaw 'to leave': 'was left' (yd edewit y gwyr hynny 'those men were left')
guahanu: gwahanu (gwahanu) — to part, separate; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethont (A guahanu a wnaethont 'and they parted'); no mutation
wnaethont: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (the 'verbal noun + a wnaethont' auxiliary construction: Bwyta a chyuedach a wnaethont 'they ate and feasted')
chwedleu: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, talk; noun f., plural chwedleu (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); ch- does not mutate here · also 'news, tidings' (Pa chwedleu yssyd yma? 'what news is there here?')
ereill: arall (arall) — other; plural ereill, the plural form of the adjective (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); modern eraill
trossei: trossi (trosi) — to turn, turn over; 3 sg. imperfect 'he would turn', of a habit (y chwedleu ereill y trossei ynteu 'he would turn to other tales'); a verb beside troi; no mutation after the particle y
odyna: odyna (oddi yna, oddyna) — from there, then, after that; adverb, od 'from' + yna 'there' (Odyna treulaw y ulwydyn 'then spending the year')
ganuet: canuet (canfed) — hundredth; ordinal, soft-mutated after possessive y/dy 'his/your' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen', literally 'on his hundredth horseman'; the idiom means a company of a hundred riders)
marchauc: marchawc (marchog) — horseman, rider; noun m., spelt -auc (ar y ganuet marchauc); base form
ryngtaw: rwng (rhwng) + ef — 'between him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., used in the idiom ryngtaw a 'between him and' = on his way to (Ef a aeth ryngtaw a llys Eueyd Hen 'he went his way to the court of Heueyd the Old') · also in its plain sense 'between him (and)' (gadu y ryngtaw ef a Guydyon 'leave it between him and Gwydion')
eueyd: Heueyd (Hefeydd) — proper name, Rhiannon's father; spelt Eueyd without the h- (Eueyd Hen 'Heueyd the Old') · also Eueyd Hir, Efeydd Hir, a messenger of Bendigeidfran in the Second Branch (Kyuodwch, Uanawydan uab Llyr, ac Eueyd Hir 'rise, Manawydan, and Efeydd Hir'); radical
uuwyt: bot (bod) — to be; impersonal preterite 'it was (been)' (llawen uuwyt wrthaw 'he was welcomed gladly', literally 'glad it was to him'), soft-mutated (b>u) after the fronted predicate llawen
llewenyd: llewenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (dygyuor a llewenyd 'a gathering and gladness')
arlwy: arlwy (arlwy) — provision, banquet, preparation of food; noun m. (arlwy mawr 'a great banquet'; y wled a'r arlwy 'the feast and the fare')
uaranned: maranned (marannedd) — wealth, stores, provisions; noun, collective; soft-mutated (m > u) after holl 'all' (holl uaranned y llys 'all the wealth of the court')
gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel') · also soft after wrth (Reit oed im wrth gynghor 'I could do with counsel') and after pa (a pha gynghor 'and what counsel')
treulwyt: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time or goods); impersonal preterite 'was spent' (holl uaranned y llys … y treulwyt 'all the court's provisions were spent'); no mutation after the particle y
kyweiryaw: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to set in order, make ready; verbal noun, spelt -yaw, fronted before a wnaethpwyt (Kyweiryaw y neuad a wnaethpwyt 'the hall was made ready')
wnaethpwyt: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; impersonal preterite 'was done', soft-mutated after a (a wnaethpwyt 'was done'), -pwyt as the impersonal ending
eistedyssont: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; 3 pl. preterite in -yssont 'they sat' (ual yd eistedyssont 'how they sat'); ss for s
enryded: anryded (anrhydedd) — honour, rank, dignity; noun f., spelt enryded (ual y bei y enryded 'according to his rank'); y 'his' gives no change before a vowel
kyuedach: kyuedach (cyfeddach) — carousing, a drinking-feast; noun m., base form (ar dechreu kyuedach 'at the start of the carousing')
gwineu: gwineu (gwinau) — auburn, chestnut-brown (of hair); adjective (guas gwineu 'an auburn-haired youth'); no mutation after a masculine noun
teyrneid: teyrneid (teyrnaidd) — kingly, princely, lordly; adjective, from teyrn 'king' + -eid (guas … teyrneid 'a lad of lordly bearing')
guisc: gwisc (gwisg) — garment, dress; noun, spelt gu for gw (a guisc o bali 'and a garment of brocade'); g- is not changed by a 'and'
gynted: kynted (cyntedd) — the upper end of a hall, where the lord and his chief guests sat (the modern sense 'porch' is later); noun m., soft-mutated (k > g) after y 'to' (y gynted y neuad 'to the upper end of the hall')
gedymdeithon: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; plural -on, soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (a'y gedymdeithon 'and his companions') · also soft as the complement after a verb (A bydwch gedymdeithon chwitheu 'and be companions, you also')
cressaw: croesaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m., spelt cressaw (Cressaw Duw wrthyt 'God's welcome to you')
eneit: eneit (enaid) — soul; used in address as an endearment 'dear one, my soul' (a dos y eisted, eneit 'and go to sit, friend')
eirchat: eirchat (eirchiad) — suppliant, petitioner, one who asks a boon; noun m. (eirchat wyf 'I am a petitioner')
erchi: erchi (erchi) — to ask, request, bid; verbal noun (y erchi it 'to ask of you')
dodwyf: dyuot (dod) — to come; old 1 sg. perfect 'I have come', beside the preterite deuthum (y erchi it y dodwyf 'I have come to ask of you'); the Red Book has dodwyf too
arch: arch (arch) — (1) request, boon, petition; noun f. (beth yw dy arch di 'what is your request'); (2) 2 sg. imperative of erchi 'ask!' (nac arch dim 'ask nothing')
erchych: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may ask' (Pa arch bynnac a erchych di ymi 'whatever request you may ask of me'); e- no change after relative a
gaffael: caffael (cael) — to get, obtain; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y 'it/its' (hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it')
itti: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition (y 'to' + ti), spelt itti (itti y byd 'you shall have it')
och: och (och) — alas; interjection of dismay (Och! heb y Riannon 'Alas, said Rhiannon')
rody: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 2 sg. present 'you give' (paham y rody di attep y uelly 'why do you give an answer so?'); no mutation after the particle y
uelly: uelly (felly) — thus, so, in that way; adverb, u for the v-sound (no mutation: f is its own first letter); often written y uelly with a particle y (attep y uelly 'an answer thus'; ac y uelly guare 'and so playing')
neus: neu + 's — the affirmative particle neu with the infixed object pronoun 's 'it' (Neus rodes y uelly 'he has given it so')
yg: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt yg before a g: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg gwyd = yng ngwyd 'in the presence of'; yg got = yng nghod 'in a bag', with c>ngh after yn 'in') · also before k-: yg kylch y ty 'around the house' (yng nghylch), the g being the trace of the nasal mutation (c>ngh)
gwyd: gwyd (gŵydd) — presence, sight; noun m., in the phrase yg gwyd 'in the presence of' (yg gwyd gwyrda 'in the presence of noblemen'), with the nasal mutation after yn written yg gwyd
garaf: caru (caru) — to love; 1 sg. present 'I love', soft-mutated after relative a (y wreic uwyaf a garaf 'the woman I love most')
kyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, base form (yd wyt yn kyscu heno 'you are to sleep tonight')
herchi: erchi (erchi) — to ask; verbal noun, with h-prefix after y 'her' (y herchi hi 'to ask her') · also with h- after eu 'their' (oc eu herchi 'by asking them')
darmerth: darmerth (darmerth) — preparation, provision; noun, paired with arlwy (y wled a'r arlwy a'r darmerth 'the feast and the banquet and the preparation')
ymma: ymma (yma) — here; adverb, spelling with mm (yssyd ymma 'is here')
kynhewi: kynhewi (cynhewi) — to fall silent, hold one's peace; verbal noun, fronted before a oruc (Kynhewi a oruc Pwyll 'Pwyll fell silent')
rodassei: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had given' (attep a rodassei 'the answer he had given')
taw: tewi (tewi) — to be silent; 2 sg. imperative 'be silent!, hush' (Taw, hyt y mynnych 'be quiet, as much as you like'); modern taw
uuscrellach: muscrell (mwsgrell) — feeble, inept, slow; comparative in -ach 'more feeble', soft-mutated (m > u) as the complement after ny bu (ny bu uuscrellach gwr 'there was never a more feeble man')
ssynnwyr: synnwyr (synnwyr) — sense, understanding, wits; noun m., spelt ss (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses')
nog: noc (nag) — than; comparative conjunction, spelt nog before ry (nog ry uuost ti 'than you have been')
uuost: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. preterite 'you were, you have been', soft-mutated after the perfective particle ry (ry uuost ti)
mynyssit: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, intend; impersonal pluperfect 'it had been intended' (y gwr y mynyssit uy rodi i idaw 'the man to whom it had been intended to give me'), with y the oblique relative
hanuod: anuod (anfodd) — displeasure, unwillingness; noun m., with h-prefix after the contracted 'm 'my' (o'm hanuod 'against my will') · also with h- after eu 'their' (oc eu hanuod 'against their will') · also with h- after y 'her' (o'y hanuod 'against her will')
guawl: Gwawl — proper name (Gwawl uab Clut), also gwawl 'light, radiance' as a common word; spelt guawl, no mutation as the subject (Guawl uab Clut)
uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uab y wr arall 'a son of another man'; yn uab y Pwyll 'a son of Pwyll') · also soft in apposition to a noun (uy nei, uab uy chwaer 'my nephew, son of my sister') and in address (Oy a uab Duw 'O son of God')
clut: Clud (Clud) — proper name, the father of Gwawl (Gwawl uab Clut); the name is spelt Clut
tormynnawc: tormynnawc — a rare word of disputed meaning, usually taken as 'with a great host, mighty' (as if from torf 'crowd'), but not certain; adjective after gwr (gwr tormynnawc, kyuoethawc)
kyuoethawc: kyuoethawc (cyfoethog) — wealthy, mighty, rich in dominion; adjective, from kyuoeth 'realm, wealth' + -awc (gwr … kyuoethawc 'a mighty man')
chan: can (can) — since, because; conjunction, spirant-mutated (k > ch) after a 'and' (A chan derw yt 'and since it has befallen you') · also the preposition can 'with, by' (= gan), spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chan hynn o wyrda 'and with these noblemen'; a chan pawb 'and by everyone')
derw: daruot (darfod) — to happen; derw = deryw, the old 3 sg. perfect 'it has happened' (a chan derw yt dywedut 'and since it has befallen you to say'); the Red Book also writes derw
yt: y 'to' — conjugated preposition, 2 sg. 'to you', modern iti, spelt yt beside itt and itti (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good'; rac anglot yt 'for fear of dishonour to you'; ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'; derw yt 'it has befallen you') · also yt (ŷd) 'corn, grain', noun m. (yr yt arall 'the other corn')
dywedeist: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. preterite 'you said' (y geir a dywedeist 'the word you said'), modern dywedaist
rac: rac (rhag) — before, lest, to prevent, for fear of; preposition (dyro ui idaw rac anglot yt 'give me to him to spare you dishonour') · also 'from' after verbs of saving (waret rac hynn 'to deliver from this')
allaf: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 sg. present 'I can', with g lost by soft mutation after ny (Ny allaf ui … 'I cannot') · also soft (g lost) after the particle a (minheu a allaf dy rydhau 'I for my part can free you')
uyth: byth (byth) — ever; with a negative, 'never'; adverb, soft-mutated (b>u) when used adverbially after the verb (dywedy di uyth 'you ever say'; na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'that he may never get me'; a uyd llawn dy got uyth 'will your bag ever be full')
chaffo: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may get', spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'that … not' (na chaffo ef uiui 'that he may not get me')
got: cot (cod) — bag, pouch; noun f., soft-mutated (c > g) after the article as a feminine noun (y got, a'r got), after dy 'your' (dy got), and as the object of a verb when separated from it (Mi a rodaf i'th law got uechan 'I will give into your hand a small bag')
uechan: bychan (bychan, bach) — small; feminine bechan, soft-mutated (b > u) after a feminine noun (got uechan 'a small bag')
eirch: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 3 sg. present 'asks, will ask' (ef a eirch y wled 'he will ask for the feast'), with ei for e in the 3 sg. present
wled: gwled (gwledd) — feast, banquet; noun f., soft-mutated after the article y as a feminine noun (y wled 'the feast'; y wled honno 'that feast')
niueroed: niuer (nifer) — company, host, number; noun m., plural niueroed (y wled y'r teulu a'r niueroed 'the feast to the household and the hosts')
amdanaf: am — conjugated preposition 'about me'; Amdanaf innheu 'as for me, for my part' (1 sg.)
genhyt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with you' (2 sg.), a variant spelling of gennyt (a'r got honn genhyt 'and this bag with you')
perllan: perllan (perllan) — orchard; noun f.; after the article it would normally be softened (y berllan, as written elsewhere), but here it stands unmutated (yn y perllan uchot 'in the orchard above')
uchot: uchod (uchod) — above, up there; adverb, spelt uchot (yn y perllan uchot 'in the orchard above')
uo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be', soft-mutated after phan 'when' (phan uo ef ar perued 'when he is in the middle of') · also soft-mutated after the relative a (llathen aryant a uo kyuref 'a rod of silver that may be as thick')
gyuedach: kyuedach (cyfeddach) — carousing; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (a'y gyuedach 'and his carousing') · also soft after the article, treated here as feminine (A'r gyuedach a dechreussant 'and the carousing they began'; dilit y gyuedach 'pursuing the carousing')
dyret: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 sg. imperative 'come!' (dyret titheu dy hun y mywn 'you come in yourself'); the ancestor of modern dere
reudus: reudus — a rare word of uncertain meaning, generally taken as 'ragged, shabby' from the beggar's disguise; adjective after dillat 'clothes' (dillat reudus amdanat 'ragged clothes about you'); the Red Book has the same word
amdanat: am — conjugated preposition 'about you' (2 sg.) (dillat reudus amdanat 'ragged clothes on you')
lloneit: lloneit (llonaid, llond) — a fill, as much as will fill; noun m. (lloneit y got o uwyt 'the bag's fill of food')
minheu: minheu (minnau) — I for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun, beside innheu (Minheu a baraf 'and I for my part will cause')
dottit: dodi (dodi) — to put; impersonal imperfect subjunctive 'were (it) put': the ending -hit, with d + h giving tt (bei dottit yssyd … o uwyt 'were all the food … put')
bydei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. habitual imperfect 'would be' (modern byddai) (na bydei launach no chynt 'it would not be fuller than before'); b is not changed after na
launach: llawnach (llawnach) — fuller; comparative of llawn, spelt launach, soft-mutated as the predicate after bydei (na bydei launach 'it would not be fuller')
byryer: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast; impersonal present subjunctive 'be thrown', after guedy (guedy byryer llawer yndi 'after much be cast into it')
llawer: llawer (llawer) — much, many; noun/adverb (guedy byryer llawer yndi 'after much has been thrown into it')
llawn: llawn (llawn) — full; adjective (a uyd llawn dy got ti uyth 'will your bag ever be full?')
dywet: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. imperative 'say!' (Dywet titheu 'you say')
ony: ony (oni) — unless, until; conjunction ('no, unless …'), causes spirant mutation of c, p, t (ony chyuyt 'unless there rise') · also with soft mutation of g (ony wybydaf i 'if I do not find out') · also 'if not' with the subjunctive (ony bei hagyr 'if it were not unseemly')
chyuyt: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 3 sg. present 'rises', spirant-mutated (k > ch) after ony 'unless' (ony chyuyt dylyedauc 'unless a nobleman rises')
chyuoethauc: kyuoethawc (cyfoethog) — mighty, wealthy; adjective, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after tra 'very' (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty')
guascu: gwasgu (gwasgu) — to press, tread down; verbal noun (a guascu a'y deudroet y bwyt 'and tread the food down with his two feet'); g not changed by a 'and'
deudroet: deudroed (deudroed) — two feet; deu 'two' + troed, the t softened (d) after deu (a'y deudroet 'with his two feet'); modern deudroed
digawn: digawn (digon) — enough, sufficient; adjective/noun (Digawn ry dodet ymman 'enough has been put here'; digawn yw hynny 'that is enough')
dodet: dodi (dodi) — to put; impersonal 'has been put', after the perfective particle ry (ry dodet ymman 'has been put here') · also impersonal preterite 'was put, was laid' after the relative a (Sef penyt a dodet erni 'this is the penance that was laid on her'; Sef enw a dodet arnaw 'the name that was given him') · also impersonal preterite after the particle y (wrth hynny y dodet ar y kymwt hwnnw 'for that reason it was put on that commote')
ymman: ymma (yma) — here; adverb, spelt ymman, with a final n (ry dodet ymman 'put here')
sseghi: senghi (sengi, sangu) — to tread, trample; verbal noun, spelt with ss for s and g for the ng sound (y sseghi y bwyt yn y got 'to tread the food in the bag'); compare ssenghi
el: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may go' (A phan el ef 'when he goes'; yny el ef dros y pen 'until he goes over the head')
tro: troi (troi) — to turn; 2 sg. imperative 'turn!' (tro ditheu y got 'you turn the bag')
glwm: clwm (cwlwm) — knot; noun m., soft-mutated (c > g) as the object directly after the imperative llad (llad glwm 'tie a knot')
garryeu: carrai (carrai) — strap, thong; noun, plural carryeu, soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'on' (ar garryeu y got 'on the straps of the bag')
bit: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperative 'let there be, let it be' (A bit corn canu da 'and let there be a good horn for blowing'; bit hynny yn arwyd 'let that be the signal'); modern bydded
corn: corn (corn) — horn; noun m. (corn canu 'a horn for blowing')
rwymedic: rwymedic (rhwymedig) — bound, tied; past participle in -edic of rwymaw (rhwymo) 'to bind'; rh- not softened after the predicative yn (yn rwymedic yn y got 'bound in the bag')
dot: dodi (dodi) — to put; 2 sg. imperative 'put!' (dot titheu lef ar dy gorn 'give a blast on your horn', literally 'put a cry')
lef: llef (llef) — cry, shout, blast; noun f., spelt lef, soft-mutated as the object of dot 'put' (dot lef 'give a cry')
arwyd: arwyd (arwydd) — sign, signal; noun m. (bit hynny yn arwyd 'let that be the signal')
rot: y rwng (rhwng) — between; y rot is the 2 sg. conjugated form 'between you', modern rhyngot (y rot a'th uarchogyon 'between you and your horsemen'), as y rof 'between me' in y rof i a Duw
uarchogyon: marchawc (marchog) — horseman, rider; plural marchogyon, soft-mutated after possessive 'th 'your' (a'th uarchogyon 'and your horsemen')
glywhont: clywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. present subjunctive 'they may hear', soft-mutated (c>g) after pan 'when' (pan glywhont llef dy gorn 'when they hear the blast of your horn')
diskynnent: disgyn (disgyn) — to descend, come down; 3 pl. imperative 'let them come down' (diskynnent wynteu am pen y llys 'let them come down about the head of the court')
madws: madws — a word of uncertain origin and exact force, generally taken as 'it is time, it is fitting'; predicate with oed (madws oed ymi cael attep 'it was time for me to get an answer')
ercheis: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 1 sg. preterite 'I asked' (am a ercheis 'for what I asked'), modern erchais
kymeint: kymeint (cymaint) — as much, so much, as great; noun/pronoun, kymeint ac 'as much as' (Kymeint ac a ercheist 'as much as you asked')
ercheist: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 2 sg. preterite 'you asked' (a ercheist 'that you asked'), modern erchaist
medyant: medyant (meddiant) — possession, power; noun m., base form (y'm medyant i 'in my possession')
darpar: darpar (darpar) — preparation, provision; noun m. (y wled a'r darpar 'the feast and the preparation') · also 'purpose, intention' (pa darpar oed yr eidaw 'what purpose was his'); after pa 'what' the soft mutation (d>dd) is not shown, d serving for both
rodeis: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 1 sg. preterite 'I gave' (hwnnw a rodeis i 'that I gave')
eidawaf: eidawaf — uncertain; it appears to be a 1 sg. present verb made from eidaw 'his, his own, property' (modern eiddo), 'I own (it)', a form not otherwise known (Hwnnw nit eidawaf y rodi y neb 'that is not mine to give to anyone'); the Red Book reads nyt adawaf i, from adaw 'leave, allow'
gwawl: Gwawl — proper name; also gwawl 'light'; subject of a verb, no mutation (Gwawl a gerdawd 'Gwawl went')
gerdawd: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, travel, go; 3 sg. preterite 'went', soft-mutated (c>g) after a (Gwawl a gerdawd ryngthaw a'y gyuoeth 'Gwawl went his way to his realm')
ryngthaw: rwng (rhwng) + ef — 'between him'; 3 sg. m. conjugated preposition, spelt with th (ryngthaw a'y gyuoeth 'on his way to his realm')
gwaul: Gwawl — proper name, a variant spelling Gwaul (Gwaul uab Clut)
annwn: Annwn — Annwfn, the realm of Arawn; proper name, in Penn Annwn 'Head of Annwfn' (Pwyll ynteu Penn Annwn); spelt Annwn here, Annwuyn in the first part (and in the Red Book here)
berllan: perllan (perllan) — orchard; noun f., soft-mutated (p>b) after the article as a feminine noun (y'r berllan 'to the orchard')
gorchymynnassei: gorchymyn (gorchymyn) — to command, instruct; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had instructed' (ual y gorchymynnassei Riannon idaw 'as Rhiannon had instructed him')
gwiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to put on, wear; verbal noun, fronted before a oruc (Gwiscaw bratteu trwm … a oruc Pwyll 'Pwyll put on heavy rags')
bratteu: brat (brat) — cloak, rag; noun m., plural bratteu, here the beggar's rags (bratteu trwm 'heavy rags')
trwm: trwm (trwm) — heavy; adjective (bratteu trwm 'heavy rags'), no mutation after a plural noun
ymdanw: am — conjugated preposition 'about him' (3 sg. m.); ymdanw is as the manuscript writes it, a slip or contraction for ymdanaw with the a omitted (the Red Book has ymdanaw); ym- is a spelling of am- (gwiscaw bratteu trwm ymdanw 'putting heavy rags about him')
chymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, put on; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymryt lloppaneu 'and putting on clouts')
lloppaneu: lloppan (llopan) — rough boot, shapeless footwear; noun, plural lloppaneu (lloppaneu mawr am y draet 'big rough boots on his feet')
draet: troet (troed) — foot; plural traet (traed), soft-mutated (t > d) after y 'his' (am y draet 'on his feet')
wedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, spelt without g, as in modern wedi (wedy bwyta 'after the eating'); the loss of g is a variant spelling, there is no clear softening word
wawl: Gwawl — proper name, g lost by soft mutation after y 'to' (kyuarch guell a wnaeth y Wawl 'greeted Gwawl')
gwraged: gwreic (gwraig) — woman, wife; noun f., plural gwraged (modern gwragedd) (a gwraged 'and women'; gwyr a gwraged 'men and women')
ro: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he give', in a wish after the particle a; r- shows no mutation (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good')
chraessaw: croesaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m., spelt craessaw, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' (a chraessaw Duw wrthyt 'and God's welcome to you')
negessawl: negessawl — having an errand, on an errand; adjective, neges 'errand' + -awl (Negessawl wyf wrthyt 'I have an errand to you')
craessaw: croesaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m., spelt craessaw (Craessaw wrth dy neges 'welcome to your errand')
gyuartal: kyuartal (cyfartal) — equal, fair, even; adjective, soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine noun arch (arch gyuartal 'a fair request')
erchy: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 2 sg. present 'you ask' (a erchy ymi 'that you ask of me')
kyuartal: kyuartal (cyfartal) — equal, fair; adjective used as a predicate, base form (Kyuartal, Arglwyd 'A fair (request), lord')
archaf: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 1 sg. present 'I ask'; the stem vowel is a (arch-), which becomes e in erchi (nyt archaf 'I do not ask'; Sef arch a archaf 'the request I ask')
didraha: didraha (didrahaus) — without arrogance, modest; adjective, di- 'without' + traha 'arrogance' (Arch didraha yw honno 'that is a modest request')
riuedi: riuedi (rhifedi) — number; noun (Riuedi mawr o sswydwyr 'a great number of officers')
sswydwyr: swydwr (swyddwr) — officer, servant of the court; plural swydwyr, spelt sswydwyr with ss for s (o sswydwyr 'of officers')
gyuodassant: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 3 pl. preterite in -assant 'they rose', soft-mutated (k > g) after the relative a (a gyuodassant y uynyd 'rose up'); plural by sense after a fronted noun of plural meaning
llenwi: llenwi (llenwi) — to fill; verbal noun (dechreu llenwi y got 'beginning to fill the bag')
uyrit: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast; impersonal imperfect 'was thrown', soft-mutated (b>u) after relative a (yr a uyrit yndi 'however much was thrown into it')
lawnach: llawnach (llawnach) — fuller; comparative of llawn, spelt lawnach (ny bydei lawnach no chynt 'it would not be fuller than before'); ll soft-mutated as the predicate after bydei
dotter: dodi (dodi) — to put; impersonal present subjunctive 'is put' (yr a dotter yndi uyth 'however much is put into it')
tir: tir (tir) — land, territory; noun m. (dylyedauc tir a dayar 'a lord of land and earth')
chyuoeth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm, wealth; noun m., spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyuoeth 'and realm')
ssenghi: senghi (sengi) — to tread, trample; verbal noun, ss for s (a ssenghi a'y deudroet y bwyt 'and tread the food with his two feet')
geimat: keimat — a word of disputed meaning, usually taken as 'champion, warrior' (compare later ceimiad), but uncertain; soft-mutated (k > g) after the vocative particle A 'O' (A geimat 'O champion')
kyuot: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 2 sg. imperative 'rise!' (kyuot y uynyd ar uyrr 'rise up quickly') · also kyuodi, verbal noun 'rising' in the short form kyuot (yn kyuot yn oreu 'rising best')
uyrr: byrr (byr) — short, brief; adjective used as a noun in ar uyrr 'at short notice, at once' (ar uyrr 'quickly'), soft-mutated (b>u) after ar 'on'
vab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., spelt vab (v for u), soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Gwawl vab Clut)
kyuodaf: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 1 sg. present/future 'I will rise' (Kyuodaf yn llawen 'I will rise gladly')
chyuodi: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (A chyuodi y uynyd 'and rising up')
dodi: dodi (dodi) — to put; verbal noun (dodi y deudroet yn y got 'to put his two feet in the bag'; dodi llef ar y gorn 'to give a blast on the horn')
gyflym: kyflym (cyflym) — swift; adjective, soft-mutated (k>g) after yn (yn gyflym caeu y got 'quickly shutting the bag') · also soft-mutated (k>g) after y in an adverbial phrase (y gyflym 'quickly')
caeu: caeu (cau) — to shut, close; verbal noun (yn gyflym caeu y got 'quickly shutting the bag')
clwm: clwm (cwlwm) — knot; noun m., base form (llad clwm 'to tie a knot'; compare glwm with soft mutation)
carryeu: carrai (carrai) — strap, thong; plural carryeu, base form after the article (ar y carryeu 'on the straps')
carchar: carchar (carchar) — prison; noun m. (yn y carchar e hun 'in his own prison': after y 'his' one would expect y garchar, as the Red Book has; the White Book's reading is uncertain)
bwrw: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast off; verbal noun (bwrw y bratteu 'casting off the rags')
loppaneu: lloppan (llopan) — rough boot; plural, written with l for ll (a'r loppaneu 'and the rough boots'); compare lloppaneu
yspeil: yspeil (ysbail) — spoil, booty; also gear, garments (yr yspeil didestyl 'the shabby gear', of Pwyll's disguise)
didestyl: didestyl — a rare word of uncertain meaning, probably 'shabby, unseemly', taken from the disguise; adjective after yspeil (yr yspeil didestyl)
mal: mal (fel) — as, like; conjunction (Ac mal y delei pob un 'and as each one came')
delei: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'would come, should come' (mal y delei pob un 'as each one came'; ual y delei 'as he came')
trawei: taraw (taro) — to strike, hit; 3 sg. imperfect 'would strike' (y trawei pob un dyrnawt ar y got 'each one would strike a blow on the bag')
gouynnei: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 3 sg. imperfect 'would ask' (y gouynnei 'he would ask'); g kept after the particle y
broch: broch (broch) — badger; noun m. (Broch 'badger', the cry in the game; guare broch yg got 'badger-in-the-bag')
medynt: medd (medd) — to say; defective verb, 3 pl. present 'say they' (medynt wynteu 'said they'), used after a quotation
chware: chware (chwarae) — play, game, sport; noun m. (Sef kyfryw chware 'such a game'; Pa chware 'what game')
taraw: taraw (taro) — to strike, hit; verbal noun, fronted before a wnai (taraw a wnai pob un dyrnawt 'each one would strike a blow')
wnai: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. imperfect 'would do', soft-mutated after a (taraw a wnai pob un 'each would strike')
ae: ae (ae) — either … or; correlative conjunction (ae a'e droet ae a throssawl 'either with his foot or with a staff'); no mutation · also interrogative particle 'is it that…?' (ae guell y gwna neb uy neges i wrthyt ti 'is it better that anyone does my errand to you…?')
droet: troet (troed) — foot; noun, soft-mutated (t>d) after possessive 'e 'his' (a'e droet 'with his foot')
throssawl: trossawl (trosol) — bar, stave, cudgel; noun, spirant-mutated (t > th) after a 'with' (ae a throssawl 'or with a cudgel')
guare: gware (chwarae) — to play, play with; verbal noun, spelt guare (guare a'r got 'to play with the bag'; guare broch yg got 'the game of badger in the bag') · also noun 'game, sport, trick' (y tremic hwnnw a'r guare 'that insult and the sport') · also as an object left unsoftened after the subject i (y dieleis i guare broch yghot 'I avenged the game of badger in the bag'; the Red Book gware)
ouynnei: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 3 sg. imperfect 'would ask', with g lost by soft mutation after relative a (a ouynnei 'who would ask')
wnewch: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 pl. present 'you do', soft-mutated after relative a (Pa chware a wnewch chwi 'what game do you play')
guarywyt: gware (chwarae) — to play; impersonal preterite 'was played' (y guarywyt broch yg got 'badger in the bag was played')
guarandawut: gwarandaw (gwrando) — to listen; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you would listen' (pei guarandawut uiui 'if you would listen to me')
dihenyd: dihenyd (dihenydd) — end, death, especially the death a man deserves; noun m. (nyt oed dihenyd arnaf uy llad y mywn got 'it was no fit death for me, to be killed in a bag')
euey: Heueyd (Hefeydd) — proper name, Rhiannon's father; Euey Hen is a scribal slip for Eueyd Hen, with the d omitted, kept as Evans prints it (the Red Book has eveyd hen)
guir: gwir (gwir) — truth, true; noun m., fronted object (guir a dyweit 'he speaks truth') · also predicate 'true' (Guir yw 'it is true')
dyweit: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 3 sg. present 'says' (guir a dyweit 'he tells the truth'); modern dywed
warandaw: gwarandaw (gwrando) — to listen; verbal noun, with g lost by soft mutation after y 'him/its' (Iawn yw yt y warandaw 'it is right for you to listen to him')
dihenyt: dihenyd (dihenydd) — end, death; spelt dihenyt with final t, in a sentence with no verb 'to be' (nyt dihenyt arnaw hyny 'that is no fit death for him')
hyny: hynny (hynny) — that; demonstrative pronoun, spelt hyny with one n, kept as written (the Red Book has hynny) (arnaw hyny 'on him, that')
perthyn: perthyn (perthyn) — to belong, pertain; 3 sg. present 'belongs', in perthyn ar 'to be the duty of' (y lle y perthyn arnat llonydu eircheit 'the place where it is your duty to satisfy petitioners')
llonydu: llonydu (llonyddu) — to quiet, content, satisfy; verbal noun (llonydu eircheit a cherdoryon 'to satisfy petitioners and minstrels')
eircheit: eirchat (eirchiad) — suppliant, petitioner; plural eircheit 'petitioners, beggars' (eircheit a cherdoryon 'petitioners and minstrels')
cherdoryon: kerdor (cerddor) — poet, minstrel, musician; plural kerdoryon, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a cherdoryon 'and minstrels')
gat: gadu (gadael) — to let, allow; 2 sg. imperative 'let!' (gat yno ef y rodi 'let him there give')
drossot: tros (tros) — over, for, on behalf of; conjugated preposition 'for you' (2 sg.), the form with d- being the regular spelling of this preposition with endings (drossot 'on your behalf')
gedernit: kedernit (cadernid) — strength, security, pledge; noun m., soft-mutated (k>g) as the object of chymer (chymer gedernit 'take a pledge')
ammouyn: ymouyn (ymofyn) — inquiry, claim, demand; noun m., spelt ammouyn (na bo ammouyn na dial 'that there be no claim or vengeance')
dial: dial (dial) — vengeance, revenge; noun m. (na dial uyth 'nor vengeance ever') · also verbal noun 'to avenge' after y 'to' (y dial Paluawt Branwen 'to avenge the Blow of Branwen'), softened, d spelling dd so the change does not show
gosp: cosp (cosb) — punishment; noun f., soft-mutated (c>g) after o 'of' (digawn yw hynny o gosp arnaw 'that is enough of a punishment for him')
geif: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. present 'will get', soft-mutated (c>g) after a (Ef a geif hynny 'he will get that')
kymmeraf: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, accept; 1 sg. present 'I will take', spelt mm (a'e kymmeraf 'and I will accept it')
kynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice; noun m., base form (Kynghor yw hynny 'that is counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel')
gynnym: gan — conjugated preposition 'with us' (1 pl.), spelt gynnym (kynghor yw hynny gynnym ni 'that is counsel with us' = 'we agree')
ueicheu: mach (mach) — surety, guarantor; plural meicheu, soft-mutated (m>u) as the object of the imperative keis (Keis ueicheu drossot 'find sureties for yourself')
uydwn: bot (bod) — to be; 1 pl. future 'we will be', soft-mutated (b > u) after the relative a (Ni a uydwn drostaw 'we will stand for him') · also 1 sg. imperfect, conditional 'I would be', soft-mutated after the particle a (mi a uydwn wrth dy gynghor 'I would be by your counsel')
drostaw: tros (tros) — for, on behalf of; conjugated preposition 'for him' (3 sg. m.) (drostaw 'on his behalf')
ryd: rhydd (rhydd) — free; adjective (yny uo ryd y wyr 'until his men are free') · also rhyd 'ford' in the place-name Melen Ryd, 'Yellow Ford' (y Uelen Ryd)
gollyngwyt: gollwng (gollwng) — to let go, release; impersonal preterite 'was released' (y gollyngwyt ef o'r got 'he was let out of the bag')
rydhawyt: rhyddhau (rhyddhau) — to free; impersonal preterite 'was freed' (y rydhawyt y oreugwyr 'his best men were freed')
oreugwyr: goreugwr — best man, chief man; noun m., goreu 'best' + gwr; plural goreugwyr, with g lost by soft mutation after y 'his' (y oreugwyr 'his best men')
gouyn: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 2 sg. imperative 'ask!' (Gouyn ueithon y Wawl weicheu 'ask Gwawl for sureties') · also verbal noun 'asking', g- lost by soft mutation after heb 'without' (heb ouyn 'without asking') and after y 'to' (y ouyn idaw 'to ask of him'); also in a gouyn a wnaeth 'asking he did'
ueithon: weithon (weithian) — now, by now, at this point; adverb, from gweith 'time' + hon 'this', softened as an adverb; written with u for w (Gouyn ueithon y Wawl weicheu 'now ask Gwawl for sureties')
weicheu: mach (mach) — surety; plural meicheu, soft-mutated (m > w, the v-sound written w) as the object of the imperative gouyn, separated from it (Gouyn ueithon y Wawl weicheu 'now ask Gwawl for sureties'); compare ueicheu
adwaenwn: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise; 1 pl. present/future 'we will know, we know' (Ni a adwaenwn y neb 'we know the one')
dylyer: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, ought; impersonal present subjunctive 'it be right, one ought' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'those whom one ought to take from him')
riuaw: riuaw (rhifo) — to count, reckon; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaeth (Riuaw y meicheu a wnaeth Heueyd 'Heueyd counted the sureties')
meicheu: mach (mach) — surety, guarantor; plural meicheu (Y meicheu a aeth 'the sureties went'), modern meichiau
llunnya: llunyaw (llunio) — to shape, devise, appoint; 2 sg. imperative 'devise!' (Llunnya dy hunn dy ammot 'devise your own agreement')
hunn: hun (hun) — self, own; spelt hunn (dy hunn 'your own self')
ammot: ammot (amod) — agreement, terms, condition; noun m. (llunnya dy ammot 'devise your terms'; yr ammot hwnnw 'that agreement')
llunnyawd: llunyaw (llunio) — to shape, devise; 3 sg. preterite 'devised' (ual y llunnyawd Riannon 'as Rhiannon devised')
briwedic: briwedic (briwedig) — wounded, bruised; past participle in -edic of briwo 'to break, bruise' (briwedic wyf i 'I am wounded')
chymriw: kymriw (cymriw) — injury, hurt; noun m., spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymriw mawr 'and a great injury')
ennein: ennein (ennaint) — bath; also ointment; noun m. (ennein yssyd reit ymi 'I need a bath')
reit: reit (rhaid) — need, necessity; noun m./f. (reit ymi 'need to me' = 'I need')
gannyat: kannyat (caniatâd) — leave, permission; noun m., soft-mutated (k>g) after possessive dy 'your' (gan dy gannyat 'with your leave')
adawaf: adaw (gadael) — to leave, let; also 'promise'; 1 sg. present with future sense 'I will leave'; a- is the radical, no mutation (a mi a adawaf wyrda drossof 'and I will leave noblemen on my behalf')
drossof: tros (tros) — for, on behalf of; conjugated preposition 'for me' (1 sg.) (drossof 'on my behalf')
ouynno: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may ask', with g lost by soft mutation after the infixed pronoun 'th (o'r a'th ouynno di 'of those who may ask you')
aethont: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. preterite 'they went', beside aethant (y'r bordeu yd aethont 'to the tables they went')
eistedyssant: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they sat', beside eistedyssont (ual yd eistedyssant 'as they sat')
eistedwys: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; 3 sg. preterite 'sat' (yd eistedwys paub y nos 'everyone sat that night')
paub: pawb (pawb) — everyone; pronoun, spelt paub with u for w (yd eistedwys paub 'everyone sat') · also left unsoftened after gan, which softens (gan paub 'by everyone'; the Red Book gan bawp)
digriuwch: digrifwch (digrifwch) — amusement, pleasure; noun m., spelt with u for f (drwy digriuwch 'in pleasure')
llonydwch: llonyddwch (llonyddwch) — quiet, ease, calm; noun m. (digriuwch a llonydwch 'merriment and ease')
lonydu: llonydu (llonyddu) — to content, satisfy; verbal noun, soft-mutated (ll > l) as the object of the verbal noun dechreu (a dechreu lonydu y kerdoryon 'and begin to satisfy the minstrels')
kerdoryon: kerdor (cerddor) — minstrel, musician; plural kerdoryon (y kerdoryon 'the minstrels')
ommed: gommed (gomedd) — to refuse, deny; 2 sg. imperative, with g lost by soft mutation after na 'do not' (na ommed neb hediw 'refuse no one today')
hediw: heddiw (heddiw) — today; adverb (na ommed neb hediw 'let no one be refused today')
uynno: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may wish', soft-mutated (m>u) after relative a (o'r a uynno da 'of those who want good things')
pheunyd: peunyd (beunydd) — daily, every day; adverb, spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (a pheunyd 'and every day')
parhao: parhau (parhau) — to last, continue; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may last' (tra parhao y wled honn 'while this feast lasts')
pheri: peri (peri) — to cause, command; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (a pheri dodi gostec 'and having a proclamation made')
gostec: gostec (gosteg) — proclamation, call for silence; noun f. (dodi gostec 'to make a proclamation')
dangos: dangos (dangos) — to show, make known; verbal noun (y erchi … dangos 'to bid (them) show themselves')
llonydit: llonydu (llonyddu) — to content, satisfy; impersonal imperfect in -it 'would be satisfied' (y llonydit pawb o honunt 'that each of them would be satisfied')
uod: bod (bodd) — pleasure, will, liking; noun m., soft-mutated (b>u) after possessive y 'his' (wrth y uod 'according to his pleasure') · also soft-mutated after o 'of' (nyt o uod y neb a uedei y llys 'not by the will of anyone who held the court')
uympwy: mympwy (mympwy) — whim, wish, fancy; noun m., soft-mutated (m>u) after possessive y 'his' (a'y uympwy 'and his fancy')
wnaethpwyd: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; impersonal preterite 'was done', soft after a (hynny a wnaethpwyd 'and that was done')
dreulwyt: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass; impersonal preterite 'was spent', soft-mutated (t>d) after relative a (Y wled honno a dreulwyt 'that feast was spent')
ommedwyt: gommed (gomedd) — to refuse; impersonal preterite 'was refused', with g lost by soft mutation after ny 'not' (ny ommedwyt neb 'no one was refused')
barhaud: parhau (parhau) — to last; 3 sg. preterite 'lasted', soft-mutated (p>b) after tra 'while' (tra barhaud 'while it lasted'; compare tra parhao with no mutation)
gychwynnaf: kychwyn (cychwyn) — to set out, start; 1 sg. present/future 'I will set out', soft-mutated (k>g) after a (mi a gychwynnaf 'I will set out')
auore: auore (yfory) — tomorrow; adverb (parth a Dyuet auore 'towards Dyfed tomorrow')
rwydhao: rwydhau (rhwyddhau) — to make easy, speed; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he speed', in a wish, soft-mutated (rh > r) after the particle a (Duw a rwydhao ragot 'may God speed you')
chyfnot: kyfnot (cyfnod) — appointed time, period, term; noun m., spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyfnot 'and a term')
kerdwn: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; 1 pl. present/future 'we will go' (y gyt y kerdwn 'together we shall go')
odymma: odyma (oddi yma) — from here; adverb, o 'from' + yma 'here', spelt odymma
ay: ay (ai) — is it?; interrogative particle (Ay uelly y mynny di 'is it so you wish?') · also ay … ay 'whether … or, either … or' (ay yma ay yn Ynys y Kedyrn 'whether here or in the Island of the Mighty') · also single ay 'whether' (e wybot ay gwir a dywedir 'to find out whether what is said is true')
mynny: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present 'you wish' (y mynny di 'that you wish') · also left unsoftened after cany 'since … not' (Cany mynny hynny 'since you do not want that'; the Red Book also mynny)
gerdassant: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, travel, go; 3 pl. preterite in -assant 'they travelled' (Wynt a gerdassant trannoeth parth a Dyuet 'they travelled next day towards Dyfed'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
attunt: at (at) + wynt — 'to them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (a doeth attunt 'came to them'); no mutation
edewis: adaw (gadael) — to leave, let go; 3 sg. preterite 'left', a>e by affection (Na gwr na gwreic o hynny nyt edewis Riannon 'not a man or woman of them did Rhiannon let go'); no mutation (vowel)
rod: rod (rhodd) — gift, present; noun f. (heb rodi rod enwauc idaw 'without giving him a gift of renown'); no mutation (object of a verbal noun; r- is written for rh-)
enwauc: enwawc (enwog) — renowned, famous; adjective, spelt -auc (rod enwauc 'a famous gift'); no mutation
gae: kae (cae) — fastening, clasp, brooch; noun m. (ae o gae 'whether of a clasp'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the preposition o 'of'
uodrwy: modrwy (modrwy) — ring, finger-ring; noun f. (ae o uodrwy 'or of a ring'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the preposition o 'of'
uaen: maen (maen) — stone; noun m. (ae o uaen guerthuawr 'or of a precious stone'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the preposition o 'of'
guerthuawr: gwerthuawr (gwerthfawr) — valuable, precious; adjective (maen guerthuawr 'a precious stone'); no mutation (follows a masculine noun; gu- is the manuscript's spelling of gw-)
llwydannus: llwydannus (llwyddiannus) — prosperous, successful; adjective (yn llwydannus 'prosperously'); no mutation (ll- is not mutated after predicative yn)
dryded: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal, feminine form tryded (trydedd) (Ac yn dryded ulwydyn 'and in the third year'); soft-mutated (t>d) as after the article y, which the White Book does not write here (the Red Book has yny dryded 'in the third')
dechreuis: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 sg. preterite 'began' (y dechreuis gwyr y wlat dala trymuryt 'the men of the land began to take sorrow'); no mutation after the particle y
dala: dala (dal) — to hold, seize, take on; verbal noun (dechreuis gwyr y wlat dala trymuryt 'the men of the land began to take sorrow'); no mutation · also with 'y 'her' before it (a'y dala hi 'and her being caught'; the sense of the clause is a little uncertain)
trymuryt: trymuryt (trymfryd) — heaviness of mind, sorrow; noun m., trwm 'heavy' + bryt 'mind', b softened inside the compound (dala trymuryt yndunt 'to grow heavy-hearted', literally 'to hold heaviness of mind in them'); no mutation
yndunt: yn (yn) + wynt — 'in them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (trymuryt yndunt 'sorrow in them'); no mutation
gerynt: caru (caru) — to love; 3 pl. imperfect 'they used to love' (gwr kymeint a gerynt 'a man so much as they loved'); a>e by affection; soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
harglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m. (a'e harglwyd 'and their lord'); h- prefixed to the vowel after the possessive e/eu 'their'
brawduaeth: brawduaeth (brawdfaeth) — foster-brother; noun m., brawt 'brother' + maeth 'nurture', m softened inside the compound (a'e harglwyd ac eu brawduaeth 'their lord and their foster-brother'; the Red Book has brawtuaeth); no mutation after eu 'their'
dietiued: dietiued (dietifedd) — without an heir, heirless; adjective, di- 'without' + etiued (yn dietiued 'without an heir'); the softening of d (dd) after predicative yn is not shown in the spelling
dyuynnu: dyuynnu (dyfynnu) — to summon, call; verbal noun (a'e dyuynnu attunt a wnaethont 'and they summoned him to them'); soft mutation (d>dd) after a'e 'his/him' is not shown, d being written for both
