doethont: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Sef lle y doethont y gyt 'this is where they came together'); -ont for -ant; no mutation after the particle y
bresseleu: Presseleu (Preseli) — proper name, the Preseli hills in Dyfed (y Bresseleu yn Dyuet 'to Preseli in Dyfed'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the preposition y 'to'
wdom: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 pl. present 'we know' (ni a wdom 'we know'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after the particle a
bydy: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. future 'you will be' (na bydy gyuoet ti a rei o wyr y wlat 'that you will not live as long as some of the men of the land'); no mutation after na
gyuoet: kyuoet (cyfoed) — of the same age, contemporary; adjective used as a noun (bydy gyuoet ti a rei 'you will be a contemporary with some', i.e. live as long as); soft-mutated (k>g) as the predicate directly after the verb
etiued: etifedd (etifedd) — heir; noun m. (na byd it etiued 'that you will have no heir', literally 'there will not be to you an heir'); no mutation (vowel)
kymmer: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 2 sg. imperative 'take' (kymmer wreic arall 'take another wife'); no mutation
ettiued: etifedd (etifedd) — heir; noun m., spelt with -tt- (y bo ettiued yt ohonei 'that there may be an heir to you from her'); no mutation (vowel)
ohonei: o (o) + hi — 'from her, of her'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. f. (ettiued yt ohonei 'an heir to you of her'); no mutation
byth: byth (byth) — ever, for ever; adverb (Nyt byth y perhey di 'you will not last for ever'); no mutation
perhey: parhau (parhau) — to last, endure; 2 sg. present with future sense 'you will last', a>e by affection (Nyt byth y perhey di 'you will not last for ever'; the Red Book has the same); no mutation after the particle y
kerych: caru (caru) — to love, wish; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may wish', the subjunctive after kyt 'though', a>e by affection (a chyt kerych di uot yuelly 'and though you may wish to be thus'); no mutation after kyt
yuelly: yuelly (felly) — thus, so, in that way; adverb, the particle y fused with uelly (a chyt kerych di uot yuelly 'though you wish it to be so'; Ac yuelly y gwnaethpwyt 'and so it was done'); no mutation
diodefwn: diodef (dioddef) — to suffer, endure, tolerate; 1 pl. present/future 'we shall bear' (nys diodefwn y gennyt 'we shall not bear it from you'); no mutation (d- unchanged after nys)
ettwa: ettwa (etwa, eto) — still, yet; adverb (nyt hir ettwa yd ym y gyt 'it is not long yet that we are together'); no mutation
damwein: damwein (damwain) — event, chance, mishap; noun, here masculine (y damwein hwnnw 'that event'; now f.) (llawer damwein 'many a chance'); no mutation
oedwch: oedi (oedi) — to delay, wait; 2 pl. imperative 'wait' (Oedwch a mi hynn hyt ym pen y ulwydyn 'wait with me until the end of the year'); no mutation
wnawn: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 pl. present/future 'we shall make' (ni a wnawn yr oet 'we shall make the appointment'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the particle a
bydaf: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. future 'I shall be' (ac wrth ych kynghor y bydaf 'and I shall be by your counsel'); no mutation after the particle y
cwbyl: cwbl (cwbl) — whole, complete; adjective/noun m., spelt cwbyl (kynn dyuot cwbyl o'r oet 'before the whole of the term came'); no mutation
mab: mab (mab) — son, boy; noun m. (mab a anet idaw 'a son was born to him'); no mutation (subject, fronted)
anet: geni (geni) — to be born; impersonal preterite 'was born' (mab a anet idaw 'a son was born to him'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after the relative a
ganet: geni (geni) — to be born; impersonal preterite 'was born' (ac yn Arberth y ganet 'and in Arberth he was born'); radical form after the particle y, no mutation
ducpwyt: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; impersonal preterite 'was/were brought' (y ducpwyt gwraged y wylat y mab 'women were brought to watch the boy'), -pwyt the impersonal ending; no mutation after the particle y
wylat: gwylat (gwylio) — to watch, keep watch; verbal noun (y wylat y mab 'to watch the boy'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to'
uam: mam (mam) — mother; noun f. (y mab a'y uam 'the boy and his mother'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive y 'his' · also soft-mutated (m>u) after un 'one' (un uam ac ef 'of one mother with him') and after the possessive 'e (o'e uam 'by his mother') · also soft after gan 'by, with' (gan uam y gilid 'with the other's mother')
mam: mam (mam) — mother; noun f. (a mam y mab, Riannon 'and the boy's mother, Rhiannon'); no mutation
hwech: chwech (chwech) — six; numeral, spelt hwech (riuedi o wraged hwech wraged 'a number of six women'); no mutation
gwylat: gwylat (gwylio) — to watch, keep watch; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethont (Gwylat a wnaethont wynteu dalym o'r nos 'they kept watch a while of the night'); no mutation
dalym: talym (talym) — a while, space of time; noun m. (dalym o'r nos 'a while of the night'); soft-mutated (t>d) as an adverbial object after the verb
eisswys: eissoes (eisoes) — yet, nevertheless, already; adverb, spelt eisswys (ac yn hynny eisswys, kyn hanner noss 'and in that, nevertheless, before midnight'); no mutation
noss: nos (nos) — night; noun f., spelt noss (kyn hanner noss 'before midnight'); no mutation
ohonunt: o (o) + wynt — 'of them, from them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (kyscu a wnaeth pawb ohonunt 'every one of them slept'); no mutation
thu: tu (tu) — side, direction; noun m. (a thu a'r pylgeint 'and towards the dawn', tu a 'towards'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
pylgeint: pylgeint (plygain) — the early hour before dawn, cockcrow; noun m. (a thu a'r pylgeint 'and towards the dawn-hour'); no mutation
deffroi: deffroi (deffro) — to wake, awaken; verbal noun (thu a'r pylgeint deffroi 'towards dawn, to wake'); no mutation
deffroyssant: deffroi (deffro) — to wake; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they woke' (A phan deffroyssant 'and when they woke'); the softening of d (dd) after pan is not shown in the spelling
dodyssynt: dodi (dodi) — to put, place; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had put' (y lle y dodyssynt y mab 'the place where they had put the boy'), -yssynt; no mutation after the particle y
neur: neur (no modern form) — perfective particle 'indeed, now', neu + ry, with a verb (neur golles y mab 'the boy is indeed lost'); causes soft mutation of the verb
golles: colli (colli) — to lose; here without an object, 'be lost'; 3 sg. preterite (neur golles y mab 'the boy has been lost'); soft-mutated (c>g) after neur (neu + the perfective ry) · also soft-mutated after yny 'until' (yny golles y deu 'until he lost the two', transitive)
bychan: bychan (bychan) — small, little, slight; adjective (bychan a dial oed 'it would be a small revenge'); no mutation
lloski: llosgi (llosgi) — to burn; verbal noun (yn lloski ni 'our burning (us)': yn is ein 'our', the possessive serving as object; the Red Book has an lloski); no mutation (ein 'our' does not soften)
dienydyaw: dienydyaw (dienyddio) — to put to death, execute; verbal noun (neu yn dienydyaw am y mab 'or our putting to death for the boy': yn = ein 'our'); no mutation
guraged: gwreic (gwraig) — woman, wife; noun f., plural gwraged (modern gwragedd), spelt guraged (heb vn o'r guraged 'said one of the women'); no mutation after the plural article r
gellast: gellast (gellast) — hound-bitch, large bitch; noun f. (Gellast yssyd yma 'there is a hound-bitch here'); no mutation
chanawon: cenau (cenau) — whelp, cub, puppy; noun m., plural cenawon, spelt canawon (a chanawon genti 'and whelps with her'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
genti: gan (gan) — 'with her'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. f., spelt genti (a chanawon genti 'and whelps with her'); no mutation
lladwn: lladd (lladd) — to kill; 1 pl. imperative (-wn) 'let us kill' (Lladwn rei o'r canawon 'let us kill some of the whelps'); no mutation
canawon: cenau (cenau) — whelp, cub, puppy; noun m., plural cenawon, spelt canawon (Lladwn rei o'r canawon 'let us kill some of the whelps'); no mutation after the plural article r
irwn: iraw (iro) — to anoint, smear; 1 pl. imperative (-wn) 'let us smear' (ac irwn y hwyneb hitheu Riannon a'r gwaet 'and let us smear Rhiannon's face with the blood'); no mutation
gwaet: gwaet (gwaed) — blood; noun m. (a'r gwaet 'and the blood'); no mutation
dwylaw: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., dual/plural dwylaw 'hands', from dwy llaw 'two hands' (a'y dwylaw 'and her hands'); no mutation
byrwn: bwrw (bwrw) — to cast, throw; 1 pl. imperative (-wn) 'let us throw', w>y by affection (a byrwn yr eskyrn gyr y bron 'and let us throw the bones beside her breast'); no mutation after a 'and'
eskyrn: asgwrn (asgwrn) — bone; noun m., plural eskyrn (modern esgyrn) (yr eskyrn 'the bones'); no mutation after the article
gyr: ger (ger) — near, beside; preposition, spelt gyr (gyr y bron 'beside her breast'; gyr llaw hwnnw 'beside that'); no mutation
bron: bron (bron) — breast; noun f. (gyr y bron 'beside her breast'); no mutation (y here is the possessive 'her')
thaerwn: taeru (taeru) — to insist, assert, maintain; 1 pl. imperative (-wn) 'let us insist' (a thaerwn arnei e hun diuetha y mab 'and let us insist against her that she herself destroyed the boy'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
diuetha: diuetha (difetha) — to destroy; verbal noun (arnei e hun diuetha y mab 'against her that she herself destroyed the boy'; a'e diuetha 'and destroying him'); no mutation
taered: taered (taeredd) — insistence, assertion, claim; noun m. (ni byd yn taered ni 'it will not be our assertion'); no mutation
chwech: chwech (chwech) — six; numeral (an chwech 'we six'); no mutation
trigwyt: trigyaw (trigo) — to stay, remain; impersonal preterite in -wyt 'it was stayed' (Ac ar y kynghor hwnnw y trigwyt 'and on that counsel they settled'); no mutation after the particle y
deffroes: deffroi (deffro) — to wake; 3 sg. preterite 'woke' (Riannon a deffroes 'Rhiannon woke'), -es; soft mutation after a not shown (d for dd)
yni: y (i) + ni — 'to us'; conjugated preposition, 1 pl., variant of ynni (na ouyn di yni y mab 'do not ask us for the boy'); no mutation
ohonam: o (o) + ni — 'of us, from us'; conjugated preposition, 1 pl. (Nyt oes ohonam ni namyn cleisseu 'there is nothing from us but bruises'); no mutation
cleisseu: clais (clais) — bruise, wound, hurt; noun m., plural cleisseu (cleisseu a dyrnodeu 'bruises and blows'); no mutation
dyrnodeu: dyrnawd (dyrnod) — blow, stroke; noun m., plural dyrnodeu (cleisseu a dyrnodeu 'bruises and blows'); no mutation
ymdaraw: ymdaraw (no modern form) — to strike one another, fight; verbal noun (yn ymdaraw a thi 'fighting with you'); no mutation
diamheu: diamheu (diamau) — certain, doubtless; adjective, di- 'without' + amheu 'doubt' (diamheu yw gennym 'it is certain to us'); no mutation
welsam: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 pl. preterite 'we saw' (na welsam eiroet 'we have never seen'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after na 'that ... not'
ynot: yn (yn) + ti — 'in you'; conjugated preposition, 2 sg. (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'); no mutation
thygyawd: tygyaw (tycio) — to avail, succeed; 3 sg. preterite in -awd 'it availed' (ny thygyawd ynni ymdaraw a thi 'it was no use to us to struggle with you'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after ny
ynni: y (i) + ni — 'to us'; conjugated preposition, 1 pl., spelt ynni (ny thygyawd ynni 'it did not avail us'); no mutation
diffetheeist: diffethaw (difetha) — to destroy; 2 sg. preterite 'you destroyed', -eist written -eeist (both the White Book and the Red Book have it; kept as written) (neur diffetheeist du hun dy uab 'you have destroyed your own son'); the softening of d (dd) after neur is not shown in the spelling
du: dy (dy) — your; 2 sg. possessive, written du here, a slip for dy (Evans prints du; the Red Book has dy hun) (du hun 'yourself'); causes soft mutation (none visible before h-) · also du 'black' (milgi bronwyn du pob un 'greyhounds, white-breasted, black each one'); a different word from dy 'your'
hawl: hawlyaw (hawlio) — to claim, demand; 2 sg. imperative 'claim' (ac na hawl ef ynni 'and do not demand him of us'); no mutation (h- is not mutable)
druein: truan (truan) — wretch; noun, plural truein 'wretches' (A druein 'O wretches', to the women); soft-mutated (t>d) after the vocative particle A
yrrwch: gyrru (gyrru) — to drive, send, put; 2 pl. imperative 'lay' (na yrrwch geu arnaf 'do not lay a lie on me'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after na (negative imperative)
geu: gau (gau) — false, falsehood; noun m. (geu arnaf 'a falsehood on me'); no mutation (radical form kept in the idiom gyrru geu ar)
arnawchi: ar (ar) + chwi — 'on you'; conjugated preposition, 2 pl., with the pronoun chwi attached (ouyn yssyd arnawchi 'there is fear on you'); no mutation
kyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — confession; noun f. (ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God'; the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); ym is taken as 'my', and the nasal mutation it brings (nghyffes) is not shown in the spelling
differaf: differu (no modern form) — to defend, protect, save; 1 sg. present/future 'I will protect' (mi a'ch differaf 'I will protect you'); no mutation (d- unchanged after the infixed ch 'you')
adwn: gadu (gadael) — to leave, allow, let; 1 pl. present/future 'we shall allow' (ny adwn ni drwc arnam 'we shall not let harm come on us'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after ny
drwc: drwc (drwg) — evil, harm, wrong; noun m. (ny chewch un drwc 'you will get no harm'); no mutation · also the adjective 'bad', as a fronted predicate (ys drwc a gedymdeith uuosti 'a bad companion you were')
arnam: ar (ar) + ni — 'on us'; conjugated preposition, 1 pl. (drwc arnam 'harm on us'); no mutation
hunein: hun (hun) — self; plural hunein (modern hunain) in ny hunein 'ourselves' (arnam ny hunein 'on ourselves'); pronoun/noun; no mutation · also 'themselves' (uyn teulu e hunein 'my warband themselves')
chewch: caffael (cael) — to get, obtain; 2 pl. present/future 'you will get' (ny chewch un drwc 'you will get no harm'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ny
wirioned: gwirioned (gwirionedd) — truth; noun, here feminine (now m.) (yr dywedut y wirioned 'for telling the truth'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the article y
dywettei: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 3 sg. imperfect 'she would say' (Yr a dywettei hi 'whatever she would say'), -ei; soft mutation after the relative a not shown (d for dd)
dec: tec (teg) — fair, pleasing; adjective (yn dec 'fairly'); soft-mutated (t>d) after predicative yn · also deg (deg) 'ten', written dec (teir llong ar dec 'thirteen ships', literally 'three ships on ten'); no mutation
druan: truan (truan) — wretched, pitiable; adjective (yn druan 'wretchedly'); soft-mutated (t>d) after predicative yn
chaffei: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. imperfect 'she would get' (ny chaffei namyn yr un atteb 'she would get nothing but the same answer'), -ei; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ny
atteb: atteb (ateb) — answer, reply; noun m. (yr un atteb 'the same answer'); no mutation (vowel)
chelu: celu (celu) — to hide, conceal; verbal noun (a chelu y damwein hwnnw 'and to hide that mishap'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
allwyt: gallu (gallu) — to be able; impersonal past 'it was possible' (ny allwyt 'it could not be done'), -wyt; soft-mutated (g>∅) after ny
chwedyl: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, report, rumour; noun m. (yd aeth y chwedyl 'the report went'; am y chwedyl 'about the story'); no mutation
phawb: pawb (pawb) — everyone; pronoun (a phawb o'r guyrda 'and everyone of the nobles'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
kigleu: klywet (clywed) — to hear; old 3 sg. preterite 'heard' (a phawb o'r guyrda a'e kigleu 'and every one of the noblemen heard it'); no mutation after a'e 'it'
wneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun (y wneuthur kynnadeu at Pwyll 'to send envoys to Pwyll', literally 'to make messengers'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to' · also soft after y 'its' (yn y wneuthur 'in the making of it'), the possessive standing for the object · also softened after dros (dros wneuthur 'instead of doing')
kynnadeu: kennat (cennad) — messenger, envoy; noun f. (also m.), plural kynnadeu (modern cenhadau; the Red Book has kennadeu) (y wneuthur kynnadeu at Pwyll 'to send envoys to Pwyll'); no mutation
yscar: ysgar (ysgaru) — to part, separate, divorce; verbal noun (yscar a'e wreic 'to part from his wife'); no mutation
gyflauan: kyflauan (cyflafan) — outrage, atrocity, deed of violence; noun f. (am gyflauan mor anwedus 'for so unseemly an outrage'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the preposition am · also soft-mutated after a in the adjective + a + noun construction ys anhebic a gyflauan … 'an unlikely outrage …' (compare Da a dwy ynys); the construction is uncertain
anwedus: anwedus (anweddus) — unseemly, indecent; adjective, an- + gwedus 'seemly' (mor anwedus 'so unseemly'); no mutation (vowel)
wnaethoed: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had done' (am gyflauan mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'for an outrage as shameful as that she had done'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the perfective particle ry: the letters ar y are best read a ry, relative a + ry (the Red Book has ac a wnathoed)
plant: plant (plant) — children; noun m. plural (na bydei plant idi 'that there would be no children to her'); no mutation
yscaraf: ysgar (ysgaru) — to part, separate; 1 sg. present/future 'I shall part' (Ac nyt yscaraf a hi 'and I shall not part from her'); no mutation
kymeret: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 sg. imperative 'let her take' (kymeret y phenyt amdanaw 'let her take her penance upon her'), -et; no mutation
phenyt: penyt (penyd) — penance, penalty; noun m. (y phenyt a gymerth 'she took her penance'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after the possessive y 'her'
dyuynnwys: dyuynnu (dyfynnu) — to summon, call; 3 sg. preterite 'summoned' (Hitheu Riannon a dyuynnwys attei athrawon 'Rhiannon on her part summoned teachers to her'), -wys; soft mutation after a not shown (d for dd)
athrawon: athro (athro) — teacher, master, learned man; noun m., plural athrawon (dyuynnwys attei athrawon a doethon 'she summoned to her teachers and wise men'); no mutation
doethon: doeth (doeth) — wise; adjective used as a plural noun, 'wise men' (athrawon a doethon 'teachers and wise men'; modern doethion); no mutation
degach: tec (teg) — fair, pleasant; comparative degach 'pleasanter' (yn degach genthi 'pleasanter to her'); soft-mutated (t>d) after predicative yn · also soft-mutated (t>d) after the noun wenith (wenith degach 'fairer wheat'); cause uncertain
ymdaeru: ymdaeru (no modern form) — to dispute, argue, contend; verbal noun (nog ymdaeru a'r gwraged 'than to contend with the women'); no mutation
penyt: penyt (penyd) — penance, penalty; noun m. (Sef penyt a dodet erni 'this is the penance that was laid on her'); no mutation
erni: ar (ar) + hi — 'on her'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. f., spelt erni (a dodet erni 'that was laid on her'); no mutation
mlyned: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; plural blyned (modern blynedd), spelt mlyned (hyt ym penn y seith mlyned 'until the end of the seven years'); nasal-mutated (b>m) after seith 'seven' · also nasal-mutated after ugeint 'twenty' in pedwarugeint 'eighty' (pedwarugeint mlyned 'eighty years')
yskynuaen: yskynuaen (esgynfaen) — mounting-block, a stone for mounting a horse; noun m., yskyn 'mount' + maen 'stone', m softened inside the compound (Ac yskynuaen a oed odieithyr y porth 'and there was a mounting-block outside the gate'); no mutation
odieithyr: odieithyr (oddieithr) — outside of; except; preposition (odieithyr y porth 'outside the gate'); no mutation
porth: porth (porth) — gate, gateway, entrance; noun m. (y porth 'the gate'); no mutation
beunyd: beunyd (beunydd) — daily, every day; adverb (eisted gyr llaw hwnnw beunyd 'to sit beside it daily'); no mutation
gwyppei: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might know' (a debygei nas gwyppei 'who thought that he did not know it'), -ei; no mutation (g- kept after nas)
gyffranc: kyfranc (cyfranc) — story, account, adventure; noun, here feminine (y gyffranc oll 'the whole story'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the article y
kynnic: kynnic (cynnig) — to offer; verbal noun (kynnic y westei 'to offer to the guest'); no mutation
westei: gwestei (gwestai) — guest, visitor; noun m. (kynnic y westei 'to offer to the guest'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to'
phellynic: pellennic (pellennig) — stranger, one from afar; noun m. (a phellynic 'and to the stranger'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
cheuyn: keuyn (cefn) — back; noun m. (ar y cheuyn 'on her back'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the possessive y 'her'
gadei: gadu (gadael) — to leave, allow; 3 sg. imperfect 'would allow' (y gadei yr un y dwyn 'one would allow her to bear him'), -ei; no mutation after the particle y
talym: talym (talym) — a while, space of time; noun m. (treulaw talym o'r ulwydyn 'spending a while of the year'); no mutation (object of a verbal noun)
teirnon: Teirnon (Teyrnon) — proper name, lord of Gwent Is Coed (Teirnon Twryf Uliant); no mutation
twryf: twrf (twrf) — noise, din, tumult; noun m., spelt twryf in the epithet Twryf Uliant 'tumult of flood' (Teirnon Twryf Uliant); no mutation
uliant: Uliant — second element of the epithet Teirnon Twryf Uliant (English Twrf Liant), usually taken as lliant 'flood, sea'; the u- of the spelling is not explained; meaning uncertain; no mutation
ty: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m. (yn y ty yd oed cassec 'in the house was a mare'); no mutation · also 'you', emphatic 2 sg. pronoun after the verb (yd wyt ty yndaw 'you are in it')
cassec: caseg (caseg) — mare; noun f., spelt cassec (yd oed cassec 'there was a mare'); no mutation (subject of the clause)
chassec: caseg (caseg) — mare; noun f., spelt cassec (na march na chassec degach no hi 'neither horse nor mare fairer than she'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'nor'
phob: pob (pob) — every, each; adjective (a phob nos Calanmei 'and every May-eve'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
calanmei: Calan Mai (Calan Mai) — May Day, the first of May (nos Calanmei 'May-eve'); noun m., calan 'first day of the month' + Mai; no mutation
moei: moi (no modern form) — to foal (of a mare); 3 sg. imperfect habitual 'she used to foal' (a phob nos Calanmei y moei 'and every May-eve she would foal'), -ei; no mutation after the particle y
wybydei: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. imperfect 'knew' (ny wybydei neb un geir 'no one knew a word'), -ei; soft-mutated (g>∅) after ny
hebawl: ebawl (ebol) — foal; noun m. (wrth y hebawl 'about her foal'); h- prefixed to the vowel after the possessive y 'her'
nosweith: nosweith (noswaith) — evening, night; noun f. (ymdidan nosweith a'y wreic 'conversing one evening with his wife'); no mutation
llibin: llibin (llibin) — feeble, wretched, miserable; adjective (llibin yd ym pob blwydyn 'wretched it is that we are every year'); no mutation
heppil: eppil (epil) — offspring, brood; noun m. (yn gadu heppil yn cassec 'losing the offspring of our mare'); h- prefixed to the vowel after yn = ein 'our'
gaffel: caffael (cael) — to get; verbal noun (heb gaffel yr un o honunt 'without getting one of them'); soft-mutated (c>g) after heb 'without'
ellir: gallu (gallu) — to be able; impersonal present 'one can' (Peth a ellir wrth hynny? 'what can be done about that?'), -ir, a>e by affection; soft-mutated (g>∅) after the relative a · also softened after cany 'since not' (cany ellir 'since it cannot be done')
wybydaf: gwybot (gwybod) — to know, find out; 1 sg. present with future sense 'I find out' (ony wybydaf i pa dileith yssyd 'if I do not find out what destruction it is'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after ony · also soft after the particle a (mi a wybydaf beth yw 'I will know what it is')
dileith: dileith (dilaith) — destruction, ruin, a destroying thing; noun; a rare word, exact sense uncertain (pa dileith yssyd yn dwyn yr ebolyon 'what destruction it is that carries off the foals'); the softening of d (dd) after pa is not shown
ebolyon: ebawl (ebol) — foal; noun m., plural ebolyon (yr ebolyon 'the foals'); no mutation
peri: peri (peri) — to cause, make, have (something done); verbal noun, fronted before a wnaeth (Peri dwyn y gassec y mywn ty a wnaeth 'he had the mare brought into the house'); no mutation
gassec: caseg (caseg) — mare; noun f., soft-mutated (c>g) after the article y (dwyn y gassec 'to bring the mare')
moi: moi (no modern form) — to foal (of a mare); verbal noun, carrying the narrative with its subject after it (moi y gassec ar ebawl mawr 'the mare foaled a big foal'); no mutation
ebawl: ebawl (ebol) — foal; noun m. (ar ebawl mawr 'a great foal'; yr ebawl 'the foal'); no mutation (vowel)
telediw: telediw (no modern form) — handsome, well made, comely; adjective (ebawl mawr telediw 'a big, handsome foal'); no mutation after a masculine noun
seuyll: seuyll (sefyll) — to stand; verbal noun (yn seuyll yn y lle 'standing at once'); no mutation
prafter: praffter (praffter) — thickness, stoutness; noun m., spelt with one f (edrych ar prafter yr ebawl 'looking at the stoutness of the foal'); the soft mutation after ar (brafter) is not written (the Red Book also has ar praffter)
twrwf: twrf (twrf) — noise, din, tumult; noun m., spelt twrwf (ef a glywei twrwf mawr 'he heard a great noise'); no mutation (object)
grauanc: crafanc (crafanc) — claw, talon; noun f. (llyma grauanc uawr 'behold a great claw'); soft-mutated (c>g) after llyma
uawr: mawr (mawr) — great, big; adjective (grauanc uawr 'a great claw'); soft-mutated (m>u) after a feminine noun · also predicative, soft-mutated directly after the verb (nyt oed uawr y weilgi 'the sea was not great') · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after yn in the adverbial yn uawr 'greatly'
fenestyr: ffenestyr (ffenestr) — window; noun f., from Latin fenestra, f written for ff (drwy fenestyr 'through a window'; the Red Book has ffenestyr); no mutation (ff- is not mutable)
ymauael: ymauael (ymafael) — to seize hold, grasp; verbal noun (yn ymauael a'r ebawl 'seizing the foal'); no mutation
uwng: mwng (mwng) — mane; noun m. (geir y uwng 'by its mane'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive y 'its'
tynnu: tynnu (tynnu) — to draw, pull; verbal noun (tynnu cledyf 'to draw a sword'); no mutation
cledyf: cledyf (cleddyf) — sword; noun m. (tynnu cledyf 'to draw a sword'); no mutation (object of a verbal noun)
tharaw: taraw (taro) — to strike; verbal noun (a tharaw y ureich 'and to strike off the arm'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
not: nod (nod) — mark, point, notch; noun m. (o not yr elin 'at the joint of the elbow'); no mutation
elin: elin (elin) — elbow; noun f. (yr elin 'the elbow'); no mutation (vowel)
diskyr: diskyr (disgyr) — scream, shriek, outcry; noun m. (twrwf, a diskyr a gigleu 'a noise and a scream he heard'); no mutation
gigleu: klywet (clywed) — to hear; old 3 sg. preterite 'heard' (a diskyr a gigleu 'and a scream he heard'; yny gigleu 'until he heard'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the relative a or after yny · also 1 sg. 'I heard' (mi a gigleu 'I have heard')
agori: agori (agor) — to open; verbal noun (Agori y drws a oruc ef 'he opened the door'); no mutation
drws: drws (drws) — door; noun m. (y drws 'the door'); no mutation
ruthyr: ruthyr (rhuthr) — rush, charge; noun m. (dwyn ruthyr yn ol y twrwf 'to make a rush after the noise'; Ruthyr a duc 'he made a rush'); no mutation
tywyllet: tywyll (tywyll) — dark; equative tywyllet 'as dark', used as a noun of degree after rac (rac tywyllet y nos 'because of how dark the night was'); no mutation
duc: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry, take; 3 sg. preterite 'took' (Ruthyr a duc 'he made a rush', literally 'a rush he took'); no mutation shown after a (d for dd)
cof: cof (cof) — memory, mind; noun m. (A dyuot cof idaw 'and it came to his mind'); no mutation
adaw: adaw (gadael) — to leave; verbal noun, a form without g- (A dyuot cof idaw adaw y drws yn agoret 'and he remembered leaving the door open'); no mutation
agoret: agoret (agored) — open; adjective, past participle in -et (yn agoret 'open'); no mutation (vowel)
ymhwelut: ymchwelut (ymchwelyd) — to turn back, return; verbal noun, hw written for chw (the Red Book has ymchoelut), fronted before a wnaeth (ymhwelut a wnaeth 'he turned back'); no mutation
llenn: llen (llen) — cloth, mantle, covering; noun f., spelt llenn (guedy troi llenn o bali 'having wrapped a cloth of brocade'); no mutation (object of a verbal noun)
gylch: kylch (cylch) — circle, circuit, surrounding; noun m. (yn y gylch 'about him'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the possessive y 'his' · also soft after 'th 'your' (i'th gylch 'around you')
gryf: cryf (cryf) — strong; adjective (yn gryf 'strong'); soft-mutated (c>g) after predicative yn
cayat: cayat (caead) — fastening, bar, lid; noun m. (Dodi cayat ar y drws 'to put a bar on the door'); no mutation
gyskeis: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; 1 sg. preterite 'I slept' (Mi a gyskeis 'I slept'), -eis; soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
doethost: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 sg. preterite 'you came' (pan doethost ti y mywn 'when you came in'), -ost; no mutation
deffroeis: deffroi (deffro) — to wake; 1 sg. preterite 'I woke' (mi a deffroeis 'I woke'), -eis; soft mutation after a not shown (d for dd)
dadyl: dadl (dadl) — account, matter, discourse, dispute; noun f., spelt dadyl (menegi y dadyl oll 'to tell the whole matter'); soft mutation after the article y not shown (d for dd)
llen: llen (llen) — cloth, mantle, covering; noun f. (Llen o bali 'a cloth of brocade'); no mutation
dynnyon: dyn (dyn) — person; noun m., plural dynnyon (modern dynion) 'people' (Mab y dynnyon mwyn yw 'he is a son of gentle folk', y 'to'); the softening of d (dd) after y 'to' is not shown
didanwch: didanwch (didanwch) — comfort, solace; noun m. (digrifwch a didanwch 'delight and solace'); no mutation
mynnut: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you should wish' (bei mynnut ti 'if you wished'), -ut; no mutation
dygwn: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I would bring' (mi a dygwn wraged yn un a mi 'I would bring women along with me'), -wn; soft mutation after a not shown (d for dd)
dywedwn: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I would say' (ac a dywedwn uy mot y ueichawc 'and I would say that I was pregnant'), -wn; soft mutation after a not shown (d for dd)
mot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, nasal-mutated (b>m) after the possessive uy 'my' (uy mot y ueichawc 'my being pregnant')
ueichawc: beichawc (beichiog) — pregnant, burdened; adjective (uy mot y ueichawc 'that I was pregnant'); soft-mutated (b>u) after the predicative particle y (yn) · also soft after bei (phy na bei ueichawc hi 'and if she were not pregnant'), as the complement after the verb
myui: mi (myfi) — I, me; 1 sg. emphatic independent pronoun (Myui a duunaf a thi 'I shall agree with you'); no mutation
duunaf: duunaw (no modern form) — to agree, be of one mind (dy- + un 'one'); 1 sg. present with future sense 'I will agree' (Myui a duunaf a thi yn llawen 'I will gladly agree with you'); the softening of d (dd) after a is not shown
gwnaethpwyt: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; impersonal preterite 'was done' (Ac yuelly y gwnaethpwyt 'and so it was done'), -pwyt; no mutation after the particle y
bedydyaw: bedydyaw (bedyddio) — to baptize; verbal noun (Peri a wnaethont bedydyaw y mab 'they had the boy baptized'); no mutation
bedyd: bedyd (bedydd) — baptism; noun m. (o'r bedyd a wneit yna 'with the baptism that was done then'); no mutation after the article r
wneit: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; impersonal imperfect 'was being done' (o'r bedyd a wneit yna 'with the baptism that was then done'), -it; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
gwri: Gwri (Gwri) — proper name, the child's first name, in Gwri Wallt Euryn 'Gwri Golden-Hair'; no mutation
wallt: gwallt (gwallt) — hair; noun m. (Gwri Wallt Euryn 'Gwri Golden-Hair'; o wallt 'of hair'); soft-mutated (gw>w) as an epithet after the name, and after the preposition o 'of'
euryn: euryn (eurin) — golden; adjective, from eur 'gold' (Gwri Wallt Euryn 'Gwri Golden-Hair'); no mutation
ben: pen (pen) — head; noun m. (ar y ben 'on his head'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the possessive y 'his' · also soft-mutated (p>b) after o 'from' (o ben yr orssed 'from the top of the mound')
kyuelynet: melyn (melyn) — yellow; equative kyuelynet 'as yellow (as)', kyf- + melyn softened (m>f, written u) + -et (kyuelynet oed a'r eur 'it was as yellow as the gold'); adjective; no mutation
meithryn: meithryn (meithrin) — to nurse, foster, rear; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethpwyt (Meithryn y mab a wnaethpwyt 'the boy was reared'); no mutation
ulwyd: blwyd (blwydd) — year (of age); noun f. (yny oed ulwyd 'until he was a year old'; cynn y ulwyd 'before his first year'); soft-mutated (b>u) as the predicate directly after oed, and after the possessive y 'his'
breiscach: breisc (breisg) — stout, bulky, robust; comparative breiscach 'stouter' (breiscach oed no mab teir blwyd 'he was stouter than a boy of three years'); no mutation after a 'and'
teir: tair (tair) — three; numeral, feminine form teir (mab teir blwyd 'a boy of three years'); no mutation
blwyd: blwydd (blwydd) — year (of age); noun f., the form used after numerals (teir blwyd 'three years old'); no mutation
dwf: twf (twf) — growth, stature; noun m. (a uei uawr y dwf a'e ueint 'that was big in his growth and his size'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the possessive y 'his' · also soft-mutated (t>d) in yn un dwf 'in one growth', where un 'one, the same' in close compound softens even a masculine noun (compare unfryd)
ueint: maint (maint) — size; noun m. (a'e ueint 'and his size'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive e 'his' · also soft after can 'with' (a chan ueint y twrwf 'and with the size of the noise')
magwyt: magu (magu) — to rear, bring up; impersonal preterite 'was reared' (y magwyt y mab 'the boy was reared'), -wyt; no mutation after the particle y
ureisket: breisc (breisg) — stout, bulky; equative ureisket 'as stout as' (kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six years'); soft-mutated (b>u) after the equative cyn
chweblwyd: chweblwydd (chwe blwydd) — six years old; compound of chwe 'six' + blwydd (mab chweblwyd 'a boy of six years'); adjective/noun; no mutation
pedwyryd: pedwerydd (pedwerydd) — fourth; ordinal (pen y pedwyryd ulwydyn 'the end of the fourth year'); no mutation
ymoprau: ymoprau (no modern form) — to bargain, strive, coax, apparently from gobr 'reward' (cf. ymobryn); verbal noun (yd oed yn ymoprau a gueisson y meirch 'he was coaxing the grooms'; the Red Book has the same); meaning uncertain; no mutation
adu: gadu (gadael) — to leave, let, allow; verbal noun (am y adu o'e dwyn y'r dwuyr 'for his being allowed to take them to the water'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after the possessive y 'his'
dwuyr: dwuyr (dŵr) — water; noun m. (y'r dwuyr 'to the water'); no mutation after the article
differeist: differu (no modern form) — to defend, protect, save; 2 sg. preterite 'you saved' (yr ebawl a differeist ti 'the foal that you saved'), -eist; soft mutation after a not shown (d for dd)
keueist: caffael (cael) — to get; 2 sg. preterite 'you got' (y noss y keueist y mab 'the night you got the boy'), -eist; no mutation after the particle y
gorchymynneis: gorchymyn (gorchymyn) — to command, charge, entrust; 1 sg. preterite 'I charged' (Mi a'e gorchymynneis y weisson y meirych 'I entrusted it to the grooms of the horses'), -eis; no mutation
weisson: gwas (gwas) — lad, servant, groom; noun m., plural gweisson (y weisson y meirych 'to the grooms of the horses'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to' (and after at) · also soft as predicate after bot (hyt ban uuant weisson mawr 'until they were big lads')
meirych: march (march) — horse; noun m., plural meirch, spelt meirych (y weisson y meirych 'the grooms of the horses'); no mutation
synnyaw: synnyaw (synio) — to heed, take note of, look after; verbal noun (a ercheis synnyaw wrthaw 'and bade (them) look after it'); no mutation
ponyt: ponyt (ponid) — 'is it not?', negative question particle, pony with t before a vowel (Ponyt oed da iti 'would it not be well for you'); no mutation
hywedu: hywedu (hyweddu) — to tame, break in; verbal noun from hywed 'tame' (peri y hywedu 'to have it broken in'); no mutation
kanys: kanys (canys) — because, for, since; conjunction (Kanys y noss y keueist y mab 'for the night you got the boy'); no mutation · also for kan 'since' + nys 'not … it' (Kanys gollyngy yr hynny 'since you will not release it for that'; the Red Book Kan nys gollynghy); radical after the infixed 's
adaf: adaw (gadael) — to leave, allow; 1 sg. present with future sense 'I leave' (Mi a adaf y ti y rodi idaw 'I leave it to you to give it to him'); no mutation (a- is the verb's own first letter)
rodet: rodi (rhoi) — to give; impersonal preterite 'was given' (Y rodet y march y'r mab 'the horse was given to the boy'), -et; no mutation after the particle y
deuth: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. preterite 'came' (ac y deuth hi at y guastrodyon 'and she came to the grooms'), spelt deuth beside doeth; no mutation after the particle y
guastrodyon: gwastrawd (gwastrawd) — groom, stable-hand; noun m., plural gwastrodyon (modern gwastrodion), spelt guastrodyon (at y guastrodyon 'to the grooms'); no mutation after the plural article
orchymyn: gorchymyn (gorchymyn) — to command, charge; verbal noun, spelt without g- (y orchymyn synyeit wrth y march 'to charge that care be taken of the horse'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after the preposition y 'to'
synyeit: synnyaw (synio) — to heed, look after; synyeit is either a verbal-noun form beside synnyaw or the impersonal imperfect 'that heed be taken'; form uncertain (y orchymyn synyeit wrth y march 'to command heed of the horse'; the Red Book has synnyeit ar y march); no mutation
hywed: hywed (hywedd) — tame, broken in; adjective (a'e uot yn hywed 'and its being broken in'); no mutation (h- is not mutable)
elei: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'would go' (erbyn pan elei y mab y uarchogaeth 'by the time the boy would go to ride'), -ei; no mutation
uarchogaeth: marchogaeth (marchogaeth) — to ride; verbal noun (y uarchogaeth 'to ride'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the preposition y 'to'
emysc: emysc (ymysg) — among, amid; preposition (Emysc hynny 'meanwhile', literally 'amid that'); no mutation
glywssont: klywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. preterite 'they heard' (wynt a glywssont chwedlydyaeth 'they heard a report'), -ssont; soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
chwedlydyaeth: chwedlydyaeth (no modern form) — report, tale-telling, rumour; noun f. (a glywssont chwedlydyaeth y wrth Riannon 'they heard a report about Rhiannon'); no mutation
phoen: poen (poen) — pain, torment, punishment; noun f./m. (am y phoen 'for her pain'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after the possessive y 'her'
douot: douot (dofod) — something found, a find; here the foundling; noun m. (o achaws y douot a gawssei 'because of the find he had come by'); no mutation
gawssei: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. pluperfect 'he had got' (y douot a gawssei 'the doubt he had got'), -ssei; soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
amouyn: amouyn (amofyn) — to ask about, inquire; verbal noun (amouyn yn lut ymdanaw 'asking about it persistently'); no mutation
lut: glut (glud) — tenacious, persistent; adjective (amouyn yn lut 'asking persistently'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after adverbial yn; rare, meaning uncertain
ymdanaw: am (am) + ef — 'about him/it'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt ymdanaw (amouyn yn lut ymdanaw 'inquiring secretly about it'); no mutation
lawer: llawer (llawer) — many, much; pronoun/noun m. (gan lawer o luossogrwyd 'by many of the multitude'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition gan
luossogrwyd: lluosogrwydd (lluosogrwydd) — multitude, great number; noun m. (o luossogrwyd 'of a multitude'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition o 'of'
mynychu: mynychu (mynychu) — to do often, frequent, repeat; verbal noun (mynychu cwynaw 'to complain often'); no mutation
cwynaw: cwynaw (cwyno) — to lament, complain; verbal noun (mynychu cwynaw truanet damwein Riannon 'often lamenting the wretchedness of Rhiannon's mishap'); no mutation
truanet: truan (truan) — wretched; equative truanet 'how wretched', used as an exclamatory noun of degree (cwynaw truanet damwein Riannon 'lamenting how wretched was the plight of Rhiannon'); no mutation
graf: craf (craff) — keen, sharp, intent; adjective, spelt graf (edrych ar y mab yn graf 'to look intently at the boy'); soft-mutated (c>g) after predicative yn · also craf (craff) 'grip, hold', noun m. (ny caei graf 'he could get no grip'); soft-mutated (c>g) as object of a negative verb
chael: caffael (cael) — to get, find; verbal noun (A chael yn y uedwl 'and finding in his mind'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no chael iawn 'than getting redress')
gueledigaeth: gweledigaeth (gweledigaeth) — sight, appearance, vision; noun f. (yn herwyd gueledigaeth 'by appearance'); no mutation
that: tad (tad) — father; noun m., spelt tat (mab a that 'a son and a father'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
debycket: tebyc (tebyg) — like, similar; equative debycket 'as like' (kyn debycket a'r mab y Pwyll 'as like as the boy to Pwyll'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the equative cyn
hyspys: hyspys (hysbys) — known, manifest, evident; adjective (Ansawd Pwyll hyspys oed gantaw 'the look of Pwyll was known to him'); no mutation
gantaw: gan (gan) — 'with him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt gantaw (hyspys oed gantaw 'it was known to him'); no mutation
goueileint: goueileint (no modern form; cf. gofal) — anxiety, care, disquiet; noun (goueileint a dellis yndaw 'anxiety took hold of him'); no mutation
dellis: dala (dal) — to hold, seize; 3 sg. preterite 'seized' (goueileint a dellis yndaw 'grief seized in him'), -is, a>e by affection; soft mutation after a not shown (d for dd)
gamhet: cam (cam) — wrong; equative kamhet 'how wrong', used as a noun of degree (o gamhet idaw attal y mab 'from how wrong it was of him to keep the boy'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the preposition o
gwybot: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; verbal noun (ef yn gwybot y uot yn uab 'he knowing that he was a son'); no mutation
yscaualwch: yscaualwch (no modern form) — leisure, an opportunity; noun m. (A phan gauas gyntaf o yscaualwch ar y wreic 'and when he first had leisure with his wife'); no mutation
uenegis: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, relate, declare; 3 sg. preterite 'told' (ef a uenegis idi hi 'he told her'), -is; soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a
poen: poen (poen) — pain, torment, punishment; noun f./m. (gadu poen kymmeint 'to allow so great a pain'; o'r poen 'from the pain'); no mutation
kymmeint: kymeint (cymaint) — as much, so great; pronoun/adjective, spelt -mm- (poen kymmeint ac a oed 'a pain as great as there was'); no mutation
wreicda: gwreicda (gwreigdda) — noblewoman, a woman of standing; noun f., gwreic + da (ar wreicda kystal a Riannon 'on a noblewoman as good as Rhiannon'; A wreicda 'O noblewoman'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after ar and after the vocative A
gytsynnywys: kytsynnyaw (cytsynio) — to agree, consent; 3 sg. preterite 'agreed' (a gytsynnywys ar anuon y mab 'agreed on sending the boy'), -wys; soft-mutated (k>g) after the relative a
thriphet: tri + peth (tri pheth) — 'three things'; written as one word, the final h not written (the second witness has thripheth; kept as printed) (A thriphet … a gaffwn o hynny 'and three things we shall get from that'); tri spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and', peth spirant-mutated (p>ph) after tri
gaffwn: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 pl. present with future sense 'we shall get' (a gaffwn o hynny 'that we shall get from that'; the Red Book adds ni 'we'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
elwissen: elwissen (elusen) — alms, charity, a charitable deed (here the merit of it); noun f., from Latin eleemosyna (diolwch ac elwissen 'thanks and alms-merit'); no mutation
diollwch: diolwch (diolch) — thanks, gratitude; noun m., spelt diollwch (diollwch gan Pwyll 'thanks from Pwyll'); no mutation
ueithryn: meithryn (meithrin) — to foster, rear; verbal noun (am ueithryn y mab 'for fostering the boy'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the preposition am
eturyt: eturyt (edfryd) — to restore, give back; verbal noun (a'e eturyt idaw 'and restoring him to him'); no mutation (vowel)
maeth: maeth (maeth) — fostering, nurture, fosterage; noun m., in mab maeth 'foster-son' (mab maeth ynni uyd 'he will be a foster-son to us'); no mutation
allo: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be able' (a goreu a allo uyth 'and the best that he may ever be able'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after the relative a
wna: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. present/future 'will do' (a wna inni 'he will do for us'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
inni: y (i) + ni — 'to us'; conjugated preposition, 1 pl. (a wna inni 'he will do to us'); no mutation
trigyssant: trigyaw (trigo) — to stay, remain; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they stayed' (ar y kynghor hwnnw y trigyssant 'on that counsel they settled'); no mutation after the particle y
drydyd: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal (ymgueiraw a oruc Teirnon ar y drydyd marchawc 'Teirnon made ready as third rider'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the possessive y 'his'
petwyryd: pedwerydd (pedwerydd) — fourth; ordinal, spelt petwyryd (a'r mab yn petwyryd 'and the boy as fourth'); no mutation shown after yn
rodyssei: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had given' (y march a rodyssei Teirnon idaw 'the horse that Teirnon had given him'), -yssei; soft mutation after the relative a not shown (r for rh)
buont: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (Ny bu hir y buont 'it was not long they were'); no mutation after the particle y
emmyl: emyl (ymyl) — edge, brink, border; noun m., spelt emmyl (yn emmyl yr yskynuaen 'at the edge of the mounting-block'); no mutation
pann: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction, spelt pann (Pann doethont 'when they came'); causes soft mutation, not shown on d- (dd)
ewch: mynet (mynd) — to go; 2 pl. imperative 'go' (nac ewch bellach hynny 'do not go any further'); no mutation
uym: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, 1 sg., written uym with the nasal on it before p (uym penyt 'my penance'; uym pryder 'my care'); causes nasal mutation, here written only on the possessive, the noun left unchanged
lad: lladd (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun (am lad o honaf uu hun uy mab 'for my killing of my own son'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition am · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive 'e 'his' (na'e lad 'nor his killing')
honaf: o (o) + mi — 'of me, by me'; conjugated preposition, 1 sg., spelt o honaf (am lad o honaf 'for the killing by me'); no mutation
thebygaf: tybygu, tebygu (tybio) — to suppose, think; 1 sg. present 'I think' (ny thebygaf i y un o hyn uynet 'I do not think one of these will go'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after ny
hyn: hyn (hyn) — these; demonstrative pronoun (y un o hyn 'any one of these'); no mutation · also 'this (time)' in o hyn 'from now' (o hyn hyt ban del amgen 'from now until another comes')
mynho: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may wish' (Aet a'y mynho 'let him go who may wish it'), -o; no mutation
diruawr: diruawr (dirfawr) — immense, vast, exceeding; adjective (diruawr llywenyd 'immense joy'); no mutation
oedit: bot (bod) — to be; impersonal imperfect in -it 'one was, people were' (Ac yn dechreu treulaw y wled yd oedit yn y llys 'and they were beginning to consume the feast in the court'); no mutation
gylchaw: kylchu (cylchu) — to go round, make a circuit; verbal noun, spelt kylchaw (o gylchaw Dyuet 'from going round Dyfed'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the preposition o 'from'
yneuad: neuad (neuadd) — hall; noun f., spelt with prothetic y- (Y'r yneuad yd aethont 'into the hall they went'); no mutation
rwg: rwng (rhwng) — between; preposition, spelt rwg (Teirnon y rwg Pwyll a Riannon 'Teirnon between Pwyll and Rhiannon'); no mutation
wnaethon: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did' (ymdidan a wnaethon 'they conversed'), spelt -on for -ont; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the particle a
megys: megys (megis) — as, like, how; conjunction (megys y buassei y mab 'how the boy had been'); no mutation
buassei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had been' (megys y buassei y mab 'how the boy had been'), -ssei; no mutation after the particle y
hardelw: ardelw (arddelw) — claim, avowal, protection; noun m. (ar y hardelw wy 'under their claim, in their keeping'); h- prefixed to the vowel after the possessive y 'their'
megyssynt: magu (magu) — to rear; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had reared' (ac y megyssynt 'and they had reared him'), -yssynt, a>e by affection; no mutation after the particle y
phwy: pwy (pwy) — who; interrogative pronoun (A phwy bynnac a dywot geu arnat 'and whoever said a lie of you'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
cam: cam (cam) — wrong, injustice; noun m. (cam a wnaeth 'he did wrong'); no mutation (fronted object)
gouut: gouut (gofid) — grief, sorrow, trouble; noun m. (y gouut a oed arnat 'the grief that was on you'); no mutation after the article
doluryaw: dolurio (dolurio) — to grieve, be pained; verbal noun, fronted before a wneuthum (a doluryaw a wneuthum 'and I grieved'); no mutation
diheu: diheu (diau) — certain, doubtless; adjective (ny bo diheu gantaw hynny 'who would not be sure of that'); no mutation
escor: escor (esgor) — deliverance, release, bearing a child; noun m. (oed escor uym pryder im 'it was a relief from my anxiety to me'); no mutation (vowel)
pryder: pryder (pryder) — care, anxiety; noun m. (uym pryder 'my care'); the nasal mutation after uy 'my' is written only on the possessive (uym), pryder left unchanged; the word behind the name Pryderi
gwir: gwir (gwir) — true, truth; adjective/noun m. (pei gwir hynny 'if that were true'); no mutation
pendaran: Pendaran (Pendaran) — proper name, the foster-father of Pryderi, Pendaran Dyuet 'Pendaran of Dyfed'; no mutation
enweist: enwi (enwi) — to name; 2 sg. preterite 'you named' (da yd enweist dy uab, Pryderi 'well did you name your son Pryderi'), -eist; no mutation after the particle yd
pryderi: Pryderi (Pryderi) — proper name, the son of Pwyll and Rhiannon, named from pryder 'care'; no mutation
gueda: gweddu (gweddu) — to suit, befit; 3 sg. present 'suits' (goreu y gueda arnaw Pryderi 'Pryderi suits him best'), spelt gueda; no mutation after the particle y
edrychwch: edrych (edrych) — to look, consider; 2 pl. imperative 'consider' (Edrychwch na bo goreu y gueda arnaw y enw e hun 'consider whether his own name may not suit him best'), -wch; no mutation
enu: enw (enw) — name; noun m., spelt enu (Mae yr enu? 'where is the name?'); no mutation (vowel)
dodyssom: dodi (dodi) — to put, give; 1 pl. preterite 'we put' (a dodyssom ni arnaw ef 'that we gave him'), -yssom; soft mutation after the relative a not shown (d for dd)
yawnahaf: iawn (iawn) — right, proper, fitting; superlative yawnahaf 'most fitting' (Yawnahaf yw hynny 'that is most fitting'), spelt yawnahaf; adjective; no mutation
hwn: hwn (hwn) — this (m.); demonstrative pronoun/adjective (y mab hwn 'this boy'); no mutation
awr: awr (awr) — hour; noun f. (hyt yr awr hon 'until this hour'); no mutation (vowel)
dalu: talu (talu) — to pay, repay; verbal noun (y dalu ytti 'to repay you'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the preposition y 'to'
ytti: y (i) + ti — 'to you'; conjugated preposition, 2 sg., spelt ytti (y dalu ytti 'to repay it to you'); no mutation
magwys: magu (magu) — to rear, bring up; 3 sg. preterite 'reared' (y wreic a'e magwys ef 'the woman who reared him'), -wys; no mutation after a'e 'him'
galar: galar (galar) — grief, mourning; noun m. (dyn uwy y galar no hi 'a person whose grief is greater than hers'); no mutation (g- does not mutate after y 'her')
coffau: coffau (coffáu) — to remember, commemorate; verbal noun (Iawn yw idaw coffau ymi 'it is right for him to remember me'); no mutation
wnaethom: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 pl. preterite 'we did' (a wnaethom yrdaw ef 'what we did for him'), -om; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
yrdaw: yr (er) + ef — 'for him, for his sake'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m. (a wnaethom yrdaw ef 'what we did for him'); no mutation · also 'for it', of a thing (seith punt it yrdaw 'seven pounds for it', the creature, pryf m.)
parhawyf: parhau (parhau) — to last, endure; 1 sg. present subjunctive 'I may last' (tra parhawyf i 'while I last'), -wyf; the soft mutation after tra (barhawyf, as in the Red Book) is not written
kynhalyaf: kynnal (cynnal) — to uphold, support, maintain; 1 sg. present/future 'I shall support' (mi a'th kynhalyaf 'I shall uphold you'); no mutation shown after a'th
allwyf: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 sg. present subjunctive 'I may be able' (tra allwyf kynnhal 'while I am able to maintain'), -wyf; soft-mutated (g>∅) after tra
kynnhal: kynnal (cynnal) — to uphold, maintain; verbal noun, spelt kynnhal (tra allwyf kynnhal y meu 'while I can maintain what is mine'); no mutation
meu: meu (meu) — mine, my own; possessive pronoun (y meu uy hun 'my own'); no mutation
iawnach: iawn (iawn) — right, proper; comparative iawnach 'more right' (iawnach yw idaw dy gynnhal nogyt y mi 'it is more right for him to support you than me'); adjective; no mutation
gynnhal: kynnal (cynnal) — to uphold, maintain; verbal noun, spelt gynnhal (dy gynnhal 'to support you'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the possessive dy 'your'
nogyt: nogyt (no modern form; cf. nag) — than; comparative conjunction (nogyt y mi 'than to me'); no mutation
megeist: magu (magu) — to rear; 2 sg. preterite 'you reared' (canys megeist ti ef 'since you reared him'), -eist, a>e by affection; no mutation
uaeth: maeth (maeth) — fosterage, nurture; noun m. (ar uaeth 'in fosterage'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the preposition ar 'on'
bydwch: bot (bod) — to be; 2 pl. imperative 'be' (A bydwch gedymdeithon chwitheu 'and be companions, you also'), -wch; no mutation · also 2 pl. future 'you will be' (yn Hardlech y bydwch seith mlyned 'in Harlech you will be seven years')
chwitheu: chwi (chwi) — you, for your part; conjunctive 2 pl. pronoun, 'you also' (A bydwch gedymdeithon chwitheu 'and be companions, you also'); no mutation
thatmaetheu: tatmaeth (tadmaeth) — foster-father; noun m., plural tatmaetheu (a thatmaetheu idaw 'and foster-fathers to him'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
ymyrrwys: ymyrru (ymyrryd) — to go in with, join, commit oneself to (now 'interfere'); 3 sg. preterite in -wys (yd ymyrrwys gwyrda y wlat y gyt ac ef 'the noblemen of the land joined themselves to him'); sense here uncertain; no mutation after the particle yd
kychwynnwys: kychwyn (cychwyn) — to set out, depart; 3 sg. preterite 'set out' (Ac y kychwynnwys Teirnon 'and Teirnon set out'), -wys; no mutation after the particle y
toryfliant: Toryfliant (Twrf Liant) — the epithet of Teirnon, elsewhere Twryf Uliant; Evans prints tozyfliant, run together and spelt with o; kept as printed (Teirnon Toryfliant); no mutation
gynnhic: kynnic (cynnig) — to offer; verbal noun, spelt gynnhic (heb gynnhic ydaw y tlysseu 'without offering him the jewels'); soft-mutated (k>g) after heb 'without'
ydaw: y (i) + ef — 'to him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt ydaw (heb gynnhic ydaw 'without offering to him'); no mutation
tlysseu: tlws (tlws) — jewel, ornament; noun m., plural tlysseu (y tlysseu teccaf 'the fairest jewels'); no mutation
hoffaf: hoff (hoff) — dear, beloved; superlative hoffaf 'dearest' (y cwn hoffaf 'the dearest hounds'); adjective; no mutation
mynnwys: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want, accept; 3 sg. preterite 'wished' (Ac ny mynnwys ef dim 'and he would accept nothing'), -wys; no mutation
amgeledus: amgeledus (no modern form; cf. ymgeledd 'care') — careful, with care; adjective (y magwyt Pryderi yn amgeledus 'Pryderi was reared with care'); no mutation (vowel)
delediwhaf: telediw (no modern form) — handsome, comely; superlative delediwhaf 'handsomest' (yny oed delediwhaf gwass 'until he was the handsomest youth'); soft-mutated (t>d) as the complement directly after oed
gwass: gwas (gwas) — lad, youth, young man; noun m., spelt gwass (delediwhaf gwass 'handsomest lad'); no mutation
theccaf: tec (teg) — fair, handsome; superlative teccaf 'fairest' (a theccaf 'and fairest'); adjective; spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
chwpplaf: kwbyl (cwbl) — complete, accomplished; superlative kwpplaf 'most accomplished' (a chwpplaf o pob camp da 'and most accomplished in every good feat'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
camp: camp (camp) — feat, accomplishment, skill, game; noun f. (pob camp da 'every good accomplishment'); no mutation
treulyssant: treulio (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they spent' (Uelly y treulyssant blwydyn a blwydyned 'so they spent a year and years'); no mutation after the particle y
blwydyned: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f., plural blwydyned (modern blynyddoedd) (blwydyn a blwydyned 'a year and years'); no mutation
teruyn: teruyn (terfyn) — end, limit; noun m. (doeth teruyn ar hoedyl Pwyll 'an end came to Pwyll's life'); no mutation
hoedyl: hoedyl (hoedl) — life, lifetime; noun f. (ar hoedyl Pwyll 'on the life of Pwyll'); no mutation
uarw: marw (marw) — dead; adjective (y bu uarw 'he died', literally 'was dead'); soft-mutated (m>u) as the predicate directly after bu
gwledychwys: gwledychu (gwledychu) — to rule, reign; 3 sg. preterite 'ruled' (Ac y gwledychwys ynteu Pryderi seith cantref Dyuet 'and Pryderi ruled the seven cantrefs of Dyfed'), -wys; no mutation after the particle y
garedic: karedic (caredig) — beloved; adjective (yn llwydannus garedic gan y gyuoeth 'prosperously, beloved by his realm'); soft-mutated (k>g) as a second adjective after yn llwydannus, as if in one phrase with it · also soft after adverbial yn (yn garedic 'kindly, lovingly')
kynydwys: kynydu (cynyddu) — to increase, gain; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'he gained' (y kynydwys trychantref Ystrat Tywi 'he gained the three cantrefs of Ystrad Tywi'); no mutation after the particle y
trychantref: tri (tri) + cantref — 'three cantrefs', tri + chantref with the spirant mutation, spelt trychantref (trychantref Ystrat Tywi 'the three cantrefs of Ystrad Tywi'); noun m.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after tri 'three'
ystrat: ystrat (ystrad) — vale, valley floor; noun m., in the name Ystrat Tywi 'the vale of the Tywi'; no mutation
tywi: Tywi (Tywi) — proper name, the river Tywi (Ystrat Tywi 'the vale of Tywi'); no mutation
phedwar: pedwar (pedwar) — four; numeral (a phedwar cantref Keredigyawn 'and four cantrefs of Ceredigion'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
keredigyawn: Keredigyawn (Ceredigion) — proper name, Ceredigion, the region of west Wales; no mutation
gelwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (Ac y gelwir y rei hynny 'and those are called'), -ir, a>e by affection; no mutation after the particle y
seissyllwch: Seissyllwch (Seisyllwg) — proper name, the realm Seisyllwg, made of Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi (seith cantref Seissyllwch 'the seven cantrefs of Seisyllwg'); no mutation
kynnyd: kynnyd (cynnydd) — increase, growth, progress; noun m. (ar y kynnyd hwnnw 'on that increase'); no mutation
wreika: gwreika (gwreica) — to take a wife; verbal noun (yny doeth yn y uryt wreika 'until it came into his mind to take a wife'); soft-mutated (gw>w) as the subject of doeth, separated from its verb by yn y uryt
uynnawd: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want, choose; 3 sg. preterite in -awd 'he wanted' (Sef gwreic a uynnawd, Kicua 'the wife he chose was Cigfa'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a
kicua: Kicua (Cigfa) — proper name, the wife Pryderi chose, daughter of Gwyn Gohoyw; no mutation
wynn: Gwynn (Gwyn) — proper name, father of Cigfa (uerch Wynn Gohoyw 'daughter of Gwyn Gohoyw'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after uerch
gohoyw: gohoyw (gohoyw) — lively, sprightly, fine; adjective, epithet of Gwyn (Wynn Gohoyw 'Gwyn Gohoyw'); no mutation
gloyw: Gloyw (Gloyw) — proper name, grandfather of Cigfa, Gloyw Walltlydan 'Gloyw Broad-Hair'; also gloyw 'bright, shining'; no mutation
walltlydan: gwalltlydan (no modern form) — broad-haired; epithet of Gloyw, gwallt 'hair' + llydan 'broad' (Gloyw Walltlydan); soft-mutated (gw>w) as an epithet after the name
cassnar: Cassnar (Casnar) — proper name, an ancestor of Cigfa, Cassnar Wledic 'Casnar Wledig'; no mutation
wledic: gwledic (gwledig) — ruler, sovereign, lord; noun m., now commonly 'rural' (Cassnar Wledic 'Casnar the Ruler'); soft-mutated (gw>w) as an epithet after the name
dyledogyon: dylyedawc (dyledog) — a man of noble birth, one with a hereditary right; noun m., plural dyledogyon (o dyledogyon yr ynys hon 'of the nobility of this island'); the softening of d (dd) after o is not shown
ynys: ynys (ynys) — island; noun f. (yr ynys hon 'this island'); no mutation
teruyna: terfynu (terfynu) — to end, finish; 3 sg. present 'ends' (y teruyna y geing hon yma 'this branch ends here'); no mutation after the particle y
geing: keing (cainc) — branch, strand, a branch of the Mabinogi; noun f. (y geing hon 'this branch'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article y
mabynnogyon: Mabynnogyon (Mabinogion) — the form used in the scribe's closing formula, looking like a plural of mabinogi; it occurs only here and is commonly taken as a scribal form (the Red Book has it too) (o'r Mabynnogyon 'of the Mabinogi'); no mutation
bendigeiduran: Proper name — Bendigeidfran (Bendigeid 'blessed' + bran 'raven, crow'), son of Llŷr, king of the Island of the Mighty; bran is soft-mutated (b>u, u = f) as the second element of the compound; the name itself is unmutated as subject (Bendigeiduran uab Llyr a oed urenhin)
llyr: Proper name — Llŷr, father of Bendigeidfran, Manawydan and Branwen; radical, no mutation (after uab 'son': a patronymic leaves the father's name unmutated)
coronawc: coronawc (coronog) — crowned; adjective from coron 'crown' + -awc (urenhin coronawc 'a crowned king'); no mutation (follows its noun)
ardyrchawc: ardyrchawc (arderchog) — exalted, splendid, glorious; adjective (ac ardyrchawc o goron Lundein 'and exalted with the crown of London'); no mutation
goron: coron (coron) — crown; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after the preposition o 'of, with' (o goron Lundein)
lundein: Proper name — Llundein (Llundain), London; soft-mutated (ll>l) after the feminine noun coron 'crown' (goron Lundein 'the crown of London')
frynhawngueith: prynhawngweith (no modern form; cf. prynhawn 'afternoon' + gwaith 'time') — one afternoon, on an afternoon; adverbial compound of prynhawn + gweith, here an adverb of time (A frynhawngueith yd oed 'and one afternoon he was'); spirant-mutated (p>ph, written f) after a 'and'
hardlech: Proper name — Harlech (hardd 'fair' + llech 'slab, rock'), the court in Ardudwy; no mutation (h- is not mutated after yn 'in')
ardudwy: Proper name — Ardudwy, the cantref in north-west Wales in which Harlech stands; no mutation (vowel after yn 'in')
garrec: carrec (carreg) — rock, crag, stone; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after the preposition ar 'on' (ar garrec Hardlech 'on the rock of Harlech')
weilgi: gweilgi (gweilgi) — the open sea, the main (a poetic word); noun f.; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the feminine article y (uch penn y weilgi 'above the head of the sea')
manawydan: Proper name — Manawydan, son of Llŷr, brother of Bendigeidfran; radical (subject, after a 'and')
urawt: brawt (brawd) — brother; noun m.; soft-mutated (b>u) after the possessive y 'his' (Manawydan uab Llyr y urawt 'Manawydan son of Llŷr his brother')
uroder: brawt (brawd) — brother; plural broder 'brothers' (modern brodyr); soft-mutated (b>u) after deu 'two' (deu uroder 'two brothers', y deu uroder 'the two brothers')
nissyen: Proper name — Nisien (the spelling has ss for s), half-brother of Bendigeidfran, the peacemaker; radical, no mutation
efnyssen: Proper name — Efnysien (ss for s), half-brother of Bendigeidfran, the maker of quarrels; radical, no mutation
gwedei: gweddu (gweddu) — to suit, be fitting, be seemly; 3 sg. imperfect 'it was fitting' (mal y gwedei ynghylch brenhin 'as was fitting around a king'); no mutation after the particle y (gw- radical)
ynghylch: yn (yn) + kylch (cylch) — 'around, about'; the preposition yn with kylch 'circle' showing the nasal mutation (c>ngh) in full (ynghylch brenhin 'around a king')
meibon: mab (mab) — son; plural meibon 'sons' (modern meibion); noun m. pl. (meibon oedynt y Eurosswyd 'sons they were to Euroswydd'); no mutation (fronted predicate)
eurosswyd: Proper name — Euroswydd (ss for s, d for dd), father of Nisien and Efnysien; radical (vowel), after the preposition y 'to'
penardim: Proper name — Penardim (so both manuscripts; later editors print Penarddun), daughter of Beli son of Mynogan, Bendigeidfran's mother and, by Euroswydd, mother of Nisien and Efnysien; radical, in apposition after o'e uam ynteu 'by his own mother'
ueli: Proper name — Beli (Beli son of Mynogan, the legendary ancestor-king); soft-mutated (b>u) after the feminine noun merch (uerch Ueli 'daughter of Beli')
mynogan: Proper name — Mynogan, father of Beli; radical (after uab 'son')
barei: peri (peri) — to cause, make, bring about; 3 sg. imperfect 'would cause' (habitual) (ef a barei tangneued 'he would make peace'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the relative particle a
tangneued: tangneued (tangnefedd) — peace; noun f. (ef a barei tangneued 'he would make peace'); no mutation (object, radical)
lu: llu (llu) — host, army; noun m.; soft-mutated (ll>l) after deu 'two' (y deu lu 'the two hosts') · also soft after 'th 'your' (a'th lu 'and your host') · also soft after 'y 'his' (a'y lu 'and his host')
ban: pan (pan) — when; conjunction, spelt ban here (ban uydynt, ban uei 'when they were, when it was'); the b is a spelling of the conjunction, followed by a soft-mutated verb · also hyt ban 'until' (hyt ban gauas y benn 'until he found his head'; o hyn hyt ban del amgen 'from now until something else comes')
uydynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. habitual imperfect 'they would be, they used to be' (ban uydynt lidyawcaf 'when they were angriest'); soft-mutated (b>u) after the conjunction ban 'when'
lidyawcaf: llidyawc (llidiog) — angry; superlative lidyawcaf 'angriest' (-af); soft-mutated (ll>l) as the complement of uydynt (ban uydynt lidyawcaf 'when they were angriest')
llall: llall (llall) — the other; pronoun, used with the article (y llall 'the other'); no mutation (subject)
ymgerynt: ymgaru (no modern form) — to love one another; ym- (reciprocal) + caru 'love'; 3 pl. imperfect 'they loved one another' (yd ymgerynt), a>e by affection; no mutation after the particle yd
llong: llong (llong) — ship; noun f. (teir llong ar dec 'thirteen ships'); no mutation (after teir)
deheu: deheu (de) — south, the right (hand); noun m. (o deheu Iwerdon 'from the south of Ireland'); after o 'from' the soft mutation (d>dd) is not shown, d serving for both
iwerdon: Proper name — Iwerddon (Ireland); noun f.; no mutation (vowel)
rugyl: rugyl (rhugl) — easy, free, fluent, swift; adjective (a cherdet rugyl ebrwyd 'and an easy, swift going'); r- for rh-; no mutation
ebrwyd: ebrwyd (ebrwydd) — swift, quick; adjective, also adverbial in yn ebrwyd 'swiftly'; no mutation (vowel)
gwynt: gwynt (gwynt) — wind; noun m. (y gwynt yn eu hol 'the wind behind them'); no mutation (subject)
nessau: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; verbal noun (yn nessau yn ebrwyd attunt 'drawing near swiftly to them'); no mutation
longeu: llong (llong) — ship; plural longeu 'ships' (llongau); soft-mutated (ll>l) as the object directly after its verb (Mi a welaf longeu 'I see ships')
hy: hy (hy) — bold, daring; adjective, here adverbial with yn (yn hy 'boldly'); no mutation (h- does not mutate)
erchwch: erchi (erchi) — to ask, bid, command; 2 pl. imperative 'bid' (erchwch y wyr y llys 'bid the men of the court'); no mutation
amdanunt: am (am) + wynt — 'about them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (wiscaw amdanunt 'to dress about them'); no mutation
eidunt: eiddo (eiddo) — that which belongs to someone, 'theirs'; the independent possessive in 3 pl. (yr eidunt 'theirs', in pa uedwl yw yr eidunt 'what intention is theirs'); no mutation (vowel)
wiscawd: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to dress, put on; 3 sg. preterite in -awd 'dressed' (y gwyr a wiscawd amdanunt 'the men dressed themselves'), singular after the plural subject; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
wayret: gwaeret (gwaered) — slope, downward way; noun used adverbially (y wayret 'downwards, down the slope'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to'
llongeu: llong (llong) — ship; plural llongeu 'ships'; no mutation (after the article y 'the'; y llongeu hynn 'these ships')
agos: agos (agos) — near, close; adjective/adverb (o agos 'from near'); no mutation (vowel)
welsynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had seen' in -synt (na welsynt eiryoet 'that they had never seen'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the negative na · also soft after the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'all they had seen of grief')
gyweirach: kyweir (cyweir) — in good order, well arrayed, fitted out; comparative kyweirach 'better arrayed' (llongeu gyweirach 'ships better arrayed'); written soft-mutated (k>g) after the plural noun llongeu; the cause is not certain
hansawd: ansawd (ansawdd) — condition, quality, appearance; noun m.; h- prefixed before the vowel after eu 'their' (eu hansawd 'their appearance')
arwydon: arwyd (arwydd) — sign, ensign, banner; plural arwydon 'ensigns'; noun (Arwydon tec 'fair ensigns'); no mutation (subject, fronted)
tec: tec (teg) — fair, beautiful; adjective, -c for -g (arwydon tec 'fair ensigns'); no mutation (follows its noun)
guedus: gweddus (gweddus) — seemly, fitting; adjective, gu- for gw- (tec, guedus 'fair, seemly'); no mutation
arwreid: arwreid (arwraidd) — heroic, splendid; adjective from arwr 'hero' + -eid (arwreid o bali 'splendid of brocade'); no mutation
nachaf: nachaf (no modern form) — behold, lo; presentative particle that sets the scene before the eyes (nachaf un o'r llongeu 'behold one of the ships'); no mutation
raculaenu: raculaenu (rhagflaenu) — to go in front, outstrip, forge ahead; verbal noun, rac 'before' + blaenu 'to go first', the b of blaenu softened (b>u) inside the compound (yn raculaenu rac y rei ereill 'going ahead of the others')
guelynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. imperfect 'they saw' (y guelynt dyrchauael taryan 'they saw a shield raised'); gu- for gw-; no mutation after the particle y
dyrchauael: dyrchafael (dyrchafu) — to raise, lift up; verbal noun (dyrchauael taryan 'raising a shield'; yn dyrchauael 'rising, prospering'); no mutation · also after y 'its' (yn y dyrchauael 'in the raising of it'); the softening (d>dd) is not shown in the spelling
taryan: taryan (tarian) — shield; noun f. (dyrchauael taryan 'raising a shield', swch y taryan 'the point of the shield'); no mutation (radical, object of the verbal noun)
bwrd: bwrd (bwrdd) — board, side of a ship, table; noun m. (yn uch no bwrd y llong 'higher than the ship's board'); no mutation
swch: swch (swch) — ploughshare, point; noun m. (swch y taryan 'the point of the shield'); no mutation (radical, subject)
nessawys: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; 3 sg. preterite 'drew near' in -wys (y nessawys y gwyr attunt 'the men drew near to them'); no mutation after the particle y; the verb stays singular before the plural subject y gwyr
ymglywynt: ymglywet (ymglywed) — to hear one another; ym- (reciprocal) + clywet 'hear'; 3 pl. imperfect 'they could hear one another' (ual yd ymglywynt ymdidan); the c of clywet is softened (c>g) after the prefix ym-
badeu: bad (bad) — boat; plural badeu 'boats' (badau); noun m. (Bwrw badeu allan 'putting boats out'); no mutation (object of a verbal noun)
chyuarch: kyuarch (cyfarch) — to greet; verbal noun (a chyuarch guell 'and greeting'; kyuarch gwell, literally 'ask better'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
clywei: clywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 sg. imperfect 'heard, could hear' (a'e clywei wynteu 'heard them'); no mutation after the infixed 'e 'them'
uchel: uchel (uchel) — high; adjective (ar garrec uchel 'on a high rock'); no mutation (vowel)
rodo: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he give' (Duw a rodo da ywch 'may God give you good'); after the particle a soft mutation of rh is not distinguishable in the spelling (r for rh)
ywch: y (i) + chwi — 'to you'; conjugated preposition, 2 pl. (rodo da ywch 'may he give good to you'); no mutation
grayssaw: graessaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m. (a grayssaw wrthywch 'and welcome to you'); the g- is the word's own initial in this spelling (not a mutation here)
wrthywch: wrth (wrth) + chwi — 'towards you'; conjugated preposition, 2 pl. (grayssaw wrthywch 'welcome to you'); no mutation
pieu: piau (piau) — to own, be the owner of; 3 sg. present 'owns' (Pieu yniuer y llongeu hynn 'whose is the company of these ships?'); no mutation
matholwch: Proper name — Matholwch, king of Ireland; radical, no mutation (subject or in apposition: mae ymma Matholwch brenhin Iwerdon)
bieu: piau (piau) — to own, be the owner of; 3 sg. present 'owns' (ef bieu y llongeu 'he owns the ships'); soft-mutated (p>b) in the relative construction after the fronted subject ef
uynnhei: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. imperfect 'would want' (beth a uynnhei ef 'what would he want?'), the courteous 'would'; soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a; -nnh- is the scribe's spelling
uyn: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. present 'wants' (A uyn ef dyuot y'r tir 'does he want to come ashore?'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the interrogative particle a · also uy (fy) 'my', with the nasal mutation of d- written as n on the possessive (uyn diua i 'my destruction') · also before teulu (uyn teulu 'my warband'), the n of the nasal mutation being written on the possessive · also uy (fy) 'my' before t- (Nit drwc uyn trawscwyd i 'my venture is not bad'), the n being the written trace of the nasal mutation; before deudecuet (ar uyn deudecuet 'with me as the twelfth')
uynn: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. present 'wants' (Na uynn 'he does not want'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the negative na
by: pa (pa) — what, which; spelt by (by ryw neges 'what kind of errand'); causes soft mutation of the following word (ryw from rhyw) · also 'if', a spelling of pei (by na bei 'if it were not that'; the Red Book pany bei)
eidaw: eiddo (eiddo) — that which belongs to someone, 'his'; the independent possessive in 3 sg. m. (yr eidaw ef 'his'; pa darpar oed yr eidaw 'what purpose was his'); no mutation (vowel)
mynnu: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; verbal noun (Mynnu ymgyuathrachu 'wanting to ally himself by marriage'); no mutation
ymgyuathrachu: ymgyuathrachu (ymgyfathrachu) — to ally oneself by marriage; ym- (reciprocal) + kyuathrach 'kinship by marriage'; verbal noun; the k of kyuathrach is softened (k>g) after the prefix ym-
branwen: Proper name — Branwen, daughter of Llŷr; radical (object of erchi 'to ask for')
lyr: Proper name — Llŷr; soft-mutated (ll>l) after the feminine noun uerch 'daughter' (uerch Lyr 'daughter of Llŷr')
ymrwymaw: ymrwymaw (ymrwymo) — to bind oneself, bind together, join; verbal noun (ymrwymaw Ynys y Kedeirn ac Iwerdon y gyt 'to bind the Island of the Mighty and Ireland together'); no mutation
kedeirn: kadarn (cadarn) — strong, mighty; plural kedeirn 'the mighty' (modern cedyrn), used as a noun in Ynys y Kedeirn 'the Island of the Mighty' (Britain); no mutation
gadarnach: kadarn (cadarn) — strong, mighty; comparative kadarnach 'stronger'; soft-mutated (k>g) as the complement after bydynt (ual y bydynt gadarnach 'so that they would be stronger')
doet: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; 3 sg. imperative 'let him come' (doet y'r tir 'let him come to the land'); no mutation
chynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice; noun m.; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chynghor a gymerwn 'and counsel we will take', the object put first)
gymerwn: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 pl. present/future 'we take, we will take' (-wn) (a chynghor a gymerwn); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
ataw: at (at) + ef — 'to him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m. (a aeth ataw ef 'went to him'); no mutation
gahat: caffael (cael) — to get; impersonal preterite 'was got' (Sef a gahat yn y kynghor 'what was got in the counsel'), kahat; soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
uatholwch: Proper name — Matholwch; soft-mutated (m>u) after the preposition y 'to' (rodi Branwen y Uatholwch), after at 'to' (at Uatholwch) and as subject after a verb (a diwedyssei Uatholwch) · also soft after wrth 'to' (wrth Uatholwch) and after y gan 'from' (y gan Uatholwch) and as object after the imperative (gossymdeitha Uatholwch 'provide for Matholwch')
tryded: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal, feminine form tryded (trydedd) (A honno oed tryded prif rieni 'and she was the third chief ...'); no mutation (soft mutation after predicative yn is not written: yn tryded) · also left unsoftened after the article before a feminine noun, where dryded would be expected (A'r tryded nos 'and the third night'; the Red Book likewise)
rieni: rieni (rhieni) — parents, ancestors; plural noun, in prif rieni taken as 'chief ancestress' (sense uncertain; some read a form of rhiain 'maiden'); after prif the soft mutation (rh>r) is not distinguishable in this spelling
morwyn: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden, girl; noun f. (teccaf morwyn 'the fairest maiden'; morwyn gystal 'so good a maiden'); no mutation (radical)
aberfraw: Proper name — Aberffraw (aber 'river-mouth' + Ffraw), the chief court of Gwynedd in Anglesey; written with a single f; no mutation (vowel after yn)
kychwyn: kychwyn (cychwyn) — to set out, start; verbal noun, also noun 'setting out' (ac odyno y kychwyn 'and from there the setting out'); no mutation (y is the article here, since the word is unsoftened)
kychwynassant: kychwyn (cychwyn) — to set out, start; 3 pl. preterite in -assant 'they set out' (Ac y kychwynassant 'and they set out'); no mutation after the particle y
llongheu: llong (llong) — ship; plural, spelt llongheu with h (llongau); no mutation (after the article y 'the'; yn y llongheu 'in the ships')
bendigeituran: Proper name — Bendigeidfran; spelling with -t (= -d) for Bendigeiduran; radical (Bendigeituran a'y niuer ynteu 'Bendigeidfran and his company')
ymywn: y mywn (mewn) — in, inside; preposition, the old y + mywn (ymywn ty 'inside a house'); no mutation
oydynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. imperfect 'they were', a spelling of oedynt (yd oydynt 'they were'); no mutation
palleu: pall (pall) — pavilion, tent; plural palleu (Nyt ymywn ty, namyn ymywn palleu 'not in a house but in pavilions'); no mutation; pall also means a mantle or covering
angassei: genni (genni) — to be contained, have room, fit; 3 sg. pluperfect angassei 'had fitted, had been held', from the stem ang- (the Red Book writes eyngassei) (Ny angassei Uendigeituran eiryoet ymywn ty 'a house had never held Bendigeidfran'); the attribution to genni is not certain; no mutation (vowel)
uendigeituran: Proper name — Bendigeidfran; spelling with -t; soft-mutated (b>u) after at 'to' (at Uendigeituran) and as subject after a verb (Ny angassei Uendigeituran 'Bendigeidfran had never been contained'), and after gan 'with'
dechreussant: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 pl. preterite in -ssant 'they began' (A'r gyuedach a dechreussant 'and the carousing they began'); no mutation shown after the relative a (the soft mutation of d- is not written)
dilit: dilyt (dilyn) — to follow, pursue, keep on with; verbal noun (Dilit y gyuedach a wnaethant 'pursuing the carousing they did'); no mutation
welsant: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. preterite 'they saw' (-sant) (pan welsant 'when they saw'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after pan 'when'
dilyt: dilyt (dilyn) — to follow, pursue, keep on with; verbal noun (no dilyt kyuedach 'than to pursue carousing'); no mutation
kyscwys: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; 3 sg. preterite 'slept' in -wys (y kyscwys Matholwch gan Uranwen 'Matholwch slept with Branwen'); no mutation after the particle y
