uranwen: Proper name — Branwen; soft-mutated (b>u) after the preposition gan 'with' (gan Uranwen 'with Branwen') · also soft after ar 'on' (ar Uranwen 'on Branwen') and after y 'to' (y Uranwen 'to Branwen') · also soft as subject directly after the verb (A fan welas Uranwen y mab 'and when Branwen saw the boy'), as object after a subject (y kynhelis Bendigeiduran Uranwen 'Bendigeidfran held Branwen') and after the feminine noun yspydawt (Yspydawt Uranwen a Matholwch 'the Hospitality of Branwen and Matholwch')
swydwyr: swydwr (swyddwr) — officer, official; plural swydwyr 'officers' (swydd 'office' + -wr); no mutation (subject, after the article)
dechreusant: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 pl. preterite 'they began' (a'r swydwyr a dechreusant ymaruar 'and the officers began to busy themselves'); no mutation shown after the relative a
ymaruar: ymaruar (no modern form) — to busy oneself, see to; verbal noun (dechreusant ymaruar am rannyat y meirych 'began to busy themselves about allotting the horses'); sense uncertain, 'see to' fits; no mutation
rannyat: rannyat (rhaniad) — sharing out, allotment; noun m., from rannu (rhannu) 'share' (am rannyat y meirych 'about the allotting of the horses'); r- for rh-, and the soft mutation after am is not distinguishable in the spelling
gweisson: gwas (gwas) — lad, young man, servant; plural gweisson 'lads' (gweision), here the grooms (rannyat y meirych a'r gweisson 'the allotting of the horses and the grooms'); no mutation
rannu: rannu (rhannu) — to share, divide, allot; verbal noun (Ac eu rannu a wnaethant 'and they divided them'); r- for rh-; no mutation
dydgueith: dydgueith (no modern form) — one day, on a day; dyd 'day' + gweith 'time', adverbial (Ac ar hynny dydgueith 'and at that, one day'); no mutation
anagneuedus: anagneuedus (no modern form) — unpeaceable, quarrelsome; adjective, an- 'un-' + tangneuedus 'peaceable' (gwr anagneuedus 'the quarrelsome man'); no mutation
dywedassam: dywedut (dweud) — to say, speak; 1 pl. preterite in -assam 'we said' (a dywedassam uchot 'whom we spoke of above'); no mutation shown after the relative a
dywanu: dywanu (no modern form) — to happen on, come by chance (the notes' sense); verbal noun (yn dywanu y lety meirch Matholwch 'chancing to the horse-lodging of Matholwch'); no mutation
lety: llety (llety) — lodging, quarters; noun m.; soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition y 'to' (y lety meirch 'to the lodging of the horses')
pioed: piau (piau) — to own; 3 sg. imperfect 'owned', 'whose was?' (pioed y meirch 'whose were the horses'); no mutation
wnant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. present 'they do' (Beth a wnant wy 'what do they do?'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative/interrogative a
gyscwys: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; 3 sg. preterite 'slept' in -wys, with the perfective particle ry written yr: 'has slept' (yr gyscwys gan Uranwen 'has slept with Branwen'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle ry
chwaer: chwaer (chwaer) — sister; noun f. (dy chwaer 'your sister'; yn chwaer y minheu 'a sister to me'); no mutation (chw- has no mutated form after dy or yn)
ueirych: march (march) — horse; plural meirych 'horses'; soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive y 'his' (a'y ueirych 'and his horses')
gwnaethant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did' (Ay yuelly y gwnaethant wy 'is it thus they did?'); no mutation after the particle y
uyghanyat: kanyat (caniatâd) — permission, leave; noun m.; nasal-mutated (k>ngh, written gh) after uy 'my' (heb uyghanyat i 'without my permission')
ellynt: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 pl. imperfect 'they could' (Ny ellynt wy tremic uwy 'they could not do a greater insult'); the g- is lost by soft mutation after ny (stem ell-)
tremic: tremic (tremyg) — insult, contempt; noun m. (y tremic hwnnw 'that insult'; tremic uwy 'a greater insult'); no mutation
guan: gwanu (gwanu) — to stab, thrust; verbal noun (guan y dan y meirych 'thrusting under the horses'); gu- for gw-; no mutation · also 'rush, dash', of the mice (yn guan adan y grofd 'rushing into the croft'; yn guan a'r tywys e ymdeith 'dashing away with the ears')
thorri: torri (torri) — to cut, break, cut off; verbal noun (a thorri y guefleu 'and cutting the lips'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
guefleu: gwefl (gwefl) — lip; plural guefleu 'lips' (gweflau); gu- for gw-; no mutation (after the article y)
danned: dant (dant) — tooth; plural danned 'teeth' (dannedd); no mutation (after y 'the', wrth y danned 'at the teeth')
penneu: penn (pen) — head; plural penneu 'heads' (pennau); no mutation (after the article y)
rawn: rhawn (rhawn) — horsehair, tail or mane; noun; r- for rh- (a'r rawn wrth y keuyn 'and the tail-hair at the back'); no mutation
keuyn: keuyn (cefn) — back; noun m. (wrth y keuyn 'at the back'); no mutation
caei: kaffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. imperfect 'could get, would get' (ny caei graf 'he could get no grip'); no mutation shown after ny (a spirant mutation, ny chaei, would be expected)
amranneu: amrant (amrant) — eyelid; plural amranneu 'eyelids' (amrannau); no mutation (after the article yr)
ascwrn: ascwrn (asgwrn) — bone; noun m. (wrth yr ascwrn 'at the bone'); no mutation (vowel)
anfuryf: anfuryf (anffurf) — disfigurement, deformity; noun m., an- 'un-' + furyf (ffurf) 'form' (A gwneuthur anfuryf ar y meirych 'and making disfigurement on the horses'); no mutation
rym: grym (grym) — power, force; here 'use, good' (sense uncertain) (hyt nat oed rym a ellit a'r meirych 'so that there was no use that could be made of the horses'); soft-mutated (g lost) as the subject after nat oed (as in modern nid oes le)
ellit: gallu (gallu) — to be able; impersonal imperfect 'could be' (a ellit a'r meirych 'that could be had from the horses'); g- lost by soft mutation after the relative a · also soft after the negative ny (ny ellit 'there could not be')
anfuruaw: anfuruaw (anffurfio) — to disfigure, maim; verbal noun, from anfuryf (dywedut anfuruaw y ueirych 'telling of the disfiguring of his horses'); no mutation
llygru: llygru (llygru) — to spoil, corrupt, injure; verbal noun (eu llygru 'spoiling them'); no mutation
mwynyant: mwynyant (mwyniant) — benefit, use, enjoyment; noun m. (un mwynyant a ellit ohonunt 'one benefit that could be had from them'); no mutation
waradwydaw: gwaradwydaw (gwaradwyddo) — to shame, disgrace; verbal noun; soft-mutated (gw>w) after dy 'your' (dy waradwydaw 'your shaming', i.e. shaming you)
uynhir: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; impersonal present 'is wanted' (-ir) (a uynhir y wneuthur 'that is wanted to be done'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a
eres: eres (no modern form) — strange, wonderful; adjective, here predicative (eres genhyf 'strange with me', i.e. I find it strange); no mutation (vowel)
genhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me' (eres genhyf 'strange with me'; ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); the gan 'with' of opinion; no mutation
gwaradwydaw: gwaradwydaw (gwaradwyddo) — to shame, disgrace; verbal noun (uy gwaradwydaw 'my shaming'); no mutation shown after uy 'my' (the nasal mutation, ngwaradwydaw, is not written)
uynhynt: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 pl. imperfect 'they wanted' (os uy gwaradwydaw a uynhynt 'if it was my shaming that they wanted'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a
kyuurd: kyuurd (cyfurdd) — of equal rank, of the same degree; adjective, kyf- 'co-' + urdd 'rank' (morwyn gystal, kyuurd 'a maiden so good, of equal rank'); no mutation
anwylet: annwyl (annwyl) — dear, beloved; equative anwylet 'as dear' (gyn anwylet gan y chenedyl 'so dear to her kindred'); no mutation
chenedyl: kenedl (cenedl) — kindred, nation, family; noun f.; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the possessive y 'her' (y chenedyl 'her kindred')
rodyssant: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they gave' (ac a rodyssant ym 'as they gave to me'); the soft mutation after a (rh>r) is not distinguishable in the spelling
wnelych: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may do' (a wnelych 'what you may do'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
arouun: arouun (arofun) — to intend, set out, make for; verbal noun (arouun y longeu a wnaeth ef 'he set out for his ships'); no mutation (vowel)
ganhyat: kanhyat (caniatâd) — leave, permission; noun m., spelt kanhyat; soft-mutated (c>g) after heb 'without' (heb ganhyat 'without leave')
chenadeu: kennat (cennad) — messenger; plural chenadeu 'messengers' (cenhadon); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (A chenadeu a aeth 'and messengers went')
kennadeu: kennat (cennad) — messenger; plural kennadeu 'messengers' (cenhadon); no mutation (subject, radical: Sef kennadeu a aeth 'the messengers who went')
idic: Proper name — Iddig (Idic), son of Anarawg, one of the messengers; radical
anarawc: Proper name — Anarawg (Anarawc), father of Iddig; radical (after uab)
guyr: gwr (gŵr) — man; plural guyr 'men' (gwŷr); gu- for gw-; no mutation (Y guyr hynny 'those men', after the article)
godiwawd: godiwes (goddiweddyd) — to overtake; 3 sg. preterite in -awd 'overtook' (a'y godiwawd 'who overtook him'), singular after the plural subject y guyr; no mutation after the infixed 'y 'him'
ouynyssant: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they asked' (a ouynyssant idaw 'and they asked of him'); g- lost by soft mutation after the relative a
gwypwn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I would know' (pei ys gwypwn 'if I had known it'); no mutation
down: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I would come' (ny down yma 'I would not have come here', modern deuwn); no mutation shown after ny · also 1 pl. present/future 'we shall come' (attat ti y down ac ef 'to you we shall come with it')
waradwyd: gwaradwyd (gwaradwydd) — shame, disgrace; noun m.; soft-mutated (gw>w) after cwbyl 'whole, complete', an adjective placed before its noun (Cwbyl waradwyd 'complete disgrace')
kyrch: kyrch (cyrch) — journey, attack, onset; noun m. (ny duc neb kyrch waeth 'no one made a worse journey'); no mutation
waeth: gwaeth (gwaeth) — worse; comparative (kyrch waeth 'a worse journey'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the noun kyrch it follows
dugum: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 1 sg. preterite 'I brought' (-um) (no'r dugum ymma 'than I brought here'); no mutation
reuedawt: ryuedawt (rhyfeddod) — wonder, marvel; noun m., written reuedawt (A reuedawt rygyueryw a mi 'and a wonder has befallen me'); no mutation after a 'and'
rygyueryw: kyuaruot (cyfarfod) — to meet, befall; 3 sg. preterite kyueryw 'met', with the perfective particle ry: 'has met, has befallen' (rygyueryw a mi 'has befallen me'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle ry
bronwen: Proper name — Branwen, here written Bronwen (modern Branwen), a spelling found once in the manuscript; radical (object of rodi 'giving')
kedeyrn: kadarn (cadarn) — strong, mighty; plural, a spelling of kedeirn 'the mighty' (Ynys y Kedeyrn 'the Island of the Mighty'); no mutation
chyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyscu genthi 'and sleeping with her')
ryued: ryued (rhyfedd) — wonder, marvel; noun m., also the adjective 'strange' (ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); no mutation
gwneit: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; impersonal imperfect 'was being done' in -it (y gwneit y gwaradwyd 'the disgrace was done'); no mutation after the particle y
gwaradwyd: gwaradwyd (gwaradwydd) — shame, disgrace; noun m. (y gwaradwyd hwnnw 'that disgrace'); no mutation (after the article)
wnelit: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; impersonal imperfect subjunctive 'should be done, was done' in -it (a wnelit ym 'that was done to me'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
uedei: medu (medu) — to hold, possess, rule; 3 sg. imperfect 'held' (a uedei y llys 'who held the court'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a
gwnaetpwyt: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; impersonal preterite 'was done' in -pwyt (y gwnaetpwyt y gwaradwyd hwnnw yt 'that disgrace was done to you'), spelt -tpwyt for -thpwyt; no mutation after the particle y
mwy: mwy (mwy) — more, greater; comparative of mawr (mwy yw gan Uendigeituran no chenyt ti 'it is greater to Bendigeidfran than to you'); no mutation (fronted predicate); also mwy dwyweith 'twice as big'
chenyt: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 2 sg. 'with you', written chenyt after no 'than' (no chenyt ti 'than with you'); the ch- is the spirant mutation after no, read as from a c- form of the preposition (gennyt with g- has no spirant form)
tebygaf: tebygu (tebygu) — to suppose, think, imagine; 1 sg. present 'I suppose' (mi a tebygaf); no mutation shown after the particle a (t> d would be expected)
eissoes: eissoes (eisoes) — yet, nevertheless; adverb (Ac eissoes ni eill ef 'and yet he cannot'); no mutation (vowel)
niwaradwydaw: diwaradwydaw (no modern form) — to take a disgrace away, undo a disgrace; di- 'un-' + gwaradwydaw; verbal noun, nasal-mutated (d>n) after uy 'my' (uy niwaradwydaw 'my undoing of disgrace')
ymchwelwys: ymchwelut (ymchwelyd) — to turn, return; 3 sg. preterite 'returned' in -wys (a ymchwelwys a'r atteb hwnnw 'returned with that answer'), singular after the plural subject; no mutation after the relative a
diwedyssei: dywedut (dweud) — to say, speak; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had said' in -ssei (a diwedyssei Uatholwch 'that Matholwch had said'), the form with di-; no mutation shown after the relative a
ymwaret: ymwaret (ymwared) — help, remedy, deliverance; noun m. (nyt oes ymwaret e uynet ef 'there is no help for his going'); no mutation (vowel)
anygneuedus: anagneuedus (no modern form) — unpeaceable, hostile; adjective, spelt anygneuedus (yn anygneuedus 'in enmity, unreconciled'); no mutation (vowel)
gadwn: gadu (gadael) — to let, allow; 1 pl. present 'we allow, will allow' (-wn) (nys gadwn 'we will not allow it'); no mutation (g- radical after ny + 's) · also kadw (cadw) 'to keep', 1 sg. imperfect with conditional sense 'I would keep' (mi a gadwn gywirdeb 'I would keep faithfulness'), soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
genhadeu: kennat (cennad) — messenger; plural 'messengers'; soft-mutated (k>g) because the adverb etwa stands between it and the verbal noun anuon (anuon etwa genhadeu 'sending messengers again')
anuonaf: anuon (anfon) — to send; 1 sg. present/future 'I will send' (Anuonaf 'I will send'); no mutation (vowel)
kyuodwch: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; 2 pl. imperative 'rise' (Kyuodwch, Uanawydan); no mutation
uanawydan: Proper name — Manawydan; soft-mutated (m>u) as a person addressed, vocative (Kyuodwch, Uanawydan uab Llyr 'rise, Manawydan son of Llŷr') · also soft after at 'to' (at Uanawydan 'to Manawydan') and after e gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also soft after o marking the doer and after y 'to' (o Uanawydan; y Uanawydan), in apposition after ef (ef Uanawydan) and as the subject straight after the verb (y llunyei Uanawydan)
unic: Proper name — Unig (Unic), in Unic Glew Yscwyd 'Unig Strong-Shoulder', one of Bendigeidfran's men; radical
glew: glew (glew) — bold, valiant, strong; adjective, in the epithet Unic Glew Yscwyd; no mutation
yscwyd: ysgwydd (ysgwydd) — shoulder; noun f., in the epithet Unic Glew Yscwyd; no mutation (vowel-like, ys-) · also 'shoulder' in ar e yscwyd 'on his shoulder' (e = y 'his'), no mutation
menegwch: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, relate; 2 pl. imperative 'tell' (menegwch idaw 'tell him'); no mutation
lygrwyt: llygru (llygru) — to spoil, injure; impersonal preterite 'were spoiled' in -wyt (o'r a lygrwyt 'of those that were spoiled'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the relative a
wynepwerth: wynepwerth (wynebwerth) — face-price, compensation for an insult to one's honour; wyneb 'face' + gwerth 'worth', the g of gwerth softened inside the compound; noun m.; no mutation (the w- of wyneb is radical) after predicative yn (yn wynepwerth idaw 'as face-price to him')
llathen: llathen (llathen) — rod, yard, measure; noun f. (llathen aryant 'a rod of silver'); no mutation
aryant: aryant (arian) — silver, money; noun m. (llathen aryant 'a rod of silver'); no mutation (vowel)
kyuref: kyuref (no modern form) — as thick as, of equal thickness; equative (the notes take it as the equative of praff 'thick') (llathen aryant a uo kyuref a chyhyt ac ef e hun 'a rod of silver as thick and as long as he himself'); no mutation
chyhyt: kyhyt (cyhyd) — as long as; equative of hir 'long'; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyhyt ac ef e hun)
chlawr: clawr (clawr) — plate, cover, board; noun m. (a chlawr eur 'and a plate of gold'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
kyflet: kyflet (cyfled) — as broad as; equative of llydan 'broad' (clawr eur kyflet a'y wyneb 'a plate of gold as broad as his face'); no mutation
anuod: anuod (anfodd) — displeasure, unwillingness; noun m. (o'm anuod inheu 'against my will'); no mutation shown (no h- after 'm, unlike o'm hanuod elsewhere)
may: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present 'is', a spelling of mae, introducing a reported fact (y may brawt un uam a mi a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that'); no mutation
brawt: brawt (brawd) — brother; noun m.; no mutation (subject after y may 'that it is'; y may brawt un uam a mi 'that it is a brother of one mother with me')
hawd: hawd (hawdd) — easy; adjective (nat hawd genhyf i 'it is not easy with me'); no mutation (h-)
ymwelet: ymwelet (ymweld) — to visit; verbal noun (y ymwelet a mi 'to visit with me', i.e. to come and see me); no mutation
dangneued: tangneued (tangnefedd) — peace; noun f.; soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (mi a wnaf y dangneued 'I will make the peace')
llun: llun (llun) — shape, form, figure, manner; noun m. (ar y llun y mynho 'on the terms he may wish'); no mutation
uanagyssant: managu (mynegi) — to tell, relate; a by-form of menegi; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they told' (a uanagyssant idaw yr ymadrawd hwnnw 'and they told him that speech'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a
ymadrawd: ymadrawd (ymadrodd) — speech, utterance, talk; noun m. (yr ymadrawd hwnnw 'that speech'); no mutation (vowel)
guerendewis: gwarandaw (gwrando) — to listen; 3 sg. preterite 'listened' (-is) (a'e guerendewis 'and he listened to it'); gu- for gw-; no mutation shown after the infixed 'e
uedylyssant: medylyaw (meddylio) — to think, consider; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they thought' (Sef kynghor a uedylyssant 'the counsel they thought'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a · also soft after yny 'until' (yny uedylyssant am wraged 'until they thought of women')
gwrthot: gwrthot (gwrthod) — to refuse, reject; verbal noun (os gwrthot hynny a wnelynt 'if they should refuse that'); no mutation
wnelynt: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. imperfect subjunctive 'they should do, were to do' (os gwrthot hynny a wnelynt 'if they were to refuse that'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after a
tebygach: tebyc (tebyg) — likely, probable, like; comparative tebygach 'likelier' (bot yn tebygach ganthunt 'being likelier with them'); no mutation shown after predicative yn (the soft form debygach is not written)
kywilid: kywilid (cywilydd) — shame, disgrace; noun m. (cael kywilid 'getting shame'); no mutation
disgynnu: disgynnu (disgyn) — to come down, alight, settle (on a decision); verbal noun (disgynnu a wnaeth ar gymryt hynny 'he settled on taking that'); no mutation
deuthant: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (y deuthant yn dangneuedus 'they came peaceably'), beside doethant; no mutation after the particle y
dangneuedus: tangneuedus (tangnefeddus) — peaceable, peaceful; adjective; soft-mutated (t>d) after adverbial yn (yn dangneuedus 'peaceably, in peace')
chyweiraw: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to arrange, put in order, prepare; verbal noun (A chyweiraw y pebylleu 'and arranging the tents'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
pebylleu: pebyll (pabell) — tent, pavilion; plural pebylleu; noun m./f. (chyweiraw y pebylleu a'r palleu 'arranging the tents and the pavilions'); no mutation (after the article y)
ureint: breint (braint) — privilege, dignity, due; noun f.; soft-mutated (b>u) after ar 'on, after' (ar ureint kyweirdeb yneuad 'in the manner of the hall's arrangement')
kyweirdeb: kyweirdeb (cyweirdeb) — arrangement, order; noun f. (kyweirdeb yneuad 'the arrangement of a hall'); no mutation
dechreuyssant: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they began' (ual y dechreuyssant eisted 'as they began to sit'); no mutation after the particle y
ardiawc: ardiawc (no modern form) — slow, listless, dull; a rare word, sense uncertain (nachaf yn ardiawc 'behold dull'); no mutation (vowel)
drist: trist (trist) — sad, sorrowful; adjective (yn drist 'sad'); soft-mutated (t>d) after predicative yn
gaei: kaffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. imperfect 'got, was getting' (a gaei gan Uatholwch 'what he was getting from Matholwch'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
lywenyt: llywenyt (llawenydd) — joy, cheerfulness; noun m.; soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive y 'his' (a'y lywenyt 'and his cheer')
athrist: athrist (athrist) — very sad; adjective, a- (intensive) + trist (bot yn athrist gan yr unben 'that it was very sad to the chieftain'); no mutation (vowel)
uychanet: bychan (bychan) — small, little; equative bychanet 'as small, how small', here used as a noun of degree, 'the smallness' (uychanet a gawssei o iawn 'how small was what he had got of compensation'); written soft-mutated (b>u)
ymdidanwr: ymdidanwr (ymddiddanwr) — talker, companion in talk; noun m., ymdidan + -wr 'man' (nit wyt gystal ymdidanwr 'you are not as good a talker'); no mutation
bychanet: bychan (bychan) — small, little; equative bychanet 'as small', used as a noun of degree, 'the smallness' (yr bychanet genhyt ti dy iawn 'for the smallness, in your eyes, of your compensation'); no mutation
gehy: caffael (cael) — to get; 2 sg. present/future 'you will get' (ti a gehy ychwanegu 'you will get an increase'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a · also in ti a gehy hynny 'you will get that'; gehy is a by-form of gey/key (the Red Book has Ti a gey here)
ychwanegu: ychwanegu (ychwanegu) — to add, increase; verbal noun; no mutation (vowel)
uynnu: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; verbal noun, soft-mutated (m>u) after dy 'your' (wrth dy uynnu 'according to your wish') · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the preposition y 'to' (y uynnu medi 'to want to reap')
talu: talu (talu) — to pay; verbal noun (ac auory talu dy ueirch yt 'and tomorrow paying your horses to you'); no mutation
ueirch: march (march) — horse; plural meirch; soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive dy 'your' (dy ueirch 'your horses') · also soft after y 'his' (y ueirch 'his horses')
delediwaf: telediw (no modern form) — fair, comely, complete; adjective, here made into a verb 'make fair, make complete' (sense uncertain); 1 sg. present/future delediwaf 'I will make fair' ← telediwaf, soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a (mi a delediwaf dy iawn)
peir: peir (pair) — cauldron; noun m. (Mi a rodaf yt peir 'I will give you a cauldron'; y peir 'the cauldron'); no mutation
chynnedyf: kynnedyf (cynneddf) — property, characteristic, peculiar virtue; noun f.; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chynnedyf y peir yw 'and the property of the cauldron is')
lader: llad (lladd) — to kill; impersonal present subjunctive 'may be killed' in -er (y gwr a lader hediw 'the man who may be killed today'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the relative a
llyueryd: llyueryd (lleferydd) — speech, utterance; noun m. (eithyr na byd llyueryd ganthaw 'except that there will be no speech with him'); no mutation
lywenyd: llywenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (diruawr lywenyd 'huge gladness'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preceding adjective diruawr · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive y 'his' (a dwyn y lywenyd y gantaw 'and taking his joy from him')
talwyt: talu (talu) — to pay; impersonal preterite 'was paid' in -wyt (y talwyt y ueirych idaw 'his horses were paid to him'); no mutation after the particle y
barhawd: parhau (parhau) — to last, continue; 3 sg. preterite in -awd 'lasted' (tra barhawd meirych dof 'while tame horses lasted'); soft-mutated (p>b) after tra 'while'
dof: dof (dof) — tame, gentle; adjective (meirych dof 'tame horses'); no mutation (follows a plural noun)
kyrchwyt: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, go to; impersonal preterite 'was gone' in -wyt (y kyrchwyt ac ef kymwt arall 'another commote was gone to with him'); no mutation after the particle y
kymwt: kymwt (cwmwd) — commote, a subdivision of a cantref; noun m. (kymwt arall 'another commote'; y kymwt hwnnw 'that commote'); no mutation
gwbyl: cwbyl (cwbl) — whole, complete; adjective; soft-mutated (c>g) as the predicate after uu (yny uu gwbyl idaw y dal 'until his payment was complete to him') · also soft-mutated (c>g) as object after ry geueist (neu ry geueist gwbyl 'you have got the whole')
dal: tal (tal) — payment, price; noun m.; soft-mutated (t>d) after the possessive y 'his' (y dal 'his payment') · also tal 'end, front, rim' (ar dal y noe 'on the end of her kneading-trough'), soft after ar 'on'
tal: tal (tal) — payment; noun m., first element of the name Tal Ebolyon (Talebolion, 'payment of colts'); also tal 'front, end', so the name may have meant something else; no mutation (radical)
rodeist: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 2 sg. preterite 'you gave' (-eist) (y peir a rodeist ymi 'the cauldron that you gave to me'); the soft mutation after the relative a is not distinguishable in the spelling
wn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. present 'I know' (ni wn 'I do not know'); g- lost by soft mutation after ni
caffo: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may get' (y caffo 'that he may have got'); no mutation after the particle y
llassar: Proper name — Llasar (Llassar), the giant in Llassar Llaes Gyfnewit, who came out of the Lake of the Cauldron; radical; llasar also means 'blue, azure'
llaes: llaes (llaes) — trailing, slack, loose; adjective, part of the epithet Llassar Llaes Gyfnewit; no mutation
gyfnewit: kyfnewit (cyfnewid) — exchange, change; noun m., the last word of the epithet Llassar Llaes Gyfnewit; soft-mutated (k>g) after the preceding adjective llaes · also soft as the object of dangossaf (a dangossaf gyfnewit 'I will show an exchange')
chymidei: Proper name — Cymidei (Cymidei Cymeinfoll), the giant's wife; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a Chymidei Kymeinuoll)
kymeinuoll: Proper name — Cymeinfoll, the second part of the name Cymidei Cymeinfoll; read as kymein + boll 'belly' with b softened to u inside the compound (sense uncertain); radical
dianghyssant: dianc (dianc) — to flee, escape; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they escaped' (a dianghyssant o'r ty hayarn 'who escaped from the iron house'); no mutation shown after a or y
hayarn: haearn (haearn) — iron; noun m., spelt hayarn (y ty hayarn 'the iron house'); no mutation (apposed after the noun ty)
wenn: gwynn (gwyn) — white; feminine form gwenn (gwen); soft-mutated (gw>w) after predicative yn (pan wnaethpwyt yn wenn 'when it was made white'), as if of a feminine noun (ystauell 'chamber')
kylch: kylch (cylch) — circle, ring, surrounding; noun m. (yn eu kylch 'around them'; yg kylch y ty 'around the house'); no mutation
gynhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me', a variant spelling of genhyf (eres gynhyf i 'it is strange with me'); no mutation
wdosti: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 2 sg. present 'you know' (gwdost) with ti 'you' run into it: wdosti = wdost ti (ony wdosti dim 'if you know nothing'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after ony 'if not'
chymeint: kymeint (cymaint) — as much, so much; equative; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymeint ac a wnn 'and as much as I know')
benn: penn (pen) — head, top, end; noun m.; soft-mutated (p>b) after ar 'on' (ar benn gossed 'on top of a mound'; ar benn y pethewnos 'at the end of the fortnight') · also soft after y 'his' (gauas y benn 'found his head') and after am 'about' (am benn hwnnw 'about that one's head') · also soft after a preceding adjective (Yspydawt Urdaul Benn 'the Hospitality of the Honoured Head') and after the feminine noun yspydawt (Yspydaut Benn 'the Hospitality of the Head') · also soft-mutated (p>b) after uch 'above' (uch benn llech 'above a slab') · also soft after dy 'your' (am dy benn 'about your head')
gossed: gorssed (gorsedd) — mound, hillock; noun f., written gossed here, a slip for gorssed (ar benn gossed 'on top of a mound'); no mutation
llyn: llyn (llyn) — lake, pool; noun m. (uch penn llyn 'above a lake'; Llyn y Peir 'the Lake of the Cauldron') · also 'drink, liquor' (o uwyt a llyn 'of food and drink'); no mutation
welwn: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. imperfect 'I saw' (-wn) (mi a welwn gwr 'I saw a man'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the particle a
melyngoch: melyngoch (melyngoch) — yellow-red, tawny; adjective, melyn + coch (gwr melyngoch mawr 'a big tawny man'); no mutation
pheir: peir (pair) — cauldron; noun m.; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (a pheir ar y geuyn 'and a cauldron on his back')
athrugar: athrugar (no modern form) — immense, enormous (the notes' reading; a- + trugar); adjective, sense uncertain (gwr athrugar mawr 'a huge, big man'); no mutation
drygweith: drygweith (no modern form) — evil aspect, villainous look (the notes' reading; drwc 'bad' + gweith); noun; sense uncertain (a drygweith anorles arnaw oed 'and a villainous look unrestrained was on him'); no mutation shown after a
anorles: anorles (no modern form) — unrestrained (the notes' guess); sense uncertain; adjective following drygweith; no mutation (vowel)
dwyweith: dwyweith (dwywaith) — twice; adverb, dwy 'two' + gweith 'time', the g of gweith softened after dwy (mwy dwyweith oed y wreic noc ef 'the woman was twice as big as he'); no mutation
ataf: at (at) + mi — 'to me'; conjugated preposition, 1 sg. (a chyrchu ataf a wnaethant 'and they made for me'); no mutation
uell: gwell (gwell) — better; written soft-mutated (gw>w, here spelt u) after the verbal noun chyuarch, though an object directly after a verbal noun is not normally softened (guell unsoftened in a chyuarch guell y'r brenhin) (kyuarch gwell 'to greet', literally 'ask better'; a chyuarch uell im 'and greeting me')
arnawch: ar (ar) + chwi — 'on you'; conjugated preposition, 2 pl. (pa gerdet yssyd arnawch chwi 'what journey is on you?'); no mutation
pethewnos: pethewnos (pythefnos) — fortnight, fifteen nights; noun f. (ym penn pethewnos a mis 'at the end of a fortnight and a month'); no mutation
mis: mis (mis) — month; noun m. (pethewnos a mis 'a fortnight and a month'; y pedwyryd mis 'the fourth month'); no mutation
beichogi: beichogi (beichiogi) — pregnancy, conception; noun m./verbal noun (y byd beichogi idi 'there will be pregnancy to her'); no mutation shown
aner: geni (geni) — to be born; impersonal present subjunctive 'may be born' (y mab a aner yna 'the son who may be born then'); the g- of ganer lost by soft mutation after the relative a
torllwyth: torllwyth (torllwyth) — litter, brood; noun f. (o'r torllwyth hwnnw 'of that litter'); no mutation
aruawc: aruawc (arfog) — armed; adjective (llawn aruawc 'fully armed'); no mutation (vowel)
kymereis: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 sg. preterite 'I took' (-eis) (Y kymereis inheu wyntwy arnaf 'I took them upon me'); no mutation after the particle y
wyntwy: wynt (hwynt) — they, them; emphatic doubled 3 pl. pronoun wyntwy (hwyntwy) (kymereis wyntwy arnaf 'I took them on myself'); no mutation
yu: y (i) + 'u 'them' — the preposition y 'to' with the infixed 3 pl. pronoun (yu gossymdeithaw 'to maintain them', literally 'to their maintaining'); no mutation
gossymdeithaw: gossymdeithaw (no modern form) — to maintain, keep, provide for (the notes' sense); verbal noun; no mutation shown after yu
keueis: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 1 sg. preterite 'I got' (y keueis wynt 'I had them'); no mutation after the particle y
diwarauun: diwarauun (diwarafun) — without grudging, ungrudged; adjective, di- 'un-' + gwarafun 'to grudge' (yn diwarauun 'ungrudgingly'); no mutation shown after yn (the soft form ddiwarauun is not written)
allann: allan (allan) — out, forth; adverb, spelt allann (o hynny allann 'from then on'); no mutation
guarauunwyt: gwarafun (gwarafun) — to grudge, forbid, deny; impersonal preterite 'was grudged' in -wyt (y guarauunwyt im 'it was grudged to me'); gu- for gw-; no mutation after the particle y
hatcassu: atcassu (atgasu) — to hate, make hated; verbal noun; h- prefixed before the vowel after eu 'their' (eu hatcassu 'their being hated')
anghynwys: anghynwys (no modern form) — unwelcome, not to be borne; adjective, an- 'un-' + kynwys 'admit' (anghynwys yn y wlat 'unwelcome in the land'); no mutation
sarahedeu: sarhaet (sarhad) — insult, injury, outrage; plural sarahedeu 'outrages' (sarhadau) (gwneuthur sarahedeu 'doing outrages'); no mutation
eighaw: eighaw (no modern form) — to molest, ill-treat (the notes' sense); a rare verb, sense uncertain; verbal noun after yn (yn eighaw ac yn gouudyaw 'molesting and vexing'); no mutation
gouudyaw: gouudyaw (gofidio) — to vex, afflict, grieve; verbal noun (yn gouudyaw guyrda a gwragedda 'vexing noblemen and noblewomen'); no mutation
gwragedda: gwreicda (gwreigdda) — noblewoman; plural gwragedda 'noblewomen', gwreic 'woman' + da 'good', the counterpart of guyrda 'noblemen' (guyrda a gwragedda); no mutation
dygyuores: dygyuor (dygyfor) — to rise up, muster, gather; 3 sg. preterite 'rose up' (y dygyuores uyg kyuoeth 'my realm rose up'); no mutation after the particle y
uyg: uy (fy) — my; possessive, here spelt uyg before k-: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation the noun would take (uyg kyuoeth = fy nghyfoeth 'my realm')
ymuadeu: ymuadeu (ymwadu) — to renounce, give up, part with; verbal noun, ymuadeu ac wynt 'to renounce them' (ymwadu â); no mutation
dodeis: dodi (dodi) — to put, place; 1 sg. preterite 'I put' (-eis) (E dodeis inheu ar gynghor uy gwlat 'I put it to the counsel of my country'); no mutation after the particle E
gwlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f. (ar gynghor uy gwlat 'to the counsel of my country'); no mutation shown after uy 'my' (the nasal mutation, ngwlat, is not written)
nyd: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not', spelt nyd before a vowel (Nyd eynt wy 'they would not go'); no mutation
eynt: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. imperfect 'they would go' (eynt, modern aent) (Nyd eynt wy o'y bod 'they would not go of their will'); no mutation
bod: bod (bodd) — will, consent, pleasure; noun m. (o'y bod 'of their will'); no mutation (y 'their' causes none)
oc: o (o) — 'of, from', spelt oc before a vowel (oc eu hanuod 'against their will'); no mutation
kyuyng: kyuyng (cyfyng) — narrow, strait, confined; adjective placed before its noun (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel'), which it softens; no mutation
causant: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 pl. preterite 'they got' (y causant gwneuthur ystauell haearn 'they got to making a chamber of iron'); no mutation after the particle y
haearn: haearn (haearn) — iron; noun m. (ystauell haearn 'a chamber of iron'); no mutation (vowel)
dyuyn: dyuyn (dyfynnu) — to summon, call; verbal noun (dyuyn a oed o of yn Iwerdon 'summoning all there was of smiths in Ireland'); no mutation
of: gof (gof) — smith; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after o 'of' (o of 'of smith, of smiths')
perchen: perchen (perchen) — owner, possessor; noun m. (o perchen geuel a mwrthwl 'of owner of tongs and hammer'); not softened after o here (the Red Book has oberchen)
geuel: gefel (gefel) — tongs, pincers; noun f. (perchen geuel 'owner of tongs'); no mutation
mwrthwl: mwrthwl (morthwyl) — hammer; noun m. (geuel a mwrthwl 'tongs and hammer'); no mutation
kyuuch: kyuuch (cyfuwch) — as high as; equative of uchel 'high' (kyuuch a chrib yr ystauell 'as high as the ridge of the chamber'); no mutation
chrib: crib (crib) — crest, ridge, comb; noun f., the roof-ridge; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'as' following the equative kyuuch (kyuuch a chrib yr ystauell)
lo: glo (glo) — coal, charcoal; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after o 'of' (o lo 'of charcoal')
guassanaethu: gwasanaethu (gwasanaethu) — to serve, wait on; verbal noun (pheri guassanaethu 'causing to be served'); gu- for gw-; no mutation shown
diwall: diwall (diwall) — without want, provided, abundant; adjective (yn diwall o uwyt a llyn 'abundantly of food and drink'); no mutation shown after yn (the soft form ddiwall is not written)
phlant: plant (plant) — children; plural noun m.; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after the possessive y 'her' (a'y phlant 'and her children')
wybuwyt: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; impersonal preterite 'was known' in -wyt (phan wybuwyt eu medwi 'when their drunkenness was known'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after pan 'when'
medwi: medwi (meddwi) — to get drunk; verbal noun (eu medwi 'their getting drunk'); no mutation
dechreuwyt: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; impersonal preterite 'was begun' in -wyt (y dechreuwyt kymyscu y tan 'the mixing of the fire was begun'); no mutation after the particle y
kymyscu: kymyscu (cymysgu) — to mix, mingle; verbal noun (kymyscu y tan a'r glo 'mixing the fire and the charcoal'); no mutation
tan: tan (tân) — fire; noun m. (y tan a'r glo 'the fire and the charcoal'); no mutation
glo: glo (glo) — coal, charcoal; noun m. (y tan a'r glo 'the fire and the charcoal'); no mutation
chwythu: chwythu (chwythu) — to blow; verbal noun (a chwythu y megineu 'and blowing the bellows'); no mutation (chw- has no spirant form after a)
megineu: megin (megin) — bellows; plural megineu (meginau); noun f.; no mutation (after the article y)
uegin: megin (megin) — bellows; noun f.; soft-mutated (m>u) after dwy 'two' (pob dwy uegin 'every two bellows')
burwen: purwyn (purwyn) — pure white, gleaming white; adjective, pur 'pure' + gwynn 'white', feminine form purwen; soft-mutated (p>b) after predicative yn (yny uyd y ty yn burwen 'until the house is white-hot')
ymherued: perued (perfedd) — middle, centre; noun m., with the nasal mutation (p>mh) after yn 'in' (ymherued llawr yr ystauell 'in the middle of the floor of the chamber')
arhoes: arhoi (aros) — to wait, stay; 3 sg. preterite 'waited' (yd arhoes ef 'he waited'); no mutation (vowel)
pleit: pleit (plaid) — wall, side, partition; noun f. (y pleit haearn 'the iron wall'); no mutation
wres: gwres (gwres) — heat; noun m.; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preceding adjective diruawr (rac diruawr wres 'for huge heat')
kyrchwys: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, charge at; 3 sg. preterite 'made for' in -wys (y kyrchwys y bleit 'he charged the wall'); no mutation after the particle y
bleit: pleit (plaid) — wall, side, partition; noun f.; soft-mutated (p>b) after the feminine article y (y bleit 'the wall')
dieghis: dianc (dianc) — to flee, escape; 3 sg. preterite 'escaped' in -is (neb ny dieghis 'no one escaped'); no mutation shown after ny
tebygu: tebygu (tebygu) — to suppose, think; verbal noun (o'm tebygu i 'by my supposing'); no mutation
uendigeiduran: Proper name — Bendigeidfran; spelling with -d; soft-mutated (b>u) after the preposition wrth 'to' (wrth Uendigeiduran 'to Bendigeidfran') · also soft as object of a finite verb (y cauas Uendigeiduran 'where he found Bendigeidfran') · also soft as the agent after a verbal noun with o 'by' (galw o Uendigeiduran y mab 'Bendigeidfran calling the boy'; A chael o Uendigeiduran hi 'and Bendigeidfran taking her'), after y gan 'from' (Y gan Uendigeiduran 'from Bendigeidfran') and as subject after a verb (no phan uuassei Uendigeiduran yn uyw 'than when Bendigeidfran had been alive')
drwod: drwod (drosodd) — across, over; adverb (y doeth ef drwod attat ti 'he came across to you'); no mutation
attat: at (at) + ti — 'to you'; conjugated preposition, 2 sg. (y doeth ef drwod attat ti 'he came across to you'); no mutation
roes: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. preterite 'gave' (y roes y peir 'he gave the cauldron'); no mutation after the particle y
erbynneisti: erbyn (derbyn) — to receive; 2 sg. preterite 'you received' (erbynneist) with ti 'you' run into it (erbynneisti wynteu 'did you receive them?'); no mutation after yd
maent: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present 'they are' (y maent yn lluossauc 'they are numerous'); no mutation
lluossauc: lluossauc (lluosog) — numerous, many; adjective (yn lluossauc 'numerous'); no mutation (ll- is not mutated after predicative yn)
uann: mann (man) — place, spot; noun f.; soft-mutated (m>u) after the feminine article y (y uann y bythont 'the place where they are')
bythont: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present habitual 'they are (wont to be)' (y uann y bythont 'where they are'); no mutation after the particle y
cherd: cerdd (cerdd) — song, music, minstrelsy; noun f.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' (a cherd a chyuedach 'and song and carousing')
niwed: diwed (diwedd) — end, close; noun m.; nasal-mutated (d>n) after yn 'in' (yn niwed hynny 'at the end of that, after that')
branuen: Proper name — Branwen, daughter of Llŷr, sister of Bendigeidfran; radical, no mutation (in apposition after the subject: Matholwch, a Branuen y gyt ac ef)
abermenei: Proper name — Aber Menai, the landing-place on the Menai Strait; no mutation (vowel after o 'from')
kychwynnyssant: kychwyn (cychwyn) — to set out, depart; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they set out' (y kychwynnyssant teir llong ar dec 'they set out, thirteen ships'); radical after the particle y
dirwawr: dirwawr (dirfawr) — huge, vast, exceeding great; adjective placed before its noun (dirwawr lywenyd 'huge gladness'), which it softens
wrthunt: wrth (wrth) + wynt — 'to, at, towards them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (a uu wrthunt 'there was to them'); no mutation
doey: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. imperfect 'used to come, would come' (Ny doey wr mawr 'no great man would come'); the soft mutation of wr after it is the subject following the verb
rodei: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. imperfect 'she would give' (ni rodei hi 'she would not give'); mutation of rh- not visible in spelling
cae: cae (cae) — a brooch, clasp (modern cae is 'field, enclosure'; here a fastening worn as a gift-jewel); noun m.; no mutation (after ae 'either')
modrwy: modrwy (modrwy) — ring, finger-ring; noun f.; no mutation (after ae 'or')
teyrndlws: teyrndlws (no modern form; teyrn 'sovereign' + tlws 'jewel') — a royal jewel, a kingly gem; noun m.; tlws softened to dlws inside the compound; rare, exact sense uncertain
cadwedic: cadwedic (cadwedig) — kept, preserved, treasured; adjective following its noun (teyrndlws cadwedic 'a treasured royal jewel')
arbennic: arbennic (arbennig) — special, chief, notable, of note; adjective, predicative after a uei (a uei arbennic y welet 'that was a notable thing to see')
ymysc: ymysc (ymysg) — among, amid; preposition; ymysc hynny 'meanwhile, amid that'
glotuawr: clotuawr (clodfawr) — renowned, much praised (clot 'fame' + mawr 'great'); adjective, soft-mutated (c>g) after predicative yn (yn glotuawr 'renowned')
hwyl: hwyl (hwyl) — course, progress, state, fortune (also 'sail'); noun f.; here 'a (fair) course'; meaning uncertain in a hwyl delediw 'and a fair course'; no mutation (h-)
delediw: telediw (telediw) — comely, fair, seemly; adjective, soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine noun hwyl (hwyl delediw 'a comely course')
glot: clot (clod) — praise, fame, renown; noun m.; soft-mutated (c>g) after the preposition o 'of' (o glot 'of renown')
damweinwys: damweinio (damweinio) — to happen, befall, chance; 3 sg. preterite 'it happened'; mutation (d>dd) after a not visible (beichogi a damweinwys idi 'it befell her to conceive')
gael: caffael (cael) — to get, have; verbal noun, soft-mutated (c>g) after the possessive y 'its' (beichogi … y gael 'pregnancy, its getting' = to conceive)
amseroyd: amser (amser) — time, season, term; noun m., plural amseroyd (amseroedd) 'times' (yr amseroyd dylyedus 'the due times'); no mutation after the article yr
dylyedus: dylyedus (dyledus) — due, owing, proper; adjective following its plural noun (yr amseroyd dylyedus 'the due times')
guern: Proper name — Gwern, son of Matholwch and Branwen (also gwern 'alder'); radical, no mutation (after Sef enw a dodet ar y mab, as predicate) · also the first word of the obscure cry Guern gwngwch uiwch Uordwyt Tyllyon, where the name is clear and the rest is not
ymodwrd: ymodwrd (no modern form) — murmuring, talk, rumour, stir; noun m.; meaning uncertain; after llyma 'behold' (llyma ymodwrd 'behold, a stir')
guaradwyd: gwaradwydd (gwaradwydd) — shame, insult, disgrace; noun m., spelt guaradwyd; after the article y 'the' (y guaradwyd), no mutation
kymry: Kymry (Cymru) — Wales (strictly the Welsh, Cymry, here the country); proper name; the nasal mutation of yg Kymry 'in Wales' (yng Nghymru) is shown only on the preceding yg · also kymryt (cymryd) 'to take', verbal noun written kymry without the t, a scribal slip (kymry llywenyd 'taking joy')
somm: som (siom) — deceit, trick; noun (a'r somm a wnathoedit idaw 'and the trick that had been played on him'); no mutation (s-)
wnathoedit: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. impersonal pluperfect (-oedit) 'had been done' (y somm a wnathoedit idaw 'the insult that had been done to him'); soft-mutated (g lost) after relative a
urodyr: brawt (brawd) — brother; plural brodyr; soft-mutated (b>u) after possessive y 'his' (y urodyr maeth 'his foster-brothers')
nessaf: nessaf (nesaf) — nearest, next; superlative of agos 'near'; adjective following its noun (gwyr nessaf gantaw 'men nearest to him')
lliwaw: lliwaw (lliwio) — to colour; also to reproach, cast up against, taunt (yn lliwaw idaw hynny 'reproaching him with that'); verbal noun after yn, no mutation
gelu: celu (celu) — to hide, conceal; verbal noun, soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'it' (heb y gelu 'without concealing it')
lonyd: llonyd (llonydd) — quiet, rest, peace; noun m., soft-mutated (ll>l) as the noun directly following the verb oed (nat oed lonyd idaw 'there was no peace for him')
chaei: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might get' (ony chaei dial 'unless he got vengeance'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ony 'unless' · also 3 sg. imperfect 'would get', spirant-mutated after na 'that … not' (na chaei chwedleu 'that he would not get tidings')
sarahet: sarhaet (sarhad) — insult, injury, dishonour; noun m.; no mutation (s-), 'his insult' after y 'his'
chymell: kymell (cymell) — to urge, compel, force; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after y 'her' (a'y chymell 'and to force her') · also spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chymell y morynyon allan 'and driving the maidens out')
bobi: pobi (pobi) — to bake; verbal noun, soft-mutated (p>b) after y 'to' (y bobi yn y llys 'to bake in the court')
kygyd: kigyd (cigydd) — butcher; noun m.; no mutation after the article (y'r kygyd 'to the butcher')
dryllyaw: dryllyaw (dryllio) — to break up, cut in pieces, chop; verbal noun after yn (yn dryllyaw kic 'chopping meat'); no mutation shown
kic: kic (cig) — meat, flesh; noun m. (-c = g); object of the verbal noun, no mutation
bonclust: bonclust (bonclust) — a box on the ear, cuff, slap (bon 'base' + clust 'ear'); noun m., object of the verbal noun tharaw, no mutation
foen: poen (poen) — pain, torment, punishment; noun; spirant-mutated (p>ph, written f) after y 'her' (y gwnaethpwyt y foen 'her punishment was carried out'); compare a fawb for a phawb
par: peri (peri) — to cause, command, have done; 2 sg. imperative 'cause!, have!' (par wahard 'have forbidden')
weithon: weithon (weithian) — now, at last; adverb, always in this softened form (gweith 'time' + hon 'this'); par weithon wahard 'have (them) forbidden now'
wahard: gwahard (gwahardd) — to forbid, prohibit; verbal noun (par wahard y llongeu 'have the ships forbidden, forbid the ships'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the adverb weithon following par
yscraffeu: yscraff (ysgraff) — a small boat, skiff, barge; noun, plural yscraffeu; no mutation after the article 'r
corygeu: corwc (corwg) — a coracle, small round boat; noun m., plural corygeu; no mutation after 'r
gymry: Kymry (Cymru) — Wales; proper name; soft-mutated (c>g) after the preposition y 'to' (y Gymry 'to Wales')
carchara: carcharu (carcharu) — to imprison, put in prison; 2 sg. imperative 'imprison!' (carchara wynt 'imprison them'); no mutation (c- radical as the verb stands first)
ua: ua (no modern form) — a scribal form of uncertain sense in carchara wynt ua na at trachefyn; the Red Book has 'hyt nat elont', so perhaps 'and' (a/ac) or 'so that'; meaning uncertain
trachefyn: trachefyn (trachefn) — back, again, backwards; adverb (na at trachefyn 'and do not let (them) back'); the modern form is archaic
diskynyssant: diskynnu (disgyn) — to descend, alight; here 'settle on, agree' (cf. disgyn ar 'decide on'); 3 pl. preterite in -yssant (ac ar hynny y diskynyssant 'and on that they settled'); radical after the particle y
blwynyded: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; plural blwynyded (blynyddoedd) 'years'; noun f., no mutation (first word of the clause)
llei: llei (llai) — less, fewer; comparative of bach; predicative (nit llei no their 'not fewer than three')
their: teir (tair) — three (f.); numeral, spelt their; spirant-mutated (t>th) after no 'than' (nit llei no their 'not less than three')
ederyn: ederyn (aderyn) — bird; noun m.; object of the verbal noun meithryn, no mutation (vowel)
drydwen: drudwen (drudwen) — starling; noun f., the singular of drudwy, here spelt drydwen, in apposition to ederyn (ederyn drydwen 'a starling bird'); d- radical; the identification is not certain
noe: noe (noe) — a trough, kneading-trough; noun f.; no mutation (n- after the article y)
dyscu: dyscu (dysgu) — to teach; verbal noun (a dyscu ieith idi 'and teaching it speech'); no mutation (d- after a 'and')
ieith: ieith (iaith) — language, speech; noun f. (dyscu ieith 'teaching speech'); no mutation
llythyr: llythyr (llythyr) — letter, writing; noun m.; no mutation (ll- after the article y)
poeneu: poen (poen) — pain, torment, punishment; noun, plural poeneu 'torments'; no mutation
amharch: amharch (amharch) — disrespect, contempt, dishonour; noun m. (y poeneu a'r amharch 'the pains and the dishonour')
rwymwyt: rhwymo (rhwymo) — to bind, tie; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was bound' (a rwymwyt am uon eskyll 'was bound around the base of the wings'); soft-mutated (rh>r) after relative a
uon: bon (bôn) — base, stump, root; noun m.; soft-mutated (b>u) after the preposition am 'about, around' (am uon eskyll 'around the base of the wings')
eskyll: asgell (asgell) — wing; the plural esgyll 'wings' (eskyll yr ederyn 'the bird's wings'); noun, no mutation
chymry: Kymry (Cymru) — Wales; proper name; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after parth a 'towards' (parth a Chymry 'towards Wales')
cauas: caffael (cael) — to get, find; 3 sg. preterite 'found' (Sef lle y cauas Uendigeiduran 'the place where it [the bird] found Bendigeidfran'); radical after the particle y
kaer: caer (caer) — fortress, walled town, fort; noun f., first element of the place-name Kaer Seint 'Caer Seint'
seint: Proper name — Seint (Seiont), second element of Kaer Seint (Caer Seiont), the Roman fort of Segontium by Caernarfon; no mutation
aruon: Proper name — Arfon, the cantref across the Menai Strait from Môn; no mutation (vowel after yn 'in')
dadleu: dadleu (dadlau) — to plead, hold pleas, hold court (of law); verbal noun after yn (yn dadleu idaw dydgweith 'holding court one day')
dydgweith: dydgweith (no modern form) — one day, on a day; dyd 'day' + gweith 'time', adverbial (yn dadleu idaw dydgweith 'debating one day')
diskynnu: diskynnu (disgyn) — to descend, alight; verbal noun (a diskynnu ar e yscwyd 'and alighting on his shoulder')
garwhau: garwhau (garwhau) — to roughen, ruffle; verbal noun, garw 'rough' + -hau (garwhau y phluf 'ruffling her feathers')
phluf: pluf (pluf) — feather, plumage; noun f., spirant-mutated (p>ph) after y 'her' (y phluf 'her feathers')
arganuuwyt: arganuot (arganfod) — to perceive, discover; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was perceived, was found' (yny arganuuwyt y llythyr 'until the letter was seen')
adnabot: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise; verbal noun (adnabot meithryn yr ederyn 'recognising the nursing of the bird')
darllewyt: darllein (darllen) — to read; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was read' (A phan darllewyt y llythyr 'and when the letter was read')
glybot: clybot (clywed) — to hear; verbal noun, soft-mutated (c>g) after o 'from' (o glybot 'from hearing')
dygyuoryaw: dygyuoryaw (no distinct modern form; cf. dygyfor 'muster') — to muster, gather; verbal noun (y dygyuoryaw yr ynys honn y gyt 'to muster this island together')
peris: peri (peri) — to cause, command; 3 sg. preterite 'he caused' (y peris ef dyuot 'he had come'); radical after the particle y
llwyr: llwyr (llwyr) — whole, entire, complete; adjective before its noun (llwyr wys 'the whole host'), which it softens
wys: gwys (gwŷs) — summons, muster, host; noun f./m.; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preceding adjective llwyr
pedeir: pedeir (pedair) — four (f.); numeral, in pedeir degwlat 'four ten-lands'
degwlat: degwlat (deg 'ten' + gwlat 'land, country') — 'ten lands'; gwlat softened (g lost) in the compound; pedeir degwlat a seithugeint is most easily 'fourteen lands and seven score' = 154, but the Red Book has pedeir gwlat a seith ugeint (144); the reckoning is uncertain
seithugeint: seithugeint (saith ugain) — seven score, 140; numeral (seith 'seven' + ugeint 'twenty')
seithwyr: seithwyr (saith gŵr) — seven men, a company of seven; seith + gwyr (adaw seithwyr 'to leave seven men'); modern has saith gŵr
dywyssogyon: tywyssauc (tywysog) — leader, prince; plural tywyssogyon (tywysogion) 'princes'; soft-mutated (t>d) after y 'to, for' = 'as' (adaw seithwyr y dywyssogyon 'leaving seven men as princes')
chradawc: Proper name — Caradog (Cradawc), son of Bran; spirant-mutated (C>Ch) after a 'and' (a Chradawc uab Bran)
bran: Proper name — Bran (Bendigeidfran), father of Caradog; radical, no mutation (after uab: patronymic leaves the father's name unmutated)
benhaf: pennaf (pennaf) — chief, foremost; superlative formed from penn 'head'; soft-mutated (p>b) after y 'as' (a Chradawc uab Bran y benhaf 'and Caradog son of Brân as chief') and after predicative yn (yn benhaf kynweisyat 'as chiefest steward')
edeirnon: Proper name — Edeirnion, a commote in north-east Wales (in the Dee valley); no mutation (vowel after yn 'in')
dref: tref (tref) — town, homestead, settlement; noun f., soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (ar y dref 'on the town') · also soft after holl (yn yr holl dref 'in the whole town') and after y 'to' (y dref arall 'to another town')
cradawc: Proper name — Caradog (Cradawc), son of Bran, chief of the seven left behind; radical, no mutation (subject or in apposition)
euehyd: Proper name — Efeydd (Euehyd) Hir 'Efeydd the Tall', one of the Seven; radical, no mutation
walltgrwn: Proper name (epithet) — Walltgrwn 'Round-hair' (gwallt 'hair' + crwn 'round'), epithet of Anarawc; soft-mutated (g>w) after the personal name Anarawc
fodor: Proper name — Ffodor son of Erfyll, one of the Seven; F written for ff (/f/), as in a fawb; ff does not change after a 'and' (a Fodor; the Red Book a ffodor)
eruyll: Proper name — Erfyll, father of Fodor; radical after uab
wlch: Proper name — Wlch Minasgwrn, one of the Seven; the name is written so in both manuscripts (ac Wlch), and a 'and' causes no softening; its origin is uncertain
minasgwrn: Proper name (epithet) — Minasgwrn, of Wlch; perhaps min 'edge, lip' + asgwrn 'bone', but meaning uncertain
llashar: Proper name — Llashar (Llasar), son of Llayssar, one of the Seven; radical
llayssar: Proper name — Llayssar (Llasar), father of Llashar; radical after uab
llaesgygwyt: Proper name (epithet) — Llaesgygwyt, of Llayssar; llaes 'long, loose, slack' + gygwyt (soft of cygwyd?); meaning uncertain
phendaran: Proper name — Pendaran Dyfed, Pryderi's foster-father in the First Branch, here a young lad with the Seven; spirant-mutated (P>Ph) after a 'and' (a Phendaran Dyuet)
ieuanc: ieuanc (ifanc) — young; adjective following its noun (yn was ieuanc 'as a young lad')
drigwys: trigo (trigo) — to dwell, stay, remain; 3 sg. preterite 'stayed'; soft-mutated (t>d) after relative a (Y seith hynny a drigwys 'those seven stayed')
kynueissat: kynweissyat (cynweisiad) — chief officer, steward; noun m., spelt kynueissat; after seith (yn seith kynueissat 'as seven stewards'), no mutation; the noun is singular after a numeral
synyaw: synyaw (synio) — to take thought, take heed, take charge (of); verbal noun (y synyaw ar yr ynys honn 'to look after this island'); sense approximate
kynweisyat: kynweissyat (cynweisiad) — chief officer, steward; noun m. (yn benhaf kynweisyat arnunt 'as chiefest steward over them'); no mutation
dywedyssam: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 1 pl. preterite 'we said, we told' (a dywedyssam ni 'which we told of'); mutation after relative a not visible
hwylyssant: hwylyaw (hwylio) — to sail, set out; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they sailed'
ueis: beis (no common modern form) — shallow water, ford; noun; soft-mutated (b>u) after y 'to' (y ueis yd aeth ef 'wading he went'; yn dyuot y ueis 'coming wading'); mynet y ueis 'go wading'
auon: afon (afon) — river; noun f. (dwy auon 'two rivers'); no mutation (vowel)
lli: Proper name — Lli, one of the two rivers of the strait (Lli ac Archan); radical
archan: Proper name — Archan, the other of the two rivers (Lli ac Archan y gelwit 'Lli and Archan they were called'); radical
amlawys: amlau (amlhau) — to increase, grow greater; 3 sg. preterite 'grew, rose' (yd amlawys y weilgi 'the sea grew')
oreskynwys: goresgyn (goresgyn) — to overcome, overrun, conquer; 3 sg. preterite 'overran'; soft-mutated (g lost) after pan 'when' (pan oreskynwys y weilgi 'when the sea overran')
tyrnassoed: teyrnas (teyrnas) — kingdom, realm; plural tyrnassoed (teyrnasoedd) 'kingdoms'; object, no mutation (after the article y)
kerdwys: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go, travel; 3 sg. preterite 'walked' (y kerdwys ef 'he went about'); radical after particle y
gerd: kerd (cerdd) — art, music, song; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after o 'of' (o gerd arwest 'of the art of music') · also soft after ryw 'some kind of' (ryw gerd 'some song')
arwest: arwest (arwest) — string (of an instrument); noun (ac a oed o gerd arwest 'and all there was of string-music'); the exact sense is uncertain
meicheit: meichat (meichiad) — swineherd; plural meicheit 'swineherds'; noun, no mutation (first word after A 'and')
lan: glan (glan) — bank, shore; noun f., soft-mutated (g lost) after ar 'on' (ar lan y weilgi 'on the shore of the sea')
moch: moch (moch) — pigs; collective plural of mochyn 'pig' (eu moch 'their pigs'); no mutation
dremynt: tremynt (no modern form; cf. trem 'look') — a sight, spectacle; noun m.; written softened (t>d) with no visible cause: Evans prints no e 'the' before it (the second witness's e dremynt would explain it) (o achaws dremynt 'because of a sight') · also soft-mutated (t>d) after a preceding adjective, the cause there (A fell dremynt oed udunt y guelet 'and a far sight it was for them to see', fell = pell 'far')
henpych: hanbot (hanfod) — to be; henpych is the 2 sg. present subjunctive 'may you be', surviving in the greeting henpych guell 'may you be better' = hail to you
genhwch: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 2 pl. 'with you' (a chwedleu genhwch 'and have you tidings')
genhym: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 1 pl. 'with us' (mae genhym ni chwedleu 'we have tidings')
rywelsom: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 pl. preterite 'we saw'; with the perfective particle ry (coet rywelsom 'a wood we have seen'); ry causes soft mutation (g lost)
prenn: prenn (pren) — tree, wood; noun m. (un prenn 'a single tree'); no mutation
welewch: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 pl. imperfect 'were you seeing, did you see'; soft-mutated (g lost) after the interrogative particle a (A welewch wchi dim namyn hynny? 'did you see anything but that?')
wchi: chwi (chi) — you (pl.); wchi is a variant spelling of the pronoun, here affixed after the verb (A welewch wchi dim 'did you see anything?')
gwelem: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 pl. imperfect 'we saw, we were seeing' (Gwelem, Arglwyd 'we did, Lord'), answering the question with the verb; no mutation
mynyd: mynyd (mynydd) — mountain; noun m. (mynyd mawr 'a great mountain'); no mutation
eskeir: esgeir (esgair) — ridge, long hill, leg; noun f. (eskeir aruchel 'a lofty ridge')
wypo: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may know' (neb a wypo dim 'anyone who may know anything'); soft-mutated (g lost) after relative a
onys: ony (oni) + 's 'it' — unless, if not (onys gwyr 'unless she knows it'); ony with infixed object pronoun s
gouynnwch: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 2 pl. imperative 'ask!' (gouynnwch idi 'ask her')
dybygy: tybygu (tybio) — to think, suppose; 2 sg. present 'you think' (beth dybygy di yw hynny 'what do you think that is?'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the interrogative beth
kedyrn: cadarn (cadarn) — strong, mighty; plural kedyrn (cedyrn) used as a noun, 'the mighty', in Ynys y Kedyrn 'the Island of the Mighty'; no mutation after the article
welat: gwelet (gweld) — to see; impersonal preterite in -at 'was seen' (y coet a welat 'the wood that was seen'); soft-mutated (g lost) after relative a
gwernenni: gwernen (gwernen) — alder tree, and so a ship's mast; plural gwernenni 'alders, masts' (gwernenni llongeu a hwylbrenni 'alders of the ships and masts')
hwylbrenni: hwylbren (hwylbren) — mast, sail-pole (hwyl 'sail' + prenn 'tree, wood', p softened to b in the compound); plural hwylbrenni
welit: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. impersonal imperfect 'was seen' (y mynyd a welit 'the mountain that was seen'); soft-mutated (g lost) after relative a
long: llong (llong) — ship; noun f.; soft-mutated (ll>l) as the noun directly following the verb oed (Nyt oed long 'there was no ship')
kynghanei: genni (genni) — to be contained, have room, fit; MW also gannu; kynghanei is the 3 sg. imperfect of its compound with kyn- (gh written for g, as in kynghor), 'he would fit' (Nyt oed long y kynghanei ef yndi 'there was no ship he would fit in'); the Red Book kyghanei; no mutation after the particle y
bop: pob (pob) — each, every; adjective, soft-mutated (p>b) after o 'from' (o bop parth 'from each side')
llidyawc: llidyawc (llidiog) — angry, wrathful; adjective, predicative (llidyawc yw 'he is angry')
lygat: llygat (llygad) — eye; noun m., soft-mutated (ll>l) after deu 'two' (y deu lygat 'his two eyes')
drwyn: trwyn (trwyn) — nose; noun m., soft-mutated (t>d) after y 'his' (y drwyn 'his nose')
uorbennyd: morbennyd (no modern form) — a rare word, apparently 'great chiefs' (mawr 'great' + penn 'head'), though mor 'sea' + penn has also been thought of; plural; soft-mutated (m>u) after holl 'all' (a'r holl uorbennyd 'and all the great chiefs'); uncertain
gymerwyt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was taken' (kynghor a gymerwyt 'counsel was taken'); soft-mutated (k>g) after relative a
kilyaw: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat, withdraw, fall back; verbal noun (nyt oes gynghor namyn kilyaw 'there is no counsel but to retreat')
linon: Proper name — Llinon, a river of Ireland (modern Llinon); soft-mutated (Ll>L) after the preposition drwy 'through' (drwy Linon)
llinon: Proper name — Llinon, the river; radical, object of the verbal noun gadu 'to leave' (gadu Llinon)
bont: pont (pont) — bridge; noun f.; soft-mutated (p>b) after the feminine article y (y bont), after am 'about, for' (am bont), and directly after oes (nyt oes bont 'there is no bridge')
sugyn: sugyn (cf. sugno 'to suck') — sucking, drawing in; mein sugyn 'sucking stones', perhaps lodestones or stones that hold ships fast; meaning uncertain
gwaelawt: gwaelawt (gwaelod) — bottom, base; noun m., preceded by y(n) 'in' (y gwaelawt yr auon 'at the bottom of the river'); the nasal mutation after yn is not shown in the spelling
llestyr: llestyr (llestr) — vessel, boat; noun m. (na llong na llestyr 'neither ship nor vessel')
gylyssant: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they withdrew'; soft-mutated (c>g) after a (Wynt a gylyssant 'they it was that withdrew')
torryssant: torri (torri) — to break; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they broke' (ac a torryssant y bont 'and broke the bridge'); left unsoftened after the relative a, where a dorryssant would be expected (the Red Book too has a torrassant)
llynghes: llynghes (llynges) — fleet; noun f. (a llynghes y gyt ac ef 'and a fleet together with him'); no mutation
glann: glann (glan) — bank, shore; noun f. (parth a glann yr auon 'towards the bank of the river'); no mutation (g not affected by spirant mutation after a 'towards')
wdost: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 2 sg. present 'you know' (ti a wdost 'you know'); soft-mutated (g lost) after the particle a
kennedyf: kynnedyf (cynneddf) — nature, property, characteristic; noun f. (kennedyf yr auon 'the nature of the river'); no mutation
drwydi: trwy (trwy) — through; conjugated preposition 3 sg. f. 'through it' (the river is feminine) (ny eill neb uynet drwydi 'no one can go through it'); MW often writes the preposition with d- (drwy) where no mutation is due, as drwy Linon
pont: pont (pont) — bridge; noun f., here as a predicate noun, radical (a uo penn bit pont 'whoever is chief, let him be a bridge'; Mi a uydaf pont 'I shall be a bridge')
dywetpwyt: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was said' (y dywetpwyt y geir hwnnw 'that word was said'); radical after particle y
diharebir: diharebu (cf. dihareb 'proverb') — to use as a proverb; 3 sg. impersonal present 'is made a proverb, is quoted' (y diharebir etwa 'it is still quoted proverbially')
gorwed: gorwed (gorwedd) — to lie, lie down; verbal noun (guedy gorwed ohonaw 'after his lying down')
traws: traws (traws) — across, athwart, crosswise; noun/adjective in ar traws 'across' (ar traws yr auon 'across the river'); radical after ar · also y traws 'the quarter, the direction' (y traws y managassei ef 'the direction in which he had shown'); exact sense uncertain
byrwyt: bwrw (bwrw) — to cast, throw, lay; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was cast' (y byrwyt clwydeu arnaw 'hurdles were laid on him'); radical after particle y
clwydeu: clwyd (clwyd) — hurdle, wattle, gate; plural clwydeu 'hurdles'
luoed: lluoed (lluoedd) — hosts, armies; plural of llu; soft-mutated (ll>l) after y 'his' (y luoed 'his hosts')
draws: traws (traws) — across; soft-mutated (t>d) after y 'his' (ar y draws ef 'across him'); cf. ar traws
kyuodes: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; 3 sg. preterite 'rose' (gyt ac y kyuodes ef 'as soon as he rose'); radical after particle y
gennadeu: kennat (cennad) — messenger; plural kennadeu 'messengers'; soft-mutated (k>g) after llyma 'behold' (llyma gennadeu Matholwch 'behold Matholwch's messengers')
annerch: annerch (annerch) — to greet, address; verbal noun (yn y annerch 'greeting him')
gyuathrachwr: kyuathrachwr (no modern form given; cf. cyfathrach 'kinship') — kinsman, relation by marriage; noun m.; soft-mutated (k>g) after y 'his' (Matholwch y gyuathrachwr 'Matholwch, his kinsman')
haedei: haeddu (haeddu) — to deserve, merit; 3 sg. imperfect 'would deserve' (na haedei arnaw namyn da 'that he deserved only good from him'); no mutation (h)
brenhinaeth: brenhinaeth (brenhiniaeth) — kingship, kingdom, sovereignty; noun f. (rodi brenhinaeth Iwerdon 'giving the kingship of Ireland'); radical as object of the verbal noun
wern: Proper name — Gwern; soft-mutated (G>lost) after the preposition y 'to' (y Wern uab Matholwch 'to Gwern son of Matholwch')
nei: nei (nai) — nephew; noun m. (dy nei ditheu 'your nephew too'); no mutation
ystynnu: ystynnu (estyn) — to stretch, extend, hand over, confer; verbal noun (yn y ystynnu y'th wyd di 'conferring it in your presence')
codyant: codyant (codiant) — affliction, hurt, injury (cf. MW codi 'hurt, vex'); noun m. (y cam a'r codyant 'the wrong and the hurt')
gossymdeitha: gossymdeithaw (no modern form) — to maintain, provide a living for; 2 sg. imperative 'maintain!, provide for!' (yn y lle y mynnych ditheu … gossymdeitha Uatholwch 'wherever you wish … provide for Matholwch'); the exact force here is uncertain
ue: uy (fy) — my; possessive, spelt ue; ue hun 'myself' (ony allaf i ue hun cael 'unless I myself can get')
urenhinaeth: brenhinaeth (brenhiniaeth) — kingship, kingdom; noun f.; soft-mutated (b>u) after the feminine article y (cael y urenhinaeth 'to get the kingship') and after dy 'your' (dy urenhinaeth 'your kingdom')
aduyd: aduyd (no modern form) — perhaps; adverb (ac aduyd ys kymeraf gynghor 'and perhaps I will take counsel'); the Red Book writes atuyd; its make-up is uncertain
kymeraf: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 sg. present 'I take, I shall take' (ys kymeraf gynghor 'I shall take counsel')
kennadwri: kennadwri (cenhadwri) — message, embassy, errand; noun f. (am ych kennadwri chwi 'about your message')
cheffwch: caffael (cael) — to get; 2 pl. present/future 'you will get'; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ny (ny cheffwch 'you shall not get')
gaffom: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 pl. present subjunctive 'we may get' (a gaffom ninheu 'that we may get'); soft-mutated (c>g) after relative a
aro: aros (aros) — to wait, await; 2 sg. imperative 'wait!' (aro ditheu yn kennadwri ninheu 'wait you for our message')
dowch: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 pl. present 'you come' (o dowch 'if you come'); after o 'if'
ehegyr: ehegyr (no modern form) — probably 'swift, ready' (o dowch yn ehegyr 'if you come quickly'); rare, meaning uncertain; the Red Book has yn ebrwyd 'quickly' instead
racdu: racdu (rhagddo) — onward, forward; rac 'before' conjugated, used as an adverb (a gyrchyssant racdu 'went on their way')
kyweira: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to put in order, prepare, arrange; 2 sg. imperative 'prepare!' (kyweira attep 'make ready an answer')
gwell: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good' (a uo gwell 'which may be better')
uendigeidwran: Proper name — Bendigeidfran; spelling -dwran for -deiduran; soft-mutated (B>u) after the preposition at 'to' (at Uendigeidwran 'to Bendigeidfran')
warandawei: gwarandaw (gwrando) — to listen, hear, heed; 3 sg. imperfect 'would listen'; soft-mutated (g>w) after ny 'not' (Ny warandawei dim 'he would hear nothing')
enghis: genni (genni) — to be contained, have room, fit; MW also gannu; 3 sg. preterite genghis (stem gang-, a > e before -is) 'was held, fitted', soft-mutated (g lost) after Ni (Ni enghis ef y mywn ty eiryoet 'he has never fitted inside a house'); compare ny angassei; the Red Book nyt eigwys
ganho: genni (genni) — to be contained, have room, fit; MW also gannu; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may fit' (y ganho ef a gwyr Ynys y Kedyrn yn y neill parth 'that he and the men of the Island of the Mighty may fit in the one side'); radical: the particle y causes no mutation; the Red Book y geingho
doro: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 2 sg. imperative doro (= dyro) 'give!' (A doro dy urenhinaeth yn y ewyllus 'and give your kingship into his will')
ewyllus: ewyllus (ewyllys) — will, desire, pleasure; noun m. (yn y ewyllus 'in his will')
gwra: gwrhau (gwrhau) — to do homage, become someone's man (gwr 'man'); 2 sg. imperative 'do homage!' (gwra idaw 'do homage to him')
ganhei: genni (genni) — to be contained, have room, fit; MW also gannu; 3 sg. imperfect 'could fit' (ty y ganhei yndaw 'a house he could fit in'); radical after the particle y; the Red Book y geinghei
tangnoueda: tangnouedu (tangnefeddu) — to make peace, be reconciled (tangneued 'peace'); 3 sg. present with future sense 'will make peace' (ef a tangnoueda a thi 'he will make peace with you'); left unsoftened after the relative a, where a dangnoueda would be expected (the Red Book too has a tangneuedha)
gennadwri: kennadwri (cenhadwri) — message, errand; noun f., soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article 'r (a'r gennadwri honno 'and that message')
gantunt: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'with them' (a'r gennadwri honno gantunt 'with that message with them')
thrwy: trwy (trwy) — through, by; preposition, spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and' (a thrwy gynghor Branuen 'and by the counsel of Branwen')
adeilwyt: adeilu (adeiladu) — to build; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was built' (y ty a adeilwyt 'the house was built')
braf: praff (praff) — thick, stout, massive; adjective, soft-mutated (p>b) after predicative yn, with f written for ff (yn uawr ac yn braf 'great and stout'; the Red Book yn braff); not modern braf 'fine'
ystryw: ystryw (ystryw) — trick, ruse, stratagem; noun f. (Ac ystryw a wnaeth y Gwydyl 'and the Irish made a stratagem')
gwydyl: Gwyddel (Gwyddel) — an Irishman; plural Gwydyl 'the Irish'; no mutation after y 'the'
guanas: gwanas (no modern form) — a peg, hook or nail for hanging (guanas o bop parth y bop colouyn 'a peg on each side of each pillar'); meaning approximate; no mutation
colouyn: colouyn (colofn) — pillar, column; noun f.; radical after bop 'each' (y bop colouyn 'to each pillar')
cant: cant (cant) — hundred; numeral (o cant colouyn 'of the hundred pillars'); left unsoftened after o, where gant would be expected (the Red Book too)
boly: boly (bol) — belly, hence a bag; noun m. (boly croyn 'a skin bag'); the unmutated singular
croyn: croen (croen) — skin, hide, leather; noun m., spelt croyn; singular used as a genitive, 'of skin' (boly croyn 'a skin-bag')
efnyssyen: Proper name — Efnysien (Efnyssyen), half-brother of Bendigeidfran; radical, no mutation (subject after Sef a wnaeth)
ymlaen: ymlaen (ymlaen) — forward, in front, ahead; adverb/preposition (ymlaen llu 'before the host')
llu: llu (llu) — host, army; noun m.; radical after ymlaen (ymlaen llu 'in front of the host')
golygon: golygon (golygon) — looks, glances; plural of golwg 'sight, look'; cognate object of edrych (edrych golygon orwyllt 'giving wild looks')
orwyllt: gorwyllt (gorwyllt) — very wild, fierce (gor- + gwyllt 'wild'); adjective, g- lost by soft mutation after golygon; cause unclear (perhaps predicative to edrych)
antrugarawc: antrugarawc (anhrugarog) — merciless, ruthless; adjective (golygon orwyllt antrugarawc 'wild, ruthless looks')
arganuot: arganuot (arganfod) — to perceive, discover; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaeth (arganuot y bolyeu crwyn a wnaeth 'perceiving the skin-bags he did')
bolyeu: boly (bol) — belly, bag; plural bolyeu 'bags' (y bolyeu crwyn 'the skin-bags')
crwyn: croen (croen) — skin, hide; plural crwyn 'skins', in apposition (bolyeu crwyn 'bags of skins')
pyst: post (post) — post, pillar; plural pyst 'posts' (ar hyt y pyst 'along the posts')
guydyl: Gwyddel (Gwyddel) — an Irishman; plural Gwydyl, here spelt guydyl (un o'r Guydyl 'one of the Irish')
blawt: blawt (blawd) — flour, meal; noun m. (Blawt, eneit 'flour, dear one')
deimlaw: teimlaw (teimlo) — to feel, touch, grope; verbal noun, soft-mutated (t>d) after the possessive y 'his' (y deimlaw 'his feeling' = feeling him, the man in the bag)
glyw: clybot (clywed) — to hear, feel; 3 sg. present 'feels' used of past events (yny glyw y uyssed 'until he feels his fingers'); soft-mutated (c>g) after yny 'until'
uyssed: bys (bys) — finger; plural byssed (bysedd) 'fingers'; soft-mutated (b>u) after y 'his' (y uyssed 'his fingers')
ymanodi: ymanodi (no modern form) — rare, apparently 'sink in' or 'meet together'; verbal noun after yn (yn ymanodi yn y ureichell 'sinking into the brain'); uncertain
ureichell: breichell (no modern form) — obscure, taken from the context as 'brain'; soft-mutated (b>u) after y 'his' (yn y ureichell 'in his brain'); the Red Book has vreithell (← breithell); uncertain
medei: medei (meddai) — said; defective verb 3 sg. imperfect, like heb used to tag speech (medei y Gwydel 'said the Irishman')
gwydel: Gwyddel (Gwyddel) — an Irishman; noun m. sg. (y Gwydel 'the Irishman'); no mutation
fawb: pawb (pawb) — everyone; pronoun, spelt fawb for phawb; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'with' (a fawb ohonunt 'with each of them')
hollwyr: hollwyr (no modern form; holl 'all' + gwyr 'men') — all the men, the whole company; plural compound (o'r hollwyr 'of the whole company')
cannwr: cannwr (no modern form; cant 'hundred' + gwr 'man') — hundred men; deu cannwr 'two hundred men'; the g of gwr is lost in the compound
guascassei: gwascu (gwasgu) — to crush, press; 3 sg. pluperfect 'he had crushed' (ual y guascassei 'as he had crushed')
benneu: penn (pen) — head; plural benneu (pennau) 'heads'; soft-mutated (p>b) as object of a finite verb (y guascassei benneu 'he had crushed the heads of')
ymedewis: ymadaw (ymadael) — to part from, leave; 3 sg. preterite 'left'; a>e by affection (Nyt ymedewis ef a hwnnw 'he did not part from him')
ladawd: lladd (lladd) — to kill; 3 sg. preterite 'killed'; soft-mutated (ll>l) after yny 'until' (yny ladawd 'until he killed him')
englyn: englyn (englyn) — an englyn, a short strict-metre verse; noun m. (canu englyn 'to sing a verse')
yssit: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present existential/relative 'is, there is' (yssit yn y boly 'there is in the bag'); variant of yssyd
amryw: amryw (amryw) — various, diverse, of many kinds; adjective before its noun (amryw ulawt 'various meal'), which it softens
ulawt: blawt (blawd) — flour, meal; noun m., soft-mutated (b>u) after the preceding adjective amryw
keimeit: keimyat (ceimiad) — champion, warrior; plural keimeit 'champions' (in the englyn); no mutation
kynniuyeit: kynniuyat (cynnifiad) — warrior, fighter (cf. cynnif 'battle, toil'); plural kynniuyeit; in the englyn, sense uncertain
diskynneit: diskynneit (no modern form) — probably those who descend or advance, assailants (cf. disgyn); plural; meaning uncertain
trin: trin (trin) — battle, combat, handling; noun f.; yn trin 'in battle' or 'engaging'; no nasal mutation shown
kydwyr: kydwyr (no modern form; cyd 'joint' + gwyr 'men') — comrades, allies; plural; rac kydwyr cad barawt 'against comrades ready for battle'; meaning approximate
cad: cad (cad) — battle, fight; noun f. (cad barawt 'ready for battle'); no mutation
dothyw: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. perfect dothyw 'has come, came', an old form (y dothyw y niueroed y'r ty 'the hosts came to the house'); radical after the particle y
ebrwydet: ebrwydd (ebrwydd) — swift, quick; equative ebrwydet 'as quick' (yn gyn ebrwydet ac 'as soon as')
duundeb: duundeb (duundeb) — agreement, concord (from duun 'agreed, at one'); noun m. (y bu duundeb y rydunt 'there was agreement between them')
rydunt: y rwng (rhwng) — between; conjugated 3 pl. 'between them' (y bu duundeb y rydunt 'there was concord between them')
ystynnwyt: ystynnu (estyn) — to stretch, extend, hand over, confer; impersonal preterite 'was conferred' (yd ystynnwyt y urenhinaeth y'r mab 'the kingship was conferred on the boy'); radical after the particle yd
galw: galw (galw) — to call, summon; verbal noun in narrative use (galw o Uendigeiduran y mab attaw 'Bendigeidfran called the boy to him'); no mutation (g- radical, opening the clause)
kyrchawd: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to go to, make for, approach; 3 sg. preterite in -awd 'went' (y kyrchawd y mab at Uanawydan 'the boy went to Manawydan'); radical after the particle y
garu: caru (caru) — to love; verbal noun, soft-mutated (c>g) after the possessive y 'his' (yn y garu 'loving him', 'in his loving')
gelwis: galw (galw) — to call; 3 sg. preterite 'called' in -is (y gelwis Nyssyen … y mab attaw 'Nisien called the boy to him'); a>e by vowel affection; radical after the particle y
nyssyen: Proper name — Nisien (ss for s), son of Euroswydd, brother of Efnysien, the peacemaker; radical, subject after y gelwis (E gan Uanawydan y gelwis Nyssyen … y mab attaw 'from Manawydan, Nisien called the boy to him')
diryon: tirion (tirion) — gentle, kind, gracious; adjective, soft-mutated (t>d) after predicative yn (yn diryon 'gently, kindly')
efnissyen: Proper name — Efnysien (ss for s), son of Euroswydd, half-brother of Bendigeidfran, the maker of quarrels; radical (heb yr Efnissyen 'said Efnysien'; pan welas Efnissyen 'when Efnysien saw')
daw: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. present 'comes' (na daw uy nei attaf i 'does my nephew not come to me?'); after na; d also spells dd, so any softening does not show
