ymtiryoni: ymdirioni (no modern form; cf. tirion 'gentle, kind') — to make friends, be on kindly terms (with a); reflexive ym- + tirion, verbal noun (da oed genhyf i ymtiryoni a'r mab 'I would be glad to make friends with the boy'); the t is left unsoftened after ym- (the Red Book ymdirioni)
anhebic: anhebic (annhebyg) — unlike, unlikely (an- 'not' + tebic 'like', the t nasalised to h); adjective, predicate after ys (ys anhebic 'it is unlikely'); the construction with the following a gyflauan is uncertain
tylwyth: tylwyth (tylwyth) — family, kindred, household; noun m.; no mutation after the article y
erwyd: herwyd (herwydd) — by, by (the hold of); preposition, written without h- (kymryt y mab erwyd y traet 'taking the boy by the feet'; the Red Book herwyd)
traet: troed (troed) — foot; noun, plural traet (traed) 'feet' (erwyd y traet 'by the feet'); radical after the article y
ohir: gohir (gohir) — delay, tarrying; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after heb 'without' (heb ohir 'without delay')
want: gwanu (gwanu) — to thrust, pierce, stab; 3 sg. preterite 'thrust' (yny want y mab yn wysc y benn 'until he thrust the boy headlong'); g- lost by soft mutation after yny 'until'
wysc: gwysc (gwysg) — course, track, direction; noun m., in yn wysc y benn 'headlong, head first' (literally 'in the course of his head'); g- lost by soft mutation after yn
gynneu: kynneu (cynnau) — to kindle, light; also what is kindled, the fire; verbal noun (yn y gynneu 'into the kindling, into the fire'; the Red Book yn y gynneu tan); soft-mutated (c>g) after y, the cause not clear, since the article does not normally soften a verbal noun
fan: pan (pan) — when; spirant-mutated (p>ph, written f) after a 'and' (A fan welas Uranwen 'and when Branwen saw') and after no 'than' (no fan doethan yno 'than when they came there')
boeth: poeth (poeth) — hot, burning; adjective, soft-mutated (p>b) after predicative yn (yn boeth yn y tan 'burning in the fire')
gynsynwys: kynsynnyaw (cysynio) — to intend, set oneself (to), resolve; 3 sg. preterite in -wys (hi a gynsynwys uwrw neit 'she made to leap'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a; the exact shade of the sense is uncertain (not cydsynio 'consent')
tarean: taryan (tarian) — shield; noun f.; spelt tarean; a'y tarean 'and his shield', no soft mutation shown after y 'his'
ymgyuot: ymgyuot (ymgodi) — to rise up, start up together; verbal noun, ym- + kyuot 'rise' (kyuodi), the k softened inside the compound (ymgyuot o bawb 'everyone rising up'); no mutation of the word itself
bawb: pawb (pawb) — everyone; soft-mutated (p>b) after the preposition o 'by' introducing the agent of a verbal noun (ymgyuot o bawb 'rising of everyone')
godwrw: godwrw (godwrdd) — din, uproar, tumult (the Red Book god6rd); noun m.; no mutation after the article y (llyna y godwrw mwyhaf 'behold the greatest uproar')
mordwyd: Proper name — Morddwyd, in Mordwyd Tyllyon 'Morddwyd Tyllion', literally 'Pierced Thigh' (mordwyd = morddwyd 'thigh'); who bears the name is not said; radical (subject after y dywot)
tyllyon: tyllyon (no modern form; cf. twll 'hole', tyllu 'pierce') — holed, pierced; plural adjective, in the name Mordwyd Tyllyon 'Pierced Thigh' (Morddwyd Tyllion); radical
gwngwch: gwngwch (no modern form) — part of the obscure cry Guern gwngwch uiwch Uordwyt Tyllyon; not known as a word in this form, and no reading of it is safe (Evans and the Red Book g6ng6ch divide it so)
uiwch: uiwch (no modern form) — part of the obscure cry Guern gwngwch uiwch Uordwyt Tyllyon; not known as a word in this form, and no reading of it is safe (the Red Book ui6ch)
uordwyt: Proper name — Mordwyd (spelt with -t), in the cry Guern gwngwch uiwch Uordwyt Tyllyon; soft-mutated (m>u), the cause unclear because the construction of the cry is obscure (perhaps vocative or object)
kynhelis: kynnal (cynnal) — to hold, support, keep up; 3 sg. preterite in -is, spelt with -h- (kynhal-), a>e by affection (y kynhelis Bendigeiduran Uranwen y rwng y taryan a'y yscwyd 'Bendigeidfran held Branwen between his shield and his shoulder'); radical after the particle y
dechrewis: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 sg. preterite in -is, dechreuis with w written for u, 'began' (y dechrewis y Gwydyl kynneu tan 'the Irish began to kindle a fire'); singular before a plural noun subject; radical after the particle y
kynneu: kynneu (cynnau) — to kindle, light a fire; verbal noun (kynneu tan 'to light a fire'); radical, object tan following
dadeni: dadeni (dadeni) — rebirth, regeneration (dad- 're-' + geni 'to be born'); noun m.; in peir dadeni 'the cauldron of rebirth', a noun in the genitive after peir; no mutation
byrywyt: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast; impersonal preterite in -wyt 'was thrown' on the stem byry- (y byrywyt y kalaned yn y peir 'the corpses were thrown into the cauldron'); radical after the particle y
kalaned: celain (celain) — corpse, dead body; noun f., plural kalaned (celanedd); radical after the article y (y kalaned yn y peir 'the corpses in the cauldron')
kyuodyn: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise; 3 pl. imperfect 'they would rise' (-yn for -ynt, habitual) (ac y kyuodyn tranoeth y bore 'and they would rise next morning'); radical after the particle y
tranoeth: tranoeth (trannoeth) — the next day, on the morrow (tra- + noeth 'night'); adverb (tranoeth y bore 'the next morning')
bore: bore (bore) — morning; noun m.; radical after the article y (y bore 'the morning'; the scribe leaves a blank before it)
calaned: celain (celain) — corpse; plural calaned (celanedd), a variant spelling of kalaned (pan welas Efnissyen y calaned 'when Efnysien saw the corpses'); radical after y
enni: enni (uncertain) — in heb enni yn un lle, said of the British dead; perhaps genni 'have room, be contained' (as in kynghanei, enghis), softened after heb with the g lost; or geni 'be born' (the Red Book eni), 'without rebirth', as in dadeni; the reading is uncertain
guae: gwae (gwae) — woe; interjection, followed by the pronoun (guae ui 'woe is me'); no mutation
wydwic: gwydwic (no modern form certain) — probably 'destruction, ruin, slaughter' by context (yn achaws y'r wydwic honn o wyr Ynys y Kedyrn 'because of this ... of the men of the Island of the Mighty'); sense uncertain; noun f., g- lost by soft mutation after the feminine article y'r
cheissaf: keissyaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; 1 sg. present 'I seek' in -af (ony cheissaf i waret rac hynn 'unless I seek to deliver us from this'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ony 'unless'
ymedyryaw: ymedyriaw (no modern form) — to move about, put oneself among, mingle; verbal noun, reflexive ym- (ymedyryaw ymlith calaned y Gwydyl 'creeping among the corpses of the Irish'); sense inferred from context, uncertain
ymlith: ymlith (ymhlith) — among, amid; preposition; no mutation (ymlith calaned y Gwydyl 'among the corpses of the Irish')
wydel: Gwydel (Gwyddel) — an Irishman; noun m. singular; g- lost by soft mutation after deu 'two' (deu Wydel 'two Irishmen')
uonllwm: bonllwm (bonllwm) — bare-bottomed, naked (bon 'base, bottom' + llwm 'bare'); adjective after its noun (deu Wydel uonllwm 'two naked Irishmen'); soft-mutated (b>u) as an adjective after a noun counted by deu 'two'; sense from the parts, uncertain
emystynnu: ymestyn (ymestyn) — to stretch, stretch oneself out; verbal noun, reflexive, spelt with e- (emystynnu idaw ynteu yn y peir 'he stretching himself out in the cauldron'); no mutation
pedwar: pedwar (pedwar) — four; numeral m.; no mutation (yn pedwar dryll 'into four pieces'; a predicative yn would soften it, not shown)
dryll: dryll (dryll) — fragment, piece; noun m., singular after a numeral (pedwar dryll 'four pieces'); no mutation
galon: calon (calon) — heart; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after the possessive y 'his' (yny dyrr y galon ynteu 'until his own heart breaks'; torri ohonaw … Gradawc y galon 'Caradog's breaking of his heart')
meint: maint (maint) — size, amount, extent; noun, spelt meint; y meint goruot 'so much victory, the whole measure of victory'; radical
goruot: goruot (gorfod) — victory, mastery; noun m.; radical (y meint goruot a uu y wyr Ynys y Kedyrn 'the amount of victory the men of the Island of the Mighty had')
oruot: goruot (gorfod) — victory; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation as the subject directly after the verb (Ny bu oruot 'there was no victory')
diang: diang (dianc) — to escape; verbal noun, -g written for -nc, with its subject following (eithyr diang seithwyr 'except the escaping of seven men'); no mutation
brathu: brathu (brathu) — to stab, pierce, wound (modern also 'to bite, sting'); verbal noun in narrative (a brathu Bendigeiduran yn y troet 'and Bendigeidfran was pierced in the foot'); radical after a 'and' (b- is not spirant-mutated)
troet: troed (troed) — foot; noun m., singular (yn y troet 'in the foot'); radical after the article y
guenwynwaew: gwenwynwaew (no modern form) — poisoned spear (gwenwyn 'poison' + gwaew 'spear'); compound noun m.; the instrument after a 'with' (a guenwynwaew 'with a poisoned spear'); no mutation
dienghis: diengyd (dianc) — to escape; 3 sg. preterite in -is 'escaped' (Sef seithwyr a dienghis 'these are the seven who escaped'); singular verb with the relative a, soft mutation of d- not written
gliuieu: Proper name — Glifiau, one of the seven survivors (Gliuieu Eil Taran); radical
taran: Proper name — Taran (taran also 'thunder'), in Gliuieu Eil Taran; how eil relates to it is unclear (perhaps 'son of Taran'); radical
talyessin: Proper name — Taliesin (Taliesin), one of the seven survivors; radical
ynawc: Proper name — Ynawc (Ynog; modern form uncertain), one of the seven survivors; radical
grudyeu: Proper name — Grudyeu (Gruddieu), son of Muryel, one of the seven survivors; radical
muryel: Proper name — Muryel (Muriel), the parent named in Grudyeu uab Muryel; radical after uab
heilyn: Proper name — Heilyn (Heilyn), son of Gwyn Hen, one of the seven survivors, who opens the door; radical
gwyn: Proper name — Gwyn (gwyn also 'white, fair'), father of Heilyn, in Heilyn uab Gwyn Hen 'Heilyn son of Gwyn the Old'; radical after uab · also in Gwyn Gloew, father of Cigfa (uerch Gwyn Gloew 'daughter of Gwyn Gloew'); radical after uerch
chymerwch: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 2 pl. imperative in -wch 'take!' (A chymerwch chwi y penn 'and take the head'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
gwynuryn: Proper name — Gwynfryn (Gwynfryn), 'White Hill', the hill in London (gwyn 'white' + bryn 'hill', b>u/f inside the compound); radical (hyt y Gwynuryn 'as far as the White Hill')
llundein: Proper name — Llundein (Llundain), London; no mutation (ll- has no nasal form after yn 'in'; also after hyt 'as far as' and as object of kyrchwch)
chledwch: cladu (claddu) — to bury; 2 pl. imperative in -wch 'bury!' on the stem cledw- (a>e by affection) (a chledwch a'y wyneb ar Freinc 'and bury it with its face towards France'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
freinc: Ffreinc (Ffrainc) — France, the Franks; proper name f., spelt Freinc (f for ff, as in ford); no mutation (ar Freinc 'towards France')
uydwch: bot (bod) — to be; 2 pl. future 'you will be' in -wch (A chwi a uydwch ar y ford yn hir 'and you will be a long time on the road'); soft-mutated (b>u) after the relative a
ginyaw: ciniaw (cinio) — meal, feast, dinner; noun; soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'at' (ar ginyaw 'at the feast'), after o 'of' (o ginyaw 'of feasting') and after y 'the' (am y ginyaw 'about the feasting'), in the last case as if feminine, though kinyaw is usually masculine (the Red Book has the same)
adar: aderyn (aderyn) — bird; plural adar 'birds'; in the title Adar Riannon 'the Birds of Rhiannon', the plural noun followed by a name in the genitive; radical
gennwch: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 2 pl. 'with you' (gennwch, beside genhwch); the 'with' of opinion (kystal gennwch y gedymdeithas 'as good in your eyes the company'); no mutation
guales: Proper name — Gwales (Gwales), the place off Penfro where the seven stay (traditionally the island of Grassholm; the identification is later); after y (= yn 'in') the nasal mutation is not written (the Red Book ygg6ales, yng Ngwales)
penuro: Proper name — Penfro (Penfro), Pembroke, the region (pen 'head, end' + bro 'region'); spelt Penuro; the nasal mutation (p>mh) after ym 'in' is not written
pedwarugeint: pedwar ugeint (pedwar ugain) — four score, eighty; numeral compound (pedwar 'four' + ugeint 'twenty'); no mutation (pedwarugeint mlyned 'eighty years')
agoroch: agori (agor) — to open; 2 pl. present subjunctive 'you open' in -och (yny agoroch y drws 'until you open the door'); no mutation (vowel)
aber: aber (aber) — river-mouth, estuary, confluence; noun m.; first element in place-names (Aber Henueleu, Aber Alau); no mutation
henueleu: Proper name — Henfelen, in Aber Henueleu, the estuary on the side towards Cornwall; spelt Henueleu here and in the Red Book once (henuelen at the second place), -leu probably an old slip for -len; no mutation
tu: tu (tu) — side, direction; noun m. (y tu ar Gernyw, y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall'); no mutation
gernyw: Cernyw (Cernyw) — Cornwall; proper name f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'towards, on' (ar Gernyw 'towards Cornwall')
gellwch: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 2 pl. present 'you can' in -wch, a>e by affection (y gellwch uot yno 'you can be there'); radical after the particle y
dilwgyr: dilwgyr (dilwgr) — uncorrupted, sound (di- 'without' + llwgr 'corruption', ll softened to l); adjective, predicative (a'r penn yn dilwgyr genhwch 'and the head uncorrupted with you'); after yn the d would be dd, which the spelling does not show
ellwch: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 2 pl. present 'you can' in -wch (ny ellwch uot yno 'you cannot be there'); g- lost by soft mutation after ny
kyrchwch: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to go to, make for; 2 pl. imperative in -wch 'go to!' (Kyrchwch Lundein 'make for London'); radical (opening the clause)
gladu: cladu (claddu) — to bury; verbal noun, soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'to' (y gladu y penn 'to bury the head')
chyrchwch: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to go to, make for; 2 pl. imperative in -wch (A chyrchwch chwi racoch drwod 'and make on across'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
racoch: rac (rhag) — before; conjugated preposition 2 pl. 'before you', here 'onward' (kyrchwch chwi racoch drwod 'go on across'; modern rhagoch; the Red Book ragoch); no mutation
llas: lladd (lladd) — to strike, kill, cut off; 3 sg. impersonal/passive preterite 'was struck, was cut' (y llas y benn ef 'his head was struck off'); radical after the particle y
gantu: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'with them' (a'r penn gantu 'with the head with them'), a variant spelling of ganthunt, gantunt; no mutation
wythuet: wythuet (wythfed) — eighth; ordinal; radical after predicative yn (Branwen yn wythuet 'Branwen as the eighth')
alau: Proper name — Alaw (Alaw), the river and its estuary in Anglesey, in Aber Alau; spelt Alau (u = w); no mutation (vowel)
gorfowys: gorffowys (gorffwys) — to rest, take rest; verbal noun, f for ff (a gorfowys 'and rested'); no mutation
ganedigaeth: genedigaeth (genedigaeth) — birth; noun f., spelt ganedigaeth, a by-form (guae ni o'm ganedigaeth 'woe … of my birth'); no mutation after the infixed 'm 'my'
diffeithwyt: diffeithaw (diffeithio) — to lay waste, devastate; impersonal preterite in -wyt 'was laid waste' (a diffeithwyt o'm achaws i 'were laid waste because of me'); relative a, the soft mutation of d- not written
ucheneit: ucheneit (ochenaid) — sigh, groan; noun f.; object of the verbal noun dodi, no mutation (vowel); the adjective follows softened (ucheneit uawr 'a great sigh')
chalon: calon (calon) — heart; noun f.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after the possessive y 'her' (y chalon 'her heart')
bed: bedd (bedd) — grave; noun m.; spelt bed; object of the verbal noun gwneuthur (gwneuthur bed petrual idi 'making a four-sided grave for her'); no mutation
petrual: petrual (petryal) — four-sided, square, oblong; adjective after its noun (bed petrual 'a four-sided grave'); no mutation
chladu: cladu (claddu) — to bury; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a'e 'and her' (a'e chladu yno 'and burying her there')
glan: glan (glan) — bank, shore, brink; noun f. (y glan Alaw 'on the bank of the Alaw'); in the text the word is divided y glan, the y standing for yn, whose nasal mutation of glan is not written; the division is an open point
alaw: Proper name — Alaw (Alaw), the river in Anglesey (also alaw 'melody, water-lily'); no mutation (vowel)
bydant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present (habitual) 'they are', a vivid present in past narrative (Val y bydant y kerdet 'as they were walking'; the Red Book has the same); radical after the particle y
gyweithyd: kyweithyd (cyweithydd) — a company, band of people; noun; soft-mutated (c>g) after llyma 'behold' (llyma gyweithyd 'behold a company')
kyuaruot: kyuarfod (cyfarfod) — to meet; verbal noun after progressive yn (yn kyuaruot ac wynt 'meeting them'); no mutation
goresgyn: goresgyn (goresgyn) — to conquer, overrun, subdue; verbal noun (onyt goresgyn o Gaswallawn 'except that Caswallon has conquered'); no mutation
gaswallawn: Proper name — Caswallon (spelt Caswallawn), son of Beli; soft-mutated (c>g) as agent after a verbal noun with o 'by' (goresgyn o Gaswallawn) and as subject after the negated verb (Ny uynhei Gaswallawn y lad 'Caswallon would not wish to kill him') · also soft after y 'to' (y Gaswallawn uab Beli 'to Caswallon son of Beli')
beli: Proper name — Beli (Beli), father of Caswallon; radical after uab (patronymic)
gradawc: Proper name — Caradawc (Caradog), son of Brân; soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'to, of' (Pa daruu y Gradawc 'what befell Caradog') and in apposition to ohonaw ynteu (ohonaw ynteu Gradawc 'he, Caradog')
caswallawn: Proper name — Caswallon (spelt Caswallawn), son of Beli; radical, subject after the verbal noun dyuot (Dyuot Caswallawn am eu penn 'Caswallon came upon them') and before a verb
chwegwyr: chwe gwyr (chwe gŵr) — six men, a company of six (chwe 'six' + gwyr 'men', like seithwyr); noun pl. compound, object of llad (llad y chwegwyr 'killing the six'); no mutation
aniuyget: aniuyget (no modern form) — grief, anguish, heart-break; noun; no mutation after o 'from, of' (vowel); the sense is inferred from the context (torri y galon o aniuyget 'to break the heart from ...'), etymology uncertain
wydat: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. imperfect 'he knew' (na wydat pwy a'e lladei 'that he did not know who was killing them'; the Red Book wydyat); g- lost by soft mutation after na · also soft after the negative ny (Ac ny wydat 'and he did not know')
daroed: darfod (darfod) — to finish, happen; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had happened' in -oed (Caswallawn a daroed idaw wiscaw llen hut 'Caswallon had put on a mantle of magic', literally 'it had happened to him to put on'); relative a, the soft mutation of d- not written
uynhei: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, desire, intend; 3 sg. imperfect 'would wish' in -hei (Ny uynhei Gaswallawn y lad 'Caswallon would not wish to kill him'); soft-mutated (m>u) after ny
geuynderw: keuynderw (cefnderw, cefnder) — cousin (male, first cousin); noun m.; soft-mutated (c>g) after the possessive y 'his' (uab y geuynderw 'the son of his cousin')
torres: torri (torri) — to break; 3 sg. preterite in -es 'broke' (a torres y gallon o aniuyget 'who broke his heart ...'); relative a, the soft mutation of t- (dorres) not shown
gallon: calon (calon) — heart; noun f., a variant spelling with -ll-; soft-mutated (c>g) after the possessive y 'his' (y gallon 'his heart')
pendarar: Proper name — Pendaran (Pendaran), Pendarar Dyuet 'Pendaran of Dyfed', the young lad who was with the seven; spelt Pendarar in both the White Book and the Red Book, the final -r presumably an old slip; radical (subject, before a oed)
ieuang: ieuanc (ifanc) — young; adjective (yn was ieuang 'as a young lad'); written with -g for -c; no mutation (vowel)
kyrchyssant: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to go to, make for; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they made for' (y kyrchyssant wynteu Hardlech 'they made for Harlech'; y'r neuad y kyrchyssant 'to the hall they went'); radical after the particle y
ymdiwallu: ymdiwallu (ymddiwallu) — to take one's fill, be satisfied; reflexive verbal noun (y dechreuwyt ymdiwallu o uwyt a llynn 'they began to take their fill of food and drink'); no mutation shown
yuet: yfed (yfed) — to drink; verbal noun (uwyta ac yuet 'eating and drinking'); no mutation (vowel after ac)
tri: tri (tri) — three (m.); numeral (dyuot tri ederyn 'there came three birds'); no mutation
glywssynt: clywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had heard' in -ssynt (oc a glywssynt o gerd 'of all the song they had heard'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
iwrthi: wrth (wrth) — conjugated preposition 3 sg. f. 'to, against, beside her/it'; with the y-prefix, in comparison (diuwyn oed pob un iwrthi hi 'every one was worthless compared with it'); no mutation
fell: pell (pell) — far, distant; adjective placed before its noun (A fell dremynt 'and a far sight'); spirant-mutated (p>ph, written f) after a 'and'
gin: gin- — a broken-off word, the first syllable of ginyaw (cinio) 'feast' (see ginyaw), written by the scribe when he began the sentence too early and then wrote it again; no grammar of its own; soft c>g after o as in o ginyaw
amlyket: amlwc (amlwg) — evident, plain, visible; equative in -et 'as plain' after kyn (A chyn amlyket oed udunt wy 'and as plain they were to them'); no mutation
seithuet: seithuet (seithfed) — seventh; ordinal before its noun (ym penn y seithuet ulwydyn 'at the end of the seventh year'); no mutation
kychwynyssant: kychwyn (cychwyn) — to set out; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they set out' (y kychwynyssant parth a Gualas 'they set out towards Gwales'); radical after the particle y
gualas: Proper name — Gwales (Gwales), the place off Penfro; spelt Gualas; no mutation (after parth a 'towards')
teg: teg (teg) — fair, lovely; adjective after its noun (lle teg brenhineid 'a fair, kingly place'); no mutation
brenhineid: brenhinaidd (brenhinaidd) — kingly, royal (brenhin 'king' + -eid for -aidd); adjective after its noun (lle teg brenhineid 'a fair kingly place'); no mutation
gayat: kayat (caead) — shut, closed; adjective; soft-mutated (c>g) after y standing for the predicative yn (y drws oed y gayat 'the door was shut'; the Red Book yngayat)
chernyw: Cernyw (Cernyw) — Cornwall; proper name f.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'to, towards' (y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall')
weldy: gwelet (gweld) — to see; the imperative gwel with the pronoun di 'you' joined to it and the g lost, as in wele 'behold': 'see there, look' (Weldy racco 'see yonder'; the Red Book weldi)
dylywn: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, ought; 1 pl. present 'we ought' in -ywn (y drws ny dylywn ni y agori 'the door we ought not to open'); no mutation of d- shown after ny
ouut: gofut (gofid) — grief, trouble, distress; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after o 'of' (o ouut 'of grief')
gewssynt: caffael (cael) — to get, have, undergo; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had had' in -ssynt on the stem cew- (yr a gewssynt e hun 'all they had suffered themselves'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
alar: galar (galar) — grief, mourning; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after o 'of' (nac o alar 'nor of grief') · also soft after the adjective diruawr standing before it (diruawr alar 'huge grief')
wybuant: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 pl. preterite 'they knew' in -uant (hyt na wybuant wy eiryoet 'so that they never knew'); g- lost by soft mutation after na
yspeit: yspeit (ysbaid) — a space of time, a while, a period; noun m.; object of dwyn (dwyn yspeit digriuach 'to pass a merrier time'); no mutation
digriuach: digrif (digrifach) — more pleasant, merrier; comparative of digrif 'pleasant, merry', spelt digriuach; adjective after its noun (yspeit digriuach 'a merrier time'); no mutation
hyurydach: hyfryd (hyfrytach) — more cheerful, more pleasant; comparative of hyfryd, spelt hyurydach (na hyurydach no honno 'nor more cheerful than that'); no mutation
anesmwythach: anesmwyth (anesmwythach) — more uneasy, less comfortable; comparative of anesmwyth (an- 'not' + esmwyth 'easy'); predicative after oed (Nyt oed anesmwythach 'it was no more uneasy'); no mutation
doethan: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came', doethant with its -t not written (the Red Book doethant) (no fan doethan yno 'than when they came there'); no mutation
wynte: wynteu (hwythau) — they for their part; conjunctive pronoun 3 pl., spelt wynte without -u (ganthunt wynte 'with them, for their part'); no mutation
gyduot: kyduot (cydfod) — to be together, dwell together (kyd 'together' + bot 'to be', b>u inside the compound); verbal noun (gyduot y penn yna 'being together there with the head'); soft-mutated (c>g), the cause not clear (the Red Book gytuot)
uyw: byw (byw) — alive, living; adjective, soft-mutated (b>u) after predicative yn (yn uyw gyd ac wynt 'alive with them') · also softened as the complement straight after a form of bot (ny bydei uyw 'he would not be alive')
gyd: kyd (cyd) — together; adverb, spelt gyd (yn uyw gyd ac wynt 'alive together with them'); soft-mutated (c>g), the cause uncertain, as in y gyt
yspydawt: yspydawt (ysbyddawd) — hospitality, entertaining of guests, a feast; noun f.; in the title Yspydawt Urdaul Benn 'the Hospitality of the Honoured Head' and Yspydawt Uranwen a Matholwch 'the hospitality of Branwen and Matholwch'; no mutation
urdaul: urdawl (urddol) — honoured, dignified, of rank (urdd 'rank, order' + -awl); adjective placed before its noun (Urdaul Benn 'Honoured Head'), which it softens
aethpwyt: mynet (mynd) — to go; impersonal preterite 'was gone, one went' in -pwyt (yd aethpwyt e Iwerdon 'it was gone to Ireland, they went to Ireland'); radical after the particle yd
guyn: Proper name — Gwyn (Gwyn), father of Heilyn, spelt Guyn (cf. Gwyn Hen in the list of the seven); radical after uab
maryf: baryf (barf) — beard; noun f.; nasal-mutated (b>m) after uy 'my' (Meuyl ar uy maryf i 'shame on my beard')
agoraf: agori (agor) — to open; 1 sg. present 'I open' in -af (onyt agoraf y drws 'unless I open the door'); no mutation (vowel)
dywedir: dywedut (dweud) — to say; impersonal present 'is said' in -ir (ay gwir a dywedir am hynny 'whether what is said about that is true'); relative a, the soft mutation of d- not written
edrychwys: edrych (edrych) — to look; 3 sg. preterite 'he looked' in -wys (A phan edrychwys 'and when he looked'); no mutation (vowel)
hyspysset: hysbys (hysbys) — known, plain, evident; adjective, equative in -et 'as plain' (yn gyn hyspysset ganthunt 'as plain to them'); no mutation
gyniuer: kyniuer (cynifer) — so many, as many, all the; noun f. (cyn 'as' + niuer 'number'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the feminine article y (y gyniuer collet 'all the loss'; a'r gyniuer car 'and all the kin'; a'r gyniuer drwc 'and all the evil')
collet: colled (colled) — loss, damage; noun, spelt collet; after gyniuer (y gyniuer collet 'all the loss'); no mutation
gollyssynt: colli (colli) — to lose; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had lost' in -yssynt (collet a gollyssynt 'the loss they had lost'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
car: car (câr) — kinsman, relative, friend; noun m., collective singular (a'r gyniuer car 'and all the kin'); radical
chedymdeith: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion, comrade; noun m.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' (car a chedymdeith 'kinsmen and companions')
dothoed: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had come' in -oed on the stem doth- (y gyniuer drwc a dothoed udunt 'all the evil that had come to them'); relative a, the soft mutation of d- not written
kyuarffei: kyuarfod (cyfarfod) — to meet, befall; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive in -ei 'would meet' (a chyt bei yno y kyuarffei ac wynt 'as if it were there that it met them'); radical after the particle y
gyuawr: kyuawr (no modern form; kyf- + awr 'hour') — the same hour, that very hour; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after the article (o'r gyuawr honno 'from that very hour')
allyssant: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 pl. preterite 'they were able, could' in -yssant (ny allyssant wy orfowys 'they could not rest'); g- lost by soft mutation after ny
orfowys: gorffowys (gorffwys) — to rest; verbal noun, g- lost by soft mutation after the subject wy 'they' (ny allyssant wy orfowys 'they could not rest'); f for ff
kychu: kychu (no modern form) — uncertain: a slip, probably for kyrchu 'to go to' (the second witness reads kyrchu) or a shortened kychwyn 'to set out' (the Red Book reads kychwynnu); verbal noun (namyn kychu a'r penn parth a Llundein 'but to go on with the head towards London')
gladyssant: cladu (claddu) — to bury; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they buried' (ac a gladyssant y penn 'and they buried the head'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
matcud: matcud (no modern form; mad 'fortunate, good' + cud 'concealment') — a fortunate concealment; noun m., spelt tc by assimilation of d + c; ordinal before it (trydyd matcud 'the third fortunate concealment'); no mutation
gudywyt: cuddio (cuddio) — to hide, conceal, bury; impersonal preterite 'was hidden' in -wyt (ban gudywyt 'when it was hidden'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ban 'when'
anuat: anuat (anfad; modern anfad means 'wicked') — unfortunate, ill-starred (an- 'not' + mad 'good, fortunate'); adjective before its noun (trydyd anuat datcud 'the third unfortunate unearthing'; tryded anuat paluawt 'the third unfortunate blow'); no mutation; whether 'unfortunate' or 'evil' is meant here is disputed
datcud: datcud (datgudd; modern datguddio 'to reveal') — uncovering, disclosure, digging up (dat- 're-, un-' + cud 'concealment'); noun m.; no mutation (after anuat 'unfortunate')
datcudywyt: datguddio (datguddio) — to uncover, reveal, dig up; impersonal preterite 'was uncovered' in -wyt (pann datcudywyt 'when it was uncovered'); d- as written, the soft form after pann not shown
ormes: gormes (gormes) — oppression, tyranny, invasion; noun f.; g- lost by soft mutation as the subject after a negated verb (cany doey ormes 'since no oppression would come')
uor: mor (môr) — sea; noun m.; soft-mutated (m>u) after drwy 'across, through' (drwy uor 'across the sea')
cud: cud (cudd) — concealment, hiding; noun m. (modern cudd 'hidden, secret'); no mutation after the article y (yn y cud hwnnw 'in that concealment')
kyuarwydyd: kyuarwydyd (cyfarwyddyd) — telling of tales, a tale, lore (perhaps the teller, cf. cyfarwydd 'storyteller'); noun m.; no mutation (y kyuarwydyd hwnn 'this tale / this story-telling')
kyfranc: kyfranc (cyfranc) — encounter, event, adventure, the story of an event; noun m.; radical after eu 'their' (Eu kyfranc wy 'their story')
gychwynwys: kychwyn (cychwyn) — to set out; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'set out' (Y gwyr a gychwynwys o Iwerdon 'the men who set out from Ireland'); singular verb after a plural antecedent; soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
en: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt en (En Iwerdon 'in Ireland'); no mutation (vowel) · also the adverbial particle yn, which leaves ll unsoftened (En llawen 'gladly')
pump: pump (pump) — five; numeral (pump gwraged 'five women'); no mutation
beichawc: beichiawc (beichiog) — pregnant; adjective after its plural noun (pump gwraged beichawc 'five pregnant women'); radical
gogof: gogof (gogof) — cave; noun f.; no mutation after y mywn 'in' (y mywn gogof 'in a cave')
diffeithwch: diffeithwch (diffeithwch) — wilderness, waste; noun m. (yn diffeithwch Iwerdon 'in the wilderness of Ireland'); the nasal mutation after yn (niffeithwch) is not written
kyfnot: kyfnot (cyfnod) — period, term, time; noun m. (yn yr un kyfnot 'in the same period, at the same time'); radical
pum: pum (pum) — five; numeral, the form before a noun (pum meib 'five sons'); no mutation
meib: mab (mab) — son; plural meib (modern meibion) 'sons, boys'; no mutation (pum meib 'five sons')
pym: pum (pum) — five; numeral, a variant spelling pym (a'r pym meib hynny 'and those five sons'); no mutation
uagyssant: magu (magu) — to rear, nurse, bring up; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they reared' (a'r pym meib hynny a uagyssant: with the sons as subject 'were reared, grew up'; the construction is loose); soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a
uuant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (buant); soft-mutated (b>u) after ban 'until, when' (hyt ban uuant weisson mawr 'until they were big lads') · also softened after a fronted predicate, the particle a unwritten (Llawen uuant wrthunt 'they were glad of them')
damunet: damunet (no modern form; cf. dymuno 'to wish') — desire, wish; noun; subject after uu (yny uu damunet gantunt eu cafael 'until a desire came to them to have them'); no mutation shown
cafael: caffael (cael) — to get, have; verbal noun spelt cafael, after eu 'their' (eu cafael 'to have them'); radical
lau: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., spelt lau (u for w), in lau heb lau 'hand past hand', in turn (kyscu pob un lau heb lau 'each sleeping in turn'; the Red Book law heb law); soft-mutated (ll>l) as an adverbial phrase
chyuanhedu: kyfanhedu (cyfanheddu) — to inhabit, settle, populate; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a'y 'and it' (a'y chyuanhedu 'and to settle it') · also spirant-mutated after a 'and' alone (a chyuanhedu yno 'and settling there')
yll: yll (ill) — the pronoun used before a numeral, 'they (all)': y rydunt yll pymp 'between them, the five of them' (modern ill dau 'the two of them'); no mutation
pymp: pump (pump) — five; numeral, spelt pymp (yll pymp 'all five'; pymp rann Ywerdon 'five parts of Ireland'); no mutation
ranyat: ranyat (rhaniad) — division, partition; noun m., r for rh; radical after the article y (y ranyat hwnnw 'that division')
etwan: etwan (no modern form; a by-form of etwa, modern eto) — still, yet, to this day; adverb (y gelwir etwan pymp rann Ywerdon 'the five parts of Ireland are still so called')
ywerdon: Proper name — Iwerddon (Ireland), spelt Ywerdon (pymp rann Ywerdon 'the five parts of Ireland'); no mutation (vowel)
aeruaeu: aerua (aerfa) — battlefield, place of slaughter (aer 'battle' + ma 'place, field', softened in the compound); noun f., plural aeruaeu (yr aeruaeu 'the battlefields'); no mutation
ytoedynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. imperfect 'they were' (oedynt) with the preverbal particle yd, written yt (yny ytoedynt yn gyuoethawc 'until they were wealthy')
gyuoethawc: kyuoethawc (cyfoethog) — rich, wealthy, powerful; adjective, soft-mutated (c>g) after predicative yn (yn gyuoethawc 'rich') · also soft after holl (Duw holl gyuoethawc 'God all-powerful')
mabinyogi: Mabinyogi (Mabinogi) — the Mabinogi, the title of the whole work; proper noun, derived from mab 'boy, son' (the exact sense of the title is debated); no mutation after the article 'r (y geing honn o'r Mabinyogi 'this branch of the Mabinogi')
paluawt: palfawd (palfod) — a blow, stroke, slap; noun f. (Paluawt Branwen 'the Blow of Branwen'; tryded anuat paluawt 'the third unfortunate blow'); no mutation
yspadawt: yspydawt (ysbyddawd) — hospitality, a feast; noun f., spelt yspadawt (Yspadawt Uran 'the Hospitality of Brân', the expedition to Ireland); no mutation
uran: Proper name — Brân (Bran, the short form of Bendigeidfran); soft-mutated (b>u) after the feminine noun yspadawt (Yspadawt Uran 'the Hospitality of Brân')
decwlat: degwlat (no modern form) — a 'ten-land', a division of ten (deg 'ten' + gwlad 'land'; gwlat softened to wlat in the compound, written dec-); noun f. (pedeir decwlat a seithugeint 'four ten-lands and seven score'); the exact sense of the term is uncertain
ganyat: canyat (caniad) — singing, song; noun m.; soft-mutated (c>g) after am 'about' (am Ganyat Adar Riannon 'concerning the Singing of the Birds of Rhiannon')
yspydaut: yspydawt (ysbyddawd) — hospitality, a feast; noun, a variant spelling of yspydawt (ar Yspydaut Benn 'about the Hospitality of the Head'); no mutation
cladu: cladu (claddu) — to bury; to dig; verbal noun (daruot … cladu penn Bendigeiduran 'finished burying the head of Bendigeidfran'); no mutation (object of the verbal noun follows it)
manauydan: Proper name — Manawydan (u spells w), son of Llŷr, brother of Bendigeidfran; radical, subject after a wnaeth (edrych a wnaeth Manauydan 'Manawydan looked')
hiraeth: hiraeth (hiraeth) — longing, grief, homesickness; noun m.; no mutation of h- after a 'and' (alar a hiraeth 'grief and longing')
uit: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperative 'let it be' (bit); soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after the negative na (na uit kyn drymhet 'let it not be so heavy')
drymhet: trwm (trwm) — heavy, grievous, burdensome; equative degree 'as heavy' (-het/-ed ending); soft-mutated (t>d) after the equative particle kyn 'as' (kyn drymhet genhyt 'as heavy with you')
gwnel: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he do' (kyn gwnel gameu it 'though he do wrongs to you'); radical gw- here, after kyn 'though' (a chyn gwnel)
gameu: cam (cam) — wrong, injury, injustice; noun m., plural camau (written -eu); soft-mutated (c>g) as the object directly after the verb gwnel (gwnel gameu 'do wrongs'); the cause of the mutation is the usual soft mutation of a direct object following an inflected verb
lledyf: lledyf (lleddf) — slanting; soft, meek, humble, yielding; adjective, before its noun (Trydyd lledyf unben 'the third lledyf chieftain', from a triad of 'Three … Chieftains'; which sense is meant there is disputed); radical (unben begins with a vowel, so any softening after the adjective does not show)
boet: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be' in -et (modern boed); after kyt 'though' (kyt boet keuynderw y mi y gwr hwnnw 'though that man be my cousin'); radical
keuynderw: keuynderw (cefnderw, cefnder) — cousin (male, first cousin); noun m.; radical (kyt boet keuynderw y mi 'though he be cousin to me'); see also geuynderw
goathrist: goathrist (no modern form in current use; cf. trist 'sad') — rather sad, grieved, sorrowful; adjective, predicate of yw genhyf i 'it is sad to me, I am sad' (goathrist yw genhyf i guelet 'it grieves me to see'); probably go- 'somewhat' + athrist 'sorrowful', analysis uncertain; fronted predicate, radical
mrawt: brawt (brawd) — brother; noun m.; nasal-mutated (b>m) after uy 'my' (uy mrawt 'my brother'); t spells d
wney: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. present/future in -i (wnei) 'you do, you will do' (A wney ditheu gynghor arall? 'will you do another counsel?'; Iawn a wney 'you do right'); g lost by soft mutation after the particle a (interrogative, relative)
chyny: cyn (cyn) + ny — 'though not, even if there were not', a contraction of kyn 'though' and the negative ny (a chyny bei itti o gyuoeth namyn … 'and even if you had no realm but …'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'; the following bei is subjunctive
wyn: Proper name — Gwyn (in Gwyn Gloyw), father of Cigfa; soft-mutated (g lost) after uerch 'daughter of' (Kicua uerch Wyn Gloyw); gwyn is also the adjective 'white, fair'
enwedigaeth: enwedigaeth (enwedigaeth) — special right, particular ownership, privilege; noun f. (enwedigaeth y kyuoeth y mi 'the ownership of the realm to me'); the exact sense 'title, ownership' is uncertain; radical, subject of bo
mwynant: mwynant (mwyniant) — enjoyment, use, benefit, as against ownership; noun m. (bit y mwynant y ti 'let the enjoyment be yours'); radical after the article y
mynhut: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you would want' in -(h)ut (phei mynhut gyuoeth 'if you should want a realm'); no mutation shown after pei
caffut: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive / conditional in -ut 'you would get' (y caffut ti hwnnw 'you would get that'); radical after the particle y
uynhaf: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 1 sg. present 'I want' (na uynhaf 'I do not want'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the negative na · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the affirmative particle a (mi a uynhaf 'I will want, I mean to')
debygaf: tebygu (GPC tebygu; modern tybio) — to suppose, think, imagine; 1 sg. present 'I think' (mi a debygaf 'I think'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a following the fronted pronoun
werendeweist: gwarandaw (gwrando) — to listen, hearken; 2 sg. preterite in -eist 'you listened' (stem gwerendew-) (na werendeweist eiryoet ar … 'that you never listened to …'); g lost by soft mutation after the negative na
ymdidanwreic: ymdidanwreic (no modern form; ymdidan 'conversation' + gwreic 'woman') — a woman to talk with, a conversational companion; noun f. (ar ymdidanwreic well no hi 'to a better woman to talk with than she'); g of gwreic lost (softened) in the compound; vowel-initial, so the softening after ar does not show
er: yr (y) — the article 'the', spelt er (Er amser 'the time (when)', the noun phrase used adverbially; the Red Book seems to read Yr amser); er 'since' is possible but less likely
delediwach: telediw (no modern form) — comely, fair, well made; adjective, comparative in -ach 'comelier, fairer' (ny bu wreic delediwach no hi 'there was no comelier woman than she'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine noun wreic
anuodlawn: anfodlon (anfodlon) — displeased, dissatisfied, discontented; adjective, an- 'not' + bodlon with soft mutation (b>u/f) after an-; predicate after bydy (ny bydy anuodlawn y phryt 'you will not be displeased with her appearance')
phryt: pryt (pryd) — form, appearance, beauty, face; noun m.; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after y 'her' (y phryt 'her appearance')
vynt: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelt with initial v for w (Vynt a gerdassant 'they walked'); fronted subject before the particle a, which softens the verb
racdunt: rac (rhag) + wynt — conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'before them' (modern rhagddynt), in -dunt; idiomatic 'on, ahead of them' (a gerdassant racdunt 'walked on their way'), and 'on their account, before them' elsewhere (a lwydwys racdunt 'prospered before them'; dygywys … racdunt 'was galling because of them')
chicua: Proper name — Cigfa (Cigfa), daughter of Gwyn Gloyw, wife of Pryderi; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' (a Chicua)
harlwyaw: arlwyo (arlwyo) — to prepare, provide, lay out (a feast); verbal noun in -aw; h- prefixed after y 'her, its' (feminine gwled, 'the feast': wedy y harlwyaw 'after its preparing, after preparing it')
kydeisted: kydeisted (cydeistedd) — to sit together, sitting together; verbal noun, kyd- 'together' + eisted 'sit' (dechreu kydeisted ac ymdidan 'beginning to sit together and talk'); radical, as the object of the verbal noun dechreu
tirioni: tirioni (no modern form in current use; cf. tirion 'gentle, kind') — to grow gentle, tender, become fond; verbal noun placed first before a wnaeth (tirioni a wnaeth y uryt 'his mind grew tender'); radical
hoffi: hoffi (hoffi) — to like, be fond of, love; verbal noun (a hoffi yn y uedwl na welsei … 'and liking in his mind that he had not seen …'); no mutation of h- after a 'and'
eiryoed: eiryoet (erioed) — ever, at any time (with a negative 'never'); adverb, here spelt -d for -t (na welsei eiryoed wreic 'that he had never seen a woman')
digonach: digawn (digon) — enough, sufficient, complete; adjective, comparative in -ach 'more complete, more perfect' (wreic digonach y theket 'a woman more perfect in her beauty'); after the feminine noun wreic it is softened, but d also writes dd, so the change does not show
theket: teced (GPC teced; also tegwch) — fairness, beauty; noun f. from têg 'fair' + -ed; spirant-mutated (t>th) after y 'her' (y theket 'her beauty')
thelediwet: telediwet (no modern form) — comeliness, grace; abstract noun from telediw 'comely'; spirant-mutated (t>th) after y 'her' (a'y thelediwet 'and her comeliness')
dywedeisti: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. preterite 'you said' in -eisti (-eist + i) (wrth a dywedeisti 'by what you said'); relative a 'what', so the soft mutation of d (>dd) is not visible
dywedwydat: dywedwydat (no modern form) — apparently a noun from dywedut 'say': 'saying, what was said'; the form is odd and its analysis uncertain (Pa dywedwydat oed hwnnw? 'what saying was that?'); after pa it is softened, but d also writes dd, so the change does not show
roessum: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 1 sg. preterite 'I gave', from the stem ro- (mi a'th roessum yn wreic 'I gave you as wife'); softened after the infixed 'th 'you', but r also writes rh, so the change does not show
uydef: bot (bod) — to be; written for uydaf, 1 sg. future 'I will be', a scribal slip (the Red Book has uydaf; compare mi a uydaf just before); soft-mutated (b>u) after the particle a (a minheu a uydef wrth hynny 'and I will abide by that')
difleis: difleis (no modern form in current use) — guileless, free from malice, harmless; adjective (mor difleis a hynny 'as guileless as that'); di- 'without'; the root is uncertain; after mor soft mutation is expected (d>dd), not visible
kyscwyt: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; impersonal preterite 'it was slept' in -wyt (y kyscwyt genti 'it was slept with her'); radical after the particle y
deryw: daruot (darfod) — to end, be over, come to pass; 3 sg. present with perfect sense, 'has ended, is over' (Ar ny deryw o'r wled 'what is not finished of the feast'); softened after ny, but d also writes dd, so the change does not show · also 'has happened, has befallen' (pa deryw ytti 'what has befallen you?'; yr hynn a deryw ymi 'what has befallen me')
treulwch: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, consume, pass (time); 2 pl. imperative in -wch 'spend, pass' (treulwch chwi 'you pass [the feast]'); radical
hebrwng: hebrwng (hebrwng) — to escort, conduct, convey, carry; verbal noun (y hebrwng uy gwrogaeth 'to bring my homage'); radical after y 'to'
lloegyr: Proper name — Lloegr, England (written Lloegyr, Loygyr, Lloygyr); radical after hyt yn (hyt yn Lloegyr 'as far as England')
kent: Proper name — Caint, Kent; after yg 'in' (yn before k), whose g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg Kent = modern yng Nghaint)
arhown: arhos (aros) — to wait, wait for, await; 1 pl. present/future in -own (-wn) 'we will wait for him' (Ninheu a'y arhown); radical after the infixed pronoun 'y 'him'
dreulyssant: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, consume, pass (time); 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they spent' (A'r wled honno a dreulyssant 'that feast they spent'; blwydyn a'r eil a dreulyssant 'a year and the second they spent'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a following a fronted object
kylchaw: kylchu (cylchu) — to go round, travel round, tour; verbal noun in -aw (dechreu a wnaethant kylchaw Dyuet 'they began to go round Dyfed'); radical
rodyaw: rodyaw (rhodio) — to walk about, wander, roam; verbal noun in -yaw (wrth rodyaw y wlat 'while roaming the land'); softened after wrth, but r also writes rh, so the change does not show
gyuanhedach: cyfanhedd (cyfanhedd) — inhabited, settled, dwelling; adjective, comparative in -ach 'more settled' (wlat gyuanhedach no hi 'a land more settled than it'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the feminine noun wlat
heldir: heldir (no modern form) — hunting-land, land for the chase; noun m., hela 'hunt' + tir 'land', with tir softened (t>d) in the compound (na heldir well 'nor a better hunting-land'); h- unchanged after na
amlach: aml (aml) — many, plentiful, frequent; adjective, comparative in -ach 'more plentiful' (nac amlach y mel 'nor more plentiful its honey'); radical after nac
mel: mel (mêl) — honey; noun m. (nac amlach y mel 'nor more plentiful its honey'); radical: y here is 'its' (for the feminine gwlat), which does not change m
physcawt: pysgod (pysgod) — fish; collective noun, MW pysgawd (written -awt) (na'y physcawt 'nor its fish'; a physcawt 'and fish'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after y 'her, its' (referring to feminine gwlat) and after a 'and'
tyuu: tyfu (tyfu) — to grow; verbal noun in narrative use 'grew' (Ac yn hynny tyuu kedymdeithas 'and in that fellowship grew'); radical
mynnei: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish, be willing; 3 sg. imperfect 'wanted' in -ei (hyt na mynnei yr un uot heb y gilid 'so that neither wished to be without the other'); no mutation shown after hyt na
ychen: ych (ych) — ox; plural ychen 'oxen', as in the place-name Ryt Ychen 'Ford of Oxen', Oxford; noun m., genitive following ryt, radical
wrogaeth: gwrogaeth (gwrogaeth) — homage, fealty, vassalage; noun f.; soft-mutated (g lost) after y 'his' (y wrogaeth idaw 'his homage')
gwledeu: gwled (gwledd) — feast, banquet; noun f., plural in -eu (modern gwleddoedd); radical after eu 'their' (eu gwledeu 'their feasts')
hesmwythder: esmwythder (esmwythder) — ease, comfort, softness; noun m.; h- prefixed after eu 'their' (eu hesmwythder 'their ease')
honei: o (o) + hi — conjugated preposition 3 sg. fem. 'of her, from her/it' (modern ohoni), written o honei; here 'from it' of the court, feminine llys (o honei y dechreuit pob anryded 'from it every honour was begun')
dechreuit: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; impersonal imperfect 'was begun' (habitual, 'used to be begun') in -it (y dechreuit pob anryded 'every honour was begun'); radical after the particle y
gwassanaethwyr: gwasanaethwr (gwasanaethwr) — servant, attendant, waiter; noun m., plural gwassanaethwyr (ss for s); radical, subject after uei
dwrwf: twrf (twrf; also twrw) — noise, din, tumult; noun m., spelt twrwf; soft-mutated (t>d) after the presentative llyma (llyma dwrwf 'behold, a noise')
gawat: cawod (cawod) — shower; noun f. (gawat o nywl 'a shower of mist'); soft-mutated (c>g) after llyma 'behold'
nywl: nywl (niwl) — mist, fog; noun m. (gawat o nywl 'a shower of mist'; yn ol y nywl 'after the mist'); n does not change after o or the article
chanhoed: kanuot (canfod) — to see, perceive, make out; 3 sg. imperfect 'saw, could see', in -oed like other compounds of bot (gwybot, adnabot) (hyt na chanhoed yr un ohonunt wy y gilid 'so that none of them could see the other'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after na
goleuhau: goleuhau (goleuo; GPC goleuhau) — to grow light, brighten, light up; verbal noun after yn (llyma yn goleuhau pob lle 'behold, every place growing light'); no mutation
edrychyssant: edrych (edrych) — to look, see; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they looked' (phan edrychyssant y ford … 'when they looked the way …'); radical (vowel-initial)
guelyn: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. imperfect 'used to see, saw', for gwelynt (final -t unwritten; -yn is the shortened -ynt) (y ford y guelyn y preideu 'the way they used to see the flocks'); gu- spells gw-, radical after the relative y
preideu: praidd (praidd) — flock, herd, cattle; noun m., plural in -eu (modern preiddiau); radical after the article y (y preideu 'the flocks')
anreitheu: anrhaith (anrhaith) — spoil, booty, plunder; hence goods, livestock, possessions; noun f., plural in -eu (y preideu a'r anreitheu 'the flocks and the herds/spoils'); the exact sense here, 'livestock' or 'possessions', is uncertain; radical after the article
kyuanhed: cyfanhedd (cyfanhedd) — dwelling, habitation, inhabited place; noun m. (y kyuanhed 'the dwellings'; ay ty ay kyuanhed 'either house or dwelling'); radical after the article y; cf. the adjective gyuanhedach · also adjective 'inhabited' (yn gyuanhed 'inhabited'), soft after yn (c>g)
thy: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m.; spirant-mutated (t>th) after na 'neither' (na thy 'nor any house')
aniueil: anifail (anifail) — animal, beast; noun m.; radical after nac 'nor' before a vowel (nac aniueil)
mwc: mwg (mwg) — smoke; noun m., spelt -c for -g; radical after na (na mwc 'nor smoke')
than: tan (tân) — fire; noun m.; spirant-mutated (t>th) after na 'nor' (na than 'nor fire')
chyuanhed: cyfanhedd (cyfanhedd) — dwelling, habitation; noun m.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'nor' (na chyuanhed 'nor dwelling')
wac: gwag (gwag) — empty, vacant; adjective, spelt -c for -g; g lost by soft mutation after predicative yn (yn wac 'empty')
diffeith: diffaith (diffaith) — desolate, waste, barren; adjective (wac, diffeith 'empty, desolate'); radical
anghyuanhed: anghyfanhedd (anghyfanhedd) — uninhabited, deserted; adjective, an- 'not' + cyfanhedd, the c nasalised to gh after an-; radical in the series wac, diffeith, anghyuanhed
uil: mil (mil) — animal, beast; noun m.; soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after heb 'without' (heb uil yndi 'without beast in it')
kedymdeithon: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; noun m., plural in -on (modern cydymdeithion) (eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions'); radical after eu 'their'
colli: colli (colli) — to lose; verbal noun (wedy eu colli 'lost', lit. 'after their losing'; yn colli 'losing'); radical after eu and after the yn of the progressive
wyll: wyll (no modern form; analysis uncertain) — contraction of wy 'they' + yll 'all, the whole company', 'they all' (onyt wyll pedwar 'except them, the four'); cf. the known yll pedwar
anniuer: niuer (nifer) — company, host, retinue; noun m.; an 'our' + niuer, written an(n)iuer (an niuer ninheu 'our company, we'); the an- is the possessive and no further mutation is shown
hundy: hundy (no modern form) — sleeping-house, bed-chamber; noun m., hun 'sleep' + ty 'house', with ty softened (t>d) in the compound; radical after the article
ymedgell: ymedgell — ym 'in' + medgell (no modern form) 'mead-cellar' (med 'mead' + kell 'cell', k softened in the compound), written as one word with the double m written once (Ymedgell 'in the mead-cellar'); noun f.; m is unchanged by the nasal mutation after yn
kegin: kegin (cegin) — kitchen; noun f.; after yg 'in' (yn before k), whose g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg kegin = modern yng nghegin)
guydlwdyn: gwydlwdyn (no modern form) — wild beast; noun m., gwyd 'wild' + llwdyn 'beast', with ll softened in the compound; used as a collective, 'wild beasts' (neb ryw dim ny welynt eithyr guydlwdyn 'they saw nothing at all but wild beasts'); gu- spells gw-; radical after eithyr
ymborth: ymborth (ymborth) — (1) food, sustenance (y caffom yn ymborth 'that we may get as sustenance'); (2) as verbal noun, to feed, live (on) (dechreu a wnaethant ymborth ar kic hela 'they began to live on the meat of the chase'); noun m. / verbal noun; radical
bydaueu: bydaf (bydaf; pl. bydafau) — swarm (of bees); plural in -eu (a bydaueu 'and swarms', i.e. bees' honey, wild bees); radical after a 'and' (a does not mutate b)
diwed: diwed (diwedd) — end, close; noun m., d spells dd; radical after the article y (yn y diwed 'in the end')
dygyaw: dygyaw (no modern form) — a rare verb whose sense is uncertain: apparently 'have had enough, grow weary, become too much'; verbal noun (dygyaw a wnaethant 'they grew weary'); the Red Book has diffygyaw 'fail, grow weary' here; radical, fronted before a wnaethant
bydwn: bot (bod) — to be; 1 pl. future 'we will be' in -wn (ny bydwn ual hynn 'we will not be like this'); radical after ny (b is not softened here)
kyrchwn: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, go to; 1 pl. imperative 'let us make for' in -wn (Kyrchwn Loygyr 'let us make for England'); radical
loygyr: Proper name — Lloegr, England (spelt Loygyr); softened (ll>l) as the object straight after the verb (Kyrchwn Loygyr 'let us make for England') · also soft (ll>l) after o 'from' (o Loygyr 'from England')
cheisswn: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; 1 pl. imperative 'let us seek' in -wn (a cheisswn greft 'and let us seek a craft'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
greft: crefft (crefft) — craft, trade, skill; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) as the direct object directly after the verb (cheisswn greft 'let us seek a craft'); cause the soft mutation of an object after an inflected verb · also soft-mutated (c>g) after pa 'what' (pa greft 'what craft')
caffom: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 1 pl. present subjunctive 'we may get' in -om (greft y caffom yn ymborth 'a craft by which we may get our sustenance'); radical after the particle y
lloygyr: Proper name — Lloegr, England (Lloygyr beside Lloegyr); radical (Kyrchu Lloygyr 'making for England'; yn Lloygyr 'in England')
henford: Proper name — Henffordd, Hereford (MW Henford, f for ff), on the English border; radical (hyt yn Henford 'as far as Hereford'; dros wyneb Henford 'throughout Hereford')
kyfrwyeu: kyfrwy (cyfrwy) — saddle; noun m., plural in -eu (modern cyfrwyau) (gwneuthur kyfrwyeu 'making saddles'); radical
llunyaw: llunyaw (llunio) — to shape, form, fashion, design; verbal noun in -yaw (llunyaw corueu 'shaping saddle-bows'; eu llunyaw ar weith taryaneu 'shaping them after the pattern of shields'); radical
corueu: corf (corf; MW also koryf) — saddle-bow, the raised front or back of a saddle; noun m., plural in -eu (llunyaw corueu 'shaping saddle-bows'); u spells f; radical as the object of the verbal noun
wed: gwedd (gwedd) — manner, fashion, way; noun f.; g lost by soft mutation after the feminine article y (ar y wed y guelsei 'in the manner that he had seen') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) after y 'his' (y liw a'y wed 'his colour and his looks'; wed 'looks, appearance')
guelsei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had seen' in -sei (y guelsei gan Lassar 'that he had seen from Llasar, seen done by Llasar'); gu- spells gw-, radical after the relative y
lassar: Llassar (Llasar) — (1) the name Llasar, in Llassar Llaes Gygnwyt (Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid), softened (ll>l) after gan 'from, with' and o 'by' (gan Lassar, o Lassar); (2) llasar 'azure, blue enamel', in calch lassar, which the text derives from the name; there it is written beside calch llassar, and the l shows no cause (calch is masculine)
gygnwyt: Proper name — the epithet Gyfnewid (written Gygnwyt) in Lassar Llaes Gygnwyt, 'Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid'; cyfnewid means 'exchange', but the spelling here is unusual and the epithet's meaning is uncertain; soft-mutated (c>g) after llaes 'trailing' as an epithet noun
chalch: calch (calch) — lime, plaster, enamel; noun m. (a chalch llassar 'and azure lime'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
calch: calch (calch) — lime, plaster, enamel; noun m. (calch lassar, calch llassar, the blue enamel named after Llasar); radical
gwnathoed: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had made' in -oed (ual y gwnathoed y gwr arall 'as the other man had made'); radical after the relative y
gueith: gweith (gwaith) — work, labour, craft, the thing made; noun m., gu- spells gw- (o'r gueith hwnnw 'of that work'; y gueith wynteu 'their work'); radical after the article and after y standing for eu 'their'
geffit: caffael (cael) — to get, have; impersonal imperfect (subjunctive/habitual) 'was got, could be had' in -it (tra geffit gan Uanawydan 'while there was to be got from Manawydan'); soft-mutated (c>g) after tra 'while'
phrynit: prynu (prynu) — to buy; impersonal imperfect 'was bought' in -it (ny phrynit gan gyfrwyd 'it was not bought from a saddler'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny and after hyt na
gyfrwyd: kyfrwyd (no modern form in common use; cf. cyfrwy 'saddle') — saddler; noun m.; soft-mutated (k>g) after gan 'from' (gan gyfrwyd 'from a saddler')
choryf: corf (corf; MW also koryf) — saddle-bow; noun m., spelt koryf (na choryf na chyfrwy 'neither saddle-bow nor saddle'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after na
chyfrwy: kyfrwy (cyfrwy) — saddle; noun m.; spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'nor'
adnabu: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise, perceive; 3 sg. preterite 'knew, came to know' in -u (yny adnabu pob un o'r kyfrwydyon 'until each of the saddlers realised'); radical after yny
kyfrwydyon: kyfrwyd (no modern form in common use; cf. cyfrwy 'saddle') — saddler; plural in -yon 'saddlers' (pob un o'r kyfrwydyon 'each of the saddlers'); radical after the article
henill: ennill (ennill) — gain, profit, earnings; noun m.; h- prefixed after 'y 'his' (o'y henill 'of his gain')
frynit: prynu (prynu) — to buy; impersonal imperfect 'was bought' in -it, spelt with f for ph (ny frynit dim ganthunt 'nothing was bought from them'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny
cheffit: caffael (cael) — to get, have; impersonal imperfect (subjunctive) 'was got, could be had' in -it (guedy na cheffit gan Uanawydan 'after nothing was to be had from Manawydan'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'not'
ymgynullaw: ymgynnull (ymgynnull; MW ymgynullaw) — to gather together, assemble; reflexive ym- + cynnull, verbal noun in -aw (ymgynullaw y gyt ohonunt 'they gathering together'); radical
duunaw: duunaw (dyuno) — to agree, come to one mind; verbal noun in -aw, du- + un 'one' (duunaw ar y lad ef 'agreeing on killing him'); radical
rybud: rybud (rhybudd) — warning, notice; noun m. (rybud a gawssont 'they got warning'; Rybud a doeth udunt 'warning came to them'); radical, placed first before a
gawssont: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 3 pl. preterite in -ssont 'they got', beside -ssant (rybud a gawssont 'they got warning'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a following the fronted object
chynghoraf: cynghori (cynghori) — to advise, counsel; 1 sg. present 'I advise' (ni chynghoraf i adaw y dref 'I do not advise leaving the town'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after the negative ni
tayogeu: taeog (taeog) — villein, serf, churl; noun m., plural in -eu (tayogeu, modern taeogion) (llad y tayogeu racco 'killing those churls yonder'); radical after the article y
ymladem: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; 1 pl. imperfect subjunctive 'we fought' in -em (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them'); radical (vowel-initial)
clot: clot (clod) — fame, reputation, renown; noun m. (clot drwc 'ill fame, a bad name'); radical, fronted subject before uydei
carcharu: carcharu (carcharu) — to imprison; verbal noun (ac yn carcharu a wneit 'and we would be imprisoned', lit. 'our imprisoning would be done', yn standing for an 'our'); radical
in: y (i) + ni — 'to us, for us'; conjugated preposition 1 pl., spelt in (ys guell in 'it is better for us'); no mutation
tref: tref (tref) — town, homestead, settlement; noun f. (kyrchu tref arall 'making for another town'); radical as object after the verbal noun; the adjective arall follows
ymossymdeithaw: ymossymdeithaw (no modern form) — to maintain oneself, make a living; reflexive verbal noun in -aw, ym- + ossymdeith 'sustenance, provision' (cf. gossymdeithaw 'provide for') (e ymossymdeithaw yndi 'to make our living in it'); the e before it is y 'to'
dinas: dinas (dinas) — city, fortified town; noun f. (kyrchu dinas arall 'making for another city'); radical as object after the verbal noun
geluydyt: celfyddyd (celfyddyd) — craft, trade, art, skill; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after pa 'what' (Pa geluydyt 'what craft') · also soft-mutated (c>g) after the feminine article y (y geluydyt 'the craft')
gwnawn: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 pl. imperative / present-future 'let us make, we will make' in -wn (Gwnawn taryaneu 'let us make shields'; gwnawn grydyaeth 'let us make shoemaking'); radical at the head of a clause
taryaneu: taryan (tarian) — shield; noun f., plural in -eu (modern tariannau) (gwnawn taryaneu 'let us make shields'; gweith taryaneu 'work of shields'); radical
prouwn: profi (profi) — to try, test, prove; 1 pl. present/future 'we will try' in -wn, spelt prouwn (Ni a'y prouwn 'we will try it'); radical after the infixed pronoun 'y 'it'
weith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, make, pattern, manner; noun m. (MW gweith); g lost by soft mutation after ar (ar weith taryaneu da 'after the pattern of good shields, on the work of good shields'); the sense 'manner, pattern' is a little uncertain · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as the object of welsynt (y lle ny welsynt eiryoet weith 'where they had never seen work'); gweith 'time' is possible but less likely · also soft after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw weith 'what kind of work') and after y (gohir ar y weith 'delay over the work') · also soft after un 'one' (yn un weith a hynny 'of one make with that')
gweith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, labour, craft, thing made; noun m. (A'r gweith hwnnw 'and that work'); radical after the article y
lwydwys: llwyddo (llwyddo; MW llwydaw) — to prosper, succeed, thrive; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'prospered' (a lwydwys racdunt 'prospered before them'); ll>l written, the soft mutation after the particle a
kyflym: kyflym (cyflym) — swift, quick; adjective, predicate placed first before oed (Kyflym oed y gueith 'swift was their work'); radical
diuessur: difesur (GPC difesur, also dimesur) — measureless, immense, immoderate, excessive; adjective/adverb, di- 'without' + mesur 'measure', soft m>u after di- (a diuessur a wneynt 'and measureless they made', i.e. they made a great deal)
dygywys: dygyaw (no modern form) — a rare verb whose sense is uncertain, apparently 'grow weary, become too much (for)'; 3 sg. preterite in -wys (yny dygywys y'w kytdrefwyr racdunt 'until it became too much for their fellow-townsmen'); the Red Book has dygwydawd here; radical after yny
w: w — apostrophe half of y'w 'to his, her, their', y 'to' + w, a contraction of ei/eu; here 'their' (y'w kytdrefwyr 'to their fellow-townsmen'); no mutation, since eu causes none
kytdrefwyr: kytdrefwr (no modern form) — fellow-townsman; noun m., plural in -wyr, kyt- 'fellow' + tref 'town' + gwr 'man', tref softened (t>d) in the compound (y'w kytdrefwyr 'to their fellow-townsmen'); radical after 'w 'their'
duunyssant: duunaw (dyuno) — to agree, come to one mind; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they agreed' (yny duunyssant ar geissaw eu llad 'until they agreed on seeking to kill them'); radical after yny
geissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try; verbal noun in -aw (ar geissaw eu llad 'on seeking to kill them'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'on'
chlybot: clybot (clywed) — to hear; verbal noun clybot (a chlybot bot y gwyr 'and hearing that the men were'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and'
bryt: bryt (bryd) — mind, intent, purpose, mood; noun m., t for d (ac y bryt ar eu dienydyaw 'and their mind on putting them to death', the y being eu 'their'); radical · also bryt ← pryt 'form, looks', soft-mutated (p>b) after dy 'your' (colli dy bryt a'th liw 'losing your looks and your colour'); a different word from bryt 'mind'
chymerwn: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 pl. future 'we will take' in -wn (Ny chymerwn inheu y gan y tayogeu 'we will not take it from those churls'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ny
adanunt: at (at) + wynt — conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'to, at them' (modern atynt), in -dunt/-anunt (Awn adanunt 'let us go at them'); no mutation
casswallawn: Proper name — Caswallon (Casswallawn, ss for s), son of Beli; radical, subject before a glywei (Casswallawn a glywei hynny 'Caswallon would hear that')
rewin: rewin (rhewin) — ruin, destruction (Latin ruina); noun, here a predicate placed first (a rewin uydem 'and ruined we would be', lit. 'ruin'); radical
uydem: bot (bod) — to be; 1 pl. imperfect (conditional) 'we would be' in -em (a rewin uydem 'and we would be ruined'); soft-mutated (b>u) after a fronted predicate, the relative a being understood
awni: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 pl. present awn 'we go' with the pronoun ni written on, awn + ni (yd awni wrthi 'by which we go to it, we set about it'); the particle yd is used before a vowel
wdam: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 pl. present 'we know' (o'r a wdam 'of what we know'); g lost by soft mutation after the relative a
grydyaeth: cryddiaeth (cryddiaeth) — shoemaking, the cobbler's trade; noun f. (crydd 'shoemaker' + -yaeth); soft-mutated (c>g) as direct object after gwnawn (gwnawn grydyaeth 'let us do shoemaking')
galhon: calon (calon) — heart, courage, desire; noun f., spelt with h (galhon); soft-mutated (c>g) after o 'of' (ni byd o galhon gan grydyon 'there will not be heart among shoemakers'); the idiom ('they will not have the heart') is not certain; the Red Book's o gallon supports calon, though the White Book's h is unexplained
grydyon: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker; noun m., plural in -yon (modern cryddion); soft-mutated (c>g) after gan 'with, among' (gan grydyon) · also soft-mutated (c>g) after holl 'all' (holl grydyon 'all the shoemakers')
ymwarauun: gwarafun (gwarafun) — to forbid, refuse, hinder; reflexive ym-, verbal noun, g lost by soft mutation after ym- (nac ymlad a ni nac ymwarauun 'neither fighting with us nor forbidding'); reciprocal sense uncertain
dyscaf: dyscu (dysgu) — to teach, learn; 1 sg. present/future 'I will teach' in -af (a mi a dyscaf it wniaw 'and I will teach you to sew'); soft mutation after a, not visible (d>dd)
wniaw: gwnïo (gwnïo) — to sew, stitch; verbal noun in -aw (spelt wniaw); g lost by soft mutation as the object following the pronoun it 'to you' (dyscaf it wniaw 'I will teach you sewing')
ymyrrwn: ymyrru (ymyrryd) — to meddle, interfere, concern oneself (with, ar); 1 pl. future in -wn 'we will meddle' (nit ymyrrwn ar gyweiraw lledyr 'we will not meddle with dressing leather'); radical after nit
gyweiraw: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to put in order, prepare, dress, mend; verbal noun in -aw (ar gyweiraw lledyr 'at dressing leather'); soft-mutated (c>g) after ar
lledyr: lledr (lledr) — leather; noun m., object of the verbal noun (cyweiraw lledyr 'dressing leather'); radical
brynu: prynu (prynu) — to buy; verbal noun, soft-mutated (p>b) after y 'its', the object of a verbal noun standing as a possessive before it (namyn y brynu yn barawt 'but buying it ready-made')
prynu: prynu (prynu) — to buy; verbal noun (dechreu prynu y cordwal 'beginning to buy the cordovan'); radical after dechreu
cordwal: cordwal (cordwal) — cordovan leather, fine leather, from Cordoba; noun m.; radical after the article y
ledyr: lledr (lledr) — leather; noun m.; soft-mutated (ll>l) after amgen 'other' (amgen ledyr no hwnnw 'other leather than that'); written l for ll
phrynei: prynu (prynu) — to buy; 3 sg. imperfect/conditional 'would buy' in -ei (ny phrynei ef 'he would not buy'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny
guadneu: gwadn (gwadn) — sole (of the foot, of a shoe); noun m., plural in -eu, used attributively (lledyr guadneu 'sole-leather, leather of soles'); gu- spells gw-
ymgedymdeithassu: ymgedymdeithasu (no modern form in ordinary use; ym- + kedymdeithas 'fellowship') — to make fellowship, associate with; reflexive verbal noun (ymgedymdeithassu a'r eurych 'making fellowship with the goldsmith'); radical
eurych: eurych (eurych) — goldsmith; noun m. (a'r eurych goreu 'the best goldsmith'); radical after the article
guaegeu: gwäeg (GPC gwäeg; not in current use) — buckle, clasp; noun f., plural in -eu (peri guaegeu y'r eskidyeu 'causing buckles to be made for the shoes'); gu- spells gw-
eskidyeu: esgid (esgid) — shoe; noun f., plural eskidyeu (modern esgidiau) (y'r eskidyeu 'for the shoes'); radical after the article
euraw: euro (euro) — to gild, cover with gold; verbal noun in -aw (euraw y guaegeu 'gilding the buckles'); radical
gwybu: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. preterite 'knew, learnt' in -u (yny gwybu 'until he knew'); radical after yny
eurgryd: eurgryd (eurgrydd) — gold-shoemaker, a shoemaker who gilds; noun m., eur- 'gold' + cryd 'shoemaker', with c>g in the compound (yn tryded eurgryd 'the third gold-shoemaker', from a triad of 'Three Gold-Shoemakers')
eskit: esgid (esgid) — shoe; noun f. (nac eskit na hossan 'neither shoe nor hose'); radical after nac
hossan: hosan (hosan) — stocking, hose; noun f., ss for s (na hossan 'nor hose'); radical after na, h- not mutated
gryd: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker, cobbler; noun m.; soft-mutated (c>g) after gan 'from' (gan gryd 'from a shoemaker')
crydyon: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker; noun m., plural in -yon (modern cryddion) (y crydyon 'the shoemakers'); radical after the article
hennill: ennill (ennill) — gain, profit, earnings; noun m.; h- prefixed after eu 'their' (eu hennill 'their gain')
llunyei: llunyaw (llunio) — to shape, form, make; 3 sg. imperfect 'shaped, used to shape' in -ei (ual y llunyei Uanawydan y gueith 'as Manawydan used to shape the work'); radical after the relative y
gwniei: gwnïo (gwnïo) — to sew; 3 sg. imperfect 'sewed, used to sew' in -ei (y gwniei Pryderi 'so Pryderi would sew'); radical after the correlative y 'so'
gausant: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 3 pl. preterite 'they got' in -sant (sef a gausant yn eu kynghor 'this is what they got in their counsel, they decided'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
pam: pam (pam) — why; interrogative adverb (Pam y kymerwn inheu hynny? 'why should we take that?'), followed by the particle y
kymerwn: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 pl. present/future/subjunctive 'we take, we should take' in -wn (Pam y kymerwn inheu hynny 'why should we take that?'); radical after the particle y
lladron: lleidr (lleidr) — thief, robber; noun m., plural lladron (the singular has the affected vowel) (y tayogeu lladron 'the thieving churls', lit. 'the churls thieves'); radical
ymladwn: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; 1 pl. future/present in -wn 'we will fight' (nyt ymladwn ac wynt 'we will not fight with them'); radical after nyt
hedrych: edrych (edrych) — to look, see, look at; verbal noun, with prosthetic h- after y 'her, its' (y hedrych 'to see it', the feminine Dyuet as referent: ac awn y hedrych 'and let us go to see it')
byhyt: pa hyt (pa hyd) — what length; Byhyt is py hyt (py, a by-form of pa 'what') + hyt 'length', written as one word (Byhyt bynnac 'however long'); noun hyt m. in an adverbial phrase; how the b arose is uncertain (008 has A pha hyt bynnac); no mutation of h-
fford: fford (ffordd) — road, way, journey; noun f. (ar y fford 'on the road'); written with ff, as against ford in 008; radical after the article y (ff does not mutate)
chynnull: kynnull (cynnull) — to gather, collect; verbal noun (a chynnull eu cwn 'and gathering their dogs'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
boregueith: boregueith (boreuwaith) — one morning; adverbial compound of bore 'morning' + gweith 'time' (gu- = gw-), like treigylgweith 'one time'; no mutation (A boregueith)
wlaen: blaen (blaen) — front, fore part; noun m., in the phrase o ulaen 'in front of', where blaen is softened (b>f) after o; here o'e wlaen 'in front of them', with 'e 'their' put inside the phrase and w written for the softened b (compare Vynt for wynt in 008). 'e 'their' leaves a consonant unmutated, so the softening is irregular here, as if carried over from the fixed o ulaen; the Red Book has the regular oeblaen
berth: perth (perth) — bush, thicket, hedge; noun f.; soft-mutated (p>b) after the feminine article ('r: y'r berth, a'r berth, o'r berth) and after the preposition y 'to' (y berth uechan 'to a little bush')
aant: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. present 'they go' (yd aant y'r berth 'as they go to the bush'), the vivid present in past narrative; no mutation (vowel stem, after the particle yd)
cheginwrych: keginwrych (modern form uncertain) — bristling hackles, the raised bristles of a boar's back; noun m., apparently a compound with gwrych 'bristles' (first element uncertain); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a cheginwrych mawr aruthyr 'and great fearful hackles')
aruthyr: aruthyr (aruthr) — dreadful, terrible, monstrous; adjective, after mawr (mawr aruthyr 'great, terrible'); no mutation
nessawn: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; 1 pl. imperative 'let us draw near' (Nessawn parth a'r berth), in -wn; no mutation
nessaant: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; 3 pl. present 'they draw near' (Pan nessaant), the vivid present in -ant; no mutation
uaed: baed (baedd) — boar; noun m.; soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after the presentative llyma (llyma uaed coed 'behold a boar of the wood')
coed: coed (coed) — wood, trees, forest; noun m., here (the old coet) as the genitive noun after baed: baed coed 'wild boar', literally 'boar of the wood'; no mutation
claerwynn: claerwynn (claerwyn) — bright white, shining white; adjective, a compound of claer 'bright' + gwynn 'white', gwynn softened (gw>w) inside the compound; describes the masculine uaed; no mutation of the whole word
hyder: hyder (hyder) — confidence, courage, heart; noun m. (o hyder y guyr 'heartened by the men', literally 'out of the confidence of the men'); radical after o (h does not mutate)
ruthraw: ruthraw (rhuthro) — to rush, charge, attack; verbal noun (ruthraw idaw 'rushing at it'); r writes rh, so any soft mutation (rh>r) cannot be told from the spelling
chilyaw: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat, withdraw; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chilyaw dalym 'and retreating a little way')
kyuarth: kyuarth (cyfarth) — baying, barking (of hounds round a beast at bay); noun m., also the verbal noun 'to bark'; kyuarth a rodei 'baying it would give' (a beast that gives kyuarth stands at bay); radical, a fronted object before the particle a
gilyaw: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat, withdraw; verbal noun, soft-mutated (k>g) after heb 'without' (heb gilyaw yrdhunt 'without retreating for them')
yrdhunt: er (er) + wynt — conjugated preposition, 3 pl. 'for them, on account of them' (modern erddynt), MW erdunt, here written yrdhunt with dh for the /ð/ sound (heb gilyaw yrdhunt 'without retreating for them', not giving ground on their account); the Red Book yrdunt; not a form of rac, which this part writes racdunt; no mutation
ynghei: ynghei (lemma uncertain) — 3 sg. imperfect 'would draw close, would close in' (A phan ynghei y guyr 'and when the men would close in'); apparently from a verb related to yng 'narrow, close'; the meaning is taken from the context and is uncertain
kilyei: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat, withdraw; 3 sg. imperfect 'he/it would retreat' (y kilyei eilweith 'it would retreat again'), habitual past; radical after the particle y
eilweith: eilweith (eilwaith) — a second time, again; adverb, eil 'second' + gweith 'time', gweith softened (gw>w) after eil inside the compound; no mutation of the whole word
torrei: torri (torri) — to break; 3 sg. imperfect 'would break' (y torrei gyuarth 'it would break bay', sense of the phrase uncertain); radical after the particle y
gyuarth: kyuarth (cyfarth) — baying, barking (of hounds); noun m.; soft-mutated (k>g) as the object directly after the inflected verb torrei (torrei gyuarth; the sense of the phrase is uncertain)
baed: baed (baedd) — boar; noun m.; radical after the masculine article (y baed 'the boar')
kerdassant: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; 3 pl. preterite in -assant 'they walked' (y kerdassant 'they went'); radical after the particle y following the fronted phrase yn ol y baed
gaer: kaer (caer) — fort, stronghold, fortified place; noun f.; soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article (y gaer, y'r gaer, yr gaer) and as the object after a verb (yny welynt gaer uawr 'until they saw a great fort')
newyd: newyd (newydd) — new, fresh; adjective (gueith newyd 'new work'); radical after the masculine noun
maen: maen (maen) — stone; noun m. (na maen na gueith 'neither stone nor work'); radical after na 'neither' · also in the name Maen Tyuyawc (y Maen Tyuyawc 'at Maen Tyfiawg'), where y most likely stands for ym 'in', the nasal mutation leaving M unchanged; the Red Book writes ymaen tyuyawc
uuan: buan (buan) — swift, quick; adjective; soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after yn making it an adverb (yn uuan 'swiftly')
ryuedu: ryuedu (rhyfeddu) — to marvel, wonder; verbal noun (ryuedu a wnaethant 'they marvelled'); r writes rh; no visible mutation
chlywynt: klywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. imperfect 'they heard' (ny chlywynt 'they did not hear'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the negative ny
gwney: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. present/future 'you do' (o gwney 'if you do'); radical gw- after o 'if' (o 'if' causes no mutation)
hynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice; noun m.; nasal-mutated (k>ngh) after uy 'my', written uyg hynghor (the g on the possessive and h on the noun spell the ngh, as in uyg kwn)
ey: mynet (mynd) — to go; 2 sg. present/future 'you will go' (nyt ey idi 'you will not go into it'), the suppletive stem e-; no mutation after the negative nyt
dodes: dodi (dodi) — to put, place; 3 sg. preterite 'put' (a dodes hut ar y wlat 'who put an enchantment on the land'); after the relative a, where d>dd would be unseen in the spelling
beris: peri (peri) — to cause, make (happen); 3 sg. preterite 'caused' (a beris bot y gaer yma 'who caused the fort to be here'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the relative a
