madeuaf: madeu (maddau) — to forgive, let go, give up; 1 sg. present/future 'I will give up' (ny madeuaf i uyg kwn 'I will not give up my dogs'); written radical (m-) after ny, where the soft form uadeuaf would be expected
kwn: ci (ci) — dog; noun, plural cwn (written kwn with k); nasal-mutated (c>ngh) after uy 'my', written uyg kwn (= fy nghwn), the g on the possessive spelling the nasal
gaffei: caffael (cael) — to get, find; 3 sg. imperfect 'would get' (Pa gynghor bynnac a gaffei ef 'whatever counsel he would get'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
mil: mil (mil) — animal, beast, living creature; noun m. (na mil 'nor any beast'); radical after na 'nor'; not the numeral 'thousand'
anhed: anhed (annedd) — dwelling, habitation; noun f. (nac anhed 'nor a dwelling'), the old spelling with h; no mutation (vowel initial)
gymherued: kymherued (modern form uncertain) — middle, centre, midpoint; noun m., a compound of kyf- + perued 'middle'; soft-mutated (k>g) after the preposition am 'about' (am gymherued llawr y gaer 'about the middle of the floor of the fort')
fynnawn: ffynnawn (ffynnon) — spring, well, fountain; noun f.; f for ff; radical (ff does not mutate), as the object of welei (Ef a welei … fynnawn a gueith o uaen marmor 'he saw … a well with stonework of marble') and after the article (ar lann y fynnawn 'on the edge of the well')
marmor: marmor (marmor) — marble; noun m. (maen marmor 'marble stone'), a borrowing from Latin; no mutation
chylch: kylch (cylch) — circle, ring, surround; noun m.; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after y 'its' (yn y chylch 'round it', literally 'in its circle'), the possessive referring to the feminine fynnawn
lann: glann (glan) — bank, edge, shore; noun f.; g lost by soft mutation (gl>l) after the preposition ar (ar lann y fynnawn 'on the edge of the spring'); not llan 'church, enclosure'
cawg: cawg (cawg) — bowl, cup; noun m. (taken up by ac ef 'with it'; also spelt cawc); radical (cawg uch benn llech 'a bowl above a slab')
llech: llech (llech) — flat stone, slab; noun f.; no mutation (uch benn llech 'above a slab'; wrth y llech 'to the slab')
chadwyneu: kadwyn (cadwyn) — chain; noun f., plural kadwyneu (-eu, modern cadwyni); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chadwyneu yn kyrchu yr awyr 'and chains rising into the air')
awyr: awyr (awyr) — air, sky; noun (yr awyr 'the air'); no mutation (vowel initial)
diben: diben (diben) — end, limit, top (of the chains); noun m. (a diben ny welei 'and an end he did not see'); radical, the object put before ny welei
gorawenu: gorawenu (gorawenu, literary) — to rejoice greatly, be elated, exult; verbal noun (gorawenu a wnaeth 'he rejoiced'), from gorawen 'great joy, exultation'; no mutation
decket: tec (teg) — fair, beautiful; equative tecket (modern teced) 'as fair, how fair', used as a noun 'fairness' (wrth decket yr eur 'at the fairness of the gold', how fair it was); soft-mutated (t>d) after the preposition wrth
dahet: da (da) — good; equative dahet 'as good, how good', formed directly on da (the usual equative is kystal) and used as a noun (dahet gueith y cawc 'how good the work of the bowl was'); radical: a 'and' gives d no mutation
cawc: cawg (cawg) — bowl, cup; noun m., spelt cawc with final c for g (y cawc 'the bowl'; ymauael ac ef 'taking hold of it'); radical after the masculine article
ymeueil: ymauael (ymafael) — to take hold, grasp; 3 sg. present 'takes hold' (yd ymeueil a'r cawc 'as he takes hold of the bowl'), the vivid present, stem vowel a>e; no mutation
glynu: glynu (glynu) — to stick, cling, adhere; verbal noun (glynu y dwylaw wrth y cawc 'his hands sticking to the bowl'); no mutation
allei: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. imperfect 'he/she could' (hyt na allei dywedut 'so that he could not speak'); g lost by soft mutation after the negative na
aros: aros (aros) — to wait, wait for, stay; verbal noun (A'e aros 'and waiting for him', 'e being 'him', the object); no mutation (vowel initial)
phrynhawn: prynhawn (prynhawn) — afternoon; noun m.; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (A phrynhawn byrr 'and a short afternoon')
byrr: byrr (byr) — short, brief; adjective, written byrr (prynhawn byrr 'a short afternoon', the day grown late); radical after a masculine noun
datcanu: datcanu (datgan) — to declare, recount, relate; verbal noun (a'e datcanu oll 'and he recounted it all', 'e being the object 'it'); d does not show the softening after 'e
uuosti: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. preterite 'you were' (buost) with the pronoun ti written on (buosti); soft-mutated (b>u, = f) as after the relative a, which is not written here but is in the parallel a golleisti (ys drwc a gedymdeith uuosti 'a bad companion you were')
golleisti: colli (colli) — to lose; 2 sg. preterite 'you lost' (colleist) with the pronoun ti written on; soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a (a gedymdeith a golleisti 'a companion that you lost')
managassei: managu (mynegi) — to show, tell; a by-form of menegi; 3 sg. pluperfect 'he had shown' in -assei (y traws y managassei ef 'the quarter that he had shown'); radical after the particle y
argel: argel (argel) — concealment, hiding, secrecy; noun m. (ny bu argel arnei 'there was no concealment on it', the gate not shut); no mutation (vowel initial)
deutroet: deudroet (deudroed) — two feet; noun m., the dual compound deu 'two' + troet 'foot' (a'y deutroet 'and her two feet'); written here with t, unsoftened, where deu normally softens (deudroet elsewhere in the work; the Red Book also deutroet); no visible mutation after 'y 'her'
dwryf: twrf (twrf) — noise, din, tumult; noun m., spelt dwryf (twryf elsewhere in this part); soft-mutated (t>d) after the presentative llyma (llyma dwryf 'behold a noise')
chawat: kawat (cawod) — shower; noun f. (a chawat o nywl 'and a shower of mist'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
difflannu: diflannu (diflannu) — to vanish, disappear; verbal noun, written with ff (difflannu y gaer 'the fort vanishing'); no mutation
gloew: Proper name — Gloew (Gloyw in 008), second element of Gwyn Gloew, father of Cigfa; the adjective gloyw 'bright, shining'; radical after Gwyn
drygyruerth: drygyruerth (modern form uncertain) — lamentation, grief, wailing; noun, with drwc 'bad' as first element; fronted before a wnaeth (drygyruerth a wnaeth 'she made lamentation'); no mutation
marw: marw (marw) — to die, dying; verbal noun/noun 'death' (no'y marw 'than her dying'); no mutation of m- after 'y 'her'
drygyruerthy: drygyruerthu (modern form uncertain) — to lament, grieve; 2 sg. present 'you lament' (os … y drygyruerthy di 'if you lament'), from drygyruerth, in -y; radical after the particle y; lemma and form uncertain
uach: mach (mach) — surety, guarantor, pledge; noun m.; soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after y, which here stands for predicative yn 'as' (Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you'; the Red Book yn vach)
gywirach: kywir (cywir) — true, faithful, loyal; adjective, comparative gywirach 'truer, more faithful' (-ach); soft-mutated (k>g) after the soft-mutated noun gedymdeith (gedymdeith gywirach 'a more faithful companion'); cause of this mutation uncertain
uynho: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish, will; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may (God) will' (tra uynho Duw it uot uelly 'while God wills it to be so for you'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after tra 'while'
et: yd (yd) — the preverbal particle, spelt et (t for d), here after bei 'if' (bei et uwni 'if I were'; the Red Book pei yt uewn i); no mutation shown on et itself
uwni: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I were' (written bwn here; the Red Book uewn, i.e. bewn), with the pronoun i written on (bei et uwni 'if I were'); soft-mutated (b>u, = f), the same in the Red Book; the cause is not clear, since the particle yd does not soften elsewhere
gywirdeb: kywirdeb (cywirdeb) — faithfulness, loyalty, truthfulness; noun m., from kywir; soft-mutated (k>g) as the object directly after the inflected verb gadwn (mi a gadwn gywirdeb 'I would keep faithfulness')
cadwn: kadw (cadw) — to keep, hold, preserve; 1 sg. imperfect with conditional sense 'I would keep' (mi a'y cadwn 'I would keep it'); radical: the infixed 3 sg. masculine object 'y 'it' causes no mutation (compare A mi a'e gwnn in this part; the Red Book mi ae cadwn)
gey: caffael (cael) — to get, have, receive; 2 sg. present/future 'you will get' (titheu a gey y gedymdeithas 'you for your part will get the fellowship'), a short form beside keffy; soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
uynych: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may want' (a uynych y genhyf i 'which you may want from me'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the relative a
gallu: gallu (gallu) — power, ability; noun m. (herwyd uyg gallu i 'according to my power'); nasal-mutated (g>ng) after uy 'my', written uyg gallu with the g on the possessive
welho: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may (God) see (fit)' (tra welho Duw 'while God sees fit'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after tra 'while'
dihirwch: dihirwch (dihirwch) — wretchedness, misery, worthlessness; noun m. (yn y dihirwch hwnn 'in this wretchedness'); no mutation after the article
goual: gofal (gofal) — care, anxiety, trouble; noun m., spelt goual with u for the /v/ sound; radical after the article ('r: a'r goual 'and the anxiety')
dalho: talu (talu) — to pay, repay; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may (God) repay' (Duw a dalho it 'may God repay you'), written with h before the ending (008 has dalo); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a
debywn: tebygu (tebygu) — to suppose, think, expect; 1 sg. imperfect 'I would suppose' (a hynny a debywn i 'and that I would suppose'), written without the g (debygwn); soft-mutated (t>d) after the relative a
ehouyndre: ehouyndra (eofndra) — fearlessness, boldness, confidence; noun m., from ehouyn (ehofn) 'fearless'; written ehouyndre, the scribe's correction of final a to e (the Red Book ehouyndra); no mutation (vowel initial)
kyfle: kyfle (cyfle) — opportunity, fit place, convenient spot; noun m. (nyt kyfle yni trigyaw yma 'it is no fit place for us to stay here'); radical
trigyaw: trigyaw (trigo) — to stay, dwell, remain; verbal noun; no mutation
gollyssam: colli (colli) — to lose; 1 pl. preterite 'we lost' (Yn cwn a gollyssam 'our dogs we lost') in -yssam; soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
allwn: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 pl. present 'we can' (ymborth ny allwn 'we cannot feed ourselves'), ending -wn (as in gwnawn, kyrchwn); g lost by soft mutation after the negative ny; a 1 sg. imperfect would have the same ending, but the sense here is 'we'
loegyr: Proper name — Lloegr (Lloegyr beside Lloygyr), England; soft-mutated (ll>l) as the object directly after the verb (Kyrchwn Loegyr 'let us make for England')
hawssaf: hawd (hawdd) — easy; superlative hawssaf 'easiest' (-af, modern hawsaf); adjective, as predicate (hawssaf yw in ymborth yno 'it is easiest for us to get food there'); no mutation
kerdyssant: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they walked' (Y gyt y kerdyssant 'together they went'); radical after the particle y following the fronted adverb
gymery: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 2 sg. present/future 'you will take' (pa greft a gymery di 'what craft will you take'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
kymer: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 2 sg. imperative 'take!' (Kymer un lanweith 'take a clean one'); no mutation
lanweith: glanweith (glanweith) — clean, neat, fine (of a craft); adjective, glan 'clean' + gweith 'work' (gweith softened inside the compound); soft-mutated (g lost) after un with a feminine noun understood (kreft): un lanweith 'a clean one'
chymeraf: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 sg. present/future 'I will take' (ny chymeraf i 'I will not take'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the negative ny
crydyaeth: crydyaeth (cryddiaeth) — shoemaking, the shoemaker's trade; noun f., from crydd 'shoemaker'; radical after namyn 'except' (namyn crydyaeth)
hoff: hoff (hoff) — dear, pleasing, beloved; adjective, predicate (nyt hoff honno 'that (craft) is not pleasing'); no mutation
glanet: glan (glân) — clean, fair, fine, pure; equative degree 'as fine', used as a noun 'fineness' (glanet y wr 'fineness for a man', construction uncertain); ending -et; radical
kygynhilet: kynnil (cynnil) — thrifty, skilful, delicate, fine; equative kygynhilet 'as delicate, as skilful', made with the equative prefix ky-, after which kynnil is softened (k>g: ky-gynnil-et), spelt with nh for nn; the exact sense here is uncertain (the Red Book kygynnilet)
thydi: ti (ti) — you; 2 sg. independent pronoun with the emphatic ending -di (tydi); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'as' (kyuurd a thydi 'of equal rank as you')
gvaegeu: gwaeg (gwaeg) — buckle, clasp; noun, plural gwaegeu (-eu); spelt gvaegeu with v for w; radical as the object of the verbal noun dechreu (dechreu gvaegeu 'beginning buckles')
waegeu: gwaeg (gwaeg) — buckle, clasp; noun, plural gwaegeu; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition o (o waegeu eureit 'of gilded buckles')
ouer: ofer (ofer) — vain, worthless, useless; adjective, u for the /v/ sound (ouer a man gueith 'worthless and petty work'); radical
man: man (mân) — small, fine, petty; adjective (man gueith 'small work'); radical after a 'and'
kynuigen: kynuigen (cenfigen) — envy, jealousy, spite; noun f. (kynuigen a chynghoruyn 'envy and spite'); radical as the object of the verbal noun dala
chynghoruyn: kynghoruyn (modern form uncertain) — envy, spite, malice; noun, spelt kynghoruyn (perhaps kynghoruynt); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chynghoruyn)
rybudyeu: rhybud (rhybudd) — warning, notice; noun m., plural rybudyeu (-yeu); r writes rh; radical, after the verb doeth (yny doeth rybudyeu idaw 'until warnings came to him')
diodeuir: diodef (dioddef) — to suffer, bear, endure; 3 sg. impersonal present 'is suffered' in -ir, stem diodeu- (pam y diodeuir hynn 'why is this endured'); radical after the particle y
aem: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 pl. imperfect 'we would go, we should go' (ni a aem 'we would go'); no mutation (vowel stem after a)
beich: beich (baich) — load, burden; noun m. (dwyn beich o wenith 'carrying a load of wheat'); radical as the object of the verbal noun dwyn
wenith: gwenith (gwenith) — wheat; noun m.; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition o (beich o wenith 'a load of wheat') and as the object of a verb (na welsei dyn wenith 'no man had seen wheat')
gwelet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun (no gwelet Arberth 'than seeing Arberth'); radical after no 'than'
tirogaeth: tirogaeth (tiriogaeth) — territory, lands, domain; noun f. (a'r tirogaeth 'and the lands'), here with t unsoftened after the article, where a feminine noun is normally softened (the Red Book also ar tirogaeth): the gender may not have been settled
kyneuinaw: kyneuinaw (cynefino) — to become accustomed, grow used (to), settle in; verbal noun (Dechreu a wnaeth kyneuinaw 'he began to grow used'); radical
pyscawt: pyscawt (pysgod) — fish; noun m., collective (hela pyscawt 'hunting fish', fishing); radical as the object of the verbal noun hela
llydnot: llwdn (llwdn) — young animal, beast; noun m., plural llydnot (-ot, modern llydnod); radical after a 'and' (ll- does not change)
gual: gwal (gwâl) — lair, bed, resting place of an animal; noun (ar eu gual 'in their lair'); gu- = gw-; no mutation after eu 'their'
ryuoryaw: ryuoryaw (lemma uncertain) — a rare verb, apparently 'to break and work the ground, to till', from the context (dechreu ryuoryaw 'beginning to till'); verbal noun; r- writes rh-; meaning uncertain
heu: hau (hau) — to sow; verbal noun, the Middle Welsh form heu (heu groft 'sowing a croft'); no mutation
groft: kroft (croft) — croft, small field (from English croft); noun f., written groft with t (heu groft 'sowing a croft'; E wylat y groft 'to watch the croft'). The form with g stands even where nothing softens: a verbal noun such as heu leaves its object unmutated. The scribe seems to take grofd/groft as the word's own form (see grofd)
guenith: gwenith (gwenith) — wheat; noun m., gu- = gw-; radical after the masculine article (y guenith 'the wheat')
deir: tri (tri) — three; feminine form teir (tair), written deir; soft-mutated (t>d) after 'e 'his' (a'e deir grofd 'and his three crofts') · also softened (t>d) as the object of the verb with it 'to you' standing between (mi a rodaf it deir punt 'I will give you three pounds'); the Red Book has teirpunt unsoftened, and pedeirpunt is unsoftened in the same position, so the rule is not applied every time
grofd: kroft (croft) — croft, small field (from English croft); noun f., written grofd with d. In this part the word is always grofd, even where nothing softens: after teir (a'e deir grofd), which does not soften the next word, and as the object of a verbal noun (edrych grofd arall 'to look at another croft'), as well as after the feminine article and the feminine ordinal (y grofd, y tryded grofd), where softening would be regular. The scribe seems to take grofd as the word's own form (compare o'e rofdeu, and the Red Book y rofft, y dryded rofft)
llwydaw: llwydaw (llwyddo) — to prosper, thrive, flourish; verbal noun (yn llwydaw 'prospering'), progressive yn + verbal noun; no mutation of ll-
tegach: tec (teg) — fair, beautiful; comparative tegach 'fairer' (-ach); adjective (wenith tegach 'fairer wheat'); radical
amseroed: amser (amser) — time, season, period; noun m., plural amseroed (-oed); object of the verbal noun treulaw; radical (vowel initial)
kynhaeaf: kynhaeaf (cynhaeaf) — harvest, autumn; noun m.; radical after the masculine article (y kynhaeaf 'the harvest')
rofdeu: kroft (croft) — croft, small field; noun f., plural krofdeu (-eu), here written rofdeu with no initial letter (o'e rofdeu 'of his crofts'), as though the g of the soft-mutated grofdeu were lost after 'e 'his'; the spelling is odd but the word is clear
aeduet: aeduet (aeddfed) — ripe, mature; adjective (yn aeduet 'ripe'), predicative after yn; no mutation (vowel initial)
uedi: medi (medi) — to reap, harvest; verbal noun; soft-mutated (m>u, = f) directly after the verb uynhaf (mi a uynhaf uedi honn 'I will reap this one')
gefyn: kefyn (cefn) — back; noun m.; soft-mutated (k>g) after y 'his' (tra y gefyn 'beyond his back', back again)
glas: glas (glas) — grey, blue, pale; adjective, of the pale light of dawn (E bore glas 'the grey morning'); no mutation after a masculine noun
dranoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — next day, the day after; adverb of time, soft-mutated (t>d) as an adverbial expression of time (E bore glas dranoeth 'at dawn next day')
medi: medi (medi) — to reap, harvest; verbal noun, radical after the verbal noun y uynnu and after uynhaf (y uynnu medi y grofd 'to want to reap the croft'; mi a uynhaf medi honn 'I will reap this one'), without the mutation seen in uedi
calaf: calaf (calaf) — stalks, straw, stubble; noun m., collective (y calaf yn llwm 'the stalks bare'); radical after the article
llwm: llwm (llwm) — bare, bleak, empty; adjective (yn llwm 'bare', predicative; y calaf llwm 'the bare straw', after its noun); no mutation of ll-
torri: torri (torri) — to break, cut off; verbal noun (daruot torri 'breaking having been done'); radical
dywyssen: tywyssen (tywysen) — ear of corn; noun f., plural tywys, tewys; soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (torri y dywyssen 'breaking the ear') and after yn y in the hard clause yn y dywyssen o'r keleuyn
keleuyn: keleuyn (celefyn) — stalk, stem of corn, the single of calaf; noun m. (o'r keleuyn 'from the stalk'; uot un keleuyn 'that there was one stalk'); radical
tewys: tywys (tywys) — ears of corn; plural/collective of tywyssen, spelt tewys (a'r tewys 'with the ears'); radical after the article; not the verb tywys 'to lead'
hollawl: hollawl (hollol) — whole, entire, complete; adjective (yn hollawl 'entirely'), adverbial yn; no mutation of h-
gorfen: gorffen (gorffen) — to finish, end, complete; verbal noun, written with a single f (yn gorfen uyn diua i 'finishing my ruin'); radical after the progressive yn
diua: diua (difa) — to destroy; verbal noun, here 'destroying, destruction' (uyn diua i 'my destroying'); the nasal mutation of d- after uy 'my' is written as n on the possessive (uyn), the noun itself keeping d (= fy nifa)
orffen: gorffen (gorffen) — to finish, end; verbal noun; g lost by soft mutation after y 'its', the possessive standing before the verbal noun for its object (yn y orffen 'finishing it')
diuawys: diua (difa) — to destroy, ruin, lay waste; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'laid waste' (a diuawys y wlad 'who laid waste the land'); after the relative a, where d>dd would not show in the spelling
wlad: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country, realm; noun f., written wlad with d for t; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the feminine article y
wylaf: gwylat (gwylio) — to watch, keep watch; 1 sg. present/future 'I will watch' (ony wylaf i 'unless I watch'; mi a wylaf y grofd 'I will watch the croft'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after ony 'unless' and after the particle a
eliwlu: eliwlu (lemma uncertain) — a rare word, apparently 'host, vast multitude' (eliwlu y byd o lygot 'the greatest host in the world of mice'); noun; meaning from the context and uncertain
lygot: llygot (llygod) — mice; plural of llygoden; noun; soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition o (o lygot 'of mice')
chyfrif: kyfrif (cyfrif) — counting, reckoning, number; noun m.; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyfrif na messur 'and count nor measure')
messur: mesur (mesur) — measure, measuring; noun m., written with ss (na messur 'nor measure'); radical after na
llygot: llygot (llygod) — mice; plural of llygoden; noun (y llygot 'the mice'); radical after the article
adan: adan (dan, 'under'; adan is the older form) — under, beneath; preposition (adan y grofd 'under the croft'); no mutation
drigyaw: dringaw (dringo) — to climb; verbal noun, apparently written drigyaw without the n (phob un yn drigyaw 'each one climbing'); radical after yn; spelling and reading somewhat uncertain
kyleuyn: keleuyn (celefyn) — stalk, stem of corn; noun m., spelt kyleuyn (ar hyt y kyleuyn 'along the stalk'); radical after the masculine article
estwng: estwng (cf. modern gostwng) — to lower, bend down, bring down; verbal noun (yn y estwng genti 'bending it down with her'); no mutation (vowel initial)
tywys: tywys (tywys) — ears of corn; plural/collective of tywyssen (a'r tywys 'and the ears'); radical after the article; not the verb tywys 'to lead'
wydyat: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. imperfect 'he knew' (ni wydyat ef 'he did not know'), spelt wydyat beside wydat; g- lost by soft mutation (gw>w) after the negative ni
lygoden: llygoden (llygoden) — mouse; noun f., plural llygot; soft-mutated (ll>l) as the subject directly after the verb bei (ny bei lygoden 'there was not a mouse')
gymerynt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 pl. imperfect 'they would take, they took' (a gymerynt eu hynt 'and they took their way'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
dicter: dicter (dicter) — anger, wrath; noun m. (rwng dicter a llit 'between anger and wrath'); radical
llit: llit (llid) — anger, wrath, rage; noun m., final t for d; radical after a 'and'
gwydbet: gwybet (gwybed) — gnats, midges; collective noun, spelt gwydbet with an extra d (ar y gwydbet 'on the midges'); radical after the article
chytdremei: kytdremu (modern form uncertain) — to keep in sight, look steadily at; 3 sg. imperfect 'he could keep in sight' (ni chytdremei ef ar 'he could not keep his eyes on'), from kyt- + drem 'sight'; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the negative ni; meaning uncertain
amdrom: amdrom (no modern form) — very heavy; adjective, am- + trom (the feminine of trwm 'heavy', for the mouse), trom softened (t>d) after am- inside the compound; yn amdrom 'heavy', predicative; perhaps heavy with young (uncertain)
tebygei: tebygu (tebygu) — to suppose, think, imagine; 3 sg. imperfect 'he thought' (ual y tebygei 'so that he thought'); radical after the particle y
uanec: maneg (maneg) — glove; noun f. (spelt manec); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after y, whether the feminine article or 'his' (yn y uanec 'in his glove') · also soft after dy, 'th 'your' (y'th uanec 'in your glove')
llinin: llinyn (llinyn) — string, cord, thread; noun m., spelt llinin (ac a llinin 'and with a string'); radical after a 'with' · also radical after the article y (maglu y llinin 'to noose the cord')
rwymaw: rhwymo (rhwymo) — to bind, tie; verbal noun, spelt rwymaw; r- writes rh-; the soft mutation (rh>r) after the fronted phrase ac a llinin cannot be told from the spelling
geneu: geneu (genau) — mouth, opening; noun m. (geneu y uanec 'the mouth of the glove'); radical as the object of the verbal noun rwymaw
ynyd: yny (hyd oni) — until; yny + yd, the preverbal particle, joined before oed (ynyd oed y crydyon yn dala 'until the shoemakers were holding'); no mutation
blwyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f.; written blwyn, an apparent slip for blwydyn (the Red Book has blwydyn); radical after a 'and' (A blwyn yuelly 'and a year thus')
thra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (A thra geffit y gantaw 'and while there was got from him'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
llinyn: llinyn (llinyn) — string, cord, rope; noun m. (ac wrth y llinyn 'and by the cord'); radical after the masculine article y
wanas: gwanas (gwanas) — peg, stake, holdfast, support; noun f. (ar y wanas 'on the peg', where the glove is hung by its string); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the feminine article y
lleidyr: lleidr (lleidr) — thief; noun m. (Lleidyr, heb ynteu 'a thief, said he'; lleidyr a geueis 'a thief I caught'); radical
lledratta: lledratta (lladrata) — to steal, thieve; verbal noun (yn lledratta arnaf 'stealing from me'; a lledratta a wnaeth 'and he stole', verbal noun + a wnaeth); radical after yn and after a
leidyr: lleidr (lleidr) — thief; noun m., the same word as lleidyr; soft-mutated (ll>l) after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw leidyr 'what kind of thief')
allut: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 2 sg. imperfect 'you could' (Pa ryw leidyr ... a allut ti y dodi y'th uanec? 'what kind of thief could you put in your glove?'); soft-mutated (g lost) after the relative particle a, following the fronted question phrase
lygryssit: llygru (llygru) — to spoil, damage, corrupt; impersonal pluperfect -yssit 'it had been spoiled' (ual yr lygryssit 'how it had been spoiled'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the perfective particle ry, written yr here
diuwynyssit: diuwyno (difwyno) — to spoil, despoil, lay waste; impersonal pluperfect -yssit 'had been laid waste' (ac y diuwynyssit y grofdeu 'and how the crofts had been laid waste'); radical after the particle y
grofdeu: kroft (croft) — croft, small field; noun f., plural grofdeu (modern croftau) in -eu; written with g as the word's own spelling (as grofd in this part), not a mutation, since the article does not soften a plural
diwethaf: diwethaf (diwethaf) — last, latest; superlative adjective from diwedd 'end' (y'r grofd diwethaf 'to the last croft'); follows its noun, no mutation
deleis: dala (dal) — to catch, seize, hold; 1 sg. preterite 'I caught' (ac a deleis 'and which I caught'); after the relative a the d is softened (d>dd), not shown in the spelling
grogaf: crogi (crogi) — to hang; 1 sg. present/future 'I will hang' (ac a grogaf inheu 'and I will hang it'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
as: a + 's (no modern form) — the preverbal particle a carrying the infixed object pronoun 's 'them', after bei 'if' (bei as caffwn oll 'if I could get them all'; bei as caffwnn i wy oll, where wy 'them' takes the pronoun up again); the infixed pronoun causes no mutation
crogwn: crogi (crogi) — to hang; 1 sg. imperfect, here conditional 'I would hang' (mi a'y crogwn 'I would hang them'; onys crogwn 'if I did not hang them'); radical (the infixed 'y and 's 'them' cause no mutation)
anwymp: anwymp (no modern form) — unseemly, unbecoming; predicate adjective, an- 'un-' + gwymp 'fine, fitting', gw softened to w in the compound (anwymp yw guelet gwr kyuurd yn crogi 'it is unseemly to see a man of rank hanging')
kymoned: kymoned (no modern form; cf. bonedd) — of equal birth, of like lineage; adjective, kyf- 'co-, equal' + boned 'lineage', the b absorbed into the prefix (kyf- + b > kym-) (gwr kyuurd, kymoned, a thidi 'a man of equal rank and birth with you')
thidi: ti + di (tydi) — you; 2 sg. pronoun with the affixed di, 'you yourself' (a thidi 'with you'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'with, as' (kyuurd a thidi 'as equal in rank as you')
crogi: crogi (crogi) — to hang; verbal noun (yn crogi y ryw bryf hwnnw 'hanging that kind of creature'); radical after yn; its object is also unmutated
bryf: pryf (pryf) — creature, vermin, worm; noun m., here a contemptuous 'creature' for the mouse; soft-mutated (p>b) after ryw 'kind of' (y ryw bryf hwnnw 'that kind of creature')
gwnelut: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you were to do' (phei gwnelut iawn 'and if you did right'); radical
ymyrrut: ymyrru (ymyrryd) — to meddle, interfere, concern oneself; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive/conditional 'you would meddle' (nyt ymyrrut yn y pryf 'you would not meddle with the creature'); no mutation
pryf: pryf (pryf) — creature, vermin; noun m. (yn y pryf, y pryf hwnnw 'the creature'; pryf a welaf 'a creature I see'); radical after the article y and as a fronted word
caffwnn: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I were to get' (bei as caffwnn i wy oll 'if I were to get them all'), a spelling of caffwn with -nn; radical (infixed 's causes no mutation)
crogaf: crogi (crogi) — to hang; 1 sg. present/future 'I will hang' (mi a'e crogaf 'I will hang it'); radical, since the infixed 'e 'it' causes no mutation
borth: porth (porth) — help, protection, defender; noun m., a different word from porth 'gate' (bot yn borth y'r pryf 'to be protector for the creature'); soft-mutated (p>b) after predicative yn
goglyt: gogelyd (gochel) — to guard against, avoid; verbal noun, gogelyd with the middle vowel dropped (namyn goglyt ansyberwyt y ti 'but guarding against discourtesy to you'); radical
defnyd: defnyd (defnydd) — material, cause, reason; noun m., here 'reason, ground' (defnyd yn y byt y dylyut ... 'any reason in the world why you ought ...'); modern defnydd means 'material, use'; no mutation after bei gwypwn inheu
dylyut: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, be bound to, ought; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you ought' (y dylyut titheu bot yn borth 'that you should be protector'); radical after the particle y
danaw: am + danaw (amdano) — 'about him, about it'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., written as two words (am danaw); danaw is the conjugating element, whose origin (dan-?) is uncertain; no mutation
chanys: kan (can) + nys (nis) — 'since … not … it': kan 'since' with the negative ny and the infixed object 's 'it' (a chanys gwnn 'and since I do not know it'); the Red Book has a chanys nys gwnn, so the White Book may instead have lost a nys after chanys; kan spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'; compare Kanys gollyngy (Red Book Kan nys gollynghy)
llygoden: llygoden (llygoden) — mouse; noun f., plural llygot (y llygoden 'the mouse'; a'r llygoden gantaw 'and the mouse with him'); ll stays unmutated after the article
sengi: sengi (sengi) — to tread, trample, press down, thrust in; verbal noun (a sengi dwy forch 'and pressing/planting two forks'); meaning here a little uncertain; radical after a (s does not mutate)
forch: fforch (fforch) — fork, forked post; noun f., written forch with f for ff (dwy forch 'two forks'); ff has no soft mutation, so the softening after dwy cannot show; plural ffyrch (written fyrch)
uchaf: uchaf (uchaf) — highest, uppermost; superlative of uchel 'high' (yn y lle uchaf 'in the highest place'); follows its noun, radical
yscolheic: ysgolhaig (ysgolhaig) — scholar, clerk, learned man; noun m. (yr yscolheic 'the clerk'); radical
hydreul: hydreul (hydraul) — worn out, threadbare; adjective, hy- + treul 'wear', t softened to d in the compound (hen dillat hydreul 'old threadbare clothes')
tlawt: tlawt (tlawd) — poor, wretched; adjective (hydreul, tlawt 'worn, poor'); after a plural noun, radical
pedwardyn: pedwar dyn (pedwar dyn) — four persons; pedwar 'four' + dyn 'person' written as one word, 'the four (persons)' (y pedwardyn y buassynt y gyt 'the four who had been together'); noun m. collective; radical
buassynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had been' (y buassynt y gyt 'who had been together'); radical after the relative particle y, which does not mutate
doaf: dyuot (dod) — to come; 1 sg. present 'I come' (Pan doaf o Loygyr 'from where I come, from England'); no mutation
ganu: canu (canu) — to sing, chant; verbal noun, here 'singing' as a cleric's work (o ganu 'from singing'); soft-mutated (c>g) after o 'from'
phaham: paham (pam) — why, for what; interrogative adverb; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (a phaham y gouynhy di 'and why do you ask')
gouynhy: gouyn (gofyn) — to ask; 2 sg. present 'you ask' (y gouynhy di 'that you ask'), -hy being the 2 sg. ending; radical after the particle y
diholedic: diholedic (deoledig) — banished, exiled, outcast; adjective, from diholi/deol 'banish' (pedwar dyn diholedic 'four outcast men'); radical
wyte: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. present 'you are' (yd wyte yndaw 'you are in it'), with an attached te, a form of the pronoun ti (uncertain); no mutation after yd
ba: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative, a variant spelling with b (Ba ryw leidyr 'what kind of thief'; cf. byhyt for py hyt); whether b is a mutation here is uncertain; causes soft mutation of a following noun
ymodi: ymodi (no modern form) — properly 'stir, move'; here 'handle, busy oneself with', a sense taken from the context; verbal noun (gueda ... ymodi pryf kyfryw a hwnnw 'it suits ... to handle such a creature'; yn ymodi y pryf hwnnw 'handling that creature'); the Red Book has teimlaw 'touch, handle' in both places; no mutation
gellwg: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; 2 sg. imperative 'let go!' (Gellwg e ymdeith ef 'Let it go away'), the spelling gellwg lacking the n of gellwng; radical
ellynghaf: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; 1 sg. present/future 'I will let go' (Na ellynghaf 'I will not release'); g lost by soft mutation after the negative na; -h- is a spelling
chyfreith: kyfreith (cyfraith) — law, legal custom; noun f. (a chyfreith lleidyr a wnaf 'and the law of a thief I will do'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
grogi: crogi (crogi) — to hang; verbal noun (y grogi 'its hanging', to hang it); soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'its, his', the possessive standing for the object
punt: punt (punt) — pound (money); noun f. (punt a geueis i 'a pound that I got'; seith punt 'seven pounds'); radical
gardotta: cardota (cardota) — to beg; verbal noun (o gardotta 'by begging'); soft-mutated (c>g) after o 'by, through'
gellwng: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; 2 sg. imperative 'release!' (a gellwng y pryf hwnnw e ymdeith 'and release that creature'), though a verbal noun 'releasing' is possible (uncertain); g radical, as a 'and' gives only spirant mutation of c, p, t
guerthaf: gwerthu (gwerthu) — to sell; 1 sg. present/future 'I will sell' (nys guerthaf 'I will not sell it'); radical (infixed 's causes no mutation); gu = gw
hagyr: hagr (hagr) — ugly, unseemly, shameful; adjective, predicate (ony bei hagyr guelet gwr kyuurd ... 'if it were not unseemly to see a man of rank ...'); radical
teimlaw: teimlaw (teimlo) — to feel, touch, handle; verbal noun (yn teimlaw y ryw bryf a hwnnw 'handling that kind of creature'); radical after yn
torei: torri (torri) — to break; here in the sense 'matter to, concern'; 3 sg. imperfect, conditional (ny'm torei 'it would not concern me'); radical after the infixed 'm
dulath: dulath (no modern form) — crossbeam, the bar laid across the two forks of the gallows; noun, second element llath 'rod, beam' (ll softened to l in the compound), the first element not clear (dodi y dulath yn y fyrch 'putting the crossbeam in the forks'); radical after the article y
fyrch: fforch (fforch) — fork, forked post; plural ffyrch, written fyrch with f for ff (yn y fyrch 'in the forks', the two posts set up on the mound); ff has no soft mutation
offeirat: offeirat (offeiriad) — priest; noun m. (nachaf offeirat 'behold a priest'); radical
gyweir: kyweir (cyweir) — in good order, well-equipped, arrayed; adjective, predicative after yn (ar uarch yn gyweir 'on a horse well-equipped'); soft-mutated (k>g) after yn
uendith: bendith (bendith) — blessing; noun f.; soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after 'th 'your' (a'th uendith 'and your blessing'), after dy (dy uendith) and after y 'his' (y uendith 'his blessing')
bendith: bendith (bendith) — blessing; noun f. (Bendith Duw it 'God's blessing to you'); radical, sentence-initial
prynaf: prynu (prynu) — to buy, redeem, ransom; 1 sg. present/future 'I will buy' (mi a'y prynaf 'I will buy it'; 'y 'it' is the mouse, as the pryf or llygoden); radical (infixed 'y causes no mutation)
uyghyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — confession, avowal; noun f.; nasal-mutated (c>ngh) after uy 'my', written uyghyffes (y dygaf uyghyffes 'I bring my confession')
werthu: gwerthu (gwerthu) — to sell; verbal noun (na'y werthu 'nor selling it'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after 'y 'its', the possessive standing for the noun's object
ollwng: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; verbal noun (na'y ollwng nas gwnaf i 'nor releasing it will I do'); g lost by soft mutation after 'y 'its', the possessive standing for the object
ymhalogi: ymhalogi (ymhalogi) — to defile oneself, pollute oneself, soil one's hands; verbal noun (yn ymhalogi wrth y pryf hwnnw 'defiling yourself with that creature'); radical after yn
gollwng: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; imperative 2 sg. 'release!' (gollwng ef e ymdeith 'let it go away') · also 3 sg. present 'he releases' after the particle y (Ac yna y gollwng hi 'and then he releases her'); radical
maglu: maglu (maglu) — to snare, tie in a noose, entangle; verbal noun (maglu y llinin am uynwgyl y llygoden 'to noose the cord about the mouse's neck'), verbal-noun narrative after sef a wnaeth; radical
rwtter: rwtter (no modern form) — company, train, retinue; noun, probably borrowed from English (compare rout 'company'), the form not certain; gender not clear (llyma rwtter escob 'behold a bishop's train'); r shows no mutation after llyma
escob: esgob (esgob) — bishop; noun m., genitive after rwtter (rwtter escob 'a bishop's retinue'); radical
swmereu: swmer (swmer) — pack, load, sumpter-load; noun m., plural swmereu (a'y swmereu 'and his packs'); radical (the infixed possessive 'y 'his' does not alter s)
escop: esgob (esgob) — bishop; noun m., spelt escop with p (yr escop e hun 'the bishop himself'; Arglwyd escop 'lord bishop'); radical
gohir: gohir (gohirio) — to delay, hold back; verbal noun (gohir ar y weith 'delaying over the work'), also noun 'delay' (heb ohir 'without delay'); radical after sef a wnaeth
doethwyf: dyuot (dod) — to come; 1 sg. 'I have come', used as a perfect (can doethwyf i ar diuetha 'since I have come upon the destroying'); built on the stem doeth- with the 1 sg. ending -wyf, its exact analysis not certain; the Red Book has deuthum; radical after can
dielw: dielw (dielw) — unprofitable, worthless; adjective, di- 'without' + elw 'profit' (pryf mor dielw 'so worthless a creature'); d would be softened (d>dd) after mor, not shown in spelling
geffy: caffael (cael) — to get; 2 sg. present/future 'you will get' (ti a geffy hynny 'you will get that'; a'r da a geffy 'and the goods that you will get'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a; = gehy
gollyngy: gellwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; 2 sg. present/future 'you will release' (Kanys gollyngy yr hynny 'since you will not release it for that': Kanys = kan 'since' + nys 'not … it', the Red Book Kan nys gollynghy); radical after the infixed 's
pedeirpunt: pedeir punt (pedair punt) — four pounds; pedeir (f. of pedwar) + punt written as one word (pedeirpunt ar ugeint 'four pounds on twenty' = twenty-four pounds); radical, unsoftened although it 'to you' stands between it and the verb (contrast deir punt), and so in the Red Book
ugeint: ugeint (ugain) — twenty; numeral m. (ar ugeint 'on twenty' = 'and twenty'); no mutation
gymeint: kymeint (cymaint) — as much, so much; noun (yr y gymeint arall 'for its as-much again', twice as much); soft-mutated (k>g) after y 'its'
collyghy: gellwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; 2 sg. present/future 'you will release' (Canys collyghy yr hynny 'since you will not release it for that', the Kanys gollyngy of two lines before; the Red Book Kan nys gellyngy); c for g and gh for ngh are spellings, not mutations; radical after the infixed 's
swmer: swmer (swmer) — pack, load, sumpter-load; noun m. (seith swmer yssyd yma, ar y seith meirch y maent arnunt 'seven packs that are here, on the seven horses they are on'); singular after a numeral; radical
rydhau: rydhau (rhyddhau) — to free, release; verbal noun (rydhau Riannon a Phryderi 'freeing Rhiannon and Pryderi'); radical · also after dy 'your' as its object (dy rydhau 'to free you'); r writes rh, so the softening does not show
phryderi: Pryderi (Pryderi) — proper name, Pryderi son of Pwyll and Rhiannon; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (a Phryderi 'and Pryderi')
uynhy: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present 'you want' (Beth a uynhy ditheu 'what do you want'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the relative a 'what'
lledrith: lledrith (lledrith) — illusion, enchantment, shape-changing; noun m. (yr hut a'r lledrith 'the enchantment and the illusion'); radical after the article 'r; also spelt lletrith
ellyngaf: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; 1 sg. present/future 'I will release' (Na ellyngaf 'I will not release'), spelt without h; g lost by soft mutation after na
phy: pei (pe) — if; a variant spelling with y (a phy ny bei hynny 'and if it were not for that'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
dillyngwn: dillwng (dillwng) — to loose, let go, release; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive/conditional 'I would release' (nys dillyngwn 'I would not release her'); radical (infixed 's causes no mutation)
gyffuryf: kyffuryf (cyffurf) — form, manner, way; noun (pa gyffuryf y doeth hi attaf i 'in what manner did she come to me'); soft-mutated (k>g) after pa
herwa: herwa (herwa, from herw 'raid') — to go raiding, plunder, harry; verbal noun after y 'to' (Y herwa 'to plunder'); meaning from context, with some uncertainty; no mutation
kil: cil (cil) — nook, retreat, corner; noun m., first element of the place-name Kil Coet 'Cil Coed' (Llwyt uab Kil Coet); radical
dieleis: dial (dial) — to avenge; 1 sg. preterite 'I avenged' (ar Pryderi y dieleis i guare broch yghot 'on Pryderi I avenged the game of badger in the bag'); radical after the particle y
yghot: yn (yn) + cot (cod) — 'in the bag'; written as one word, the nasal mutation (c>ngh) of cot after yn (guare broch yghot 'badger-in-the-bag')
aghynghor: anghynghor (anghyngor) — bad counsel, ill advice; noun m., an- 'un-' + kynghor; the k is nasal-mutated (k>ngh) after the prefix, the n being dropped in writing (o aghynghor 'out of ill counsel')
clybot: clybot (clywed) — to hear; verbal noun (guedy clybot dy uot yn kyuanhedu 'after hearing that you were settling'); radical after guedy
kyuanhedu: kyuanhedu (cyfanheddu) — to dwell in, settle; verbal noun (yn kyuanhedu y wlat 'settling the land'); radical after yn
rithyaw: rithiaw (rhithio) — to change the shape of, transform; verbal noun (eu rithyaw yn llygot 'to transform them into mice'); radical (eu 'their' causes none)
diuayssant: diua (difa) — to destroy; 3 pl. preterite -yssant 'they destroyed' (ac y diuayssant y dwy grofd 'and they destroyed the two crofts'); radical after the particle y
rithaw: rithiaw (rhithio) — to change the shape of, transform; verbal noun, a variant of rithyaw (y erchi im eu rithaw 'to ask me to transform them'); radical
ritheis: rithiaw (rhithio) — to change the shape of, transform; 1 sg. preterite 'I transformed' (ac y ritheis inheu 'and I transformed them'); radical after the particle y
nis: ny (ni) + 's — negative particle with infixed 3 sg. f. object pronoun 'not her' (nis gordiwedut ti 'you would not overtake her'); a spelling variant beside nys; no mutation
gordiwedut: gordiwes (gorddiwes) — to overtake, catch up with; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you would overtake' (nis gordiwedut ti); radical (the infixed 's causes none)
waredaf: gwaret (gwared) — to deliver, rid, remove; 1 sg. present/future 'I will remove' (ac a waredaf yr hut 'and I will remove the enchantment'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the particle a
lletrith: lledrith (lledrith) — illusion, enchantment, shape-changing; noun m., spelt with t (a waredaf yr hut a'r lletrith 'I will remove the enchantment and the illusion'); radical after the article 'r
uenegeis: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, relate; 1 sg. preterite 'I told' (Minheu a uenegeis yti 'and I told you'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the particle a
ymdiala: ymdial (ymddial) — vengeance, revenge; noun m. (na bo ymdiala ar Pryderi 'that there be no vengeance on Pryderi'); the final -a is uncertain (perhaps a verbal-noun ending); radical
medreist: medru (medru) — to hit (a mark), know how; 2 sg. preterite 'you hit' (da y medreist 'well have you hit', you have hit the mark); radical after the particle y
metrut: medru (medru) — to hit (a mark), know how; 2 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'you had hit' (Bei na metrut hynny 'had you not hit on that'), written with t; m left unsoftened after na
nodeis: nodi (nodi) — to appoint, fix, stipulate; 1 sg. preterite 'I stipulated' (y nodeis inheu 'I stipulated'); radical after the particle y
rytha: rydhau (rhyddhau) — to free, release; 2 sg. imperative 'free!' (Rytha weithon wy gwreic im 'free my wife now for me'), spelt with t; radical
rydhaaf: rydhau (rhyddhau) — to free, release; 1 sg. present/future 'I will free' (Na rydhaaf 'I will not free'); r stands for rh, so no mutation is visible after na
welwyf: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. present subjunctive 'I see' (yny welwyf Pryderi 'until I see Pryderi'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after yny 'until'
graessawu: graessawu (croesawu) — to welcome; verbal noun (a'y graessawu 'and welcoming them'); g- is the word's own initial in this spelling, as in grayssaw, not a mutation
wrda: gwrda (gwrda) — good man, worthy man; noun m., vocative (A wrda 'good sir'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the vocative particle a
ngwreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f.; nasal-mutated (g>ng) after uy 'my' (uy ngwreic 'my wife')
nodeist: nodi (nodi) — to appoint, fix, stipulate; 2 sg. preterite 'you stipulated' (a nodeist 'what you stipulated'); radical after the relative a
trewis: taraw (taro) — to strike; 3 sg. preterite 'he struck' (y trewis ynteu hi a hudlath 'he struck her with a magic wand'); radical after the particle y
hudlath: hudlath (hudlath) — magic wand; noun f., hut 'magic' + llath 'rod', ll softened to l in the compound (a hudlath 'with a magic wand'); h is not mutated by a 'with'
datrithwys: datrithaw (datrithio) — to un-transform, restore to one's own shape; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'he restored' (y datrithwys hi yn wreigyang 'he turned her back into a young woman'), dat- 'un-' + rithaw; radical after the particle y
wreigyang: gwreigyang (no modern form; cf. gwraig ieuanc) — young woman; noun f., gwreic + ieuanc 'young' in close compound (the Red Book has wreic ieuanc); soft-mutated (gw>w) after predicative yn 'into, as' (yn wreigyang 'into a young woman')
geccaf: teccaf (tecaf) — fairest; superlative of tec (teg); written geccaf, a readable scribal slip for deccaf (the Red Book and the second witness have deccaf); softened (t>d) as an adjective after the feminine singular noun (yn wreigyang deccaf a welsei neb 'into the fairest young woman anyone had seen')
anhedeu: anhed (annedd) — dwelling, habitation; noun m., plural anhedeu (modern anheddau) (yr holl anhedeu 'all the dwellings'); radical after holl
gyuanhed: kyuanhed (cyfanhedd) — inhabited, settled; here adjective, predicative after yn (yn gyuanhed 'inhabited'); soft-mutated (k>g) after yn
alauoed: alaw (alaf) — wealth in cattle, herds; plural alauoed (alafoedd) (o'y holl alauoed 'with all its herds'); radical after holl (vowel)
hanedeu: anhed (annedd) — dwelling; plural anedeu (a'y hanedeu 'and its dwellings'); h- prefixed after y 'her, its' (the land, gwlat f.)
wassanaeth: gwassanaeth (gwasanaeth) — service, duty, office; noun m. (Pa ryw wassanaeth 'what kind of service'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after ryw 'kind of'
yrd: ord (gordd) — sledge-hammer, mallet; noun f., plural yrd (gyrdd) (ac yrd porth uy llys i 'with the gate-hammers of my court'); what the gate-hammers were (knockers or mallets) is not certain; radical after ac 'with'
mynweireu: mynweir (mynwair) — collar, neck-band; noun, mwn 'neck' + gweir 'band, loop'; plural mynweireu (mynweireu yr essynn 'the collars of the asses'); radical
essynn: asyn (asyn) — ass, donkey; plural essynn (spelt with ss, nn) 'asses' (yr essynn 'the asses'); the plural form is uncertain; radical after the article
bydyn: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. habitual imperfect 'they used to be, had been' (wedy bydyn yn kywein gueir 'after they had been carting hay'), a slip for bydynt or a 3 pl. without -t (the Red Book has bydynt); radical after wedy
kywein: cywain (cywain) — to gather, carry in, haul; verbal noun (yn kywein gueir 'carrying hay'); the sense is uncertain; radical after yn
gueir: gwair (gwair) — hay; noun m. (kywein gueir 'carrying hay'), gu = gw; the sense is uncertain (the Red Book has geir); radical as object
mynwgyl: mynwgyl (mynwgl) — neck; noun m. (am y mynwgyl hitheu 'about her neck'); radical after y 'her' (the mutation of y 'her' is spirant/h-, not soft, so m stays)
kyuarwydyt: kyuarwydyt (cyfarwyddyd) — tale, story, storytelling (the old sense; the modern word means 'guidance'); noun m. (y kyuarwydyt hwnnw 'that tale'); radical after the article
mabinogi: mabinogi (mabinogi) — the Mabinogi; noun m., here the title in Mabinogi Mynweir a Mynord; the original meaning (tale of youth?) is disputed; radical
mynweir: mynweir (mynwair) — collar, neck-band; noun, mwn 'neck' + gweir 'band'; in the title Mabinogi Mynweir a Mynord 'the Mabinogi of Collar and Hammer' (Red Book mynnweir), for Rhiannon's ass-collars; radical
mynord: mynord (no modern form) — apparently a neck-hammer, mwn 'neck' + ord 'hammer' (cf. Pryderi's yrd porth); second element of the title Mabinogi Mynweir a Mynord; the Red Book has mynoad, a different form of unclear sense; meaning not certain; radical
mabinogy: mabinogi (mabinogi) — the Mabinogi; noun m., spelt with -y (o'r Mabinogy 'of the Mabinogi'); radical after the article 'r
math: Math — personal name: Math son of Mathonwy, lord of Gwynedd (Math uab Mathonwy oed arglwyd ar Wyned 'Math son of Mathonwy was lord over Gwynedd'); radical here (soft form Uath is separate)
mathonwy: Mathonwy — personal name, the father of Math (Math uab Mathonwy); genitive in a patronymic, no mutation
wyned: Gwyned (Gwynedd) — proper name, the kingdom of north-west Wales; soft-mutated (Gw>w) after ar 'over' (arglwyd ar Wyned 'lord over Gwynedd')
morgannhwc: Morgannwc (Morgannwg) — proper name, Morgannwg/Glamorgan, a region of south Wales (spelt here with -nhwc); radical, one of the cantrefs of the south listed after seith 'seven'
kyredigyawn: Keredigyawn (Ceredigion) — proper name, the region of west Wales, here spelt Kyredigyawn; radical (a phedwar Kyredigyawn 'and four of Ceredigion')
thri: tri (tri) — three (m.); numeral; spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and' (a thri Ystrat Tywi 'and three of Ystrat Tywi')
ymlyc: yn + plyc (plyg) — in the fold of; yn 'in' assimilated to ym before p, with plyc 'fold' (ymlyc croth morwyn 'in the fold of a maiden's lap'); the nasal mutation (ym mhlyc) is not fully shown in the spelling
croth: croth (croth) — womb, belly, lap; noun f.; radical, a genitive-like noun after ymlyc
kynwryf: kynwryf (cynnwrf) — commotion, tumult, uproar; noun m. (kynwryf ryuel 'a commotion of war'); radical, subject of the clause
ryuel: ryuel (rhyfel) — war; noun m.; radical (genitive after kynwryf)
llesteirei: llesteiraw (llesteirio) — to hinder, prevent; 3 sg. imperfect in -ei (a'y llesteirei 'that prevented him', with infixed 'y 'him'); no mutation after the infixed 'y
goewin: Goewin — personal name: Goewin daughter of Pebin of Dol Pebin in Arfon, Math's foot-holder; radical
pebin: Pebin — personal name, the father of Goewin (Goewin uerch Pebin; Dol Pebin 'Pebin's meadow'); no mutation
dol: dol (dôl) — meadow, water-meadow, dale; noun f.; first element of place-names (Dol Pebin 'Pebin's meadow', Dol Penmaen); after o 'from', which softens, but d > dd does not show in this spelling (o Dol Pebin)
hoes: oes (oes) — age, lifetime, generation; noun f. (yn y hoes 'in her lifetime'); h-prefixed before the vowel after y 'her' (the possessive 'her' aspirates / adds h- to a vowel)
wydit: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; impersonal imperfect 'was known' (o'r a wydit yno 'of those that were known there'); soft-mutated (g lost) after the relative a
dathyl: Dathyl — second element of the place-name Kaer Dathyl, Math's court in Arfon (cf. Tathyl); radical
wastatrwyd: gwastatrwyd (gwastadrwydd) — constancy, steadiness, permanence; here (y wastatrwyd) his settled seat or constant abode (sense approximate); noun m.; soft-mutated (g lost) after y 'his'
gylchu: kylchu (cylchu) — to go round, make a circuit of, travel about; verbal noun, soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'to' and after the verb allei (ny allei gylchu y wlat 'he could not go round the land'; y gylchu y wlat 'to go round the land')
giluathwy: Giluathwy (Gilfaethwy) — personal name: Gilfaethwy son of Don, brother of Gwydion; radical
don: Don — personal name; in a patronymic (uab Don 'son of Don'): Gilfaethwy, Euyd and Gwydion are sons of Don, and Don is Math's sister (nyeint ueibon y chwaer)
euyd: Euyd (Eufydd) — personal name: Euyd son of Dôn, named in the White Book beside Gilfaethwy as Math's nephew (the Red Book spells it eueyd; later editions emend to Gwydion); radical after a 'and'
nyeint: nei (nai) — nephew; plural nyeint 'nephews' (modern neiaint); (o nyeint ueibon y chwaer 'as/of nephews, sons of his sister'); the sense of o here is uncertain; radical
ueibon: mab (mab) — son; plural meibon 'sons' (modern meibion), spelt ueibon; soft-mutated (m>u) as a noun in apposition to the preceding nyeint ('nephews, sons of his sister')
giluaethwy: Giluaethwy (Gilfaethwy) — personal name, a variant spelling of Giluathwy: Gilfaethwy son of Don; radical
charu: caru (caru) — to love; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after y 'her' (a'y charu 'and (to) love her')
wnay: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. imperfect 'would do, was to do', spelt -ay for -ei (na wydat beth a wnay ymdanei 'that he did not know what he should do about her'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
ymdanei: ymdan (amdan) — about; conjugated preposition 3 sg. f. 'about her' (modern amdani) (beth a wnay ymdanei 'what he should do about her'); no mutation
atueilaw: atueilaw (adfeilio) — to decay, waste away; verbal noun (yn atueilaw 'wasting away', said of his colour and looks); no mutation (vowel)
guydyon: Gwydion — personal name: Gwydion son of Don (also spelt Wydyon, Gwydyon), Math's nephew; Guydyon with u for w; radical (after the particle y in heb y Guydyon 'said Gwydion')
urawd: brawt (brawd) — brother; noun m., d spelling t; soft-mutated (b>u) after y 'his' (Guydyon y urawd 'Gwydion his brother', i.e. Gilfaethwy's brother)
synnyeit: synnyeit (synied) — to look at, observe, perceive; verbal noun naming the deed after Sef a wnaeth (synnyeit dydgweith arnaw yn graf 'gazing closely at him one day'); radical
ham: am (am) — about, for; in pa ham 'why' (modern paham, lit. 'for what'); the h is part of the compound as written, not a mutation caused by pa (pa softens)
gwelaf: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. present 'I see' (Gwelaf arnat 'I see on you'); radical, verb in first place with no particle
frwytha: ffrwytho (ffrwytho) — to bear fruit, prosper, avail; 3 sg. present 'it avails, profits' (ny frwytha ymi 'it does not avail me'); ff does not mutate, single f is the scribe's spelling; after ny 'not'
adef: adef (addef) — to confess, admit, acknowledge; verbal noun (y adef y neb 'to confess it to anyone'); no mutation (vowel)
kynedyf: kynedyf (cynneddf) — inborn quality, special property, nature, endowment; noun f. (kynedyf Math 'Math's special property'); radical, object of wdost
hustyng: hustyng (hustyng) — whisper, secret word; noun m. (ba hustyng bynnac 'whatever whisper'); radical (h does not mutate)
kyuarfo: kyuaruot (cyfarfod) — to meet, come upon, reach; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may meet' (o ry kyuarfo y guynt ac ef 'if the wind should meet it'); the perfective ry would be expected to soften k>g, not shown in the spelling
guynt: gwynt (gwynt) — wind; noun m.; radical gu- (= gw-) after the article y
guybyd: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. present/future 'will know' (ef a'y guybyd 'he will know it', with infixed y 'it'); g kept after infixed y
caru: caru (caru) — to love; verbal noun, fronted for emphasis before yd wyt ti (caru Goewin yd wyt ti 'it is loving Goewin that you are'); radical
dromhaf: trwm (trwm) — heavy; superlative trymaf, spelt dromhaf 'heaviest', sigh being a feminine noun; soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine noun ucheneit (ucheneit dromhaf 'the heaviest sigh')
ucheneidaw: ucheneidaw (ochneidio) — to sigh, groan; verbal noun, with th 'your' before it (a'th ucheneidaw 'and your sighing'); no mutation (vowel)
goruydir: goruot (gorfod) — to overcome, prevail, succeed; impersonal present 'one prevails' (nyt o hynny y goruydir 'it is not by that that one prevails'); radical after the particle y
dygyuori: dygyuori (dygyfori) — to muster, rally, stir up; verbal noun, longer form of dygyuor (dygyuori Gwyned a Phowys a Deheubarth 'to muster Gwynedd and Powys and Deheubarth')
gwyned: Gwyned (Gwynedd) — proper name, the kingdom of north-west Wales; radical (object of dygyuori; Gwyned a Phowys a Deheubarth)
phowys: Powys — proper name, the kingdom of east and mid Wales; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
deheubarth: Deheubarth — proper name, the southern realm (deheu 'south' + parth 'part'); radical
lawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, merry; adjective, soft-mutated (ll>l) as the complement after byd (a byd lawen di 'and be glad')
paraf: peri (peri) — to cause, bring about, arrange; 1 sg. present 'I will cause' (a mi a'y paraf yt 'and I will bring it about for you'); p kept after infixed y 'it'
uath: Math — personal name; soft-mutated (M>u) after at 'to' and ar 'on, to' (at Uath; ar Uath uab Mathonwy) and in yguelei Uath (cause there uncertain)
bryuet: pryf (pryf) — creature, animal, worm; plural pryfet 'creatures' (modern pryfed), spelt bryuet; soft-mutated (p>b) after ryw 'kind of' (y ryw bryuet 'some kind of creatures')
henw: enw (enw) — name; noun m. (eu henw wy 'their name'); h- prefixed to the vowel after eu 'their'
hobeu: hob (hob) — pig, hog; plural hobeu, the name the strange beasts are first given before moch (Hobeu, Arglwyd 'Hobs, lord'); radical
aniueileit: aniueil (anifail) — animal, beast; noun m., plural aniueileit (modern anifeiliaid); radical (vowel)
bychein: bychan (bychan) — small, little; adjective, plural bychein (modern bychain) agreeing with the plural aniueileit (aniueileit bychein 'small animals'); radical after its noun
chic: kic (cig) — meat, flesh; noun m., spirant-mutated (c>ch) after no 'than' (guell eu kic no chic eidon 'their flesh is better than the flesh of oxen')
eidon: eidon (eidion) — ox, bullock, cattle (beef); noun m., here generic (kic eidon 'ox-flesh, beef'); radical (genitive after chic)
ynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present 'they are' (Bychein ynt wynteu 'small they are'); no mutation
symudaw: symudaw (symud) — to change, alter, move; verbal noun (yn symudaw enweu 'changing names'); radical
enweu: enw (enw) — name; plural enweu (modern enwau); object of the verbal noun symudaw, no mutation (vowel)
biewynt: piau (piau) — to own, be the property of; pwy biewynt wy 'whose are they?' (lit. 'who owns them'); the -ynt is a 3 pl. ending; the b- form is usual after pwy (pwy bieu), but pwy is not a softening word; the exact analysis of the form is uncertain
anuonet: anuon (anfon) — to send; impersonal preterite 'was sent' (yd anuonet idaw o Annwn 'was sent to him from Annwn'); no mutation (vowel), after particle yd
cadw: cadw (cadw) — to keep, preserve, retain; verbal noun (yd ys yn cadw o'r enw hwnnw 'keeping of that name'); radical after yn
hwch: hwch (hwch) — sow; noun f.; radical (hanner hwch 'half a sow')
hob: hob (hob) — pig, hog; singular of hobeu (hanner hwch, hanner hob 'half sow, half hob'); noun m.; radical
keffir: caffael (cael) — to get, obtain; impersonal present 'is got' (ba furuf y keffir wy y gantaw ef 'by what means are they got from him'); c unmutated after the particle y
deudecuet: deudecuet (deuddegfed) — twelfth; ordinal (ar uyn deudecuet 'with me as the twelfth'); radical, the nasal mutation being written on uyn
beird: bardd (bardd) — poet, bard; plural beird 'poets' (yn rith beird 'in the guise of poets'); radical
necau: necau (nacáu) — to refuse, deny; verbal noun, with ych 'you' before it as its object (ych necau 'refuse you'); the same verb as nacau; radical
trawscwyd: trawscwyd (no secure modern form) — device, contrivance, stratagem (sense from the context; the word is rare); noun m. (Nit drwc uyn trawscwyd i 'my contrivance is not a bad one'); after uyn 'my' the nasal mutation is written on uyn and t is left plain
kerda: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; 2 sg. imperative 'go!' (kerda ragot 'go on your way'); radical
deguyr: deg + gwyr — ten men; deg 'ten' + guyr (gwyr) 'men' written as one word, the two g's written once (a deguyr gyt ac wynt 'and ten men with them'); deg does not soften what follows
heredigyawn: Keredigyawn (Ceredigion) — proper name; nasal mutation (c>ngh) after yg 'in', spelt yg Heredigyawn with the h standing for the gh of the nasal (hyt yg Heredigyawn 'as far as in Ceredigion')
elwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (y lle a elwir 'the place that is called'); g lost by soft mutation after the relative a
rudlan: Rudlan (Rhuddlan) — proper name, in Rudlan Teiui 'Rhuddlan Teifi', the place of Pryderi's court in Ceredigion (probably rud 'red' + glan 'bank'); no mutation
teiui: Teiui (Teifi) — proper name, the river Teifi; genitive in Rudlan Teiui, no mutation
awrhon: awrhon (yr awrhon, awr hon) — this hour, now; awr 'hour' + hon 'this' run together, adverbial (yr awrhon 'now, at the present'); no mutation
neillaw: neillaw (no modern form) — one side; neill 'other, one' + llaw 'hand' written as one word (ar neillaw Pryderi 'at Pryderi's side'); noun f.; no mutation shown
gossodet: gossot (gosod) — to place, set, seat; impersonal preterite 'was placed' (y gossodet Guydyon 'Gwydion was seated'); radical after y
cahel: caffael (cael) — to get, have; verbal noun, spelt cahel beside cael (da yw genhym ni cahel kyuarwydyt 'we are glad to get a tale'); radical
gwreinc: gwreang (gwreang) — youth, young man; plural gwreinc 'young men' (rei o'r gwreinc racco 'some of the young men yonder'); radical. Not modern gwrêng 'common people'
delher: dyuot (dod) — to come; impersonal present subjunctive 'one comes' (y nos gyntaf y delher at wr mawr 'the first night that one comes to a great man'); radical d after the particle y
penkerd: pencerdd (pencerdd) — chief of song, chief poet; noun m. (dywedut o'r penkerd 'to be told by the chief poet'); radical after the article r, o 'by' marks the agent
gyuarwydyd: kyuarwydyt (cyfarwyddyd) — tale, story; noun m., spelt with -yd; soft-mutated (k>g) as the object of dywedaf (Mi a dywedaf gyuarwydyd 'I will tell a tale')
wydyon: Gwydion — personal name (Gwydyon, Wydyon); soft-mutated (G>w) after gan 'with', after e 'to' and in apposition to ynteu (Ynteu Wydyon 'he, Gwydion')
didanu: didanu (diddanu) — to comfort, entertain, amuse; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaeth (didanu y llys a wnaeth 'he entertained the court'); radical
ymdidaneu: ymdidan (ymddiddan) — conversation, talk; plural ymdidaneu (modern ymddiddanion); noun m., radical after ar
chyuarwydyt: kyuarwydyt (cyfarwyddyd) — tale, storytelling; noun m., spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyuarwydyt 'and (with) a tale')
didan: didan (diddan) — pleasant, entertaining, comforting; adjective as predicate after yn (yn didan gan Pryderi ymdidan ac ef 'and pleasant to Pryderi was conversing with him'); d not shown softened after yn
tauawt: tauawt (tafod) — tongue; noun, usually m. (Tauawt lawn da 'a full good tongue'); radical
lawn: llawn (llawn) — full; here as an adverb before an adjective, 'very' (Tauawt lawn da 'a very good tongue'); written with one l, where the Red Book has llawn da: whether this is a softening (as after a feminine noun) or only a spelling is not clear
teu: teu (tau) — yours; independent possessive pronoun 2 sg., with the article (y teu di 'yours'), di echoing; no mutation
ymadolwyn: ymadolwyn (no modern form) — to beseech, entreat; verbal noun, ym- + adolwyn 'beseech', with a 'with' of the person entreated (ymadolwyn a thidi 'to entreat you'); radical
elont: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. present subjunctive 'may go' (nat elont y genhyf 'that they may not go from me'); radical
hilyont: hilyaw (hilio) — to breed, multiply, bear young; 3 pl. present subjunctive 'may breed' (yny hilyont eu deu kymeint 'until they breed twice as many'); radical
geireu: gair (gair) — word; plural geireu (modern geiriau); radical after the article r with a plural
gallaf: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 sg. present 'I can' (Sef ual y gallaf 'this is how I can'); radical after the particle y
nacaha: nacau (nacáu) — to refuse, deny; 2 sg. imperative 'refuse!' (ac nacaha ui ohonunt 'and refuse me of them'); the sense needs a lost negative, na, as the established text notes; radical
dangossaf: dangos (dangos) — to show, offer; 1 sg. present/future 'I will show' (Auory minheu a dangossaf gyfnewit 'tomorrow I for my part will show an exchange'); the soft form after a is not shown in the spelling
lletty: llety (llety) — lodging, quarters; noun m. (y'r lletty 'to the lodging'); radical after the article
chawni: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 pl. future/present chawn 'we shall get' with the pronoun ni 'we' run on (ny chawni y moch 'we shall not get the pigs'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after ny
drawscwyd: trawscwyd (no secure modern form) — device, contrivance, stratagem (sense from the context; the word is rare); noun m.; soft-mutated (t>d) after pa 'what' (pa drawscwyd 'by what contrivance')
keir: caffael (cael) — to get; impersonal present 'is got' (pa drawscwyd y keir wynteu 'by what means are they to be got'); radical c after the particle y
geluydodeu: keluydyt (celfyddyd) — art, skill, craft; noun f., plural keluydodeu (modern celfyddydau); soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'his' (yn y geluydodeu 'into his arts')
dechreuawt: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 sg. preterite 'began' (ac y dechreuawt dangos y hut 'and he began to show the enchantment'); radical after y
hudwys: hudaw (hudo) — to enchant, conjure by magic; 3 sg. preterite 'conjured' in -wys (yd hudwys deudec emys 'he conjured twelve emys'); radical after yd
deudec: deudeg (deuddeg) — twelve; numeral, c spelling g, followed by a singular noun (deudec milgi, deudec torch); no mutation
emys: amws (amws) — stallion, war-horse; plural emys 'stallions' (deudec emys 'twelve stallions'), the same beasts later called meirch 'horses'; noun m.; radical
milgi: milgi (milgi) — greyhound; noun m., singular after a numeral (deudec milgi 'twelve greyhounds'); radical
bronwyn: bronwyn (bronwyn) — white-breasted; adjective, bron 'breast' + gwyn 'white', with gwyn softened (gw>w) in the compound; follows its noun (milgi bronwyn 'white-breasted greyhound')
torch: torch (torch) — torque, neck-ring, collar; noun f. (deudec torch 'twelve collars'); radical after a numeral
kynllyuan: kynllyuan (cynllyfan) — leash, lead; noun m., singular after a numeral (deudec kynllyuan 'twelve leashes'); radical
kyfrwy: kyfrwy (cyfrwy) — saddle; noun m., singular after a numeral (deudec kyfrwy 'twelve saddles'); radical
frwyneu: ffrwyn (ffrwyn) — bridle; noun f., plural ffrwyneu (modern ffrwynau); the single f is the scribe's spelling of ff, no mutation (a'r frwyneu 'and the bridles'; eu frwyneu 'their bridles')
graessaw: graessaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m. (a graessaw wrthyt 'and welcome to you'); radical; modern croeso is the same word in a later form
rydit: rydit (rhyddid) — freedom, release; noun m. (llyma rydit yti am y geir 'here is release for you concerning the word'); r for rh
rodut: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 2 sg. imperfect/conditional in -ut 'you would give' (nas rodut 'that you would not give them'); radical after nas
guerthut: gwerthu (gwerthu) — to sell; 2 sg. imperfect/conditional in -ut 'you would sell' (nas guerthut 'that you would not sell them'); radical after nas, since the infixed 's causes no mutation
deudeg: deudeg (deuddeg) — twelve; numeral, spelt with g (y deudeg meirch 'the twelve horses'); no mutation
gyueir: kyueir (cyweir) — ready, equipped, in harness; adjective (ual y maent yn gyueir 'as they are, equipped'); soft-mutated (k>g) after predicative yn
torcheu: torch (torch) — torque, collar; plural torcheu (modern torchau); radical after eu 'their' (eu torcheu 'their collars')
kynllyuaneu: kynllyuan (cynllyfan) — leash, lead; plural kynllyuaneu (modern cynllyfanau); radical after eu 'their'
rithassei: rithyaw (rhithio) — to shape, conjure into a form; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had shaped' in -assei (a rithassei ef o'r madalch 'he had shaped out of the fungus'); after the relative a rh would be softened to r, but this spelling writes r for both
madalch: madalch (madarch) — mushrooms, toadstools, fungi; collective plural noun; radical after the article r ('o'r madalch' 'out of the toadstools')
gaussant: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 3 pl. preterite 'they got, they had' in -ssant (Sef a gaussant yn y kynghor 'this is what they had in their counsel'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
kymeryssant: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 pl. preterite 'they took' in -yssant (y kymeryssant wy ganheat 'they took leave'); radical after y
ganheat: kanhead (caniatâd) — leave, permission; noun m., in kymryt ganheat 'to take leave'; soft-mutated (c>g) as object of the verb
geimeit: keimyat (ceimiad) — champion, warrior; plural keimeit, in address (A geimeit 'O warriors'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the vocative a
bryssur: prysur (prysur) — hasty, quick, busy; adjective; adverbial after yn (yn bryssur 'hastily'), with p softened to b after the adverbial yn
phara: para (para, parhau) — to last, continue, endure; 3 sg. present/future 'will last' (Ny phara yr hut 'the enchantment will not last'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after ny
ygwarthaf: yg + gwarthaf (ar warthaf) — upon, at the top of; gwarthaf 'summit, top' (hyt ygwarthaf Keredigyawn 'to the upper part of Ceredigion'); written as one word, the g the trace of yn + gwarthaf; sense approximate
achaus: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m., spelt achaus with u (o achaus hynny 'because of that'); radical
mochtref: Mochtref — place-name (moch 'pigs' + tref 'homestead'), the name of the places where the pigs spent the night; radical
elenit: Elenit (Elenydd) — proper name, the mountain upland of mid Wales (dros Elenit 'over Elenydd'); no mutation
keri: Keri (Ceri) — proper name, Ceri in mid Wales, between Ceri and Arwystli; radical
arwystli: Arwystli — proper name, a district of mid Wales; radical
powys: Powys — proper name, the kingdom of east and mid Wales; radical (nasal mutation not shown after ym 'in': ym Powys)
mochnant: Mochnant — place-name in Powys (moch 'pigs' + nant 'valley'), named from the pigs; radical
odynha: odyna (oddyna) — from there, then, afterwards; adverb, spelt odynha (variant with h) beside odyna; no mutation
ros: Ros (Rhos) — proper name, the cantref Rhos in north Wales (cantref Ros); radical
gwydyon: Gwydion — personal name: Gwydion son of Don (Gwydyon); radical (the y before it in heb y Gwydyon is the particle that introduces a named speaker)
gyrchwn: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to go to, make for; 1 pl. present/future 'we will make for' (ni a gyrchwn 'we will make for'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
kedernit: kedernit (cadernid) — strength, stronghold, fastness; noun m. (kedernit Gwynet 'the stronghold of Gwynedd'); radical, also as the object straight after a verb, where softening would be expected (ni a gyrchwn kedernit; the Red Book likewise); after yg 'in' the nasal is shown only on the preposition (yg kedernit)
gwynet: Gwynet (Gwynedd) — proper name, the kingdom of north-west Wales, spelt with t; radical (genitive after kedernit)
lluydaw: lluydaw (lluyddu) — to muster, raise a host, march with an army; verbal noun (yd ys yn lluydaw yn an ol 'is mustering a host after us'); radical after yn
arllechwoed: Arllechwoed (Arllechwedd) — proper name, a district of Gwynedd, ar 'on' + llechwedd 'slope'; radical after o in o Arllechwoed
creu: creu (modern form uncertain) — sty, pen, enclosure for animals; noun m. (gwneuthur creu y'r moch 'making a sty for the pigs'); radical
creuwryon: Creuwryon — place-name, the name given to the upper township after the sty (creu); the second element is of uncertain meaning; radical
tathyl: Tathyl — second element of Kaer Tathyl, Math's court, spelt Tathyl beside Dathyl; radical
hwyret: hwyr (hwyr) — late, slow; equative hwyret 'so late, so slow' (Ryued uu hwyret y kerdyssawchi 'it was a wonder how slowly you travelled'); radical
kerdyssawchi: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, travel; 2 pl. preterite 'you travelled' in -yssawch with chi 'you' run on (kerdyssawch chi); radical after y
aethawch: mynet (mynd) — to go; 2 pl. preterite 'you went' (yd aethawch yn eu hwysc 'that you went after them'); radical
hwysc: (g)wysc (wysg) — track, course; spelt without its g, and so taking h- after eu 'their' as a vowel-initial word does (yn eu hwysc 'on their track, after them'; the Red Book likewise); eu does not change g to h
issot: issot (isod) — below, lower down; adverb, (y cantref arall issot 'the other cantref below'); no mutation
clywynt: klywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. imperfect 'they heard' (llyma y clywynt yr utkyrn 'behold, they heard the horns'); radical after y
utkyrn: utgorn (utgorn) — horn, trumpet; plural utkyrn (modern utgyrn); noun m., radical after the article r
guiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to dress, put on armour, arm; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethant (guiscaw a wnaethant wynteu 'they armed themselves'); radical (gu- = gw-)
uydant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present-future 'they are, they will be', used in narrative after yny 'until' (yny uydant ym Pennard 'until they were at Pennardd'); soft-mutated (b>u) after yny
pennard: Pennard (Pennardd) — proper name, a place in Arfon (Penn 'head' + ard 'height'); radical after ym 'in' (nasal mutation not shown)
ymhwelwys: ymhoelut (ymchwelyd) — to turn, turn back, return; 3 sg. preterite 'returned' in -wys (yd ymhwelwys Guydyon 'Gwydion returned'); radical after yd
chiluathwy: Giluathwy (Gilfaethwy) — personal name; spirant-mutated after a 'and', spelt Chiluathwy as if the radical began with C, though elsewhere in the text it begins with G (a Chiluathwy y urawt 'and Gilfaethwy his brother'); the spelling is irregular
yguelei: yg + gwelei (yng ngwely) — in the bed of; yn 'in' + gwely 'bed', spelt with -ei, the nasal mutation shown by the g of yg (Ac yguelei Uath 'and in Math's bed'); the Red Book also has ygwelei
goewyn: Goewyn — personal name, a variant spelling of Goewin: Goewin daughter of Pebin, Math's foot-holder; radical
morynyon: morwyn (morwyn) — maiden, girl; plural morynyon (modern morynion); radical after the article y with a plural
amharchus: amharchus (amharchus) — disrespectful, shameful, insulting; adjective, adverbial after yn (yn amharchus 'shamefully'); no mutation (vowel)
arhoynt: aros (aros) — to wait, await, stay; 3 pl. imperfect, here subjunctive in sense 'they should wait for' (ba tu yd arhoynt Pryderi 'in which quarter they should await Pryderi'), stem arho-; radical
yghymherued: yg + kymherued — in the middle of, between; kymherued 'middle, midst' (cf. perued, perfedd); the yg-h shows nasal mutation (c>ngh) after yn 'in' (yghymherued y dwy uaynawr 'in the middle of the two manors'); sense approximate
uaynawr: maenawr (maenor) — manor, a territorial unit; noun f., soft-mutated (m>u) after dwy 'two' (y dwy uaynawr 'the two manors')
arhoed: aros (aros) — to wait, await; impersonal preterite in -ed 'there was waiting, one waited' (yd arhoed 'they waited'); radical after yd
maynawr: maenawr (maenor) — manor, a territorial unit; noun f., first element of the names Maynawr Bennard and Maynawr Coet Alun; radical
bennard: Pennard (Pennardd) — proper name; soft-mutated (P>b) after the feminine noun maynawr (Maynawr Bennard 'the manor of Pennard')
alun: Alun — proper name in Coet Alun 'Alun's wood' (the river/personal name Alun); genitive, radical
phyderi: Pryderi — personal name, written Phyderi: spirant-mutated after a 'and' (p>ph), but with the r lost, a scribal slip for Phryderi (A Phyderi a'y kyrchwys 'and Pryderi attacked them')
lladua: lladua (lladfa) — slaughter, killing; noun f. (y llas lladua uawr 'a great slaughter was made'); radical
enkil: enkil (encilio) — to retreat, withdraw; verbal noun, short form (reit y wyr y Deheu enkil 'the men of the south had to retreat'); radical
enkilyssant: enkil (encilio) — to retreat, withdraw; 3 pl. preterite 'they retreated' in -yssant (lle yd enkilyssant 'where they retreated'); radical after yd
nant: nant (nant) — valley, brook; noun m., first element of the place-name Nant Call; radical
call: call (call) — wise, prudent, sensible; adjective, in the place-name Nant Call (the sense of the name is uncertain); radical after the masculine noun nant
ymlidywyd: ymlit (ymlid) — to pursue, chase; impersonal preterite 'was pursued' in -ywyd (hyt yno yd ymlidywyd 'as far as there they were pursued'); radical after yd
ayrua: ayrua (aerfa) — slaughter, carnage; noun f. (yr ayrua diueuessur y meint 'the slaughter was immeasurable in size'); radical (vowel) after yr
diueuessur: diuessur (difesur) — immeasurable, beyond measure; adjective, di- 'without' + messur 'measure', softened (m>u) after di-; spelt diueuessur with a dittography as the established text notes; follows its noun
kilyssant: kilyaw (cilio) — to withdraw, retreat; 3 pl. preterite 'they retreated' in -yssant (y kilyssant hyt y lle a elwir Dol Penmaen 'they retreated to the place called Dol Penmaen'); radical after y
penmaen: Penmaen — second element of the place-name Dol Penmaen (pen 'head' + maen 'stone'); unsoftened as Evans prints it after the feminine dol, where the modern name Dolbenmaen has b
clymu: clymu (clymu) — to bind, knot, join; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethant (clymu a wnaethant 'they came together / bound themselves', sense approximate); radical
cheissaw: keissaw (ceisio) — to seek, try, attempt; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a cheissaw ymdangneuedu 'and seeking to make peace')
ymdangneuedu: ymdangneuedu (no secure modern form; cf. tangnefeddu) — to make peace with one another; verbal noun, reciprocal ym- + tangneuedu, with t softened to d after ym-
gwystlaw: gwystlaw (gwystlo) — to pledge, give a hostage; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaeth (gwystlaw a wnaeth Pryderi 'Pryderi gave a pledge'); radical
wystlwys: gwystlaw (gwystlo) — to pledge, give as hostage; 3 sg. preterite in -wys (Sef a wystlwys 'this is what he pledged'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
gwrgi: Gwrgi — personal name (Gwrgi Guastra), the hostage given by Pryderi; radical
guastra: Guastra (Gwastra) — personal name or epithet of Gwrgi (Gwrgi Guastra); meaning uncertain; radical
