ueibyon: mab (mab) — son; plural meibyon (modern meibion), spelt ueibyon; soft-mutated (m>u) after o 'of' (o ueibyon guyrda 'of sons of noblemen')
traeth: traeth (traeth) — shore, beach, strand; noun m., in y Traeth Mawr 'the Great Strand'; radical after the article y
uelen: melen (melyn) — yellow; adjective, here the feminine form, in the place-name Melen Ryd 'Yellow Ford'; soft-mutated (m>u) after the article y (y Uelen Ryd)
pedyt: pedyt (no modern form) — foot-soldiers, infantry; collective noun (y pedyt 'the foot-soldiers'); radical
reoli: reoli (rheoli) — to rule, control, restrain; verbal noun (ny ellit eu reoli 'they could not be restrained'); radical
ymsaethu: ymsaethu (no separate modern form; cf. saethu) — to shoot at one another; verbal noun, ym- reflexive + saethu 'shoot' (o ymsaethu 'from shooting at each other'); radical
guahard: guahard (gwahardd) — to forbid, hinder, restrain; verbal noun/noun (erchi guahard y deulu 'to ask the restraining of the two hosts'); radical
baryssei: peri (peri) — to cause, bring about; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had caused' in -ssei (canys ef a baryssei hynny 'for he had caused that'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the relative/particle a
genhat: kennat (cennad) — messenger, message, errand; noun f.; soft-mutated (k>g) after the article y (y doeth y genhat 'the message/messenger came'); sense 'message' or 'envoy' approximate
gadaf: gadu (gadael) — to leave, let, allow; 1 sg. present/future 'I will allow' (mi a'e gadaf yn llawen 'I will allow it gladly'); radical after infixed e 'it'
chymellaf: kymell (cymell) — to urge, compel, force; 1 sg. present 'I compel' (Ni chymellaf inheu ar neb 'I will not compel anyone'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after ni 'not'
ohanam: o (o) — of, from; conjugated preposition 1 pl. 'of us' (modern ohonom), spelt ohanam (wneuthur ohanam ninheu 'doing from us, we for our part'); no mutation
med: medd (meddai) — says; defective verb used only to report another's words (teg, med Pryderi 'fair, says Pryderi'); radical
gorf: corff (corff) — body, person; noun m., f for ff; soft-mutated (c>g) after y 'his' (dodi y gorf yn erbyn y eidaw 'to put his body against his')
segur: segur (segur) — idle, at rest, at peace; adjective, adverbial after yn (gadu y deu lu yn segur 'to leave the two hosts at rest'); no mutation (s does not mutate)
dodaf: dodi (dodi) — to put, set; 1 sg. present/future 'I will put' (mi a dodaf uyg korf 'I will put my body'); soft form after a not shown
korf: corff (corff) — body, person; noun m., f for ff; radical k after uyg 'my' (uyg korf), the g of uyg being the written trace of the nasal mutation
my: uy (fy) — my, spelt my, in my hun 'myself' (namyn my hun 'but myself'); the Red Book also has my hun
neilltuwyt: neilltuaw (neilltuo) — to set apart, separate, put aside; impersonal preterite 'was set apart' in -wyt (E gwyr hynny a neilltuwyt 'those men were set apart'); radical after a
grym: grym (grym) — force, power, strength; noun m. (o nerth grym ac angerd 'by strength, force and might'); radical
angerd: angerd (angerdd) — fury, ardour, might; noun m.; radical
oruu: goruot (gorfod) — to overcome, prevail; 3 sg. preterite 'prevailed' (Guydyon a oruu 'Gwydion prevailed'); g lost by soft mutation after the particle a
las: llad (lladd) — to kill; impersonal preterite 'was killed' (a Phryderi a las 'and Pryderi was slain'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the particle a
tyuyawc: Tyuyawc (no secure modern form) — second element of the name of a stone, Maen Tyuyawc, above Y Felenrhyd; the meaning is uncertain (perhaps from tyfu 'grow'); follows its noun, radical
cladwyt: claddu (claddu) — to bury; impersonal preterite 'was buried' in -wyt (y cladwyt 'he was buried'); radical after y
ued: bed (bedd) — grave; noun m., soft-mutated (b>u) after y 'his' (y may y ued 'his grave is there')
argan: argan (no common modern form) — lament, wailing, outcry; noun m. (ac argan truan ganthunt 'and a wretched lament with them'); radical
truan: truan (truan) — wretched, miserable, pitiful; adjective after its noun (argan truan 'a wretched lament'); radical
goreuguyr: goreuguyr (goreugwŷr) — best men, chief men; compound of goreu 'best' + gwyr 'men' (llawer oc eu goreuguyr 'many of their best men'); radical after eu 'their'
harueu: arueu (arfau) — arms, weapons; plural (modern arfau); noun m.; h- prefixed to the vowel after eu 'their' (eu harueu 'their arms')
